author: bassdr
body:
G_MW_SEGMENT indexes `mSegmentPointers[16]` with `offset / 4`, and `offset` arrives as `C0(0, 16)` — a full 16-bit field. `segNumber` reaches 16383: an unbounded 64-bit write up to ~128 KB past the array. The `G_MW_SEGMENT_INTERP` case directly below it already wraps with `offset % 16`.

`SegAddr` has the matching read: `segNum = (uint32_t)(w1 >> 24)`, unmasked, on a `uintptr_t`. A display list word of `0x24C00157EB` indexes entry 9408.

The RSP segment number is a 4-bit field, so wrapping is what the hardware does.

Found chasing a `gfx_dl_handler_common` SIGSEGV that ended in `double free or corruption (out)` — consistent with the stray write corrupting the heap and the segment table, then the next display list resolving a segment against garbage. Both copies (F3DEX2 and F3D) are fixed.

body:
Closes #513. Part **B of two**, stacked on #614 (the classifier, merged as `e9f3e92`). `

It now paints all three, where a browser does. ## The mechanism, and the thing approach 2 could not do A `display: inline` element holding an in-flow block-level box is **flattened out of the box tree exactly as a `display: contents` wrapper already is** (`Node::is_split_inline`, from PR A). `collect_run_units` recurses into it instead of pushing it, so its children become units of the nearest block container — which mints the anonymous block boxes *there*, around each inline run, with the block as their sibling. That is CSS 2.1 §9.2.1.1's box tree. Approach 2 (#596) produced a textbook-correct box tree inside the `` and every box was `0x0`, because the `` was still removed from its container's Taffy children. Geometry is the whole problem, and this is where it comes from: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | container's Taffy children | `[a]` | `[anon1, block, anon2]` | | ``'s Taffy children | `[text, block, tail]` | `[]` | | ``'s Taffy parent | `None` (detached) | `None` (never in any list) | | `.layout` | stale, or `0x0` by luck | `0x0`, **enforced by `E ghost box`** | | `block`'s Taffy parent | `` (unreachable) | the container | | container is an IFC root | yes | no — every inline unit carries a `run_box` | **No new `set_children` achieves the reparent.** Taffy's own `set_children` removes an adopted child from its previous parent (`taffy-0.12.2/src/tree/taffy_tree.rs:705-729`, which `sync_display_contents` already relies on), so the existing rebuild steals the block out of the `` and the anonymous boxes steal their members. The `` ends childless and parentless without being told to. And `` is not in `box_tree_children`, so paint, hit testing, stacking and `layer_bounds` never enter it. Every node is reachable in the box tree **exactly once**: `text` via anon1, the block via the container, `tail` via anon2. No double draw, no drop. ### Measured before it was designed The machinery this routes a split inline through is the machinery `display: contents` already uses, so the twins of these shapes were measured on the pre-fix base: ``` contents-wrapped text/block/tail h = 70 (Chrome: 70) ✓ contents-wrapped block only h = 30 (Chrome: 30) ✓ block only h = 0 (Chrome: 30) ✗ ``` That is a **third twin** the falsifier did not have, and a stronger control than the unwrapped one for this design: same shapes, same code path, already the browser's numbers. `an_inline_wrapper_agrees_with_a_display_contents_wrapper` now asserts the inline wrapper agrees with it. ## What this does NOT do **Fragment identity is not modelled.** CSS gives the inline box one real fragment per side, each a box with its own border and padding. rinch gives the fragments' *geometry*, plus a background rectangle per fragment, and keeps no box for the element itself. Do not read "block-in-inline splitting landed" as "rinch has inline fragments" — per-fragment **borders** are unbuilt. Stated in `paint::drawn_by_its_ifc`, at the zeroing in `read_layout_results`, and in the test module doc, so a future reader hits it. **#591 and #592 are deliberately untouched**, and they want opposite treatments, which is why they stayed separate issues: CSS 2.1 §9.4.2 says an out-of-flow box neither breaks an inline formatting context nor forces anonymous-box generation, so splitting around one would encode a rule that is simply wrong; and an `inline-block` is a block container that must generate anonymous boxes *inside itself*. Two fixtures stay `#[ignore]`d, retargeted to those issues and measured as unchanged. One side effect, measured rather than claimed: an out-of-flow child of an inline that *also* holds an in-flow block does now get laid out, because the split makes it a unit of the container. That does not generalise to #591's own shape and is not claimed to. ## The pieces - `collect_run_units` recurses into a split inline — the fix, one arm. Its three readers (run grouping, `box_tree_children`, `run_bookkeeping_violations`) stay one authority, so the run-bookkeeping invariant holds unchanged. - `box_tree_children`'s O(1) borrow now also requires no split child. Needed because `
card
` mints no run at all. - `effective_taffy_owner` / `taffy_child_list_owners` walk past a split inline, as they already walk past `Contents`, keeping #597's invariant true. **`box_tree_parent` deliberately does not** — a click walks it to find a `data-rid` (checked: `click_handling.rs` dispatch walks `node.parent`), and the position sum is made exact by the zeroing instead. Two consumers wanting opposite things, resolved the way `collect_taffy_contribution` vs `collect_effective_taffy_children` already is. - `split_inline_boxes` takes each split inline's boxes into its container's Taffy list and records `tree.split_inlines`; `restore_split_inlines` undoes it next pass. Without the first, a block-only split inline **after a block sibling** is positioned relative to the `` by Taffy and reached from the container by paint — drawn over its sibling. Without the second, an element that stops being split is left parentless and childless: #520/#597's shape, a third time. - `read_layout_results` zeroes a split inline's `layout`, and `taffy_tree_violations` puts it in the `boxless` set so **`E ghost box` enforces that**. This turns "it happens to be `0x0`" — the fixed point mutants in this region hide on — into an assertion, on the `block → inline` path where Taffy would otherwise keep serving a real stale box. - `contents_is_inline_transparent` finally reads `contributes_in_flow_block`; `scan_contents_children` and its per-call subtree walk are deleted. PR A's fixture asserted the *old* answer to keep that PR inert; it now asserts the new one, and its doc records both halves. - A split inline's background is bridged onto its fragments — one span per ancestor per **contiguous stretch** of the run, so two members inside one `` are one rectangle rather than two with a doubled seam. It covers element members, not just text. ### The two `break` arms are kept `mark_inline_descendants`' `InFlowBlock => break` and `walk_inline_children`'s `_ => break` are now **believed unreachable**: an IFC root's units cannot contain an `InFlowBlock`, because `has_inline && has_block` mints runs, every inline unit gets a `run_box`, and the root scan skips those. I tried to construct a survivor and could not — which is an argument, not a proof, and #585 is this repo's precedent for that distinction resolving as *live-but-untested*. Both stay fail-closed, each with the argument in a comment and **#615** named for the lost witnesses. Do not delete them on the strength of "no test covers this": coverage removed by a correct fix reads exactly like coverage that never existed. ## The waiver is retargeted, not deleted Your brief said the 16 waived `D detached` lines were all #513. Measured per-test: **exactly 1 survives, and it is the #591 shape** (`text
tail`) — the prediction held. Three lines appear in total, because two of this PR's own new fixtures build that shape deliberately as a control. So `block_in_inline_detachments` is renamed `strandings_under_a_detached_inline` with **no logic change** — it was always structural rather than a description of #513's markup, which is exactly why the retarget is a rename plus a doc rewrite. author: jordansmall
body:
Closes #3445

Every dispatch pass now leads with a byte-identical block, so prompt caching
gets a real prefix match across the passes of a run.

## What changed

- **Host-side issue read** (`cmd/launcher/internal/forge/issuetext.go`): a new
  `CommentLister` surface alongside `IssueTracker.Issue` renders the issue body
  plus a last-10-comment snapshot into one `ISSUE_TEXT` string, capped at 64KB
  with an explicit truncation marker. github (`gh` exec), forgejo (paginated
  REST), jira, and the fake tracker all implement it.
- **Transport** (`dispatch`, `main.go`): `ISSUE_TEXT` rides into the Box as a
  plain env var. `main.go` memoizes the lookup per issue number so the up-to-three
  `buildBoxEnv` calls behind one dispatch see byte-identical text. A fetch error
  now fails the dispatch rather than silently dropping the section the prompt
  promises the agent is there.
- **Assembly** (`promptassembly`): the rendered issue text is *appended* after
  the template body, wrapped by the new `promptfence` package's dynamic
  CommonMark fence with an explicit "quoted, not host-authored" preamble — the
  comment-injection trust boundary means any GitHub user's comment can reach
  this prompt.
- **Seeded blocks** (`orchestrator/run.go`): the three seeders now append their
  run-state block after the prompt instead of prepending it, so a pass's stable
  prefix is never displaced by per-pass state.
- **Prompts**: the `*issue-read-*` fragments no longer tell the agent to
  `gh issue view` / `fj issue view` the issue — the text is already in the
  prompt. A new check in `nix/checks/prompts.nix` bans those literals in every
  issue-read fragment so the instruction cannot creep back.

## Tests

`pass_kind_prefix_family_test.go` pins the per-pass prefix families
(implement/fix/land, review/delta-review, scout, research,
self-contained-research); `seed_prefix_invariant_test.go` pins the seeded append
order; a new `covered-cell-issue-text` golden exercises the fenced section
through the bash entrypoint path, with a fixture body carrying a literal
triple-backtick run.

## Reviewer notes

- Two non-blocking review findings were queued for filing as follow-ups (a
  shared comment mapper across the gh-exec and REST forge adapters, and the
  near-identical github/forgejo issue-read fragments). Both are design calls
  beyond this issue's scope.
- The 64KB `ISSUE_TEXT` cap is a new limit #3445 did not ask for; it exists
  because the transport is a single env var, and it is documented in
  `docs/reference.md`.
- Round 1 review blocked on three findings (unpaginated forgejo `Comments`,
  jira missing `CommentLister`, a dropped `ISSUE_TEXT` on fetch error); all
  three are fixed and folded into the commits they belong to. The run ended
  before a confirming second review round ran, so this branch's fixes have not
  been re-reviewed by an agent pass.

author: romulosutil
body:
## Resumo

Grupo B da feature **Pedidos MVP** (T04–T13): domínio do Pedido, serviço de aplicação e persistência PostgreSQL com a ficha cifrada. Base: `feat/pedidos-mvp` em `02b6d09` (Grupo A, #71).

Não usa nem referencia `crm.deals*`, `modules/deals-pipeline` ou `modules/qualification` (ADR 004). Nenhum arquivo de outro grupo foi alterado.

## Tasks

| Task | Commit | Arquivos | Gate | Testes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T04 módulo `modules/orders` | `b710653` | `modules/orders/package.json`, `src/index.js`, `package-lock.json` | `npm run check:boundaries && npm run typecheck` ✅ | — |
| T05 valor em reais | `5ff569a` | `domain/money.js`, `domain/errors.js`, `test/orders-money.test.js` | quick ✅ | 3 |
| T06 ficha: validação, totais, pré-ficha | `68f4d68` | `domain/ficha.js`, `test/orders-ficha.test.js` | quick ✅ (snapshot sintético = 32) | 9 |
| T07 agregado Pedido | `9f2d2c4` | `domain/order.js`, `test/orders-domain.test.js` | quick ✅ | 8 |
| T08 porta + repositório em memória | `f4e4c0d` | `ports/contracts.js`, `adapters/in-memory-order-repository.js`, `test/orders-repository-contract.test.js` | quick ✅ | 11 |
| T09 serviço: intenção, criação manual, projeção | `5a2e796` | `application/order-service.js`, `test/orders-service-create.test.js` | quick ✅ | 9 |
| T10 serviço: seção, confirmar, reabrir | `5a3b6db` | `application/order-service.js`, `test/orders-service-commands.test.js` | quick ✅ | 9 |
| T11 serviço: leituras | `9dc34e6` | `application/order-service.js`, `test/orders-service-read.test.js` | quick ✅ | 5 |
| T12 migration `0023_orders.expand.sql` | `2dbead1` | migration, `test/migrations.test.js`, `test/migrations-live.test.js` | `npm run test:database` 9/9 ✅ · `npm run test:database:live` 2/2 ✅ | 1 unit + 1 live |
| T13 `PostgresOrderRepository` | `05a5edb` | `adapters/postgres-order-repository.js`, `adapters/envelope.js`, `test/orders-postgres-live.test.js`, `package.json` (`test:orders:live`) | `npm run test:orders:live` 14/14 ✅ | 11 do contrato + 3 |

quick = `node --test <testes da task> && npm run lint && npm run typecheck`.

### Verificação final no branch

- `npm test`: 417 testes, 414 pass, 3 skipped, 0 fail
- `npm run test:orders:live`: 14/14
- `npm run test:identity:live`: 11/11 (inclui `migrations-live` com a migration nova)
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:boundaries`: ok

Os testes live rodaram num PostgreSQL 17 descartável em Docker local (`crm_silmer_test`, porta 5433 em 127.0.0.1), nunca no banco do Easypanel.

## SPEC_DEVIATION

- **T12:** `id`, `conversation_id`, `confirmed_by`, `reopened_by` e `created_by` são `text`, não `uuid` como em `design.md`. `crm.conversations.id` e `crm.users.id` são `text`, e a FK com `uuid` falharia. Registrado no cabeçalho da migration e no commit.

## Decisões de implementação (para revisão)

- **Chave do envelope:** o repositório do n8n recebe `N8N_INTEGRATION_ENVELOPE_KEY` via `readEnvelopeKey` em `apps/api/src/n8n-runtime.js`. `PostgresOrderRepository` recebe a opção `envelopeKey`, e a composição (T15) deve passar essa mesma chave. Nenhuma variável de ambiente nova.
- **Cifragem:** mesmo envelope AES-256-GCM de `encryptJson`/`decryptJson`, cópia local em `adapters/envelope.js` (como `inbox-channels`), com AAD `order-ficha:<id>`. Nome, telefone, endereço e toda a ficha ficam só em `ficha_envelope`; colunas abertas guardam apenas `total_pieces` e `missing_fields`. O teste live usa um canário e confirma que ele não aparece na linha nem no evento.
- **Eventos:** toda escrita grava `crm.domain_events` (`aggregate_type='order'`, `aggregate_version` = versão do pedido) na mesma transação. Payload só com `{orderId, conversationId}`, pronto para T19. Tipos: `order.created`, `order.section_saved`, `order.briefing_projected`, `order.confirmed`, `order.reopened`.
- **Erros de domínio:** o `OrderError` do OpenAPI lista 6 códigos. Usados: `INVALID_AMOUNT`, `INVALID_GRADE` (com `itemIndex`/`index`), `ORDER_NOT_CONFIRMABLE` (com `fields`), `VERSION_CONFLICT`, `ORDER_NOT_FOUND`. Adicionados: `ORDER_INVALID` (400, forma inválida da seção), `ORDER_STATUS_CONFLICT` (409, edição/confirmação/reabertura fora do status), `ORDER_PENDING_EXISTS` (409 interno; o serviço devolve o pendente existente), `CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND` (404) e `FORBIDDEN` (403).
- **Pré-ficha → ficha:** só vai para a ficha o que não exige adivinhar (cliente, nome do evento, técnica, tipo, modelo, malhas, grade parseável). Cores, data desejada, notas e quantidade ficam em `serviceData`.
- **Projeção do agente (PAG-01):** atualiza só nome, aplicação e tipo/modelo/malhas/grade do primeiro item; preserva cores, entrega confirmada, observações e demais itens do vendedor. Só com `automationState='assistant'` e só em pendente.
- **Confirmação (A01):** bloqueiam só valor, condição e ao menos um item com grade; campos vazios aparecem em `missingFields`. Data do pedido em `America/Sao_Paulo` (D00.6-05).
- **Portas injetadas no serviço:** `conversations.readOrderContext` (pré-ficha + nome do contato), `conversations.searchConversationIds` (busca por cliente/telefone pelo caminho do contato, sem dado pessoal aberto) e `authorizeOwnership` (dono ou `COMMERCIAL_ADMIN`, implementado no runtime de T15).
- **Lista:** `12`/`12-CRM` busca por número exato; texto também resolve conversas pela porta (OR). `counts` ignoram o filtro de status. Cursor opaco `(updated_at, id)`.
- **Suíte de contrato reutilizável:** `defineOrderRepositoryContract` é exportada de `test/orders-repository-contract.test.js`; roda em memória só quando o arquivo é entry point (`import.meta.main`) e é a mesma suíte usada em `test/orders-postgres-live.test.js`.

## Pendências

- **Nome do cliente em pedido confirmado:** a spec pede que o pendente reflita o nome atual do contato e o confirmado mantenha o nome da confirmação. Hoje o nome é gravado na criação e `saveStatus` não reescreve a ficha. Resolver no Grupo C (enriquecimento na leitura + snapshot na confirmação) ou num ajuste da porta.
- **Composição (T15):** montar `createOrderService` com `PostgresOrderRepository`, `N8N_INTEGRATION_ENVELOPE_KEY`, `FAB_CODE` e as portas de conversa/posse.
- **Nomes de atores:** `confirmedBy`/`reopenedBy` são IDs; o tipo `Order` da API espera `{id, name}` e `seller`, e o enriquecimento cabe à camada de API.

body:
Service C — переход на PostgreSQL, рефакторинг и автоматическая очистка данных

REST и gRPC переведены на работу через хранилище; сохранена выдача последних 10 записей.
Добавлена автоматическая очистка записей старше 10 часов: запуск при старте сервиса и повтор каждые 10 часов.

Итог: Service C теперь использует персистентное хранилище PostgreSQL, автоматически удаляет устаревшие данные, имеет более разделённую архитектуру и упрощённую конфигурацию.

author: pmjpraveen
body:
## Summary
- Rebuilt the hero around a huge display name with your photo in a small rotated polaroid-style frame overlapping it — adapted from a reference layout, keeping the structural idea (huge name, casual "Hi, I'm" greeting) while dropping the parts that were another designer's specific personal signature (letter-substitution photo placement, selection-highlight subtitle styling).
- Tightened spacing: more room below the hero, less gap between the "Selected Works" heading and the first case study.
- Added a fine-pointer-only custom cursor (dot + ring, ring scales over links/buttons). Position and hover-scale are deliberately split across two nested elements — the position element has no CSS transition so pointer tracking is always exactly 1:1, while only the inner scale transform animates. (A single element doing both was the actual bug fixed in this branch: transitioning `transform` eases the whole matrix, so position updates visibly lagged and snapped.)
- Native cursor is hidden only via a class the component adds after confirming it mounted — never unconditionally in static CSS — so a JS failure always falls back to the real cursor.

## Reviewer notes
- The hero's photo-in-name placement is a deliberate simplification vs. the reference it was inspired by (see commit message) — "Praveenkumar" doesn't have a convenient dotted letter to substitute the way the reference name did.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified in-browser at desktop and mobile widths: hero fits without overflow, no console errors

Adds [Alibaba Cloud Model Studio](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/get-api-key) as an OpenAI-chat provider. Stacked on #1694: the branch is based on `add-xkiro-provider`, so this PR shows one new commit on top of it and collapses to a provider-only diff once #1694 lands. ## Why Model Studio is Alibaba Cloud's pay-as-you-go model platform with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1`). Its live catalog serves 165 chat models — the qwen3.5–3.8 series, deepseek-v4, glm-5.2, kimi-k3, qwen3.8-max-0902 — first-party Qwen hosting that the existing `qwencloud` / `qwencloud_coding` providers (subscription-bound) don't cover, which makes it useful as a direct alternative to multi-vendor gateways. ## How - Register `alibaba_modelstudio` through the standard provider catalog: descriptor, Settings fields (`ALIBABA_MODELSTUDIO_API_KEY` / `ALIBABA_MODELSTUDIO_BASE_URL` / `ALIBABA_MODELSTUDIO_PROXY`), OpenAI-chat profile, admin manifest entries, `.env.example`, README table row, and a smoke default model (`alibaba_modelstudio/qwen3-max`). - The default base URL is the international (Singapore) endpoint; `ALIBABA_MODELSTUDIO_BASE_URL` also accepts the regional hosts (Beijing, US, Hong Kong) and the dedicated workspace form `https://{WorkspaceId}.{region}.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` — all serve the same catalog. - The reasoning profile follows DashScope's hybrid-reasoner semantics: Qwen models vary in their default (qwen3-max answers directly while qwen3.8-max-0902 reasons out of the box), so the `enable_thinking` boolean forwards the client's resolved intent through `extra_body` — verified to switch thinking in both directions on both model kinds — and `reasoning_content` deltas are replayed as thinking history (`ReasoningReplayMode.REASONING_CONTENT`). - Credential validation probes `GET /models`: unlike xKiro's public catalog, it is auth-gated (invalid key → 401 `invalid_api_key`). - Dedicated provider test file (`tests/providers/test_alibaba_modelstudio.py`) plus the contract/test-runtime synchronization every provider addition requires: catalog order, probe case, instantiation table, runtime settings mock. - Version bump (minor, `uv lock` in the same commit), per the provider-addition precedent. ## Validation Local `scripts/ci.ps1` (suppressions, ruff format/check, ty, pytest): 5,352 passed, 149 skipped, 0 failed. Live checks against the compatible-mode endpoint confirmed: identical 165-model catalogs on the international and workspace hosts, chat completions on qwen3-max and qwen3.8-max-0902, `enable_thinking` honored in both directions (thinking model → no reasoning; hybrid model → reasoning), reasoning deltas streamed on `reasoning_content`, and 401 `invalid_api_key` for a malformed key.

Confidence Score: 5/5

Safe to merge. What we checked: - We verified that the provider's chat requests use deterministic mocked responses and that default reasoning omits enable_thinking, with false and true values sent for disabled and enabled reasoning, while the follow-up request history preserves assistant reasoning content, tool calls, and matching tool results. - We confirmed that credential validation requests target the configured Model Studio /models endpoint with bearer authentication. - We ran the focused provider, credential-validation, runtime, and catalog test suites and observed 107 tests passed. - Before this PR, the Alibaba-specific catalog constant could not be imported in the before-change worktree, establishing that the provider did not exist prior to the change.

Summary

- Adds Alibaba Cloud Model Studio as an OpenAI-compatible chat provider, including configuration, runtime registration, credential validation, reasoning controls, model discovery, documentation, smoke defaults, and focused tests. - The provider sends the intended DashScope thinking setting for enabled and disabled reasoning, preserves the default model behavior when reasoning is unspecified, and retains reasoning and tool-call history in follow-up requests. body:
`matrixark_mcp_local_adapter._model_registry_identity` puts the record's `provider` string straight
into the tuple it de-duplicates context_model_registry rows by. The record took that string raw
from the environment, so one encoder spelled three ways is three identities:

  on main                       on this branch
    openai     -> 'openai'        openai     -> 'openai'
    OpenAI     -> 'OpenAI'        OpenAI     -> 'openai'
    ' OPENAI ' -> 'OPENAI'        ' OPENAI ' -> 'openai'
    3 identities                  1 identity

A deployment that retyped its provider with different capitalisation wrote a duplicate registry row
each time. Not data loss -- the identity is a dedup key, not the encoder-conflict check -- and
worth saying plainly, because the same field name in the same record would be a much worse bug if
it were the conflict check.

WHY THIS ONE SITE AND NOT THE OTHER FOUR THAT READ IT UNNORMALISED

`embedding_provider_name` already draws the line, in its own docstring: sites that REPORT the raw
configured string read the variable directly and should, because they answer "what is set", not
"what will run". matrixark_gateway_metrics and the portal display are on that side and are left
alone. An identity is not a reporting field, so this one is not.

Checked before assuming: the other unnormalised readers pass the value into `_encoder_applies`,
`_hosted_encoders_for` and `embedding_provider_effect`, and all three normalise internally --
`OpenAI`, ` openai` and `OPENAI` already behave identically through every one of them. This was
the only site where the raw spelling survived into something that compares strings.

  the raw spelling comes back        FAILS
  the field is filled for every kind FAILS

A third mutation -- lowercasing here instead of calling `embedding_provider_name` -- does NOT fail,
and saying so is the point: the two rules compute the same answer today, so nothing can separate
them until one learns a spelling the other has not. That is the whole reason the guard asks the
encoder rather than restating its rule, and it is also why no test can prove it yet.

author: whilp
body:
## Why

Two fixes gitboard depends on, both landed upstream today.

**`cosmo.Fetch` resolves the proxy by scheme.** It read `http_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY` for every request regardless of scheme and never consulted `HTTPS_PROXY` or `NO_PROXY`. In an environment publishing only `HTTPS_PROXY` — a Claude Code remote session among them — an `https://` request went **direct** rather than through the proxy, and failed much later as a credential error. `_work.api`'s GitHub client returned `HTTP 401: Bad credentials` on every call.

With this pin, and no proxy variable set by hand:

```
$ env -u HTTP_PROXY -u http_proxy GITBOARD_PROVIDER_TOKEN_ENV=GH_TOKEN \
    bin/cosmic --make run <probe>
activate: true
GET /repos/cosmic-lua/work -> status 200
```

**`cast-justify` finds a multi-line cast's justification beside its `as`.** Without it this bump does not land. The release before it turns **24 sites red** across `_work/apiauth_test.tl` (3), `_work/gh_test.tl` (4), `_work/ghwrite_test.tl` (16) and `_work/gitverdict_transport_test.tl` (1) — files unchanged here and green on the previous pin — because the rule moved to an AST anchor reporting a cast's *first* line while the justification sits on the line carrying the `as`.

That was measured on this bump, not predicted: the first attempt failed `ci: FAIL (lint)` with exactly those 24 and was held back until the upstream fix landed rather than relocating 24 correct comments to work around it.

## Verification

- `bin/cosmic --make ci` with `o/bootstrap` removed first, so the new release was genuinely fetched and its sha verified: **`ci: PASS (4 stages)`**, lint PASS over 259 files, coverage PASS over 123.
- The pin's sha256 was computed from the downloaded binary and matches both the release's published `SHA256SUMS` and GitHub's asset digest.

## Known, and not fixed here

The `cast-justify` fix searches a cast's whole span, so a `-- cast:` written for a nested cast — or a stale one — justifies the outer cast. Zero live instances across cosmic's 158 cast sites or the four files above, and it is tracked upstream as its own item; the narrowing will ride a later pin.

author: savant0x
body:
## Root cause (reproduced in isolation)
`emitTyped` extracted `io.to(room).emit` into a variable and invoked it **detached**. A detached call loses `this`, and socket.io's `BroadcastOperator.emit` reads `this.adapter` → `undefined.adapter` TypeError. Wrapped in try/catch + console.error, every broadcast failed **silently** — production log showed 6 failures, 0 successes. Player-online pings, tile updates, clan and global events: the entire WebSocket fanout was a no-op.

## Fix
`emitTyped` invokes emit as a member call (`io.to(room).emit(...)`), preserving `this`. The operator is `any`-widened on that single audited line (socket.io's overload can't resolve generic keys); payload contracts stay enforced by the helper's signature and call sites remain fully typed.

## Tests
Real socket.io server + client (node env pragma — jsdom breaks socket.io-client):
- `broadcastToAll` delivers to a connected client (pre-fix: guaranteed timeout)
- `broadcastToLocation` delivers to room members — the exact player-online path
- race-free fixture (room joins registered before `listen()`)

## Live verification
Server restarted on the new build; browser reconnect produced:
`[Game Handler] fame came online at (131,5)` / `[Broadcast] Event 'game:player_online' sent to location (131,5)` — failures since restart: **0**.

- [x] tsc 0 · eslint 0 · build clean

author: egcgap04
body:
## Description

Adds a fade to and from black around combat, so the overlay no longer cuts in and out, and closes two separate ways a combat could start when it should not have.

The fade is a full-screen black `ColorRect` inside `combat.tscn`, above the rest of the UI and with `mouse_filter = IGNORE` so it never swallows clicks on the Attack button. It starts opaque and fades to 0 in `Combat._Ready()`; the first turn begins only once that finishes. On the way out it fades back to 1 *after* the result has been on screen for `ResultDelay`, so the transition never hides the result text. A new `TurnState.Transition` keeps both the button and the `confirm` input from attacking mid-fade.

The two trigger gaps:

- **Re-trigger after losing.** `Main` now ignores combat requests for `CombatCooldown` (1s) after a fight ends. The cooldown is started before unpausing on purpose, because `SceneTreeTimer` ignores the pause state and the guard has to be active on the first physics frame the world map runs again.
- **Phantom contact at startup.** The player is now spawned in `Main._EnterTree()` instead of `_Ready()`. A `CharacterBody2D` registers its transform with the physics server when it enters the tree, and a parent's `_EnterTree` runs before its children enter, so spawning there means the server never sees the position authored in `main.tscn`. Spawning afterwards left enemy areas paired against that stale transform, reporting a `body_entered` on physics frame 2 that was retracted by a `body_exited` on frame 3 — too late, the combat had already started. `WorldMap.PlayerSpawnPosition` becomes a computed property so it can be read that early.

Closes #40

## Change type

<!-- Check the ones that apply -->

- [x] `feat` - New functionality
- [x] `fix` - Bug fix
- [ ] `docs` - Documentation
- [ ] `refactor` - Code reorganization without behavior change
- [ ] `chore` - Maintenance/configuration
- [ ] `test` - Tests

## Checklist before merging

- [x] The project compiles without errors in the Godot editor
- [x] I tested the change manually in the editor/game
- [x] I updated the README or other documentation if applicable
- [x] I updated CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] with a summary of this change
- [x] I did not leave debug code/temporary comments in

## Additional notes

**The manual check is deliberately left unticked:** everything below was verified headless, with no display available, so nothing *visual* has been confirmed. Worth checking in the editor before merging: that the black rect really covers the whole screen (it is placed at fixed 640x360 offsets, not anchored), and whether `FadeDuration` (0.25s) feels right. Both `FadeDuration` and `CombatCooldown` are `[Export]`s, so they can be tuned from the Inspector without recompiling.

Verified headless (`dotnet build --configuration Debug`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, plus `godot --headless`):

- **Fade in:** the overlay goes from alpha 1 to 0 over ~25 frames with the Attack button disabled and attack input ignored throughout, and the first turn starts only afterwards.
- **Fade out:** fires after `ResultDelay`, and `CombatFinished` is emitted only once it completes.
- **Win:** 3 rounds against the weak enemy, enemy freed, player position preserved.
- **Loss:** 3 rounds against the strong enemy, player returned to `PlayerSpawn`.
- **Cooldown:** losing to the strong enemy and respawning on top of the weak one logs the incoming trigger as ignored with the cooldown active. A control run with `CombatCooldown = 0` starts the second combat immediately, confirming the cooldown is what prevents it rather than some side effect.
- **Phantom contact:** with the `Player` node in `main.tscn` placed on an enemy and `PlayerSpawn` elsewhere, no combat starts anymore; before the fix a full fight against that enemy began on frame 2.
- `combat.tscn` still runs standalone (the fade completes without `Main` or a paused tree).

The three alternatives to the `_EnterTree` fix were ruled out by measurement, not assumption: an explicit `PhysicsServer2D.BodySetState`, deferring the teleport with `CallDeferred`, toggling the enemies' `monitoring` off and on deferred, and awaiting one `SceneTree.PhysicsFrame` before confirming the overlap all still reported the stale contact. `Area2D.OverlapsBody()` is unusable as a guard for the same reason — it reads the same stale monitoring state and returns `true`. Details and logs in the [Issue comment](https://github.com/EGCGAP04/godot-rpg-project/issues/40#issuecomment-5649825226).

All temporary scaffolding (auto-attack driver, position logging, moved markers) was reverted; `main.tscn` and `world_map.tscn` are untouched by this PR.

body:
# Plugin workflow reconciliation

## What changed and why

Core needed an explicit, testable contract for referencing agent-swarm
workflow state and normal memory-plugin contributions without importing
either plugin, plus a specification of what restart reconciliation may and
may not claim. Core already records tool facts (ToolCallProposed,
DispatchResolved, ToolCallCompleted) for every MCP dispatch; this change
derives plugin workflow references purely from those facts, reconciles
them after a restart through ordinary dispatch, and states plainly which
plugin steps cannot resume.

New module `src/harness/plugin_reconciliation.py`:

- `PluginWorkflowRef` and `ReconciliationReport` (frozen dataclasses).
- `project_plugin_workflows(envelopes)`: pure, total fold of completed
  `mcp__SERVER__workflow__workflow_*` calls into refs. Never raises; an
  unexpected result shape still yields a ref with `last_phase=None`.
- `count_memory_contributions` / `count_accepted_records`: fold completed
  `mcp__memory__*` calls (context reads and accepted writes) from the same
  log.
- `reconcile_from_log(envelopes)`: log-only report. Every ref is reported
  `unknown` -- core never invents a status without a live check.
- `reconcile(kernel)`: the live version. Re-dispatches
  `workflow__workflow_get_state` through `kernel.loop.dispatcher` for every
  ref -- ordinary dispatch, ordinary permissions, ordinary log. Classifies
  `active`, `finished`, or `unavailable`; unavailable refs are listed in
  `non_resumable`.
- `main`: read-only `harness plugins reconcile SESSION_ID --base-dir DIR`,
  wired into `harness` at `src/harness/cli.py` right after the `budget`
  ladder entry. Never starts or contacts an MCP server.
- `harness status` (`src/harness/status_cli.py`) now joins one summary
  line: `plugins: N workflow refs (M unavailable), K memory contributions,
  J accepted records`.

New test fixture `tests/fixtures/agent_swarm_stub.py`: an in-memory-only
stdio MCP server exposing `workflow__workflow_start`,
`workflow__workflow_get_state`, `workflow__workflow_advance_phase`, and
`workflow__workflow_stop`. It exists only under `tests/fixtures` and is
never installed as a real plugin; state does not survive a process
restart by design, which is what proves non-resumability in the tests.

`docs/plugin-reconciliation.md` documents the contract, the explicit law
(an in-memory plugin workflow lost across a plugin restart is not
resumable by core), and the four independence properties. One paragraph
was added to `docs/architecture.md` under Plugins pointing at it.

## Roadmap items advanced

Task 3 (plugin workflow reconciliation) from the harness remaining-roadmap
manifest: an explicit, testable contract for referencing agent-swarm and
memory plugin state without importing either, proven against a reference
memory plugin and a stub agent-swarm server with the M5 gate independence
properties.

## Validation

Ruff:

```
All checks passed!
```

Focused suite (tests/test_plugin_reconciliation.py, 11 tests, stub and
reference memory server started and stopped cleanly, no leaked process
after the run):

```
11 passed in 1.21s
```

Complete suite, Python 3.13:

```
2369 passed, 7 skipped, 6 warnings in 681.00s (0:11:21)
```

Complete suite, Python 3.12 (first attempt hit one unrelated flake in
tests/test_coordination_admission.py, a timing-sensitive test racing a
0.1s deadline against a 3s wait under host load from concurrent sibling
worktrees on this shared machine; a second attempt hit a different
unrelated flake in tests/test_tui.py::test_tui_pipes_mcp_child_stderr_to_file,
which carries its own comment noting its 5s timeout depends on host load.
Neither test, nor any file either touches, appears in this diff; the first
failure was confirmed to pass in isolation. A third attempt was clean):

```
2369 passed, 7 skipped, 6 warnings in 615.52s (0:10:15)
```

Build:

```
Successfully built dist/harness-0.0.1.tar.gz
Successfully built dist/harness-0.0.1-py3-none-any.whl
```

Smoke (scripts/smoke_wheel.sh dist/harness-0.0.1-py3-none-any.whl):
every shipped module imports cleanly from the installed wheel, including
ok harness.plugin_reconciliation, ending with:

```
== wheel smoke OK
```

git diff --check: clean.

## Known limits and deliberate omissions

- reconcile(kernel) classifies a ref as unavailable whenever the
  dispatch comes back an error, whether the cause was the server being
  disabled, never connected, or a genuine live failure -- one code path,
  since the dispatcher already turns every one of those into a graceful
  is_error tool outcome rather than raising. The distinction between
  disabled and failed is therefore not separately recorded.
- reconcile_from_log (and the harness plugins reconcile / harness
  status join) never classifies a ref as unavailable or finished from
  historical log evidence alone; every ref is unknown until a live check
  runs. This is deliberate (core never invents a plugin status), not an
  oversight.
- The environment this task ran in exports PYTHONPATH pointing at the
  agent-swarm plugin install directory for its own tool routing; that
  directory ships its own scripts package, which shadows this
  repository top-level scripts/ namespace package under Python
  namespace-package resolution rules and breaks collection of 9 unrelated
  scripts.*-importing test files. All validation commands above were run
  with PYTHONPATH cleared to avoid that collision; nothing in this diff
  touches scripts/ or depends on that variable.

## Commits

- 9827f33 feat(plugins): reconcile agent-swarm workflow refs and memory
  contributions from the log

## Orchestrator note (agent-swarm pipeline, 2026-09-12)

Dispatched as task `3-plugin-workflow-reconciliation` of the remaining-roadmap
queue (`docs/handoffs/2026-09-12-agent-swarm/` on `docs/remaining-roadmap-workflow`).
Advances the M5 plugin-interoperability gate with the reference memory plugin
and a stub agent-swarm server; the live installed agent-swarm server is a
separate qualification step. The repository's automated reviewer is paused
until 2026-09-24; an agent-swarm reviewer pass is dispatched and its findings
recorded in the workflow status file. Hosted CI on this PR head is the
clean-environment suite result for both interpreters.

body:
## Summary
Add the durable broker and private artifact transport for the isolated Paddle worker. Based on #631, which carries the separately validated maintenance fixes above #629.

## What does this change
- Revisioned worker policies, durable train/evaluate jobs, leases, and per-attempt compute reservations. Policies start disabled and require an approved worker code hash.
- Private, bounded, hash-verified model upload/sealing/download with explicit retention cleanup and storage reservations for both staging and sealed copies.
- A pull-worker client that downloads only leased assets, isolates compute credentials, obeys deadlines and disk limits, and submits idempotent results.
- Candidate model registration and server-side grading, with no production activation path.

## Why are you changing it
Training and evaluation need durable, attributable results without allowing stale workers, revoked data, changed policies, or lost maintainer authority to authorize new work. Uncertain retries must remain charged to the budget.

## How did you accomplish this
- Reuse the frozen corpus and its transaction lock for live eligibility checks. Bind callbacks to the lease, worker build, dataset, source, target, pipeline, and exact leased frame/timestamp evidence.
- Reject invented selection times and sampler-feature times, including a zero-second timestamp for a still image. The two new regressions failed before this validation was added.
- Keep archive contents allowlisted, reject unsafe paths, verify model and archive hashes, and release storage reservations only after confirmed absence of both objects.
- Add migration `0163_ocr_worker_control` and its journal entry together.
- Globally exclude `.data` and `workers/ocr` from web traces; add control-plane size and forbidden-runtime checks.
- No new user-facing copy and no score-submit, commander-mutation, or notification integration.

#### Test plan
All seven local gates ran in order against the guarded dedicated local test database:
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npm run lint` (existing warnings)
- [x] `npm test`: 5,043 passed, 39 skipped
- [x] `npm run i18n:validate` (existing warnings)
- [x] `npm run db:validate-journal`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm run test:e2e`: 411 passed, 2 skipped
- [x] Focused control-plane database suite: 9 passed
- [x] Real broker test: train, verify weight updates, seal/transfer/reload the model, evaluate held-out pixels, reject revoked training data, and clean up expired artifacts
- [x] Python suite with `OCR_WORKER_MODEL_TEST=1`: 16 passed, including real training/export/reload and transport isolation
- [x] Husky passed without bypassing hooks

## Qualification blockers
- `npm run vercel:analyze-function-trace` still exits nonzero on this macOS checkout because Linux libvips shared objects are unavailable. Linux qualification remains required; no native requirement was disabled. All measured size budgets and forbidden-path checks pass: control handlers are 5.0–5.3 MB against 120 MB budgets, and the dispatch queue is 3.3 MB. No `.data` or Python-worker runtime is bundled.
- Synthetic execution fixtures do not establish real-footage accuracy or improvement. Approved recordings, matching scope, measured thresholds, and production resource qualification remain pending.
- Automatic collection/learning, guarded live shadow/canary/promotion/rollback, and the operator UI are subsequent slices. This PR does not claim completion of the full closed loop. Production OCR selection remains unchanged.

author: 0pcom
body:
`EnsureAndObtainSession` re-checks the session map and then dials without holding `sesMx` — it must not hold it, since the dial path can re-enter session establishment through a self-hosted discovery and would self-deadlock. So callers arriving together for a server with no session all miss the check and all dial. A dmsg server keeps one session per client PK, so each new session evicts the previous one at the server, and the client's own newest-session-wins registration closes it again locally: every racing caller but the last is left holding a session that was just closed from the far end.

The pinned-rendezvous hostname in `pkg/dmsgweb` — `<server-pk>.<dest-pk>.dmsg` — is how a user reaches that. One page is several requests, each is its own SOCKS5 CONNECT, and each dials the named server. Six parallel fetches dialled six sessions, failed with `session shutdown`, and cost the proxy a live session (and every stream on it) that the Serve loop then re-dialled.

This coalesces session establishment per server PK: one dial in flight, everyone else takes its result. The flight covers only the dial, not the discovery lookup before it, so the re-entrancy `sesMx` is released for cannot land inside it; a bounded wait degrades to the old duplicate dial rather than wedging if that reasoning is ever wrong. Two regression tests, both verified failing before the change: `TestEnsureAndObtainSession_CoalescesConcurrentDials` (6 concurrent callers got 6 distinct sessions) and `TestSOCKS5PinnedRendezvous_ParallelFetchesKeepOneSession` (parallel pinned fetches through the real SOCKS5 path).

author: anpatton
body:
Two entry points for data that no named family fits, in the same shape as `what_is_this`.

```python
from probably.dx import fit_johnsonsu, fit_shash

distribution, diagnostics = fit_johnsonsu(returns)
diagnostics[0]["verdict"]                          # 'yes' — checked, not just fitted
distribution, _ = fit_shash(returns, quick=True)   # fit only, ~500x faster
```

Both return the existing `Identification(distribution, diagnostics)`, so they unpack the
same way and hand back a plain frozen scipy distribution.

## Johnson SU and sinh-arcsinh

`scipy` ships `johnsonsu`; sinh-arcsinh it does not, so `_shash.py` defines it as an
`rv_continuous` subclass (~40 lines). Because that maths is ours rather than scipy's, it
is proved rather than assumed — tests pin that the density integrates to 1 across four
parameter settings, that `ppf` inverts `cdf`, that `logpdf` agrees with `log(pdf)`, that
`fit` recovers known parameters, and that at `eps=0, delta=1` it is *exactly* the normal.
It is written in log space because the `exp(-sinh(.)**2 / 2)` term underflows well before
the tail stops mattering. A test also pins that the frozen distribution pickles, since a
custom `rv_continuous` is exactly the thing that quietly fails to, which would rule it out
of multiprocessing and any saved-model workflow.

## `quick`

Fitting is cheap; checking the fit is not. Because the parameters were estimated from the
same data being tested, there is no valid table of critical values, so scipy simulates the
null — 199 synthetic datasets drawn from the fitted distribution, each one refitted. That
is ~400 extra fits per call, and it dominates the runtime regardless of sample size.

| | fit | fit + check |
|---|---|---|
| `fit_johnsonsu` | 17 ms | 8.9 s |
| `fit_shash` | 56 ms | 22.6 s |

`quick=True` skips only the grading, never the fit — a test pins that both paths produce an
identical distribution. The verdict comes back `None` with a reason saying why. It is for
fitting inside a resampling loop; the default stays `quick=False` because a flexible
four-parameter family returns *something* for almost any input, and without the check there
is no signal that it is wrong.

Both families correctly reject bimodal data and warn — four flexible parameters still cannot
make one mode into two. Without that, a returned distribution reads as an endorsement.

## Test suite: 180s → 89s

The five heaviest Monte Carlo tests now carry a `slow` marker, skipped by default.

- **Skipped, not deselected**, so they still show in the count with a reason rather than
  looking like tests that do not exist.
- **CI runs `pytest --cov --runslow`**, so this defers the cost rather than deleting the
  coverage.
- One checked-path test stays on by default: `test_a_sample_from_the_family_is_not_rejected`
  is parametrized so Johnson SU (6.5s) always runs and SHASH (24.5s) is marked slow, so the
  verdict path is never wholly untested locally.

Verified both ways — 494 pass under `--runslow`, 489 pass / 15 skip without.

## Notes

- **Not added to `what_is_this`.** That function answers "which *named* family is this?", and
  a catch-all would change the question. Measured first: Johnson SU never displaces the true
  family in the AIC race (it lands +2 to +30 behind at n=100/300/1000), so adding it later
  would not corrupt the rankings if wanted.
- **One refactor came along.** `what_is_this._check` and the new fitters both needed "run a
  family's battery, reduce to a verdict", so that is now a single `check_fit` in
  `_families.py` that both use. `Identification` moved there too, and is still importable
  from its old location.
- The remaining 89s is mostly pre-existing (`test_dx_what_is_this` is ~50s of it), left alone
  as outside this change.

ruff, black, and mypy `--strict` all clean.

fleet-ops#4467 (merged as #4469, 2026-09-08) made pick_seat spend expiring prepaid subscriptions (ClinePass, SuperGrok) while they are behind pace, instead of letting the weekly allowance lapse. Its termination required a 3-day population proof posted after merge; #4478 tracks that proof. This PR is the proof, as one evidence-only report: `docs/reports/seat-utilization-population-proof-2026-09-12.md`. No code, no config, no mechanism. Note: the mechanism under proof was retired one day after the window closed by #5993 (LiteLLM groups own routing); the report judges it during its deployed life, which is what the termination asked.

Scope:
- One new file, `docs/reports/seat-utilization-population-proof-2026-09-12.md` (+107): each #4478 criterion with measured numbers and the exact commands that produced them; the criterion-3 shipped-meter reading root-caused; the #5993 supersession recorded. The population proof itself is posted as the #4478 issue comment.

Proof window: 2026-09-08T05:59:48Z (#4469 merged) -> 2026-09-11T05:59:48Z (+3 days).
- Criterion 1 (measure.sh prints every expiring seat with meter and pace): PASS — see run-proof below; also passed at report time 2026-09-12 (`cline: 10% pace 80%` / `xai-oauth: 423% pace 80%`).
- Criterion 2 (each of cline, xai-oauth >= 10 sessions in-window): PASS — pick-audit `running on` attempts, all units, window-bracketed: cline 22, xai-oauth 42 (prior retained week: 22); delivered-success and counter cross-checks cited in the report.

Metering moved to LiteLLM /spend by #5993, which also retires this counter.
- Criterion 4 (devin+ollama share, baseline 82%, toward/below 60%): PASS — 45.4% in-window (1047/2306); like-for-like retained-audit immediately before merge: 70.9%.

## Problema
En producción `/api/health`, `/api/relay` y `/api/faucet` devolvían 500:
`Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '/var/task/web/server/config' imported from /var/task/web/api/health.js`.
Vercel transpila cada `api/*.ts` sin empaquetar y mantiene los imports relativos sin extensión, que Node ESM (`"type": "module"`) no resuelve.

- `*.tsbuildinfo` en `.gitignore`.

author: jeanibarz
body:
## Summary

OSS contribution capture could store repository names and issue or pull-request numbers that cannot identify GitHub work. Captures of newly opened pull requests and scouted issues now reject invalid identities before changing contribution history, saving it, or notifying dashboards. This prevents unusable history rows while preserving valid callers and the existing skip for repositories in the user's own namespace.

Closes #3190.

## Changes

- Require exactly one owner/repository pair and reuse the existing segment validator for character and length limits. Validation ignores case, while stored identities retain their original representation.
- Require positive safe-integer issue and pull-request numbers, retaining compatible numeric strings. A missing or null optional issue number still means no issue linkage; an explicitly invalid value returns HTTP 400.
- Preserve dot-prefixed repository names such as `.github`, including the maximum-length boundary, while rejecting exact `.` and `..` segments. Check the original `.git` suffix before adapting dot-prefixed names for validation.
- Keep validation local to the capture route. Shared validators and stored records are unchanged; whitespace in repository segments is rejected rather than trimmed into a different identity.

## Test plan

Published head: `a3f9a5d7ae2a1bdf220ce071fa4699bbe66fd035`.

- Reproduced on the old route: 80 new regression cases received HTTP 200 instead of HTTP 400.
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/server/routes/oss-attempts-routes.test.ts`: 166 tests passed, covering both event kinds, malformed and boundary-length repository pairs, invalid and boundary integers, persisted casing, optional linkage, and side-effect prevention.
- `pnpm build`: passed before the final route-only correction. Final server and E2E typechecks passed in the enforced pre-push hook.
- `pnpm verify`: **FAILED** in the supplemental local-only smoke filesystem assertion. The identical failure reproduces on unchanged base `cb0f9982` with `pnpm build:dtach && pnpm test:smoke`: 81 tests pass, then `scripts/local-only-smoke.ts:117` rejects `last-good-health.json`, `server.lock.sqlite`, `tasks.json.pre-sqlite-<timestamp>`, `tasks.sqlite`, and `timer-health.state.json`.
- Supervisor-authorized delivery with a documented baseline exception: retain this failed result, leave shared smoke code unchanged, and deliver only after typechecks, the full suite, touched-surface checks, the normal enforced pre-push hook, and independent review of the final commit pass. No hook is bypassed.
- `pnpm test:hooks`: **FAILED** (31 suites passed, one failed). The unchanged `verify-script.test.sh` detects that `scripts/verify.sh` omits the pre-push lane `check:faa-gate`; reproduced on base `cb0f9982`. The normal enforced pre-push hook still runs that lane.

author: mammalwithashell
body:
## Summary

A clause-by-clause DCGO oracle exam of the three Medusamon printings, plus the one real engine bug and three harness gaps it surfaced.

```
Medusamon core — 15 clauses:  10 confirmed · 0 diverged · 5 unmeasured
  Medusamon (BT21-029)  5/5
  Medusamon (BT24-017)  4/5
  Medusamon (EX11-012)  1/5
```

Still unmeasured: `BT24-017#effect#1` (<Progress>), and `EX11-012#effect#0/#1/#3/#4` (<Rush>, <Progress>, Token `[On Deletion]`, leave-battle-area replacement). The wider 66-card archetype remains mostly unmeasured.

## Engine: tokens count as Digimon for rules

`Permanent::is_digimon_for_rules` matched only `Digimon | Dual`, but every token's `CardData` is `CardKind::Token` (`TokenDef` has no kind field; `to_card_data` hardcodes it). Every rule phrased "your opponent's Digimon" therefore skipped tokens.

Measured on Medusamon (BT24-017)'s `<Raid>`, holding all other filters equal:

| opponent | `is_digimon_for_rules` | Raid window |
|---|---|---|
| ordinary Digimon | true | opens |
| Petrification Token (unsuspended, Standard, 3000 DP) | **false** | never offered |

`general_rule.pdf` §16-22-1 targets the opponent's unsuspended **Digimon**, the token prints as `(Digimon/white/3000 DP/…)`, and DCGO's `Raid.cs` applies no token filter. The engine already treated tokens as Digimon elsewhere (`play_token`'s `CannotPlayDigimonByEffect` routing; Medusamon (BT21-029)'s "when any of your opponent's Digimon are deleted" fires on a token deletion), so this closes an inconsistency. `is_digimon` (printed kind) is deliberately unchanged.

**39 call sites** use the predicate, so it was baselined first. Before vs after, `--no-fail-fast`:

| suite | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| archetypes | 204 / 8 failed | 204 / 8 failed — the same 8 |
| cards_behavioral | 7817 / 0 | 7817 / 0 |
| replacements | 125 / 0 | 125 / 0 |

⚠️ The 8 archetype failures are **pre-existing on main** (`dna_omnimon` ×3, `machine_bt25` ×1, `omnimon_ace` ×3, `puppet_sister` ×1) and unrelated to this PR. `archetypes` is in CI, so expect it red for reasons outside this change.

## dcgo-harness

- **`select: { …, sim_only: true }`** — mirror of `dcgo_only`: answers a prompt only our engine parks, emits zero wire rows. Needed where DCGO builds a "you may" effect non-optional (`SetUpActivateClass(…, isOptional: false, …)` + `canNoSelect`) and asks one cancellable pick where we ask gate + pick (Medusamon BT24-017, EX11-012).
- **`dcgo_only` trace alignment.** A `dcgo_only` step has no `StepSpec`, but `lower_and_run` still called `session.step()` for it, pulling the next step forward and shifting every later projection one ahead. It now repeats the prior projection, and the new `pair_by_wire_rows_with_ownership` consumes DCGO rows for such a step without pairing, counting it unpairable on **both** sides (otherwise a clean run reads `TRUNCATED` and records `diverged`). The original `pair_by_wire_rows` is kept so its tests still pin the old behaviour.
- **Interleaved prompt orders.** Two invariants relaxed, worth a careful look: the pending-selection check now **skips** `dcgo_only` rows when finding the step that answers our parked prompt, and the `dcgo_only` branch no longer errors on a live prompt of ours. Needed when the engines order a pair differently — Medusamon (BT24-017)'s attack parks our Raid pick while DCGO first asks a `MultipleSkills` row. Mislabelling a shared decision as `dcgo_only` is still caught, because the next non-`dcgo_only` row must answer our prompt.

`cargo test -p dcgo-harness`: 333 + 24 + 3 passed.

## QA

- 10 oracle-confirmed scenarios under `qa/dcgo-exams/{BT21,BT24,EX11}/`, each with a header documenting the line, the witness for its clause, and any prompt-shape accommodation.
- `medusamon_pool.json`: `medusamon-liberator` (a quiet Red LIBERATOR chain whose inherited effects are DP-only, so attacks fire no stray triggers) and `medusamon-progress` (identical but carrying Raging Serpentine (BT21-093) as a security bomb for `<Progress>`).
- `qa/exam-clause-text.json` extended additively by 15 clauses; existing entries unchanged and no verdict invalidated.

## Not in this PR — needs the DCGO fork

Two DCGO-side fixes were required for these runs and live in the **base-repo DCGO submodule**, uncommitted there (it carries ~8k unrelated dirty assets, so they need an explicit single-path commit to the fork):

- `Harness/CardIdentity.cs` (new) + routing in `StateDumper`, `SelectPermanentEffect`, `SelectCardEffect` ×2, `SelectHandEffect` ×2, `SelectAttackEffect`, `ActionEncoder`: tokens have an empty `CardID`, so the state sidecar and every selection-candidate list described all tokens as `""`. Any scenario ending with a token diverged on representation alone, and any `select:` naming a token was unmatchable. Now derives `TOKEN_<NAME>` from `CardName_ENG`, matching our engine.

Re-running the Medusamon token scenarios against the oracle requires a player built with that change.

## Findings recorded but not acted on

- **Once-per-turn on Medusamon (BT21-029) clause (d)** — printed as one `[Once Per Turn]` over two "or"-joined conditions, which reads as one Token per turn; **both engines give two** (DCGO caps per `ActivateClass` via `timesPerTurn`, not via `SetHashString`). Confirmed as parity, left open as a possible shared deviation pending a ruling.
- **`G-DECLARATIVE-KEYWORD` looks stale** for these cards: `<Progress>`, `<Raid>`, `<Piercing>`, `<Rush>` install at runtime, and `<Security A. +1>` is oracle-confirmed. The `#[ignore]`d BT21-029 keyword test and the tracker entry should likely be retired in a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p dcgo-harness` — 333 + 24 + 3 passed
- [x] Engine suites before/after the predicate change — identical (table above)
- [x] All 10 Medusamon scenarios pass `exam --sim-only`
- [x] All 10 confirmed CLEAN against a local DCGO oracle build
- [ ] CI: expect `archetypes` red on the 8 pre-existing failures

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Align token rules, exam trace handling, and MCP binary discovery while adding oracle coverage for Medusamon’s implemented clauses.

New Features:
- Add Medusamon DCGO oracle exam scenarios and verdict tracking covering 10 confirmed clauses across three printings.
- Allow exam scenarios to mark selections as simulation-only when the local engine prompts for a decision the oracle does not.
- Support trace alignment and ownership-aware pairing when DCGO-only prompts are interleaved with local-engine prompts.

Bug Fixes:
- Treat token permanents as Digimon for rules-based targeting and effects while preserving their printed Token card kind.
- Prevent DCGO-only steps from advancing local projections and producing false divergences during exam comparisons.
- Resolve MCP binaries from per-worktree Cargo target directories when launched outside an interactive shell.

Enhancements:
- Relax prompt-order validation to accommodate legitimate differences between engine and oracle prompt sequencing while retaining safeguards against mislabeled shared decisions.

Tests:
- Add launcher tests covering explicit, derived, fallback, and release/debug binary resolution.
- Add Medusamon QA scenarios, clause metadata, card pools, and oracle verdict reports.

author: blairham
body:
Closes #2502

#2477 landed the marking and fixed the route it was measured on — an rc file
whose last act is `printf 'LEFTOVER'`. It did not fix the route it was filed
about. Measured through a pseudo-terminal and replayed onto an 80-column grid,
with a `precmd` standing in for the progress line powerlevel10k prints while it
loads:

| | screen |
|---|---|
| real zsh | `%` / `P>` |
| main (`dea6cfab`) | `[plugin] fetching ..%` / `P>` |
| this branch | `%` / `P>` |

and with a command that leaves a partial line and a hook that prints after it:

| | screen |
|---|---|
| real zsh | `CMD%` / `P>` |
| main | `CMDHOOK%` / `P>` |
| this branch | `CMD%` / `P>` |

## The shape

The whole sequence was written in one block immediately before the prompt. It is
two blocks, and the prompt hooks run between them:

```
CMD  mark <79 spaces> \r <space> \r  HOOK  \r  <erase>  P>
```

`PROMPT_SP`'s mark is the last thing done about the **previous command's**
output, before the hooks; only `PROMPT_CR`'s return and the erase come after
them. With no hook the two are adjacent and read as one, which is how they were
first written down — an rc file cannot tell them apart, and that was the only
route #2477 was measured on. A shell that marks after the hooks marks the
hook's half-written line and leaves the command's output with the prompt against
it: the reported bug with an extra step.

Real zsh erases a hook's partial line rather than marking it, which falls out of
the same two-block shape and needs no rule of its own.

## Four smaller corrections, each measured

- **Padding is `cols` less the mark's display width, not `cols-1`.** Given a
  longer mark real zsh pads 77 and paints out 3 for `abc` against 79 and 1 for
  `%`; the one-column default made `cols-1` look like a rule. Width on the
  screen, not bytes — the default mark is six escape sequences around one `%`.
- **A continuation prompt marks nothing.** Measured on `for i in 1 2` + Enter.
- **The erase is the dialect's text, not a flag in the substrate.** `\e[J` was
  hardcoded under `repl/`, which is what `EditorStyle`'s own note says must not
  happen. It is `ClearBeforeThePrompt` now, and zsh's answer is
  `\e[0m\e[27m\e[24m\e[J`. With that, all four measured rows are **byte-identical**
  to real zsh rather than merely close, and bash still writes nothing.
- **A pty test.** Everything here was tested by handing the editor a
  `func() int` for the width; the padding really comes from an ioctl, and a
  width that never arrives writes no mark, so that failure was silent by
  construction. One of the new tests drives the real session loop with the
  hook's output on the same stream as the editor's, which is the only place the
  ordering this PR is about can be observed.

## Verification

`make check` green, no oracle drift. Every assertion is a mutation watched
fail: marking after the hooks, marking at a continuation prompt, padding by
`cols`, padding by byte length, a hardcoded width, the halves fused back into
one block, and each option ignored in turn. All four `PROMPT_SP`/`PROMPT_CR`
combinations compared byte-for-byte against real zsh 5.9.

## Deliberately not here

`promptsp` and `promptcr` stay `recorded(…)` though the front end reads them.
Moving them to `storeBacked` is correct on its face and was tried: it makes them
participate in `emulate`, and ours resets every non-recorded option where real
zsh's resets only the portability-relevant ones unless `-R` is given. Measured,
`setopt nopromptsp; emulate sh` leaves it off in real zsh and turns it back on
here. That divergence already affects `histignorespace` and is not this change's
to widen onto the plugin path this fix serves; it is recorded in #2502.

author: camshaft
body:
## What

Fix a `dead_code` clippy red on `cdz-platform` (blocking the `cdz-platform-clippy` gate sub-check) introduced by #8901: `is_qctor_nullary`'s only non-test callers were the **build-time-generated** contract readers, so in any environment where that generated `contracts` module is stale (pre-#8901, still calling the old empty-payload helpers) or not wired, `is_qctor_nullary` has no always-compiled caller → `cargo clippy -p cdz-platform --all-targets -D warnings` fails. (Reported via v-mutate-query-tag.)

## The fix

`log_value::read_bound`'s `Unbounded` arm now delegates its nullary check to `is_qctor_nullary` (symmetric with `bound_value` already using `qctor_nullary`), removing the duplicated manual tail-parse. Both nullary helpers now have an always-compiled, non-test caller in `log_value`:

- `qctor_nullary` ← `bound_value`

author: jjackson
body:
Prerequisite for the embedded agent widget (#748), and a live leak on its own.

## Two bugs, opposite directions

**by-id was too loose.** `_session_or_404` gated on workspace membership alone, so any co-tenant holding a session UUID could read a conversation the list already refused to show them. That helper backs **14 endpoints** — get, messages, send, place, answer-menu, close, stop, attach, detach, backfill, transfer, archive, reset, unarchive.

**the list was wrong about *why*** — and this is the part that bites. It granted co-tenant visibility to anything with a `RunnerBinding`:

```python
.filter(Q(created_by=request.user) | Q(runner_binding__isnull=False))
```

But a **web** session acquires a binding the moment a runner picks it up. So a private chat became co-tenant-readable *as soon as it started running.* That's confirmed by test rather than argued — `test_list_does_not_leak_a_bound_web_session_to_a_cotenant` fails before this change.

## The fix

`origin` is the property that actually separates "nobody in-app created this" from "someone did". Three ways in, no fourth:

1. you created it
2. you're a `SessionParticipant` — which is what multiplayer means here
3. it's a runner-**discovered** session a runner is actually reporting

Runner-discovered sessions stay tenant-visible **deliberately**: `harness/services.py` creates them with no `created_by` and no participant row, so anything stricter makes the entire emdash-discovered-session flow unreachable by everyone.

Both callers now read one predicate in `apps/canopy_sessions/access.py`, and a parity test asserts they agree for every session shape — the same guard shape `test_claim_schedule_parity` uses after those two hand-written harness predicates drifted.

## Verification

`1854 passed, 1 skipped` — full backend suite. The 8 new tests split 4-fail/4-pass before the change, which is what established that the list leak was real and that runner-discovered visibility needed preserving.

One fixture in `test_session_transfer.py` described a shape the app cannot produce — web-origin with no creator, when `services.create_session` always sets one and adds an OWNER participant. Defaulted from `ws.created_by` rather than editing 19 call sites.

## One judgment call, documented in the code

`Session.created_by` is `on_delete=SET_NULL`, so deleting a user now drops their web sessions out of the API for everyone instead of opening them to every co-tenant. Losing them from a list is the cheaper mistake than publishing a departed colleague's private conversations — they remain in the DB and reachable via admin. `access.py` names the one leg that reverses the trade if you'd rather it went the other way.

I could not check how many orphaned web sessions exist on labs today, so that behaviour change is unmeasured on real data.

author: zrcoderre-ux
body:
Correction to #72, which assumed an organization policy meant *somebody else's* organization and sent you off to build a project outside it. A personal setup can have its own organization — and then the right fix is the opposite one: grant the exception.

Changes:

- **Names the constraint.** Every organization created since 3 May 2024 enforces `constraints/iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation` as part of Google's security baseline. That's what stops the JSON key download, and nobody chose it.
- **Gives the project-level override** for an organization you own — unblocking one project rather than switching the policy off everywhere — with the role it needs (`roles/orgpolicy.policyAdmin` at the org level; project Owner isn't enough), and the useful detail that re-enforcing afterwards leaves an existing key working, so you can re-lock immediately.
- **Says which credential to prefer unblocking:** an API key can be restricted to Text-to-Speech alone; a service-account JSON can't be restricted after the fact, which is precisely why it's blocked by default.
- **Keeps the build-it-elsewhere route** for an organization you don't own, where relaxing the policy isn't yours to do.

Docs-only.

body:
## Summary

Package N5a of the Operations Centre brief (`docs/briefs/PHASE_N_OPERATIONS_CENTRE.md`): the server-side personal alerts table, resolution engine, sweep and precise-wake scheduling. Migration 066.

- **`migrations/066_ops_alerts.sql`** — `ops_alerts` table verbatim to the brief's SQL: unique index `(org_id, order_id, kind, user_id, due_key)` for idempotency, partial index on open rows.
- **`shared/orders/opsAlerts.ts`** — pure recipient/presence/chime/due_key rules: `stationRecipients`, `shouldAlertAssigned`, `shouldAlertNewUnassigned`, `shouldAlertDueSoon`, `dueSoonOrLateRecipients`, `delayedRecipients`, `chimeFor` (severity order `customer_waiting > late > assigned > new_unassigned > due_soon`).
- **`server/services/opsAlerts.ts`** — `createInTx` (single `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` insert path), `resolveOpsAlertsForTransition` (the brief's resolution table), `sweepOpsAlerts(now)`, `nextOpsAlertAt(now)`, `listFor`.
- **`server/routes/opsAlerts.ts`** — `PATCH /api/operations/alerts/:id/ack`, `POST /api/operations/alerts/ack-all`, own rows only, idempotent.
- **`server/services/orderTransitions.ts`** — wired alert creation/resolution into `claim`/`assign`/`ready`/`arrived`/`hold`/`complete`, replacing N3b's `TODO(N5a)` stub.
- **`server/routes/reportCapture.ts`** — `delayed` alert on a declared delay.
- **`server/services/opsBoard.ts`** — `alerts` now reads real rows instead of `[]`.
- **`server/workers/index.ts`** — `sweepOpsAlerts` runs every tick; `computeNextWakeDelayMs` folds `nextOpsAlertAt` into the worker's wake scheduling.

One file outside the literal touch list, `server/__tests__/orderBoardRoute.test.ts`, needed a single new DB-mock branch — an unavoidable consequence of `opsBoard.ts`'s alerts query, not a scope expansion.

**Deliberate scope boundary**: `server/routes/orders.ts` (create/delete) is out of N5a's touch list, so the create-time `assigned` alert for orders created with a default owner has no home in this package — flagging as a small follow-up rather than expanding scope. DELETE is still covered: `sweepOpsAlerts`'s orphan cleanup resolves alerts for orders that no longer exist.

## DoD verification (against a real database)

- Assignment creates exactly one row, for the assignee only; self-claim creates none.
- T-minus-lead and late alerts each fire exactly once across two independent sweep calls (simulating a restart), proven via the unique index.
- Zero SLA-derived alerts when the org toggle is off; exactly one when it's on (same order).
- A colleague's claim resolves every other present member's `due_soon` row, but not the claimant's own.
- `computeNextWakeDelayMs` is a pure function; injected-clock unit tests confirm the wake lands within 2 seconds of the next alert's due instant.
- Completed orders' alerts resolve both via the `complete` transition and via a defensive sweep-time path (status flipped outside the transition machinery).

## Verification

```
npm run check                              → clean
npm test                                   → 115 files, 1035 tests passed
npx vitest run (the 3 new/touched unit-db files) → 59/59 passed
node scripts/audit-storage-orgid.mjs       → ok
node scripts/audit-ui-wiring.mjs           → ok
node scripts/audit-schema-drift.mjs        → ok
node scripts/audit-migration-numbers.mjs   → ok
npm run build                              → clean
migration 066 applied fresh + applied twice (idempotent) + db:push after → zero drift
```

## Known pre-existing environment issue (not this PR's)

While investigating unrelated journey-test failures (`operationsApi.spec.ts`, `operationsBoard.spec.ts`), root-caused a **non-idempotent `scripts/seed.ts`**: re-running the seed script creates a second `"Arcarna Demo Org"` and re-points the shared `seed-admin`/`seed-cashier`/`seed-manager` identities to it, while cached fixture expectations and `resolveOrgId()`'s org-listing pick assume the original org. `git diff --stat` against merge-base confirms zero overlap with this PR's files (`tests/journeys/`, `orders.ts`, `dailyClose.ts`, `orderCompletion.ts` all untouched). This needs a human call — either make the seed script idempotent (reuse-by-name), or repoint the seed identities' `org_id` back — and is being tracked as a candidate for the N9a cleanup package rather than fixed here.

Accepted #48 and #52 already characterize two materially different state-driven policies that settle into different repeatable non-terminal structures under flat decay. Accepted #53 then provides bounded evidence that proportional decay `4.2 * (energy / 100) * dt` turns unchanged #48 into `WON`, unchanged #52 into ordinary terminal `BLACKOUT`, while preserving scripted `WON` and ordinary `BLACKOUT` in the probe.

That is enough evidence to stop broad heuristic shopping. It is not evidence that proportional decay is already accepted runtime.

## DIRECTION DECISION
Close Adaptive Completion as a **diagnostic characterization milestone**, not as a successful adaptive-win claim.

Open **Adaptive Resolution Repair Slice**: validate the already-evidenced proportional relay-decay candidate on exact current accepted reality before adding another heuristic family or new mechanic.

The emerging game identity is a compact maintenance-triage loop where route cost, live urgency, recoverable consequences, and useful partial repair should combine into terminal outcomes. The smallest coherent next question is whether partial maintenance progress can persist enough to resolve under state-driven play without changing the game's verbs or chamber.

## DELTA

- `GAME_CHARTER.md` — closes Adaptive Completion characterization and defines the new exact-composition milestone gate;
- `studio/STUDIO_STATE.json` — compresses the stale oversized snapshot into current factual v0.3 state anchored to accepted #69, accepted #48/#52/#53 evidence, and live proportional composition ownership;

No runtime, tests, assets, dependencies, geometry, controls, presentation, or rule values change.

## OWNERSHIP / GOVERNANCE
Integration PR #60 remains the proportional composition/provenance lane, but its current head predates accepted #69. Integration already recorded that it must rebuild/retarget onto current `main` rather than overwrite accepted focus/time/status behavior.

Integration retains ordinary dependency ordering, exact-head verification, final overlap rescan, and merge landing. Systems owns the relay rule. QA owns reproduction/failure truth. World owns spatial/route preservation. Gameplay and Experience keep their existing behavior/readability boundaries.

No additional Mike or Director approval is required once the accepted direction and exact final gates are satisfied. Mike remains the experiment observer, not the routine merge/CANON gate.

**BLOCKED / NOT TESTED:** proportional decay on exact accepted #69 runtime remains unverified. The new milestone explicitly leaves that work to Integration/Systems/QA/World/Gameplay/Experience on the final composition.

## CURRENT COMPOSITION GATE
Before proportional runtime landing, the exact final head must preserve accepted #69 focus/time/input/status semantics and re-prove the bounded proportional rule, unchanged #48 adaptive `WON`, honest #52 terminal result, scripted `WON`, ordinary `BLACKOUT`, historical constant-decay provenance, route/urgency and spatial continuity, focused-time resource equivalence, Gameplay input/retry/focus contracts, Experience focus/recovery feedback, and local/offline Integration smoke.

If that candidate fails on current accepted reality, the failure returns to the owning specialist lane rather than being tuned until a preferred result appears.
