author: madmatah
body:
## Summary

The shader warm-up worker (the second WebGL2 context that links programs off the presenting thread, so the game's own link is a cache hit) is retired far too often on ANGLE D3D11, the one backend where `auto` runs it, and its breaker has holes that keep a useless worker alive. This PR makes the breaker judge the worker on evidence it can trust, and runs `auto` on D3D11 as a one-release A/B so the fleet decides whether the worker stays.

### The problems

**A healthy worker is retired for the whole session by one bad instant.** On an RTX 3060 (Windows, Chrome, ANGLE D3D11, cold caches) the worker was retired during world entry by the cannot-serve rule after 6 settled links, although the same machine warmed 174 programs on the next launch with every held gate coming back warm. The chain:

1. One program failed to link on the worker's context.
2. The worker's AIMD budget treats a link failure as congestion and halved its window from 3 to 1.
3. The cannot-serve rule divides the queue ahead of the oldest hold by the window of the last stats message: about 28 requests at 384 ms, one at a time, read as ten seconds against a five second cap.
4. The verdict was final for the session.

The fleet shows the same shape: over 4 days of 0.42.x on d3d11, 290 sessions were retired by `cannot-serve:hold-cap`, 227 of them already on their first report, which is sent 75 s after the reporter starts. That these retirements happen during the entry burst is an inference (the first minute also covers whatever the player did), but it matches the 3060 run.

**The breaker has two holes that keep a worker that delivers nothing.** A production capture (RTX 4060 Ti, ANGLE D3D11) showed the worker alive all session with zero programs warmed. That session held only two gates, fewer than any rule needs, so no rule change would have retired it; what it exposes are two holes that keep a longer session on such a machine from ever retiring the worker:

- **A worker-side failure reset the wedged streak.** The worker's link deadline (4 s) is shorter than the hold cap (5 s), so on a machine whose links never settle a single-program hold never expires: it ends on the worker's deadline, and that zeroed the streak.
- **The cannot-serve rule was blind at zero settled links**, exactly where no link ever settles.

**Whether the worker pays on D3D11 in game has never been measured.** It was enabled on D3D11 on per-link evidence (a cold link 464 ms against 41 ms after the worker, and no presented frame lost while the worker links). A cold link on the game context does stall frames on D3D11 (the 4060 Ti capture lost 0.4 to 2.3 s per driver cache miss), so the worker's gain is fewer frozen frames. Its cost is the hold: a gate hides the new object behind its stand-in while it waits, about a second on average on the healthy 3060 run. No one has compared the two on real players.

### The fixes

**A rejected program is not congestion.** In the worker's budget only, a program the context rejects (or will not create) no longer halves the window (`markRejected` in `adaptive_link_budget_core.ts` and `shader_warm_worker_core.ts`). A link past its deadline still halves it. The boot lane is unchanged. The readout now names the first programs the worker failed, by source key (`failedPrograms`), so a capture can tell a dry-assembly source mismatch from a program nothing can link.

**Cannot-serve releases instead of retiring.** The verdict prices one burst, so it now ends that burst's held gates at once (they link on the game context, which is what the rule was built for) and gives their requests back the way an expiry does: the worker drops what no other request waits for, instead of linking the same text a second time on the driver the verdict just found too busy. Until the worker owes nothing (in practice, until the links already in flight settle), no gate holds (bypass `standing-down`), and a hold a gate asks for after the release (a gate decides before its assembly unit runs) is refused on the spot. A second release can therefore only come from a later burst, and the third retires the worker as before (`SHADER_WARM_RELEASE_BREAKER`). A worker that posts nothing for two link deadlines while the gates stand down is not ticking (it answers every link by its own deadline and posts stats while it works) and is retired as `standing-down:silent`, so standing down can never keep a silent worker's context for the page. A release exempts only the holds it ends early: a third unanswered expiry that also trips a release still retires the worker as wedged. A released hold is marked on the hold itself and never reaches the wedged streak or the expired share.

**The breaker holes are closed.**

- A hold that ended on the worker's link deadline counts toward the wedged streak like an expiry; a hold that ended on a fast rejection never does. The new cause is `hold-failures:wedged`.
- The worker reports a deadline give-up as `link-deadline` with the wall the link ran, a lower bound the client keeps apart as `censoredLinks`. The cannot-serve rule reads that pool only while no link has settled at all, at the same three-sample floor, and a retirement on it is named `cannot-serve:hold-cap:censored`. One settled link puts the rule back on settled evidence, bit-identical to before.

**`auto` on D3D11 becomes a one-release A/B.**

- A browser profile draws an arm once (`localStorage`, `shaderWarmAbArmFor`) where the setting is `auto` and `auto` would start the worker. An explicit On or Off is never drawn. Where storage is blocked, the arm is drawn once per page load and kept across renderer rebuilds.
- The `off` arm runs the pre-worker path, the one every other backend runs, and reports the refusal token `ab:off`.
- The perf beacon's worker block gains the summed and wall hold time (the time at least one gate was held), the release count and the arm, bounded on the server. The two cost terms cover the page's life, like the long-task total they are weighed against.

### Decision rule, written before the release

Fleet checkpoint seven days after the release, on first reports, both arms selected by `raw_summary.shaderWarm.abArm`, Chromium only (Firefox has no long-task observer), rows whose `raw_summary` survived on both sides:

- **saved** = mean `browser.longTasks.totalMs` in the `off` arm minus the same in the `on` arm;
- **paid** = mean `holdWallMs` in the `on` arm;
- **the worker stays on D3D11 if saved is at least paid**; otherwise `WORKER_WORTH_BACKENDS` becomes empty, with a re-decision at the next backend change.

One second of hold (objects hidden behind their stand-in) weighs one second of long task (the whole screen frozen), which favours the `off` arm, so a win for the worker is solid. "Paid" also counts holds on hidden prewarm groups, which is conservative. Read beside the rule, not deciding: the share of worst 10 s windows at the 250 ms clamp, long-task p95, frame p95, releases per session, and the share of `on` sessions retired before their first report. With about 850 sessions per arm in 7 days, a clamp-share gap of about 7 points is detectable at 80 percent power; a close result is reported as close. There is no early stop. The decision PR removes the A/B arm in both outcomes.

The rule depends on PR 4009 (perf report fidelity), which stops `raw_summary` from being dropped whole, shipping in the same release.

### Notices

- **`ab:off` is not a refusal.** Every reading of the d3d11 refusal share or of `shader_warm_worker_active` must exclude it for this release, or the refusal share roughly doubles and the active share halves. DEPLOY.md says so; the fleet report scripts and the telemetry skill need the same filter.
- **The arm is per browser profile, not per player.** A player on two machines, or who clears site data, can land in both arms. The NVIDIA shader cache is per OS user, so two profiles on one machine can share a warmed driver cache across ar

Fixes #109495.

## Summary
- re-check source-specific gateway admin authority inside `_handle_yolo_command`, where the security state changes
- allow session YOLO only when the session belongs to a single authenticated principal
- refuse shared groups, shared/default threads, and broadcast sources (`ntfy`, `raft`, `a2a`) that report `chat_type="dm"`
- preserve existing behavior for paired DMs, policy-disabled installs, and participant-isolated group/thread sessions
- cover both the real `_handle_message` dispatch path and the downstream dangerous-command approval path

## Root cause
The central slash gate can intentionally expose `/yolo` through `user_allowed_commands`, so the handler must independently enforce admin authority. Separately, YOLO state is keyed by session rather than sender; enabling it in a multi-principal session lets later members inherit the approval bypass.

## Validation
- the direct-toggle regression failed before the admin guard
- the shared group/thread regressions failed before the single-principal guard
- `77 passed`: gateway YOLO, slash dispatch, approvals, running-session toggles, login, and tool YOLO suites
- Python compilation and `git diff --check` passed

This PR was opened at 2026-09-13 01:07 UTC. Overlapping PR #109503 was opened at 01:14 UTC; this earlier branch remains the contribution being maintained and now includes the shared-session review findings.

author: marcoslide
body:
## O que foi feito

Pacote executável (não um plano) de provisionamento/diagnóstico/benchmark/monitoramento
para o nó GPU principal do projeto. **Decisão oficial de hardware da V1: NVIDIA RTX 4090
(24GB VRAM)** — substitui um plano anterior de RTX 5090 ainda não mesclado a `main`
(`claude/gpu-avatar-factory-spec`). B200 fica reservada como arquitetura futura (AI
Heavy/Burst), nada instalado para ela agora.

Três unidades lógicas do build inicial, um commit cada:

1. **`infra/gpu/`** — biblioteca bash compartilhada (`lib/common.sh`: logging, `--dry-run`,
   idempotência, registro estruturado PASS/WARN/FAIL/SKIP/NOT_TESTED/REQUIRES_GPU em
   JSONL); 11 scripts de bootstrap (00-preflight → 10-final-validation); diagnostics
   (gpu-info, cuda-test via ctypes+libcudart, pytorch-test, tensorrt-test com engine
   mínimo real, nvenc-test, ffmpeg-test, disk/network benchmark); benchmarks estruturados
   (matriz NVENC 1080p/4K × H264/HEVC/AV1, VRAM, disco); preflight de Unreal/Audio2Face/
   MetaHuman com o gate `AUDIO2FACE_UNREAL_COMPATIBILITY`.
2. **`services/gpu_engine`** (`dhf-gpu-engine`, novo membro do workspace uv) —
   `capabilities.py` (detecção real via subprocess, nunca hardcoded), `vram_manager.py`
   (HOT/WARM/UNLOADED com thresholds configuráveis), `model_manager.py` (base
   load/unload/status), `orchestrator.py` (compõe tudo + `prepare_job`/`release_job`),
   `telemetry.py`, `reports.py` (gera `GPU_ENGINE_REPORT_<timestamp>.json/.md`), e o CLI
   `dhf-gpu health|status|capabilities|benchmark|report`.
3. **`tests/gpu_engine/`** — testes reais (sem mocks no caminho "sem GPU", que é
   literalmente verdade neste ambiente).

## Correção pós-revisão (3 erros técnicos P1, todos corrigidos nesta rodada)

Uma revisão encontrou 3 erros técnicos no build inicial. Os commits mais recentes deste
PR corrigem todos:

1. **Matriz CUDA/TensorRT/PyTorch errada para o Audio2Face-3D SDK.** O build inicial
   pedia CUDA 13.4 + TensorRT 11.x — incompatível com o Audio2Face-3D SDK oficial
   (`github.com/NVIDIA/Audio2Face-3D-SDK`, requisito confirmado por fetch direto ao
   README: CUDA >=12.8,<13.0 (12.9 recomendado), TensorRT >=10.13,<11.0). "Suportado pela
   GPU" não é o mesmo que "pode escolher a versão mais nova" — a stack inteira precisa
   compartilhar uma faixa compatível. Corrigido para CUDA 12.9 / TensorRT 10.13.x
   (`tensorrt-cu12`) / PyTorch `cu128` (primeira tag cu12x publicada a partir da 2.7.0,
   compatível em runtime com CUDA 12.9 pela política de minor-version da própria
   NVIDIA). `lib/common.sh` ganhou `version_ge`/`version_lt`/`version_in_range` +
   detecção real de versão instalada (`sort -V`), usados para validar a faixa de
   verdade, não só documentar em comentário. Removidas também as claims especulativas
   "última versão da série UE5"/"UE6 em 2027" (não pertencem ao bootstrap técnico).
2. **Audio2Face-3D modelado como NIM-only (errado).** A NVIDIA distribui o SDK
   (C++/Python, MIT) + modelo oficial (NVIDIA Open Model License) rodando local via
   CUDA/TensorRT, separado do NIM (container de deployment escalável via NGC).
   `audio2face/verify-requirements.sh` agora tem `AUDIO2FACE_MODE=local_sdk` (padrão) vs.
   `nim`, com checagens explicitamente separadas por modo: `local_sdk` valida
   CUDA/TensorRT/build tools/CMake/python3/acesso ao modelo e **nunca** exige
   Docker/`NGC_API_KEY`; `nim` continua exigindo Docker/nvidia-ctk/`NGC_API_KEY`.
3. **MetaHuman Animator generalizado como Windows-only por inteiro (errado).** No
   MetaHuman 5.8, Linux suporta Creator, Animator **facial** (offline e realtime),
   geração de animação facial, uso em cena e Movie Render Queue — todo o pipeline Avatar
   Factory (MULTIVIEW→MESH MASTER→REFINEMENT→METAHUMAN CREATOR→FROM CUSTOM MESH→RIG)
   roda nisso. A limitação real e específica é **body animation/markerless body
   capture**. `metahuman/preflight.sh` agora separa
   `metahuman_animator_facial_linux=PASS` de
   `metahuman_body_markerless_linux=SKIP` (Windows-only), e reporta
   `metahuman_identity_performance_linux=NOT_TESTED` em vez de generalizar (não
   exercitado nesta missão; um workflow específico com requisito DX12 deve ser
   registrado individualmente).

19 novos testes (`tests/gpu_engine/test_bash_preflight.py`) rodam os scripts bash de
verdade via subprocess (nvcc/tensorrt dublados via PATH/PYTHONPATH fake) provando as 3
correções, incluindo um bug real de override encontrado rodando o próprio script durante
esta revisão (`versions.env` sobrescrevia incondicionalmente um `AUDIO2FACE_MODE` já
exportado pelo chamador).

## Riscos identificados (já refletindo a correção acima — ver `infra/gpu/README.md`)

1. **Unreal Engine no Linux não tem binário oficial via launcher** — único caminho
   documentado é compilar do código-fonte com conta GitHub vinculada à Epic.
2. **`NGC_API_KEY` só é necessária no modo `nim` do Audio2Face** (não no `local_sdk`,
   padrão desta V1) — self-host de dev é gratuito (até 16 GPUs, sem SLA); produção exige
   licença paga ou uso via API hospedada com custo por uso. Os termos exatos da NVIDIA
   Open Model License do modelo usado pelo `local_sdk` não foram reconfirmados nesta
   revisão.
3. Boa parte da pesquisa original veio de busca indexada, não fetch direto às páginas
   oficiais (mesmo bloqueio de rede já documentado em sessões anteriores para
   `ghcr.io`/Docker Hub) — mas a matriz CUDA/TensorRT do Audio2Face-3D SDK (item 1 da
   correção acima) foi confirmada por fetch direto ao GitHub oficial nesta revisão. Os
   demais números de `versions.env` devem ser reconfirmados manualmente antes de
   produção; os `diagnostics/` fazem exatamente essa reconfirmação em runtime.

## Testes

- `uv run pytest -m "not requires_services and not requires_worker_offline"` →
  **129 passed, 3 skipped** (integração sem credencial) — inclui os 19 novos testes da
  correção P1 + os 110 já existentes do monorepo.
- `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` — limpos em todo o repositório.
- `shellcheck --severity=warning --external-sources` em todos os 23 scripts de
  `infra/gpu/` — limpo.
- `gitleaks detect --no-git` — nenhum segredo encontrado.
- **Tudo rodado de verdade neste ambiente** (Ubuntu 24.04.4 real, sem GPU): preflight
  reporta FAIL genuíno de RAM/disco/rede deste sandbox (não da instância real), ffmpeg
  fez encode/decode real, disk-benchmark mediu velocidades reais, `dhf-gpu` CLI real via
  `uv run --project services/gpu_engine`, os scripts de Audio2Face/MetaHuman corrigidos
  foram executados de ponta a ponta (inclusive com `nvcc`/`tensorrt` fake para exercitar
  os limites exatos de CUDA 13.0/TensorRT 11.0), todo caminho que precisa de GPU real
  reporta `REQUIRES_GPU` honestamente.

## Conflito com Codex

Nenhum. Nada em `services/storage`, OAuth, `StorageProvider` ou testes de Storage foi
tocado — só `infra/gpu/`, `services/gpu_engine/`, `tests/gpu_engine/` e
`pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock` (novo membro de workspace).

## Próximo passo

Provisionar a RTX 4090 real na Hostinger e executar o bootstrap
(`infra/gpu/bootstrap/00-preflight.sh` em diante) contra hardware de verdade — tudo que
hoje reporta `REQUIRES_GPU`/`NOT_TESTED` passa a ser validado nesse momento. PR
permanece **draft** — sem merge.

author: ozzyfromspace
body:
A field could hold its pending spinner **forever**: `aria-busy="true"` over a validation that had already finished, whose error was already committed to `errorCells`, invisible because `showErrors` reads `displayState === 'error'`. The user types, blurs, and the spinner never clears. Submit still re-validates, so nothing invalid gets through, but the field is silently stuck.

Found while investigating the recurring `docs-demos-smoke > async-refinements` CI flake, which turns out to be this bug rather than a slow runner. Both previous responses to that flake raised a wait ceiling, and neither could have worked: nothing was ever slow.

## The bug

```ts
if (target === lastFiredTarget) { clearTimer(); return }
```

The forward-progress guard refused to re-arm for any deadline equal to the one it had just fired, on the stated premise that *"legit timing always advances the deadline or drops it"*.

The min-visible hold breaks that premise by design. While a spinner is inside its window the reducer re-emits `pendingShownAt + minVisible`, the **same instant on every pass**. When the timer fired a fraction early, the reducer re-emitted that deadline while `lastFiredTarget` still held it, so the engine cleared the timer and armed nothing. Nothing else was scheduled to re-evaluate the field.

The guard now refuses only a re-fired deadline that has **also already passed**, which is the busy-loop shape it was written for. Re-arming a still-future deadline cannot spin: the delay is positive, and once a fire lands at or past the target the guard engages again.

## The structural half

Fixing one guard leaves the shape intact, so the engine now floors any stored `'pending'` machine that carries no usable deadline with a review of its own.

The reducer is policy and the engine owns the clock, so liveness belongs there. `getDisplayState` is a consumer-overridable extension point that the engine already treats as untrusted for `NaN`, `Infinity`, and fixed-or-past deadlines; returning `'pending'` with no `reviewAt` was the same hazard with none of those tells, and it is reachable from outside the library. The library's own reducer does it on the in-flight branch.

A settled verdict is deliberately untouched: `error` and `success` are terminal until something changes, and a timer for them would be a wakeup with nothing to do.

## Evidence

600 runs driving the demo at a latency just over `FOCUS_OUT_GRACE`, measured per arm in separate processes:

| arm | hangs / 600 |
| --- | --- |
| baseline | 16, 23 |
| liveness floor only | 12 |
| guard fix only | 0 |
| both | **0** |

The two are not redundant. The floor alone barely helps, because the machine that stranded came from the min-visible hold, which *does* emit a deadline, so the floor never applied and the old guard still refused to arm it. The guard fix closes this bug; the floor closes the shape the guard fix cannot see.

Also 0/720 across a latency sweep and 0/400 on the original reproduction. A sweep below the grace never hangs (0/120, twice, in both sweep directions), which is what localised it: the field has to actually reach `'pending'`.

## Why it hid for so long

The demo's 700ms `setTimeout` is a real timer, so CPU load does not touch it. Measured under coverage it takes 1086ms, identical to without, against a 5000ms budget. That kills the slowness theory outright, and it is the measurement to reach for first next time.

Compressing that cosmetic delay is also what made the bug reproducible at all, at 40x more trials per second. A long fake delay hides races as well as wasting CI time.

## Test-side changes

`compressDemoLatency` scales demo delays at or above 300ms down by 10. The threshold sits in a wide gap: Attaform's `DEFAULT_TIMINGS` are 120/120 and `debounceMs` defaults to 0, while the smallest demo latency is 350ms, so runtime timing is never compressed. Scaled rather than clamped so a demo staging two delays in a deliberate order keeps it. The factor is 10 rather than larger for a reason recorded in the helper: at 50 the compressed delays straddle `FOCUS_OUT_GRACE` (16ms) and whether a spinner appeared became a coin flip.

`async-refinements` drops 1086ms to ~30ms, the smoke suite's test time 4.38s to ~1.4s, and both hand-tuned wait budgets (5000ms, 2000ms) are deleted: `waitUntil`'s 1000ms default is now ~35x the settle time, so a timeout there means the pipeline stopped.

## Two tests changed rather than worked around

`display-state.test.ts` had a case whose comment described the continuity branch as holding `'pending'` with no engine timer, *"it trusts the settle to be a reactive event"*, pinned by `expect(vi.getTimerCount()).toBe(0)`. The fragile design was codified in a test that would have blocked the fix. Its real guarantee is kept and still asserted: the settle releases the spinner promptly, on the reactive event, **with timers advanced by zero**. That assertion is what proves the floor is a backstop and not the release path.

Two engine tests asserted a non-finite `reviewAt` arms no timer at all. They now assert what matters: the bad deadline never reaches `setTimeout` (proved by the timer not being due a tick later) and the spinner still gets reviewed.

The regression test is written against the engine rather than a demo, because the demo only reaches this at ~2-3% per mount. It fails against the unfixed guard.

body:
Gives Locus CI. Until now `.github/workflows/` held only `release.yml`, which fires on `v*` tags — **nothing has ever run on a pull request.** No formatting check, no clippy, no tests. Every PR merged to date went in unchecked.

Closes the `fmt` / `ci.yml` / `CONTRIBUTING` part of DEV-611. The toolchain pin (step 1) landed separately as a8e328a.

## Why now

Two failures this week, both of the kind a gate catches and a reviewer does not.

**PR #18 sat open for two weeks with a hard compile dependency on #17.** GitHub reported `mergeable=CLEAN` the entire time, because `mergeable` answers a question about *text* — do these patches apply — not about whether the result builds. A `cargo test --workspace` gate would have failed it the day it opened.

**A 1-in-15 flake lived in `delegate.rs` for months** and nobody saw it, because a single local run is not evidence about a suite. Fixed as DEV-613 (ccf5f9a) — and found by repetition, which is what CI *is*.

Worth being precise about the second one, because it cuts against this PR as much as for it: **master is green per run, not green as a property.** Everything below is a measurement of particular runs on one machine. That is the strongest claim available before CI exists, and the weakness of it is the argument for merging this.

## Three commits

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `7eaee07` | `cargo fmt --all` — machine output, 8 files, nothing else |
| `70fe43a` | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — alone |
| `e14b60a` | `.github/workflows/release.yml` — alone, same rustup root cause |
| `d621a42` | `CONTRIBUTING.md` — alone |

Squash is the only merge method allowed on `master`, so these collapse into one commit on merge. The split is for review legibility — read `7eaee07` last, or not at all.

Rebuilt rather than rebased, twice. The held branch had been cut from `d6dc1c7`, six commits back, and a stale formatting commit rebased forward conflicts in every file it touches. When #33 then landed on three of the formatting files, the pass was discarded and re-run against `52a18a6` rather than merged forward. The three policy commits cherry-pick cleanly across all of it; only the machine-generated one is ever regenerated, which is the point of keeping it separate.

## Re-measured against `52a18a6`

The formatting count had moved three times before this (54 → 72 → 61 in the ticket), and twice more while this PR was being prepared as #31 and #33 landed. That is five measurements, no two of the first four alike — which is the argument for the gate, not an embarrassment. Measured against `52a18a6`:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | **75 diff sites across 8 files** |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` | **15 distinct warnings**, 9 auto-fixable (ticket says 13) |
| `cargo test --workspace --all-features` | 260 passed, 0 failed — *this run* (ticket says 184) |

Per file: `hook.rs` 24, `stop_verifier.rs` 18, `run.rs` 17, `delegate.rs` 9, `upgrade.rs` 3, `agents.rs` 2, `sync.rs` 1, `config_gen.rs` 1. `bundled.rs` had 3 sites until #33 rewrote those regions clean, which is exactly why the pass was re-run rather than rebased.

## The formatting commit is machine output — checked, not asserted

77 hunks is more than anyone will read honestly, so it was checked mechanically two ways. Both are described in the commit message; the short version:

**Token identity.** Each file lexed before and after and compared as span-free token vectors, normalising only a trailing `,` in final position of a delimited group (grammatically optional in Rust). String literals compare as single opaque tokens, so nothing inside a literal can be normalised away — which is why this is done at the token level and not by stripping whitespace. **7 of 8 files are token-identical.**

`hook.rs` is the one exception, and its *complete* divergence set is three inserted matched brace pairs — no deletions, no reordering anywhere in the file:

- `workflow_denial` — `.and_then(|v| …)` gains a block body
- `derive_slug_from_path` — `.map(|c| …)` gains a block body
- `sync_prd_to_work_json` — `.filter(|l| …)` gains a block body

All three are rustfmt wrapping a closure body in a block because the body no longer fits on one line (`rewrite_closure` falling back to `rewrite_closure_with_block`). `|x| e` and `|x| { e }` are the same closure: the block's tail expression carries the same type, the same value, and the same temporary drop point.

**Comment payload.** Token comparison is blind to `//` and `/* */`, so every comment was extracted separately with a Rust lexer state machine and compared with interior whitespace normalised. **1002 comments across the 8 files, zero payload changes** — rustfmt re-indented comments, it did not rewrite any.

No file outside the 8 was touched. Worth stating explicitly: rustfmt recurses the whole module tree and `--skip-children` no longer exists, so running it on a file with `mod` declarations can silently reformat unrelated files.

## One deviation from the ticket, and it matters

The ticket specifies `rustup show` to install the pinned toolchain, "reads the toml — no action needed". **That has been untrue since rustup 1.28.0 (March 2025)**, which removed auto-installation of the active toolchain. `rustup show` now returns 0 while leaving the job on whatever Rust the runner image ships — a pin that looks honoured and isn't, which is worse than no pin.

This workflow uses the migration command from the [1.28.0 release notes](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/03/02/Rustup-1.28.0/) instead, plus an explicit `rustup component add`:

```yaml
run: |
  rustup show active-toolchain || rustup toolchain install
  rustup component add rustfmt
```

**This is not hypothetical, and `release.yml` had the same bug** — so `e14b60a` fixes it here.

`release.yml` used bare `rustup show`. Its last green run was 2026-08-16; the pin landed 2026-09-13. It has **never once run against a `rust-toolchain.toml`** — its green history is evidence about the runner's default toolchain and nothing else. And the failure is worse than "builds with the wrong Rust": the very next step is `rustup target add ${{ matrix.target }}`, which resolves against the pinned-but-uninstalled toolchain and dies with `toolchain '1.93-…' is not installed`, taking all five release targets with it and publishing no assets.

A latent break fixed before its first run rather than a regression — but it would have surfaced on a tag, mid-release, which is the worst place to find it.

## Shape

| Check | Runs on | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rustfmt` | ubuntu-latest | blocking-capable |
| `test` | ubuntu-latest + macos-14, `fail-fast: false` | blocking-capable |
| `clippy` | ubuntu-latest | advisory (`continue-on-error: true`) |

Plus `permissions: contents: read`, concurrency with `cancel-in-progress`, and `timeout-minutes` on every job (10 / 20 / 30).

**No `architecture` job.** Allele has one because it gates `tests/architecture.rs`. Locus has no equivalent, and a job that asserts nothing is the exact defect class this repo keeps tripping over.

`clippy` is advisory because master carries 15 warnings. It flips to blocking in the same PR that clears them (ticket step 5), not before — a permanently-red check is one everyone learns to ignore.

## What this PR does not do

**It does not block a single merge.** I checked the actual repo config rather than assuming. The `Default` ruleset (id 20907411, active on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`) contains exactly five rules:

```
deletion · non_fast_forward · creation · required_signatures
pull_request (0 approvals, squash-only)
```

There is **no `required_status_checks` rule**, and `branches/master/protection` returns 404, so there is no legacy protection either. Nothing today requires any check to pass.

That is a recent change: the ruleset *did* require contexts named `rustfmt`, `clippy` and `test`, and because no workflow produced them, every PR in the repo was blocked. They were removed to unblock the queue. So this PR is the thing that

No new contract was needed. `GOV.ORCH.6` is FROZEN and already names these cuts; the files had simply regrown past them.

**Nothing was lost, and that was checked rather than asserted.** The set of document references in `CURRENT_STATE.md` before and after is identical — zero lost. Four backticked tokens did not survive: three OP.2 class names that live in the source and in the phase document, and one backlog id whose row keeps both its `CE.2` label and its relay id. **Two corrections the Product Owner made to the worker's draft.** It referred to a `SESSION_CLOSE` report that does not exist — the run was cut off at its budget ceiling before writing one — and it did not know about the Palo Alto gate lift merged in parallel. The next action now states plainly that it is blocked on the Product Owner's Panorama measurement rather than on engineering.

**Note on the run.** `NXS-LOCAL-0131` reported `failed` on its $5.00 ceiling at 109 turns, with every validation step green and **zero commits** — the packet asked for frequent commits and the worker made none. The work itself was complete; it is committed here after review.

**Evidence.** Cold-start, architecture-convergence, contract-authority and project-files-budget suites: 39 passed. `project_queue.py check` clean. Repository privacy gate 0 findings.

author: evetev-dev
body:
## Lo primero: la tienda estaba abierta

`eve-store-one.vercel.app` llevaba **nueve días en público** (último despliegue, 3 de septiembre) y no pasivamente: `robots.txt` con `Allow: /`, sitemap de 29 URLs, feed de 24 productos y las fichas servidas desde el servidor. Comprobado pidiéndola con cada agente:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Googlebot · GPTBot · ClaudeBot · PerplexityBot · OAI-SearchBot | **HTTP 200** a todos |
| `noindex` | ninguno |

No hay rastro de indexación —URL huérfana, sin dominio propio ni un solo enlace entrante—, pero estaba haciendo cuanto podía por ser encontrada. Que es exactamente para lo que se construyó.

**Ya está cerrada por dos vías**: Deployment Protection del proyecto pasó de *Standard* (que deja producción abierta) a **All Deployments** —verificado, 302 a `vercel.com/login` para los cinco agentes—, y este PR añade el cierre en el código.

## Cerrada por defecto

Sin `TIENDA_ABIERTA=1`, todo lo público es `/en-construccion` con `noindex, nofollow`; el robots prohíbe todo, el sitemap va vacío y el feed responde 404. `/panel` sigue vivo: la tienda está cerrada al público, no a quien la monta.

El sentido por defecto es deliberado. Una variable que se olvide deja la tienda **cerrada**: el fallo posible pasa a ser «sigue en obras de más» —se nota y se arregla en un minuto— y no «salió a la venta un catálogo a medio revisar». Es la disciplina que ya tiene el schema, `publicado ... default false`.

La puerta vive en el middleware para que una página nueva no pueda saltársela por descuido. Y ahí salió una fuga propia: el matcher excluía el prefijo `marca/` para ahorrarse comprobaciones de sesión en los SVG, y con eso dejaba fuera las **páginas** de marca. Con la tienda cerrada, `/marca/dermanat` seguía enseñando el catálogo entero. Ahora el corte va por extensión: los archivos fuera, las rutas dentro.

## El diseño

**Cabecera** — era la palabra «Eve-Store» y un buscador que se comía la fila. Ahora son tres franjas: la promesa (envío, existencias, sin registro), marca y búsqueda, y navegación por marcas. Esas promesas vivían enterradas en un párrafo de la portada, o sea que solo las leía quien entraba por la raíz; quien llega desde una búsqueda cae en una ficha.

**Marca** — era la única app del repo sin `/marca` ni favicon. Se añade al manifiesto de `marca-sync` y se sirve desde su propio origen.

**Jumbotrones** — portada y las cuatro marcas, con `app/jumbotron.tsx` y un registro de portadas por marca. Tres cosas que se midieron en vez de suponerse:

- **El velo no es adorno.** `object-cover` recorta distinto en cada ancho, así que apoyar el texto en «la zona despejada de la foto» es apoyarlo donde algún tamaño de ventana pondrá una cara.
- **Dos fallos de contraste bajo AA**: la entradilla en `pizarra` sobre velo claro daba ~3,7:1, y sobre velo oscuro no servía ninguno de los dos colores. El titular ahora elige según el fondo.
- **La altura de la banda crece con el ancho.** Con alto fijo pasaba de 2,4:1 en un portátil a **4,6:1** en un monitor y se comía media foto — en Ilovepinch desaparecía el producto entero. Es el fallo que solo se ve si miras en la pantalla correcta.

**Y además**: dos columnas en móvil (una tarjeta por fila son 25 desplazamientos para ver el catálogo), «Agotado» sobre la foto en vez de bajo el precio, pie en azul noche con las marcas enlazadas, `<h1>` en la búsqueda —no tenía ninguno—, migas de pan en la ficha, y `<Pie minimo />` en el checkout, donde la cabecera quitaba con cuidado las salidas y el pie las devolvía todas.

## Lo que salió al usarlo

**El puerto.** `eve-store` declaraba el 3003, que ya era de `eve-studio` y de `eve-merchants`: no se podían levantar a la vez. Pasa al **3006**, y la tabla de `CLAUDE.md` gana la fila que le faltaba.

**Tres de los cuatro comandos del README no funcionaban.** `db:check` y `db:import` fallaban con «Falta DATABASE_URL» aunque `creds` dijera que todo estaba bien: leen `process.env`, y nadie carga `.env.local` en un `node` suelto. `scripts/entorno.mjs` lo arregla sin pisar lo que ya venga exportado. `db:migrate` sigue necesitando el export a mano —es `psql`, no Node— y ahora el README lo dice.

**Fixture.** `TIENDA_FIXTURE=1` sirve el catálogo desde `catalogo/catalogo.json` para trabajar el diseño sin base. **No es un respaldo**: no se enciende solo, porque una base caída viéndose igual que una sana es, en una tienda, vender lo que no hay. Puesto en producción, rompe el arranque a propósito.

## Imágenes

Todas por `scripts/marca-imagen.mjs`, que convierte, nombra y apunta en el manifiesto:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `spa-still-life` | 10 127 KB → **201 KB** |
| `Allen_nutririon-pic2` | 2 084 KB → **107 KB** |
| `I_love_pinch-pic2` | 1 871 KB → **87 KB** |
| `dermanat-pic` | 1 424 KB → **23 KB** |
| `bioessens-pic` | 48 KB → **36 KB** |

Las fuentes pesadas (~15 MB en `.png`/`.jpg`) **no entran al repo**: en esa carpeta solo viven `.webp`.

## Comprobado

`typecheck`, Prettier y `marca:check` en verde. `next build` pasa en los dos estados —abierta (34 páginas) y cerrada (35, con el letrero)—. El cierre se verificó ruta por ruta: portada, fichas, las cuatro marcas, carrito, checkout, búsqueda y pedido, más que los SVG de marca siguen sirviéndose.

## Queda pendiente

- **Bio Essens es la única foto blanda**: la fuente son 750 px estirados a 1 905 en monitor.
- **Páginas legales**: Términos, Privacidad y Tratamiento de datos son obligatorias en Colombia y no existen ni aquí ni en `apps/website`. No las enlacé para no dejar 404.
- El plan Free de Supabase volverá a pausar la base; hoy hubo que reanudarla a mano.

author: lingyuzhi
body:
Add **EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning** (arXiv, 2026) to `1.3.1 Interaction with Grounded Task Environments`.

EnvHarness uses execution trajectories to customize existing environments while retaining their underlying logic and verifiers. The resulting environments support **both skill-based learning and reinforcement learning**.

I learned about this paper in the [Qingke AI community](https://qingkeai.online/blog/EnvHarness-Talk) and think it's a good piece of work.I propose this category based on its **grounded environment feedback and demonstrated GRPO policy training**. The paper's main experiments also study skill extraction, so it spans both parametric and non-parametric learning.

- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19880
- Official code: https://github.com/google-research/envharness
- Homepage: https://www.envharness.com

This PR adds one README table row using the existing format.

author: abbyshekit
body:
## What this changes

Depends on #946 at `a0c668fd0ed148e0e6cee98131963e0a7192de83`; this draft targets upstream `main` because the dependency branch lives in the contributor fork. The combined diff includes #946, while the [participant-only commit](https://github.com/abbyshekit/trace-commons-server/commit/6ee100ccbf885d91ef991ec36ee06c3e10e0d691) isolates this packet for review until the base can be reconciled after #946 lands.

The operator ledger currently accepts manually asserted participant hashes. This adds immutable readable Cloud-credit offers, account-derived reservation identities, and self-only reservation/history routes using the existing cookie and native-account authentication. Operators publish and suspend offers through the existing CLI.

V71 preserves account-merge aliases, lifetime duplicate checks and cap usage under forced RLS and separate runtime grants. Foreign replay returns the same ownership-safe refusal as an unknown reservation. Request admission occurs before database checkout, so a reservation waiting on a tenant lock cannot consume the whole default pool.

The [operator runbook](https://github.com/abbyshekit/trace-commons-server/blob/6ee100ccbf885d91ef991ec36ee06c3e10e0d691/docs/operator/participant-rewards.md) covers deployment, the four HTTP operations and limits, including required volume profiling for ledger-derived capacity and awarded totals. Evidence admission, native screens and provider delivery remain later packets.

## Verification

All checks ran on the final reviewed source with Rust 1.96.1 and `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings"`. The default package run aggregated **2,463 passed, 0 failed, 37 ignored** across its test binaries. The selected live suites ran separately against disposable PostgreSQL databases:

| Suite | Passed | Failed | Ignored |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Existing mission rewards | 13 | 0 | 0 |
| Participant rewards | 8 | 0 | 0 |
| Real TCP HTTP lifecycle and contention | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Account merge | 9 | 0 | 0 |
| Reward migration upgrade | 1 | 0 | 0 |

Live coverage includes valid and invalid authentication, foreign replay, direct table-access denial, capacity races, expiry, suspension, merged aliases, revoked-grant rollback, operator CLI publication, and unchanged reward review/invalidation semantics. Foreign replay and pool starvation were reproduced before their fixes and passed afterward. CI now explicitly invokes the participant suites and verifies that they created reservation rows.

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo check -p trace-commons-server --bins`
- [x] `RUSTFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo test -p trace-commons-server -- --test-threads=4`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p trace-commons-server --all-targets` with the repository allow-list
- [x] Strict maintainability review, five review lenses, fixes and final re-verification

## Licensing

- [x] I license this contribution under **MIT OR Apache-2.0**, per CONTRIBUTING.md, including the AGPL-distributed server code.
- [x] New server `.rs` files carry the copyright and SPDX header.
- [x] No permissive crate gained an AGPL dependency; license-boundary tests passed.

author: rabpitvn1-create
body:
## Root cause
Two Level 0 Lucia gates were correct in isolation but disconnected in the runtime path:

1. The writer was required to advance `storyArc` / `luciaEncounter`, while the reducer exposed no accepted operation capable of carrying those fields.
2. Even after a valid Lucia decision, Game State Core could reject Party add because Lucia was not registered in `characters` with active presence and join eligibility.

## Fix
- add a dedicated `lucia_story` operation with machine-validated `first_contact` and `join` stages
- keep first contact and join on separate turns using the existing start-of-turn story gates
- make `join` write the validated decision state and canonical Lucia Party member instead of depending on the generic survivor roll path
- reject invalid/replayed `lucia_story` operations in the deterministic rejected-op audit
- register Lucia in Game State Core after validated first contact and update `joinEligible` only after the validated decision state
- create Lucia inventory/equipment containers when the story-managed character first becomes known
- add Kotlin regressions for first-contact registration and a PartyEngine join after decision
- expand the generated-Java integration regression to verify the runtime transport and Core bridge

## Compatibility
No Save/Load runtime changes. No relaxation of the existing Lucia Arrival / first-contact / decision ordering. Generic Party and survivor behavior remains unchanged.

author: liloleblanc
body:
Measured against the deployed worker:

```
/adsb/callsign/ACA123    max-age=90  x-adsb-cache: miss  ac: 1
/adsb/callsign/ZZZ9999   max-age=30  x-adsb-cache: neg   ac: 0  upstream: 429
```

A flight that is flying caches for 90 seconds. One that is **not transmitting
caches for thirty** — and FR24 is tried *ahead* of the community ring, so every
re-ask is a paid call.

A departure sitting two hours on stand is asked about **240 times per callsign
variant**, and `_adsbTelemetry` tries up to four variants. That is the origin of
the 80% empty-response rate in your usage figures, and the largest single line
in the bill: **3,258 position requests for 6,920 credits, four in five returning
nothing.**

The community ring can't absorb it — it's blocked from a Cloudflare Worker and
answers 429 essentially always, which is exactly what `upstream: 429` above
shows. So reaching the negative path says nothing by itself.

### What it turns on

What FR24 said on the way past:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| FR24 answered, carrying nothing | the aircraft isn't transmitting | **300s** |
| FR24 skipped / over budget / errored | we don't know | 30s, unchanged |

The 429-stampede recovery this TTL was originally added for is untouched.

**Five minutes, not ten.** The cost curve is already flat by then (240 lookups
per variant over a 2h stand → 24), and the exposure is a departure that starts
transmitting just after a miss was cached waiting that long for its aircraft
panel. Five minutes is tolerable; ten isn't.

The same distinction is applied to the ring's own ok-but-empty answer, which was
cached at the *live-position* TTL — a value chosen for how fast a position goes
stale, not for the absence of one.

### Diagnosable from outside

`X-Adsb-Cache: quiet` when the aircraft isn't transmitting, `neg` when the
lookup failed, with a matching `_quiet` flag in the body.

### Expected saving

Roughly **10x fewer paid empty lookups**. Against the measured ~3,000 credits/day
that should bring the positions path well inside 1,000/day — which matters,
because the Explorer allowance drops back to 30k (1,000/day) at year end.

### Tests

Eight, each mutation-checked: TTL long enough to matter but not so long a
just-airborne flight waits, transient path still recovering in 30s, only a
parsed empty array counting as quiet, the flag defaulting false on every path
that skips FR24, and the served header matching the TTL actually cached — those
two drifted apart once during this change, with the edge holding the new value
while the response advertised the old.

527 tests pass.

author: fcsouza
body:
Third of the stack: #254 adds the type, #255 makes `@vttforge/testing` use it,
this makes the templates use it. Base is #255's branch, so the diff shows only
this change.

## What

The four templates carried a hand-written `FoundryNamespace`, kept in step by
hand. They import the shared one now.

## Why it is not cosmetic

A scaffolded project and `@vttforge/testing` both declare the Foundry globals,
and two `declare global` blocks naming one global have to agree on the type.
Two structurally identical interfaces are still two types, and tsc says so in a
sentence that reads like a riddle:

```
error TS2403: Subsequent variable declarations must have the same type.
  Variable 'foundry' must be of type 'FoundryNamespace', but here has type
  'FoundryNamespace'.
```

#255 closes five of the six errors. This closes the sixth.

## The test was weaker than it looked

Finding the right shape for the regression test turned up something worth
saying out loud: the existing template typecheck never checked these
declarations at all.

`@vttforge/types` does not resolve from a scaffolded project in a temp
directory, `skipLibCheck` is on, and an unresolved import inside a `.d.ts` is
silently ignored. Every global became `any`, and everything passed. That is how
six errors shipped in a repo that typechecks its templates on every run.

The new test checks the declaration on its own, with `skipLibCheck` off and both
packages mapped to source. It is deliberately not the whole scaffolded project:
what is under test is whether two `declare global` blocks can coexist.

## Verification

Put a local `FoundryNamespace` back in one template and the test fails with the
TS2403 above. Restore the import and it passes.

typecheck, test, build and lint green with `--force`.

## One thing this does not fix

Mapping `@vttforge/types` to source in the *full* project typecheck surfaces two
real type errors in the system template, both hidden until now by the `any`
above:

- `ActorLike<CharacterData, GearItem>`: `CharacterData` is a class, so it has no
  index signature, and the `System` parameter wants one.
- `CONFIG.Item.documentClass.create(...)`: `documentClass` is typed `AnyClass`,
  which carries a construct signature and no statics.

A user with `@vttforge/types` installed, which the template declares, hits both
today. They belong in the `types` scope and are not in this PR.

## What and why

Adds a new job-catalogue filter, "Auto-apply available": a true-or-absent
facet that is `true` when a posting's ATS provider (`source`) is one
`cmd/auto-apply` can currently attempt to fill and submit for
(`greenhouse`, `lever` via chromedp; `ashby`, `workable` via the
cloud-agent fallback). It's a best-effort, provider-eligibility signal,
never a submission guarantee — the checkbox carries a
"Best-effort — successful submission isn't guaranteed" caption.

Prompted by a live investigation of `auto_apply_queue`/`atsapply`
production data: most parked attempts fail on things knowable in advance
from the posting's own provider (Recruitee has no fill path at all;
captcha/white-label layouts are provider-shaped risks), so surfacing this

author: sridharkalaibala
body:
Owner: "Live voice is switched off for this shop ... i didnt do. may be db reset?" and "open ai setting gone."

He was right, and **yesterday's keep did not save him**. Today's reset fell through two holes at once.

## One: the seeder never set up online ordering

The box did not *restore* its snapshot, it *rebuilt* from `seed.js` — and `seed.js` has never configured online ordering. Right now:

```
GET https://develop.posnic.io/online-ordering
{"type":"error","message":"This shop is not taking online orders yet.","data":{"reason":"none_configured"}}
```

No store address, so `/order/ABC` is gone and every printed code points at nothing. Every rebuild has always done this; it went unnoticed because the nightly reset usually restores a snapshot where the address had been set by hand.

The seeder now switches ordering on, at a **fixed** address (`SEED_STORE_ADDRESS`, default `ABC`) rather than a generated one. An address that changes on each rebuild breaks every QR code and every pasted link — which is what happened when it went ABC123, then FJ5AF, then ABC. It will not stamp over a shop that already has one.

## Two: the keep could not re-home what it saved

The keep dumps `branch_secrets` and `branch_preferences` and puts them back, but their rows are keyed by **licence and branch id**. A rebuild mints new ones, so the restored rows pointed at a branch that no longer existed, and the shop read as though nothing had ever been configured. The keep worked for a restore and did nothing for a rebuild — the exact case it was added for.

`keep-branches.js` now handles both. A restore lands the ordinary way. When the old branch is gone and there is **exactly one** shop now, the ordering configuration and the settings rows are re-homed onto it, so a key typed yesterday is still a key today. One shop is not a guess; several would be, and then it does nothing and says so. An account row belongs to the licence rather than a branch, so it takes the new licence and keeps its null branch.

## Tests

`tests/sandbox-scripts-deployed.test.js` (7 now): the seeder configures ordering at a fixed address and will not overwrite an existing one; the keep re-homes both collections, treats account rows correctly, refuses to guess when there is more than one shop, still handles the restore case, and cleans up its working copy.

## After this deploys

The next reset brings the shop back at `/order/ABC` with whatever is configured at that moment. **This does not restore what today's rebuild already lost** — the key and the switches will need entering once more, and then they stay.

Rebuilds the two pieces of work from the previous session that never made it to the remote.

## 1. Weeks 4–27: phase-wise syllabus (`src/data/scheduleData.js`)

The old generator loop stamped **all 7 days of a week with the identical lecture range** (`Module 14` / `Lecture 1 to 4`), so 168 of the 189 days were placeholders.

- Replaced it with an explicit **phase-wise curriculum table** across five phases:
  - **Phase 1 · Foundation** (W1–9) — Discrete Mathematics core + Engineering Mathematics / Calculus
  - **Phase 2 · Logic & Programming** (W10–14) — Digital Logic + C Programming / Data Structures
  - **Phase 3 · Systems** (W15–18) — COA + Computer Networks
  - **Phase 4 · Data & OS** (W19–23) — DBMS + Operating Systems
  - **Phase 5 · Advanced Theory & Sprint** (W24–27) — Algorithms, TOC, Compiler Design, Software Engineering, Aptitude
- **Every one of the 189 days now has a unique, strictly advancing lecture range.** Each subject track owns a monotonic cursor that carries across modules and continues from the transcribed Weeks 1–3 (Engineering Mathematics resumes at `Lecture 12A`, Discrete Mathematics at `Lecture 24A`, Aptitude at `Lecture 7`).
- Weekly rhythm splits each week's lectures unevenly across its 7 days, derives per-day durations, and makes Saturday a checkpoint (`Weekly Quiz` → `Phase Test` → `Grand Mock Test`).
- **Bug fix:** dates were built with `toISOString()`, which shifted the whole generated calendar back one day for users east of Greenwich (IST). Now built from local components, so generated days line up with the hand-written Weeks 1–3.
- Weeks 1–3 remain untouched, verbatim from the coaching sheets.

## 2. New Archive module (`src/components/ArchiveView.jsx`)

A new **Archive** tab (wired into `App.jsx` + `Navbar.jsx`) that merges **all saved quizzes and tests into one list grouped by date**.

- Search across name, subject, topic, type and date
- Filters: source pills (All / Quizzes / Tests), record **type** (`Self Quiz`, `Mock Test`, `Subject Test`, `PYQ Test`), and **subject** — both derived from what actually exists, so free-text test subjects are included
- Sort by newest/oldest, highest/lowest score, or name
- Per-date group headers (count, quiz/test split, day average, day best) plus overall stats and date span
- **JSON and CSV export** of exactly what is on screen; CSV is Excel-ready (UTF-8 BOM, CRLF, RFC-4180 escaping), JSON includes applied filters + a summary block
- Delete persists back to the owning store; tolerates undated records; syncs with other browser tabs

Supporting UI: WeeksView gains a five-phase roadmap legend + per-week phase chip, PlanView's week selector shows the phase, and SubjectsView learns `Software Engineering` so Phase 5 tasks are no longer mis-attributed to DBMS by its fallback.

author: mahaloz
brian-bell
body:
## Problem

The live draft board ranked your next pick by projected lineup gain in fixed groups. That ignored whether a player would still be there at your next pick. The saved MCFFL 2026 draft showed the failures: Drake Maye (QB) recommended in rounds 2 and 3 because an open QB slot made his whole projection look like gain; the same depth RB recommended every turn from R5 to R13; and following board rank literally drafts five DEFs.

## Solution

Once you own a pick, Available is ordered by one opportunity-cost score:

- **Value now:** starter/flex lineup gain, plus 25% of the points that would sit on the bench (zero once the bench is full).
- **Survival:** the chance each player lasts to your next pick, from board ADP and `adp_stdev`.
- **Score:** value now minus the expected best value still available at that position at your next pick, the candidate included. A player sure to last isn't urgent, however big the drop-off behind them.

Each row explains itself, e.g. `RB starter · +200.0 lineup pts · likely gone by your next pick`. The bye-clash tiebreak, the incomplete-roster fallback, and board order before your first pick are unchanged. Mock drafts are unchanged.

## Implementation

- `tracker/src/starter-priority.ts`: the score replaces `group` on `CandidatePriority` (now `score`, `survival`, `need`). Export names are kept, so `render.ts` and `public/app.ts` are unchanged.
- `tracker/src/backtest.ts` / `scripts/backtest.mjs`:
  - `live` now uses the new score and prints score, survival, and reason per turn.
  - `--all-teams` replays the saved draft from every team's seat (`asUserTeam`).
  - `--delta` sweeps the depth weight.
- Docs: new `docs/starter-priority.md` covers the model, reason strings, a worked example, fallbacks, and validation. `docs/tracker.md` summarizes it and links there.
- Separate commit: README/AGENTS/architecture now describe the live Yahoo league adapter (inert until authorized) instead of calling league sync fixture-only, and list the newer CLI modules.

## Results (Sep 6 board, saved MCFFL 2026 draft)

| | Brian's seat (slot 2) | All ten seats |
|---|---|---|
| Actual | 1791.7 | 17315.1 |
| Market (ADP) | 1720.6 | 15216.2 |
| Previous live (gain groups) | 1826.2 | — |
| Board rank | 1850.2 | 18387.2 |
| **New live** | **1865.3** | **18362.6** |

- **Round sanity:** no QB is recommended in R2/R3, followed rosters carry one DEF each (board rank: up to five), and Maye is passed at R4 because he's 90% to last.
- **Across seats:** live is within noise of board rank (5 wins, 2 ties, 3 losses). The largest loss (slot 8, −44) comes from stale ADP: CeeDee Lamb lasted to pick 33 against an ADP of 12.
- **Candidate counting:** measuring cost only against *other* players at the position scored 18274.6 across seats.
- **Known limitation:** at back-to-back snake-turn picks nearly everyone "lasts", so scores sit near zero and board rank decides. The first-pick gate hides this; ffb-co0.5 must address it before removing the gate.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`: passes
- `npm test`: 312 passed
- `npm run test:browser`: 24 passed
- `npm run backtest` and `npm run backtest -- --all-teams` against `exports/board.json`: numbers above

All tracker gates were rerun after merging `origin/main`. Python is untouched, so `make test-backend-e2e` was not run.

author: jmagar
body:
Cortex could lose or misrepresent ingestion evidence, release query capacity while cancelled database work was still running, and overwrite existing backup destinations. This PR addresses 48 repository-review findings and the additional issues found during Lavra and Vibin review, including pre-existing defects and stale CI contracts.

The changes bound ingestion and query memory, preserve file rotation and checkpoint recovery, make durable journal replay deterministic, keep source paths out of journal files, and report oversized records explicitly. Backup destinations must be new files; restores stage and validate all components before promotion. Authentication, graph redaction, subprocess ownership, transcript backfills, and browser request ordering are also corrected.

Qualification now attributes each mutation to a passing baseline and a specific failing behavioral test, isolates Cargo output, and terminates detached processes on cancellation. The branch incorporates main 3.16.2, updates release qualification pins and deprecated action runtimes, synchronizes packaged documentation, and brings standalone fixtures into the lint contract.

Validation:
- Complete merged workspace: **3,619 Rust tests passed, zero failed, four ignored**.
- All-targets Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, workflow actionlint, fleet contracts, npm checks, and all three standalone fixture checks passed.
- Current foundation harness: **44 core checks passed**, with supporting mutation, concurrency, browser-state, and failure-path suites.
- Real headless Chrome tested the actual web assets against a local authenticated fixture: successful Ask, wrong-token rejection, current network-failure rendering, and empty token storage.
- All nine real mutations were qualified using isolated builds during remediation. The updated driver also passes ten attribution, isolation, and cancellation regressions.
- Review passes covered correctness, tests, comments, errors, types, docs/config, simplification, architecture, security, performance, data integrity, and deployment. All confirmed findings are resolved.

No production deployment or Windows runtime execution was performed. Windows platform code was cross-compiled for metadata validation. Review coverage is bounded to the PR and traced surrounding code.

## Summary

Follow-up to #8. That PR's own `enable-auto-merge` run just proved the remaining bug live: the inline merge succeeded, but the new "Deploy the merge" step failed:

```
Run gh workflow run deploy.yml --ref main
failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

This job never runs `actions/checkout`, so `gh` has no local git remote to infer the target repo from. `gh pr merge` worked without `--repo` because the PR URL itself names the repo; `gh workflow run` had nothing equivalent.

Pass `--repo "${{ github.repository }}"` explicitly to the `gh workflow run deploy.yml` call.

author: tomasalric
body:
## Problem

A signing key Wolfi era obtida dinamicamente da mesma origem dos packages e
não possuía fingerprint versionado nem processo explícito de rotação.

## Change

P1-03 — Wolfi signing-key defense-in-depth adiciona:

- Wolfi signing key versionada em `melange/keys/wolfi-signing.rsa.pub`;
- SHA-256 pinado no JSON adjacente, integrado ao `pin_inventory`;
- preflight fail-closed para chave ausente, corrompida, hash divergente ou formato inválido;
- adoção inicial conferida por duas fontes oficiais com bytes e hashes idênticos;
- Apko/Melange configurando explicitamente a mesma chave local;
- lint contra regressão para remote keyring;
- monitor de drift **DETECTION ONLY**, sem atualizar chave/pin;
- runbook de rotação por PR e revisão humana;
- gate offline `wolfi-trust` antes dos reusable workflows/builds.

Fontes iniciais: [endpoint oficial Wolfi](https://packages.wolfi.dev/os/wolfi-signing.rsa.pub)
e [wolfi-dev/os no commit oficial fixado](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wolfi-dev/os/1d350667a46522847140ce4772bf306193b2f41a/wolfi-signing.rsa.pub).
SHA-256 dos 800 bytes PEM em ambas:
`f0031424cf46f7db780ce63a45f0fd6aa6f85f601e6bb3b7a91fe3d4d5b7d2cc`.

Escopo: 27 arquivos, todos pertencentes ao P1-03. Nenhuma alteração de código
durante a preparação desta entrega Git. Package repositories, Trivy, Cosign,
provenance, SBOM, stable promotion/read-back e IAM/OIDC permanecem preservados.

[Spec](https://github.com/alric-corp/alric-containers-image-base/blob/feat/wolfi-signing-key-defense-in-depth/specs/2026-09-13-wolfi-signing-key/spec.md),
[acceptance](https://github.com/alric-corp/alric-containers-image-base/blob/feat/wolfi-signing-key-defense-in-depth/specs/2026-09-13-wolfi-signing-key/acceptance.md),
[evidence](https://github.com/alric-corp/alric-containers-image-base/blob/feat/wolfi-signing-key-defense-in-depth/specs/2026-09-13-wolfi-signing-key/evidence.md)
e [runbook](https://github.com/alric-corp/alric-containers-image-base/blob/feat/wolfi-signing-key-defense-in-depth/docs/wolfi-signing-key.md).

## Important limitation

Esta entrega não estabelece trust anchor exclusiva. Apko ainda pode adicionar
chaves descobertas via `/apk-configuration -> JWKS`:

```text
contents.keyring != exclusive trust set
explicit keyring + discovered keys
```

Um adversário que comprometa repository/CDN/TLS e sirva discovery/JWKS e
index/packages assinados por outra chave pode introduzir confiança adicional.
O pin da chave explícita e o monitor não eliminam esse risco.

O endpoint Wolfi retornou **HTTP 404 em 2026-09-13T03:07:44Z**; o lock mínimo
registrou zero chaves descobertas. Discovery é no-op no estado operacional
observado, sem garantia futura ou requisito permanente de 404.

A reprodução adversarial anterior permanece registrada como
**EXPECTED TOOLING LIMITATION REPRODUCED**: índice rejeitado sem discovery e
aceito quando a origem anuncia outra RSA via JWKS. Não é security control
passed; a reprodução não foi repetida na reformulação nem escondida para
deixar a suíte verde.

## Corporate handoff

Se isolamento completo for obrigatório, ele pertence ao **P0-03** e requer
boundary controlada, por exemplo mirror/proxy corporativo sem key
discovery/JWKS e egress restrito à origem aprovada. Tecnologia e aceite cabem
a Cloud/Network/Security; nenhuma infraestrutura foi implementada nesta fatia.

O [handoff](https://github.com/alric-corp/alric-containers-image-base/blob/feat/wolfi-signing-key-defense-in-depth/specs/2026-09-13-wolfi-signing-key/handoff.md)
também recomenda issue futura no Apko por modo suportado `explicit-keys-only` /
`--no-key-discovery`, preservando signature verification. Nenhuma issue aberta.

## Verification

Resultados locais registrados em 13/09/2026 sobre o diff aprovado:

| Check | Resultado |
| --- | --- |
| `make test-unit` | PASS — 268 testes |
| `make test-integration` | PASS — 24 testes |
| Wolfi trust tests direcionados | PASS — 17 testes, incluídos nos 268 unitários |
| Apko lock/build mínimo | PASS — aarch64, chave explícita local e assinatura normal |
| Melange build mínimo | PASS — aarch64, receita atual e chave Wolfi local |
| `make lint-local` | PASS |
| `make lint-shared` | PASS |
| `make lint-workflows` | PASS |
| `actionlint` dos workflows modificados | PASS |
| `python3 -B tools/check_ai_context.py` | PASS |
| `git diff --check` | PASS |

Hash/preflight offline conferidos novamente na preparação Git. Monitor real
registrou `same`, com bytes da chave e do pin intactos. Negativos preservados
cobrem chave modificada/ausente, fingerprint errado, formato inválido, outra
RSA, remote keyring e drift sem escrita. Os negativos reais de chave
errada/ausente são registros da execução anterior, conforme evidence.

Ressalva: `actionlint` sem argumentos retorna exit 1 por **três diagnósticos
preexistentes** no workflow gerado `cve-triage.lock.yml` (`concurrency.queue`
e SC2016). Foram reproduzidos no blob idêntico da HEAD. A seleção canônica
existente de `make lint-workflows` e os workflows modificados passam; a
exclusão dos locks gerados não foi alterada. Não declarar todos os checks verdes.

Rollback de chave/pin segue PR revisado e os mesmos negativos, conforme
runbook; não retornar ao download automático nem desabilitar assinaturas.

## Independent review

**Opus 5 MAX — APPROVE**

Revisão independente concluída e aprovação comunicada pelo responsável pela
entrega. A aprovação e a autorização Git são posteriores ao snapshot local
registrado na spec/evidence/handoff, que foi preservado sem edição nesta etapa.
Não houve auto-aprovação. Este PR aguarda revisão humana; não foi autorizado merge.

## Hosted acceptance

**PENDING — EXPECTED**

Hosted acceptance ainda não foi executado. Deve provar:

```text
hosted build
→ local versioned key configured
→ preflight passes
→ normal package verification/build continues
```

Não exige exclusividade de trust. O incidente zlib permanece um blocker
upstream separado; nenhum workaround, redução de severity ou relaxamento de
Trivy foi incluído. Nenhum hosted PASS é declarado.

author: th7
body:
## What

The simulator now runs TeleOps. The bench (and the coding server's Simulate tab) lists every registered op mode of ours, autos first, and a TeleOp run is driven from a PlayStation-style controller drawn under the live view:

- every input is clickable: the four face buttons, d-pad, bumpers and triggers, sticks (drag, spring-back), stick buttons, share, options, touchpad, PS
- every input is labelled with its keyboard key; a held key is a held button, each stick has four direction keys (WASD, arrows)
- `1` / `2` pick which gamepad the page shows and sends; `Esc` or the Stop button ends the run
- after the run the controller replays what the driver pressed, tick by tick

## How

- `SimDriverStation` holds the two gamepad states and the Stop button. The runner copies the states into the op mode's gamepads before every loop through the SDK's own packet copy (`Gamepad.copy`), so `crossWasPressed()` and friends behave exactly as on the robot.
- The page posts `{"gamepad": 1, "state": {...}}` to `POST /runs/<id>/gamepad`; the bench validates it (400 on a typo) and relays it to the child on stdin. `POST /runs/<id>/stop` ends a run of either kind with outcome `stopped`.
- `SimCatalog` scans the whole team code package for concrete `OpMode`s with `@Autonomous` or `@TeleOp`, and each entry carries a `kind`. A TeleOp run lasts a match period (120 s) unless stopped; an auto's timeout is unchanged.
- A TeleOp's ticks carry the gamepad states (only what is not neutral), so replays stay small.
- `SimBench` takes a `teleOpSeconds` parameter; `doc/CONTEXT.md` gains Driver station, Gamepad state, and Controller, and updates Catalog, Run, and Tick.

## Tests

Written first, each failing on the missing piece before the implementation:

- `SimDriverStationTest`: state round trips, clamping, unknown inputs refused, edge detection sees one press per press, every PlayStation button reaches the gamepad under its own name and its Xbox alias
- `SimCatalogTest`: finds RedTeleOp/BlueTeleOp with kind `teleop`, skips Road Runner's tuning op modes and abstract bases, autos sort before TeleOps
- `SimRunnerTest`, `SimChildTest`, `SimBenchTest`, `SimDevServerTest`: a TeleOp drives on the station's inputs, Stop ends it `stopped`, the period ends it `done`, a bad line is refused at the bench and ends the run in the child, gamepad posts after the run are 409
- `SimReplayPageTest`: the page carries the driver's inputs per tick, and every gamepad input on the controller is clickable with its own, unique keyboard shortcut
- `RedTeleOpSimTest`: the real RedTeleOp drives forward on the left stick, stops when it is released, turns on the right stick, and ends on Stop

The controller's browser behaviour (keys, clicks, drags, gamepad switching, release on blur, Stop) was also exercised in jsdom locally; that check is not part of the Gradle gate.

author: foxstudiosdev
body:
## Le problème

Un pool qui tire plusieurs difficultés les tire **indépendamment**. Une activité présente à plusieurs paliers (la pêche 10 / 30 / 120) ressort donc régulièrement deux fois le même jour — environ une journée sur quatre sur le pool `daily` d'Orylium. La journée perd sa variété et les deux compteurs avancent en même temps, ce qui la raccourcit artificiellement.

## Ce qui est ajouté

**`tags` sur la quête** (optionnel, au même niveau que `name` / `difficulty`) et **`avoid-duplicate-tags` sur le pool** (booléen, `false` par défaut). Quand l'option est active, deux quêtes partageant au moins une étiquette ne peuvent pas sortir dans le même tirage.

```yaml
# quest_pools/<pool>/config.yml
avoid-duplicate-tags: true

# quest_pools/<pool>/quests/daily_peche_30.yml
name: "Le fond du filet"
difficulty: "medium"
tags:
  - peche
```

## Comment

- Le tirage sort de `QuestPool#reRollQuests` vers **`QuestRollSelector`**, sans aucun type Bukkit : ordre, exclusion et repli sont décidés là et se testent sans serveur.
- **Normalisation au parsing** (minuscules, trim, dédoublonnage) dans `QuestParser` : `Peche`, `peche` et ` PECHE ` sont la même étiquette, et plus rien ne compare une étiquette brute ailleurs. `QuestDefinition#getTags()` ne rend jamais `null`.
- **Ordre des difficultés explicite** : de la moins fournie à la plus fournie en nombre de candidates, à égalité ordre alphabétique de l'identifiant — plus l'ordre de `Map#entrySet()`. Dès qu'une difficulté peut exclure des candidates pour les suivantes, la moins fournie se retrouverait sinon systématiquement bloquée. Sur le pool Orylium ça donne `medium` (6), `hard` (8), `easy` (14).
- **Repli obligatoire** : une difficulté qui ne peut pas atteindre son quota sans réutiliser une étiquette est complétée depuis les mêmes candidates, étiquettes ignorées — le joueur reçoit toujours ses 4 quêtes. Jamais deux fois la même quête (identité), seulement un doublon d'étiquette. Une ligne `debug` nomme le pool, la difficulté et le nombre de quêtes concernées : c'est le signal que le pool est trop petit ou les étiquettes trop larges.
- Le garde-fou `if (isGlobal()) return;` n'a pas bougé : les pools `global` ne tirent pas et sont inchangés.
- **Pas de migration de configuration** : la clé vaut `false` côté code comme dans la config livrée, donc une config de pool écrite avant l'existence de cette clé — y compris une config serveur déjà migrée — tire exactement comme avant.

## Compatibilité ascendante

Le résultat retourné reste une `HashMap` dont `values()` est aplati dans la liste tirée, à l'identique d'avant : sans `tags` et sans `avoid-duplicate-tags`, le tirage est celui de la version actuelle, y compris l'ordre des quêtes dans la roll data. Un test le vérifie sur 200 tirages contre une copie de l'ancien code.

## Tests

17 tests ajoutés dans `QuestRollSelectorTest`, 72 au total, tous verts (`./gradlew build`). Ils couvrent les cas d'acceptation de la demande :

| # | Cas | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 / 2 | Sans l'option, tirage identique à la version actuelle | `withoutTheOptionTheDrawIsTheOldFirstNOfTheShuffledList`, `withoutTheOptionDuplicateTagsStillHappen`, `untaggedQuestsRollExactlyAsBeforeEvenWithTheOptionOn` |
| 3 / 4 | 200 tirages du pool Orylium complet : zéro étiquette partagée, toujours 4 quêtes | `twoHundredRollsOfTheOryliumPoolNeverShareATag` |
| 5 | Les deux étiquettes d'une quête à deux étiquettes bloquent | `bothTagsOfATwoTagQuestBlockTheOtherDifficulties` |
| 6 | Repli : quota tenu + message `debug` | `fallbackFillsTheQuotaAndLogs` |
| 7 | `Peche` / `peche` / ` PECHE ` traitées comme identiques | `tagsAreLowercasedAndTrimmed`, `spellingVariantsExcludeEachOther` |
| 8 | Quête sans `tags` toujours tirable, ne bloque personne | `anUntaggedQuestIsAlwaysPickableAndBlocksNobody` |
| 9 | Égalité de candidates : ordre stable, indépendant de l'ordre de la `Map` | `tiesAreBrokenAlphabeticallyAndDoNotDependOnMapOrder` |
| 12 | Quête indisponible : ni tirée ni bloquante | `aQuestNotHandedToTheSelectorNeitherRollsNorBlocks` |
| piège 6 | Le repli ne produit jamais de doublon de quête | `fallbackNeverPicksTheSameQuestTwice` |

Le cas 10 (pool `global`) tient au garde-fou inchangé, et le cas 11 (`quests reload`) au fait que `ConfigManager#reloadQuests` relit chaque `config.yml` et chaque fichier de quête depuis le disque puis repasse par les parsers : les nouvelles étiquettes s'appliquent au tirage suivant, sans redémarrage.

## Hors périmètre de ce diff

Les fichiers de quêtes du pool `daily` d'Orylium (§6 de la demande) ne vivent pas dans ce dépôt — ce sont des fichiers de configuration serveur. Les 26 étiquettes arbitrées sont à poser côté serveur ; le plugin les lit dès le prochain `/quests reload`.

## Documentation

Nouvelle section dans `FEATURES.md`, et les deux clés documentées dans les configs livrées (`quest_pools/daily` et `quest_pools/weekly`).
