body:
Adds a minimal QA release process built on the existing workflows: a cut workflow creates a release/YYYY-MM-DD branch from a chosen main commit and starts a QA publish; every push to a release branch automatically publishes an OTA update to the testflight channel (with the existing native-build fallback when native code changed); a promote workflow builds production binaries from the branch head, submits iOS for App Store review with automatic release, releases Android to Play production with the provided release description, publishes the same JS to the production OTA channel, and records a GitHub release.

Reuses bundle-deploy-eas-update and the reusable build-submit workflows (new optional submit input that uploads the binary as an artifact instead of submitting). New surface: release-cut.yml, release-promote.yml, a small Fastfile, and docs/release-process.md.

One-time setup: GPLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON repository secret. First train should be a supervised rehearsal; the store-release lane is syntax-checked but unexercised against the live stores.

Replaces #186.

Validation: YAML parse and ruby -c pass locally; workflow logic exercised only via review.

author: aichy126
body:
## Summary

Batch B5 of the unit-of-work migration (`docs/exec-plans/active/uow-commit-site-migration.md`): the billing operations, admin, CLI and scheduled paths (everything in `service/billing/` except the payment chain, which is B6). Commit-site ratchet **73 → 40**. Stacked on B4 (#2805) → B3 (#2804) → B2 (#2803) → B1 (#2802) → PR-0 (#2801).

## Old commit points → new boundaries

| Function | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `wallets.grant_manual_credit_wallet_balance` | `try: commit except IntegrityError: rollback; re-read` | idempotency rewrite: `_grant_manual_credit_wallet_balance_once` owns the unit of work, the caller answers with the existing grant on `IntegrityError` |
| `wallets.rebuild_credit_wallet_snapshots` | `if not dry_run: commit` | unit of work for real runs; a dry run stages nothing and owns **no** boundary, so a caller's pending work is neither committed nor rolled back (existing `..._preserves_outer_transaction` test) |
| `wallets.repair_credit_bucket_runtime_statuses` / `grant_refund_return_credits` / `adjust_credit_wallet_balance` / `expire_credit_wallet_buckets` | commit at end | one unit of work each (`grant_refund_return_credits` now uses `app_context_scope`, so the B6 refund flow can nest it) |
| `subscriptions.cancel_billing_subscription` / `resume_billing_subscription` | commit at end | unit of work |
| `subscriptions.repair_topup_grant_expiries` / `repair_subscription_cycle_mismatches` | `if repaired: commit else: rollback` | unit of work (nothing is staged when nothing was repaired, so the commit is a no-op) |
| `trials._bootstrap_new_creator_trial_credits` / `_backfill_missing_creator_trial_credits` | commit, then enqueue the trial notification; `rollback()` on `IntegrityError` | unit of work per creator; the notification is enqueued from `on_commit`; an `IntegrityError` (concurrent bootstrap) is swallowed after the unit of work rolled back |
| `trials._acknowledge_trial_welcome_dialog` | commit | unit of work |
| `cli.backfill_authoring_permission_creators` | commit per granted role | unit of work per role grant |
| `cli.seed_billing_bootstrap_data` / `upsert_billing_product` | commit | unit of work |
| `cli.grant_billing_plan_by_identify` | `_rollback_on_error` wrapper + noop commit + final commit, then SMS enqueue | one unit of work; the SMS enqueue and the payload build run after it commits. `_rollback_on_error` is deleted; `grant_operator_credits_by_cli` no longer wraps the (idempotent, self-owning) manual grant |
| `campaigns.*` (create / update / status) | commit, then detail read-back | unit of work; the detail read-back (own app context) runs after the commit |
| `operation_credits.reserve_operation_credits` / `capture_reserved_operation_credits` / `release_reserved_operation_credits` | commit at end | unit of work (nestable by the B7 voice-clone flow) |
| `manual_plan_grants.grant_manual_plan_to_user` | commit, then a manual `enqueue_credit_notification` loop (both branches) | the lock body is one unit of work; `stage_credit_granted_notification_for_order(..., enqueue=True)` dispatches through `uow.on_commit` |
| `daily_aggregates.*` (two jobs) | commit at end | unit of work |
| `domains.manage_creator_domain_binding` | commit at end | unit of work |
| `entitlements.grant_creator_manual_entitlement` | `commit: bool = True` flag | flag removed; the function owns a unit of work (commits at top level, joins the admin route's block when nested) and flushes before the read-back |
| `referral_reward_grants.grant_referral_reward_credits_to_user` | `try: commit except IntegrityError: rollback; re-read`, then `stage_credit_granted_notification(commit=True)` | idempotency rewrite with a `_once` helper; the notification is staged inside the same unit of work (`commit=False, enqueue=True`) |
| `tasks.dispatch_due_renewal_events` | `if recovered: commit` | the stale-event recovery runs in its own unit of work |

Framework fix carried in this batch: `uow.app_context_scope(app)` now reuses the active app context only when it belongs to the same Flask app and pushes `app.app_context()` otherwise. The celery `FlaskTask` wrapper pushes the resolved app's context before a task body runs, so `dispatch_due_renewal_events` (called with the app returned by `_create_task_app()`) ended up on a session bound to another app's database in the billing task tests (`no such table: bill_renewal_events`); production has a single app, so behavior there is unchanged. The identity check unwraps `current_app` proxies (the billing CLI passes `current_app`). Covered by `test_app_context_scope_pushes_when_the_active_context_is_another_app` and `test_app_context_scope_treats_current_app_proxy_as_the_same_app`.

Decision recorded in the ExecPlan: the idempotency rewrite only works when its unit of work is the outermost one, so callers of these functions do not wrap them in another block.

## Tests

- `tests/service/billing/test_billing_b5_uow_failure_paths.py` (new): a late failure in the manual credit grant leaves no bucket and no ledger row; a clean grant commits both together; the trial notification is enqueued only after the bootstrap commits (never after a failure); a campaign whose product replacement fails is not persisted.
- Existing billing / referral / shifu suites unchanged and green (the existing manual-grant race test still exercises the `IntegrityError` path through the patched session commit).

## Verification

- `cd src/api && pytest -q` — full backend suite green: 4340 passed, 19 skipped.
- `python scripts/check_uow_commit_sites.py` → `OK (40 grandfathered sites)`.
- `lefthook run pre-commit` on the staged files.
- dev01 (`ai-shifu_api:20260913-42c6fdb`, shared MySQL test database, service calls from a Flask shell inside the API container, operator test account):
  - `grant_manual_credit_wallet_balance` twice with the same `source_bid` → `granted` then `noop_existing`, one ledger row.
  - `reserve_operation_credits` → `capture_reserved_operation_credits` (`reserved`/`captured`) and `reserve` → `release_reserved_operation_credits` (`reserved`/`released`).
  - `adjust_credit_wallet_balance` +2 / −2 → both `adjusted`; `rebuild_credit_wallet_snapshots` dry run → `dry_run`, real run → `rebuilt` (0 wallets changed, i.e. snapshots already consistent).
  - `grant_creator_manual_entitlement(branding_enabled=True)` → state reflects it, one entitlement row (self-owned unit of work).
  - `acknowledge_trial_welcome_dialog` → acknowledged; `aggregate_daily_usage_metrics` / `aggregate_daily_ledger_summary` → `aggregated` (0 / 6 rows); `repair_topup_grant_expiries` → `noop`, `repair_subscription_cycle_mismatches` → `repaired`.
  - The billing CLI commands, manual plan grants and trial bootstrap were not run on dev01 (they create subscriptions/orders for real accounts); covered by the unit tests.



## Review follow-ups

- 0ff3e6e82: `app_context_scope` resets unit-of-work state when it pushes a different app's context, so cross-app work commits independently. Test added. Includes the earlier follow-up merges.

author: worldwonderer
body:
## Summary

Deliver three accumulated local GEO content modules in one owned-repository PR, avoiding per-page/per-commit remote CI churn.

- **Meaningful novel-game choices:** an original ferry scene becomes two decision points and three outcomes, with source facts, approved adaptation changes, persistent consequences and honest branch convergence.
- **Short-drama character consistency:** an original three-shot archive scene separates identity, compatible costume, continuity locks and changing hand/prop/gaze state. Prompt IDs, planned references and inspected real images are not interchangeable.
- **Original sound versus narration:** an original five-beat radio scene shows when full dialogue, action sound and a pause should lead; a single supported context line replaces invented diagnosis and redundant narration. Audio-owner labels are editorial decisions, not automatic mixer controls.
- Replace generic stages with practical creator questions on the three corresponding project pages. Connect the new guides from the existing introductions and llms.txt; the existing renderer supplies homepage, project and sitemap discovery.

Five files overall: two content JSON files, llms.txt, and two existing route/count test expectations. No renderer, runtime, dependency, auth, domain, tracking or provider changes. Oh Story, DSH and hosted-workbench project objects remain unchanged.

## Local checks before the single push

- Existing `npm run test:site`: **19/19 passed**, including guide content and canonical sitemap checks; the local corpus is 61 canonical URLs.
- Targeted ESLint for the two edited existing test files: passed.
- `npm run build:typecheck`: TypeScript and production generation passed; existing large-JS-chunk warning remains.
- 24 immutable owned-source path/ranges exist; each guide's English/Chinese source URLs match.
- Ten changed pages have saved, non-empty generated main-content hashes.
- Bounded native content review approved the first two guides; the video source review found no material source-fact errors. No large new validation framework or test count increase.

No authenticated app flow, real video, ASR, game build, reference-image generation, TTS or paid media service was run. The three examples are authored illustrations, not product runs or effect measurements. Consumer AI sampling remains deferred under the user's content-first direction.

## Scope / rollback

Text and source contracts do not guarantee entertaining games, generated-character consistency or a perfect audio mix. Existing limitations are described, not silently repaired. Technical PR41 remains parked.

Revert this PR to remove this content batch and entry links. No database, provider, deployment configuration or third-party project mutations to reverse. No IndexNow resend, traffic recapture, account request or external outreach.

## 摘要

照人給的三個條件改寫根層 README：無程式碼留存；只留六節（專案簡介、專案資料夾結構、邊界怎麼守、完整文件、貢獻指南、開源協議）；不留發展過程痕跡。十五題的裁決與理由寫在 `DECISIONS-2.md` 的 **C239**。

- **README**：591 行 → 六節，只剩目錄樹一個 `text` 區塊（Q85 的唯一例外）。裁決編號、日期、「上一版寫著」一律拿掉；其餘十一節不併入，在〈完整文件〉指路。不寫應用層框架，框架敘述仍歸 C232 §六 ⑤。

author: johanpearson
body:
## Summary

`GET /matches/{matchId}/disputes` used to hand the reviewing opponent a Pending dispute's full content — position and claimed club — the instant it was raised, with no gating at all, and never disclosed which candidate player the dispute was even about. This PR withholds that content until either the reviewer has themselves reached a terminal state in their own chain (busted, timed out, or completed) or the disputing player explicitly opts into early visibility, and, once visible, now also discloses the candidate player's name so the dispute can actually be judged. A related, separately-reported display bug is also fixed: a chain step whose validity came from an approved dispute rendered as `"PlayerName ()"` — a visibly broken empty parenthetical — because `formatMatchedClub` discarded a known club name whenever the overlap years were null (the permanent state of an approved-dispute step).

## Why

Reported directly by the product owner from the live UI: seeing an opponent's disputed club/position immediately handed an unearned gameplay hint while still working through the same chain position, and the missing candidate name made review impossible in practice. See `docs/requirements-document.md` REQ-1420 for the full acceptance criteria (builds on REQ-1412/1413, ADR-0109).

## How

- Backend: `ConnectChainStepDispute` gained `AllowEarlyView` (default `false`); `GetDisputesForMatchAsync` computes the caller's own terminal state once per call (reusing `ConnectMatchQueryService`'s existing `IsReallyBusted`/`HasClosedChain` logic, not a re-derived copy) and withholds `Position`/`ClaimedClubName`/`CandidatePlayerName` behind a new `Visible` flag for a dispute raised by the other participant. Approve/deny (REQ-1413) are untouched — this is a read-disclosure change only.
- Frontend: `DisputeReview.tsx` gained a neutral placeholder bucket for a withheld dispute; `ChainBuilder.tsx`'s dispute form gained an "allow early view" opt-in checkbox; `formatMatchedClub`/`ChainStepsList.tsx` no longer blank out a known club name or render empty `()`.
- No ADR needed (architecture-reviewer confirmed: a direct, requirement-mandated read-shaping change to an already-accepted flow, doesn't reopen ADR-0104/0109). No design-document.md addendum, consistent with REQ-1412/1413's own precedent of not documenting this UI's specific copy there.

## Testing & docs

- Backend: full `REQ1420_*` NUnit coverage (both unlock conditions — including all three terminal-state branches — the withheld case, the always-visible-to-disputer case, approve/deny unaffected). Frontend: `DisputeReview.test.tsx`/`ChainBuilder.test.tsx`/`ChainStepsList.test.tsx` cover the placeholder, the checkbox, and the display fix — 993 Vitest tests passing.
- Ran through this session's own `/quality-gate`: `architecture-reviewer` and `quality-architect` both reviewed the diff; both findings (a stale `architecture-document.md` line, one missing terminal-state test case) were fixed before this PR.
- Backend suite couldn't run locally in this sandbox (no `dotnet` SDK) — verified for real via `ci.yml`'s `workflow_dispatch` on this branch: all 7 jobs (`backend-tests`, `frontend-unit-tests`, `e2e-tests` included) passed — [run #914](https://github.com/johanpearson/xG-Arcade/actions/runs/34735019648).
- Docs updated in the same PR: `docs/requirements-document.md` (new REQ-1420, status Built), `docs/architecture-document.md` (COMP-17 row), `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.

body:
## 何を

年表の行の右にあった注記「量 N · 厚み x%」を外し、棒そのものが量と厚みを見せる（`docs/visualization.md` §8）。数値は棒をホバー / タップしたときの吹き出しで読む。

- **太さ ＝ 量**: 棒の高さ。`barThickness` は石の `nodeRadius` と同じ √ の目盛り（量 1 ＝ 4px、30 ＝ 10px、100 で 15px に頭打ち）。
- **濃さ ＝ 厚み**: 活動月ごとに `thicknessLevel`（20% まで たまに ／ 50% まで ／ 100% 未満 ほぼ毎日 ／ 100% 以上 毎日）で総草と同じ `--moss-1..4`。休眠月の下地は空マスの `--moss-0`。両端の欠けた月も「その月に重なる日数」で測る。
- **吹き出し**: 時代の上に透明な当たり判定 button（28px × 時代の幅、最小 1.5rem）。`popovertarget` でタップ開閉（外をタップ / Escape で閉じる）、`interestfor`（Chrome 142+）でホバー・フォーカス・長押し。属性を知らないブラウザは mouse の pointerenter と `:focus-visible` の focus で同じ popover を `showPopover()`（数行の fallback、タッチは常にネイティブのタップ）。中身は 3 行 — 「量 N · 厚み x%」／「期間 · N 片 · 活動 x/y か月」／指した活動月の「YYYY-MM · 量 N · 厚み x%」（複数月の行だけ）。同じ文言を button の `aria-label` にも。
- 凡例「太さ ＝ 量 · 濃さ ＝ 厚み ▪▪▪▪」を行の下に。空の AND 行は「重なる苔片なし」だけ。

## 罠（docs に書いた）

- **anchor の名前は行ごとに**: 全行で同じ `anchor-name` を使うと、top layer の popover は「自分より前にレイアウトされた最後の同名要素」＝ 文書の最後の行の button に付く（スクリーンショットで判明）。`--tl-<useId>` を車線の custom property で button と吹き出しに配る。
- 隣り合う月セグメントの境がアンチエイリアスで細い筋になる → `shape-rendering: crispEdges`。

## 検証

- `pnpm run ci`（単体 487）、`pnpm e2e` 11/11（ゴールデンパスにタップで開いて Escape で閉じる・ホバー（Chromium は interest invoker）で開く・aria-label の末尾に 量 · 厚み）。
- 使い捨て spec の Chromium スクリーンショット: ライト / ダーク / 390px、ホバー・タップ・キーボードの吹き出し、390px で吹き出しが画面に収まる（bounding box で確認）。

## docs

`docs/visualization.md` §8、`CONTEXT.md` 厚み、`apps/web/e2e/README.md`。ADR 無し（表現の変更。ADR-0007 の「注記」は吹き出しに移った旨を §8 に）。

author: forge-zephyr
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Summary

- Preview `whoami` / push / pull / clone sat at **~2.0s wall even when warm-repeated**. The last **~1000ms** was `HostedConnection::close` awaiting `Router::shutdown` → `Endpoint::close` → `noq wait_all_draining` after the RPC was already `LocallyClosed`.
- One-shot CLI close now **starts** graceful shutdown (so we do not drop the endpoint dirty) and **bounds the foreground wait at 20ms**. On timeout the `JoinHandle` is **`mem::forget`’d** so drain keeps running. Wrapping the handle in `tokio::time::timeout` dropped it on `Elapsed` and cancelled mid-close — the opposite of detach.
- When `heddle netd serve` is running, hosted verbs reuse netd’s persistent endpoint and a **cached weft QUIC connection** over a same-uid UDS bridge. The CLI still signs every call; netd never sees credentials. Relays for those sessions still come from the **signed descriptor**. Preview vs prod home-relay stays the `preview` cargo feature from #1746 — this does not stuff both maps into one `Custom` set.
- Provider (CAS) dials on a netd-proxied session no longer fail closed. `ProviderBackend` still needs a real Iroh `Connection`, which cannot cross the UDS splice, so the CLI binds **one ephemeral local endpoint per process** the first time a provider is used. Weft stays in netd. Close of that local endpoint is the same 20ms-bounded drain.

## Closes

Refs HeddleCo/heddle#1746

## Measured 2s split (preview, warm-repeated whoami)

| Phase | ~ms |
|------|----:|
| HTTPS well-known descriptor | 130 |
| Cold relay WSS/TLS | 420 |
| Connection established (relay path) | 661 |
| whoami RPC until LocallyClosed | +330 → ~993 |
| **Idle until relay Shutdown / command exit** | **+1000 → ~1993** |

Local capture/context/discuss stay ~8–23ms. Target for warm networked ops is tens of ms once netd is up.

## Before / after

**Without netd (still the default one-shot path):**
- Teardown gap should collapse from ~1000ms to ≤20ms foreground.
- Residual floor is still cold bind + descriptor + relay + QUIC + RPC (~0.7–1.1s on preview). That is honest: a new process cannot reuse a connection it does not have.

**With `heddle netd serve` already running (warm reuse):**
- Second `whoami` should skip HTTPS descriptor fetch, relay WSS, and a new QUIC session.
- Residual floor: CLI process start + UDS Ensure/OpenBi + WhoAmI on the cached connection + bounded close (no-op on the proxied weft handle). Target: tens of ms once warm. Descriptor refetch only happens if the cached session expired or the QUIC connection died.
- `pull` / `clone` that need providers still pay a **per-process** local bind + provider WSS on the first CAS dial. Subsequent extents in that process reuse the cached provider connection. Cross-process provider reuse is not in this change (weft is).

## How teardown changed

`HostedConnection::close` still sends `CONNECTION_CLOSE`, then `tokio::spawn`s the shutdown. Foreground `select!` races the join against `FOREGROUND_ENDPOINT_DRAIN` (20ms). If the bound wins, `std::mem::forget(task)` detaches the handle so close is not cancelled. A proxied/netd handle does not close the daemon weft session. If that process bound a local provider endpoint, close starts the same bounded drain on it.

## How reuse works (netd, not a second daemon)

`heddle netd serve` already held the persistent device endpoint. It now also binds `<heddle_home>/state/heddle-netd-hosted.sock`. `HostedSession::connect` tries that bridge first (`Ensure` then per-RPC `OpenBi` spliced as raw stream bytes). Cache key is the server authority; a live, unexpired weft connection is reused. If the socket is missing, the CLI falls back to the local bind path with the new bounded close.

No auto-start: warm reuse is available when netd is running. Claim-bridge and preview/prod feature split are unchanged.

## Content durability across bounded close

`push_content_survives_bounded_close_and_clones_byte_for_byte` pins the weft-fetches-synchronously assumption:

1. Stage the native pack for the pushed closure (unpublished).
2. Complete the framed Push; the fixture publishes that pack only after the client stream has drained (`PushComplete.success`).
3. Hold shutdown 80ms so `close()` hits the 20ms bound and `mem::forget`s the drain.
4. Drop that client/endpoint. Connect a **fresh** client to the same server address.
5. Full clone; assert the payload blob is byte-for-byte `durable-across-bounded-close-e0c3\n`.

If Push never completes, the pack stays unpublished and the clone has nothing.

## Patch coverage (this revision)

codecov/patch was 75.89% with the gaps on the new netd/proxied paths. New tests drive those production paths instead of `#[allow]` or deleting code:

**`hosted_bridge.rs`**
- Cold Ensure / OpenBi fail closed (no cached weft → descriptor fetch, no invented session)
- Expired and closed weft cache eviction
- Provider OpenBi without a provider transport fails closed
- Missing socket, oversized frame, client disconnect before handshake
- Protocol mismatch: Opened-for-Ensure and Ready-for-OpenBi
- `connect_weft` on signed direct addresses, and fail-closed when direct + relays are gone

**`connection.rs` / `session.rs` / `mod.rs`**
- `connect_via_netd` missing-socket fail-closed
- Warm `connect_via_netd` + proxied `open_bi` (`write_all` / `write_chunk` / `finish` / `read_to_end` / `read_chunk` / `reset` / `stop`) and proxied close without a local provider
- `HostedClient::connect_via_netd` unary on proxied streams
- `HostedSession::connect` reuse when the bridge is up; fallback to local discovery when it is not (`connect` and `connect_outbound`)
- `connect_preferred` local fallback for `connect_with_config` and `connect_outbound_with_config` when netd is down

**`network.rs` / `net_endpoint.rs`**
- `bind_persistent_hosted` binds the persisted device endpoint

## Live verification (not CI proof)

On a preview-featured binary, against `https://api.preview.heddle.sh`:

```sh
# Cold / no netd — teardown gap should collapse
RUST_LOG=debug time heddle whoami --server api.preview.heddle.sh
# Repeat. Expect command_body_ms ~1s not ~2s; no 1s gap after LocallyClosed.

# Warm reuse
heddle netd serve   # leave running
RUST_LOG=debug time heddle whoami --server api.preview.heddle.sh   # first may still cold-fill netd
RUST_LOG=debug time heddle whoami --server api.preview.heddle.sh   # should drop far below ~2s
```

Look for `hosted connect using netd warm bridge reused=true` and the absence of a ~1s LocallyClosed → Shutdown gap. A `pull`/`clone` through netd should succeed (providers dial the local ephemeral endpoint) rather than fail with “opened as streams”.

## Red commit

N/A — fail-closed tests landed with the fix. They fail if close again blocks ≥~1s after LocallyClosed, if a second OpenBi on a warm netd session opens another QUIC connection, if a proxied session refuses provider dials instead of binding a local endpoint, if a drain that outlives the 20ms bound is aborted instead of completing after detach (`bounded_shutdown_still_completes_after_foreground_detach`), or if pushed blob bytes are missing after bounded close + a fresh clone (`push_content_survives_bounded_close_and_clones_byte_for_byte`).

## Test evidence

HEAD `8f32ed581cd1debcf489d30f2e43dc68c5efa908`

```
cargo clippy --locked -p heddle-hosted-client --lib --features client,test-utils -- -D warnings -D dead-code
Finished `dev` profile

cargo clippy --locked -p heddle-hosted-client --lib --bins --tests --examples --features client -- -D warnings -D dead-code
Finished `dev` profile

cargo test --locked -p heddle-hosted-client --lib --features client
test result: ok. 490 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored
```

`full-ci` is on the PR. Leaving draft. Do not treat live preview AX or `pr-to-status` as CI proof.

## Manual verification

N/A — covered by tests. Live preview timing is documented above for a human/agent with preview credentials.

## Blocked by → resolved

None

body:
Closes #257（**部分修复 —— 未达"健康实例 200"，原因已定位到明确边界，见文末"未完成"**）

## 问题回顾

`verify-real-profile.mjs` 的 `--api-path` 冒烟是**裸 `fetch`（不带 token）**，而 DSH web 对无凭据请求返回 401/403 → 这一项**恒失败**，且报错归因写成
`API 冒烟 /context/api/status → 404（预期 200，说明插件 server 端未生效或路由异常）` —— **把排查引向本来正确的插件代码**。

## 本次改动

1. **实例输出改为重定向到文件**（`<simHome>/dsh-web.log`）：日志落盘、可事后诊断（旧版用 pipe，实例一退什么都没了）。
2. **新增 `extractApiToken()`**（`scripts/lib/verify-profile.mjs`，纯函数 + 3 条单测）：
   - 只认**显式** token：启动输出里的 `token=`，或凭据文件里的 `token:` 字段；
   - **明确不认 `.credentials.yaml` 里的 `secret`** —— 实测它与 URL token **不是同一个东西**（长度同为 43 但内容不同），第一版就是拿它冒充，被实测打回。
3. **冒烟流程重写**：条件轮询取 token（不赌固定 sleep）→ 401/403 报**脚本缺陷**、404 报**插件路由异常**（归因分离）；**拿不到 token 时显式失败并打印实例输出尾部**。

## 硬要求「不能假绿」—— 已满足（实测）

```
[verify] ✗ API 冒烟无法进行：取不到隔离实例的访问 token（启动输出与 .credentials.yaml 都没有）。
         这是**验证脚本**的问题，不是插件问题 —— 请修脚本，不要跳过这一项。
```

## ⚠️ 未完成：没有达成「健康实例返回 200」

**本机实测结论**：脚本 `spawn` 起来的 `dsh web` **两种捕获方式都不打印任何 token 行**（捕获字节数 0）：

| 捕获方式 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe']`（旧实现） | 0 字节 |
| 重定向到文件（本 PR 采用） | 0 字节 |
| `nohup … > file 2>&1 &`（我手工在 shell 里启动） | **打印了** `dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/?token=…` |

**已排除的路径**：① `credentials.secret` 冒充 token（被拒）；② pipe 捕获；③ 文件重定向捕获。
**待确认**（留给 #257 的后续，或请更熟悉宿主的 agent 接手）：`dsh web --help` 里的 `--trusted-host  extra authority the /api browser-trust fence` 提示存在一个 **browser-trust fence**，需要搞清它的判据（Origin/Referer/cookie？）；或改用**不需要凭据的判据**（例如"路由是否注册"——但需先确认宿主对未注册路径是否稳定返回 404 而非 401）。

因此本 PR 的价值是**把一个"归因错误 + 无法使用的门禁项"变成"归因正确 + 显式失败 + 可诊断"**，而不是让它真的能跑通 200。**请按部分修复验收。**

## 测试

- `verify-profile.test.mjs` 33 → **36**（新增：显式 token 解析、**绝不把 secret 当 token**、脚本接线断言）；
- 全套 **470 passed**；`push` 时 pre-push 12 通过 / 0 失败（19 插件全过）。

author: ericw9888
body:
## Summary

- give authoritative mailbox receipts a durable provider-native transaction identity enforced by PostgreSQL
- make replay idempotent, adopt exactly one matching legacy fill, and route ambiguous overlaps to review
- add an explicit dry-run-first recovery endpoint for legacy mailbox duplicates and rebuild positions/cash after approved repair
- preserve transaction provenance in API responses

## Root cause

Mailbox ingestion persisted receipt evidence before posting the transaction. A retry could therefore replay the economic fill, and exact numeric matching could miss legacy float tails. The transaction ledger had no source-owned uniqueness invariant.

## Migration and concurrency

The forward migration adds and conservatively backfills `transactions.source_identity`, leaving ambiguous historical claims unset, then creates `uq_transactions_source_identity`. Concurrent creators converge through the database constraint and `IntegrityError` recovery; mailbox import keeps its existing advisory-lock serialization.

- 17 focused mailbox/provenance/reconciliation tests
- 705 backend tests; 52% branch coverage
- migrated-schema constraint inspection and Alembic autogenerate check
- concurrent PostgreSQL replay test
- Black, isort, flake8, Bandit

author: sridharkalaibala
body:
Owner, after seeing the timings: *"is there way to improve?"*

Yes. This is the last big piece.

## Measured, on the running till

| | Order to paper |
|---|---|
| Before | **2,080 ms** |
| After | **184 ms** to paper, both printers |

The breakdown before, from the app's own timestamped log:

| Stage | Time |
|---|---|
| Event debounce | 250 ms |
| Asking the API which tickets are pending | **9 ms** |
| Building the sheet and printing the first copy | **1,114 ms** |
| Second printer | 252 ms |

So the API was never the problem. The cost was the rendering: HTML into a hidden `BrowserWindow`, render, convert to PDF, hand to SumatraPDF, and again for the second printer. A receipt covering the same ground already took **124 ms**, because it renders straight to ESC/POS.

## What changed

The kitchen ticket is now built the same way a receipt is: ESC/POS bytes, straight to the roll, through the warm print helper. No window, no PDF, no second program.

The layout follows how a cook reads a ticket. The serial keeps the biggest type because that is what the pass calls out, the table is set double because that is what is needed next, the body is plain.

```
        Additional Order
              #7
     13-09-2026 8:41:15 PM
             Dine in
             SID1042
            TABLE 5
             Pax: 4
------------------------------------------------
SWEET CORN SOUP - CHICKEN                     x2
   ** no coriander **
------------------------------------------------
```

## What is deliberately kept

- **The window path stays** for non-thermal printers, and as the fallback when a ticket cannot be drawn as bytes.
- **A refusing printer does not fall back.** Falling through there would put the same order on paper twice. A refusal is reported as a refusal, as before.
- **What a ticket says is worked out once**, in `_ticketFields`, and both the bytes and the HTML are built from it. Two copies of the rules about what a cancellation is called and which field holds the table is exactly the pair that drifts until one printer says something the other does not.

## One visible difference

ESC/POS has no strike-through, so cancelled lines are no longer struck out. The heading carries it instead: Item Cancelled, Items Cancelled, Order Cancelled, which is what those headings already mean after #642.

## Tests

`tests/kitchen-ticket-as-bytes.test.js` renders real tickets and reads the bytes back: the headings, the table, the quantities, the size commands, the cut, the narrow roll, and both printers receiving it. The electron stub in it **throws if a window is constructed**, so reaching the old path fails the test rather than passing it slowly. Desktop suite 1,943 passing.

author: donlim1
body:
## Why

flyctl writes the BuildKit progress — every `#N [i/n] RUN …` step and its `#N DONE 123.4s` timing — to **stderr**. `build_remote` logged stderr only on failure, so a *successful* build stored no per-step timing at all. A customer's 18-minute Next.js build on 2026-09-12 (`dep_54ae75e5f634`) produced a 48-line build log with zero step durations; "where do the 18 minutes go" was unanswerable, and a fast-vs-slow build could not be diffed.

## What

On success, log stderr's lines into the build log as well (the timeout path already did; the failure path already folds stderr into the error). Six lines.

## Tests

`test_remote_builder_keeps_buildkit_progress_from_stderr_on_success`: a successful `CompletedProcess` with progress on stderr → `#5 DONE 240.3s` / `#7 DONE 605.2s` present in `result.logs`. Worker suite 54 passed; ruff clean.

## Parity

runtm-cloud ships `worker_build/docker.py` over this file in the image; the same change is in runtm-cloud#474 so prod gets it with that deploy. This PR keeps the OSS worker identical; no rush to bump.

author: sh00tg0a1
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1514. On the **public surface** of `mf-model-manager` and `mf-model-api`, the auth middleware appended the verified identity (`x-account-id` / `x-account-type`) to the **end** of `request.scope['headers']`, while handlers read it with `headers.get()` — which returns the **first** match. A client that sent its own `x-account-id` ahead of the appended one had that spoofed value read downstream, letting **any authenticated caller** (including a `bak_` AppKey holder on mf-model-api) act as an arbitrary account. Setting `x-account-id` to the built-in admin id — which is also the hardcoded bypass in `llm_controller.py:368` — escalated to full model-factory admin (create/edit/delete any model config, incl. upstream provider credentials; read all; alter any user's quota/prompts).

## Change

- Add `_set_trusted_identity()` in both services: it strips **every** client-supplied `x-account-id` / `x-account-type` from `scope['headers']` before appending the verified identity, so `headers.get()` can only observe the trusted value.
- Applied to all injecting branches on the public surface: anonymous (auth disabled), Hydra introspection, and the `bak_` AppKey branch (mf-model-api).
- **Private surface (`/api/private`) is deliberately untouched.** The middleware passes it through with no introspection and no injection; its "header is identity" behaviour is the in-cluster S2S contract used by `bkn-backend`, `ontology-query`, `context-loader`, and `execution-factory` to pass the on-behalf-of user (see `bkn-backend/.../model_factory_access.go` + `common/setting.go` pointing at `/api/private/mf-model-*`). The private surface is **not** routed through the external ingress (ingress exposes only `/api/mf-model-*`, and `/api/private/*` does not match that prefix), so internal module calls are unaffected.

## Tests

- New regression suite `app/test/test_auth_middleware_identity.py` in each service: verifies a spoofed `x-account-id` placed ahead of the appended one is stripped, that `headers.get()` then returns the token subject, and that unrelated headers survive. Covers the Hydra branch (both) and the `bak_` AppKey branch (mf-model-api).
- Wired into the `authz-unit` CI job for both services (runs in `model-factory-base:v2`).

## Verification

- **Pre-fix, black-box:** confirmed on a running deployment — same admin token, `GET /api/mf-model-manager/v1/llm/list` returned `count: 4` with no header and `count: 0` with a forged `x-account-id`, proving the app trusted the header over the token and that the ingress does not strip it.
- **Fix mechanism + algorithm:** confirmed in the real runtime (`starlette 0.27.0`, in-pod): `Headers.get()` returns the first occurrence, and after strip-before-append `get()` returns only the trusted value. The full unit suite runs in CI's `model-factory-base:v2` (the deployed VM mf-model image is from an older codebase whose module layout is incompatible with main, so the main-based suite runs in CI rather than against that pod).

## Notes / follow-up

- The hardcoded admin bypass at `llm_controller.py:368` keyed on a fixed UUID amplified the impact; once identity is trusted again it is far less dangerous, but it should still move to a trusted-role check rather than a fixed id (out of scope here).

author: matto00
body:
## Summary

Prod backend application/Flyway logs never reached Cloud Logging in a queryable form. Root
cause: `backend/src/main/resources/logback.xml`'s `<if>` conditional-processing construct
(guarding `LOG_FORMAT`-based appender selection) silently left the root logger with **no
attached appender at runtime**, in this repo's exact toolchain (logback-classic 1.5.38 + Janino,
packaged via `sbt-assembly`'s fat jar). Joran reported a clean "End of configuration" but
`Logger.callAppenders()` found nothing attached, so every application/Flyway log call was
silently dropped after logback's own ~13-line internal bootstrap narration.

Probe-confirmed via a real Docker build of the actual prod `Dockerfile`, run against a real
throwaway Postgres container, reproducing prod revision `helio-backend-00077-55c`'s exact
"13 logback-bootstrap lines then silence" signature — confirmed independently against live prod
via read-only `gcloud logging read`/`gcloud run services describe` (which also disproved an
earlier theory that `LOG_FORMAT` was unset in prod; it was already `json`).

## What changed

- **Root-cause fix**: removed `<if>` from `logback.xml` entirely. Both appenders (`json`,
  `plain`) are now declared unconditionally; selection is via a new
  `LogFormatPropertyDefiner.scala` (plain JVM code, no conditional-processing construct anywhere
  in the appender-attachment path) that case-insensitively normalizes `LOG_FORMAT` into a clean
  `LOG_APPENDER` value feeding a single `<appender-ref>`.
- **Hardening**: added `LOG_FORMAT=json` explicitly to `.github/workflows/cd-backend.yml`'s
  deploy env vars — the actual deploy path never set it itself; the live value only existed via
  a historical, undocumented `infra/deploy-backend.sh` run. Independent of the root-cause fix.
- **New regression check**: `docs/verify-backend-logging.sh` — a repeatable red/green check
  (real Dockerfile + real throwaway Postgres) asserting Flyway/startup lines reach stdout as
  structured JSON with `severity`, across `LOG_FORMAT=json`/`JSON`/`garbage`/unset.
- Spec delta for `structured-json-logging` capturing the new "no conditional-processing
  construct" requirement.

## Test plan

- `sbt test`: 4246/4246 passed (re-verified independently by two cold skeptic reviews and the
  evaluator, not just the executor).
- `docs/verify-backend-logging.sh`: exit 0, both `LOG_FORMAT=json` (JSON output with `severity`)
  and unrecognized-value (plain-text fallback, never silence) cases confirmed against a real
  Docker image + real throwaway Postgres.
- Full Husky pre-commit chain green (lint, typecheck, format, schema-drift, openspec hygiene,
  scala-quality, credential-leak, jest).
- This delivery went through 3 design-gate rounds (2 REFUTE, 1 CONFIRM) and 3 final-gate rounds
  (2 REFUTE — a case-insensitivity regression in round 1's fix, then a spec-delta document defect
  in round 2 — both fixed and re-confirmed) before reaching CONFIRM, each round independently
  re-verifying against a real Docker+Postgres reproduction rather than trusting prior claims.

## Open item — explicitly NOT verified by this PR

**AC 3 ("verified against a real deploy") is intentionally left open.** This delivery's scope
excluded any Cloud Run deploy, live env/secret change, or release tag. ACs 1–2 (startup/Flyway
lines queryable with `severity` parsed; a known app log line findable by a structured field) are
verified **locally only**, via the real-Dockerfile + real-Postgres reproduction above. Real
Cloud Logging ingestion against a live deploy must be verified separately after the next release
cut.

No database migration in this change.

author: cnasajon
body:
Fecha a fase 4 e, com ela, o escopo da especificação: painel inicial, interface traduzida em português, espanhol e inglês, tela de auditoria e o polimento visual.

## O que entra

**Interface em três idiomas.** Todas as telas leem os rótulos de `messages/{pt,es,en}.json`: início, painel, textos, editor, histórico, alertas, importação, exportação, pastas, usuários, organizações, configurações globais, auditoria e os componentes de cliente. O idioma vem de quem está olhando — preferência do usuário → padrão da organização → cookie → português —, sem `/pt/` na URL, como a seção 12 pede.

**As mensagens de erro deixam de ser frases dentro da `lib/`.** As validações devolvem chave e valores (`src/lib/avisos.ts`); quem monta a frase é a ação de servidor, que sabe o idioma de quem pediu. A política de senha reúne o que falta com a conjunção do idioma, via `Intl.ListFormat`.

**O worker também traduz.** Não tem sessão nem requisição, então usa o idioma padrão da organização da pasta ao gravar o erro de uma publicação ou o texto de um alerta — é quem vai ler isso no histórico e no painel. A tradução fora do next-intl fica em `src/lib/mensagens.ts`, separada de `avisos.ts` de propósito: ali os três arquivos de mensagens entram no pacote, e `avisos.ts` é alcançado por código de navegador.

**O layout só entrega ao navegador os grupos que os componentes de cliente usam.** O provedor do next-intl serializa na página tudo que recebe — a tela inicial de um usuário comum carregava os rótulos das telas de sistema. Isso apareceu como um teste de isolamento HTTP falhando, e a correção foi no código, não no teste.

**Datas e horas na ordem do idioma:** 14/09 em português e espanhol, 9/14 em inglês, sempre no fuso da pasta e com a sigla do fuso ao lado. Uma data como 09/14 lida na ordem errada não parece errada, parece outra data.

Sai também o componente `EmConstrucao`, sem uso desde que a fase 3 entrou.

## Testes

`npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`, 139 testes e mais 14 de isolamento nas rotas HTTP, todos passando com Postgres real.

Três testes novos em `tests/mensagens.test.ts`, agora na lista de testes obrigatórios do `CLAUDE.md`:

- as três línguas têm exatamente as mesmas chaves;
- nenhuma chave usada no código está sem tradução — cobre as telas, as ações de servidor e as validações;
- nenhum grupo usado por componente de navegador ficou fora da lista que o layout entrega ao cliente.

Antes de confiar no verificador, troquei uma chave por outra inexistente e confirmei que o teste falha.

Os testes que conferem a mensagem visível passam por um ajudante que monta a frase em português a partir do arquivo de mensagens, o que de quebra prova que a chave existe.

## Verificação no navegador

As 12 telas nos 3 idiomas, em 1366×768: sem scroll horizontal, sem erro de console, sem chave crua na tela. As faixas de validação saem traduzidas (`Telegram no acepta <div>` / `Telegram does not accept <div>`). Conferido no build que nenhuma mensagem de servidor vazou para os pacotes do cliente.

## O que continua em português, deliberadamente

- **O conteúdo dos arquivos de exportação** (cabeçalhos das colunas em PDF, XLSX, CSV, JSON e XML). São documentos gerados, não interface.
- **Os títulos dos tipos de alerta enviados ao Telegram** pelo worker: o grupo de alertas é único e global, sem idioma próprio. No painel esses títulos já aparecem traduzidos.

Ambos estão registrados no README, na seção **Idiomas**. Diga se prefere que eu traduza qualquer um dos dois.

author: jmagar
body:
## Summary

Fix concurrent job retry/recovery and cancellation, source-ledger retention, resource bounds, and stale Android/Palette async state. Harden SSH first trust, OAuth credentials, output-directory authorization, SFTP byte/path/close boundaries, installer verification, and deployment readiness.

Address 69 deduplicated findings: the 38 original review findings plus follow-up PR review and qualification findings, including transient ownership-read failures, attachment cancellation, Incus false-positive health, and the map output-directory CI regression. Refresh four vulnerable transitive dependencies covering nine advisories. Final security qualification fixes panel credential logging, cleartext HTTP validators, partial sanitization, and a migration-script ReDoS, and independently removes an unused raw-HTML builder path; three stale inline test modules now use sidecars. Fix a pre-existing lease-loss test race by keeping filesystem setup and cleanup on real time and advancing virtual time only at the blocked-provider checkpoint. Own Git clone subprocess groups through cancellation and timeout, and remove zero-test CI selectors and stale local test recipes.

The original risk-focused review inspected 292 of 5,105 eligible files, including partial reads. The follow-up reviews covered the resulting PR changes; this is not a claim of exhaustive repository coverage.

## Validation

- Final-head GitHub workspace tests: **6,138 passed, eight intentionally skipped**; all four new Git lifecycle regressions passed on Linux. Focused local validation also included 1,822 affected library tests, 88 release tests, 77 workflow-shape tests, and ownership/heartbeat/map authorization regressions.
- Palette: 171 native tests, 583 frontend tests, type checking, clean lint, and production build. Dependency audit reports zero vulnerabilities.
- Android: full unit task with strict dependency verification, plus metadata/content cancellation regressions.
- Generated contracts, layering, monolith checks, formatting, Clippy with warnings denied, workflow lint, and hermetic operational regressions. Security follow-up: eight conditional HTTP tests, one credential-free startup notice test, 45 Chrome extension tests, bounded parser regressions, and Xtask sidecar compilation. Lease-loss regression: 20 repeated passes and 16/16 dispatch tests. Git clone lifecycle: eight hermetic tests covering success, failure, cancellation and timeout. Canonical watch recipe: 78/78 tests.
- Independent Rust, apps, tooling, simplicity, and security review passes found no remaining actionable issues. All 69 original CodeQL alerts were triaged: six map to four fixes and 63 were dismissed with source evidence. The unused raw-HTML path is one separate hardening finding with no linkage to alerts 44 or 47; a post-merge full scan confirmed those alerts point to safe `appendChild(Node)` composition, and both were dismissed with independent receipts. A subsequent password-path notice alert was independently confirmed to contain no credential and dismissed. Three secret-scanning alerts were verified as inactive synthetic security-test fixtures and resolved.

PR #611 was squash-merged at `62b8e538ac92ae670d1dc7f4fa8a7336f934a3fd` after exact head `52629d9a419c1ef174dbdf88b2a9bdf1216d1c61` recorded 35 successful checks and six intentional skips and 6,138 workspace tests with eight intentional skips. Live Incus/systemd deployment tests were not performed. Windows installer regressions use PowerShell with download/verifier doubles. Post-merge live homelab verification and default-branch Rust CodeQL results for alerts 55 and 132 remain pending.

Post-merge qualification added one finding outside this PR's closed 69-finding scope. Main homelab run `34741252208` failed admission because its Workload Identity Federation audience, gateway variables, and secret projections were absent; it created no resources and cleanup was clean. A names-only pre-build fail-fast check is in progress on `codex/full-review-homelab-admission-20260913`, and completion requires the user-supplied secret-store location. The combined tracker therefore contains 70 canonical findings: 69 fixed and one in progress.

author: nategrey0130
body:
Rifts World Book 18: Mystic Russia pp.79–82 — also known as the Gypsy Witch and
Mistress of Life and Death. **Applied `--remote` before this merge**: 267 live
classes.

**Clean on the first `class-check`**, which is what the Night Witch bought: the
`Language: Russian` and `Literacy: Russian` rows it created already carry the
second class, and this one needed no catalog row at all.

## The magic is the interesting half

The Hidden Witch doesn't train — she *instinctively knows* a new set of spells
at junctions in her life. So the book prints a **fixed named set per level**
rather than a pick. Modelled as `spells_schedule` entries whose `count` equals
the length of their own `from` list, which hands over the whole set: levels 3,
5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and 15 — **27 spells**, on top of nine granted at level one.

## Four names needed the catalog's spelling

| the book | the catalog |
|---|---|
| Cure Minor Disorder | `Cure Minor Disorders` |
| Purification (of food and water) | `Purification` |
| Curse Phobia | `Curse: Phobia` |
| Basic Math | `Mathematics: Basic` |

And the book prints **"Cure Illness" twice in one sentence** — a typesetting
repeat, not two spells.

## Two things stay prose

Both are **rolled**, and the fields take integers: the level-one allotment of
*1D4+2 Spoiling spells of choice* (excluding 8th level or higher), and the
*+1D4 to P.B.* `spell_traditions_allowed: ["spoiling"]` is set so that pool is
reachable.

**Three of the nine** O.C.C. Related Skills must be Rogue skills — carried as
`occ_related_skills.minimums`, so it's refused on save rather than merely
described.

## One more digit-cipher sighting

The N.P.C. money figure reads **`106x10,000`** in the text layer — the
substitution this cache carries on 72 pages. It's `1D6x10,000`, and it's
recorded as prose since `starting_money` is the player character's coin.

## Checks

- `class-check --remote` on draft and emitted `.sql` — **ready, 0 errors**, all
  catalogs ok
- `--field-sources`: the `Money:` paragraph is whole on one page, confirming
  `1D6x1000`
- pure ASCII, no CR; `smoke.mjs` 1989 passed
- pinned counts **266 → 267** in `operations.md` **and** the README's spelled-out
  sentence, which regression compares separately

**16 classes remain.**

- `_load_bridge_config`, `send_cmd._load_hermes_env`, `doctor_state._doctor_memory_config` expanded `${VAR}` **before** the managed overlay; they now expand the user layer first and the managed layer against the process env only, like `load_config()`. A managed `api_key: ${FOO}` now expands on every surface.
- All nine sites gain `_normalize_root_model_keys` (`model: {name: x}` / root `provider:` resolve everywhere, not only in the gateway) and last-known-good recovery on torn YAML (previously `{}` → all overrides dropped for that read).

- `hermes send` sanitizes non-ASCII from `*_TOKEN`/`*_KEY` values like every other entrypoint.
- `hermes worktree` archives land under the active `HERMES_HOME` (profile) instead of `~/.hermes`.
- Gateway per-message config reads: same dict as before for the same files (invariant test below), so system-prompt bytes are unchanged.

## Validation

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `${VAR}` in managed config, `hermes send` bridge | literal `${VAR}` exported | expanded |
| `model: {name: x}` in cron / TUI gateway | empty model | `x` |
| torn config.yaml during a gateway turn | `{}` → every override dropped for that read | last good config served, loud warning |
| worktree archive under `HERMES_HOME=<root>/profiles/work` | `~/.hermes/archive/...` | `<profile>/archive/...` |

Tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_config_effective.py` — (1) `load_user_config_effective` == the legacy gateway raw→overlay→canon→expand pipeline for a fixture with managed overlay + `${VAR}` on both layers, and carries no `DEFAULT_CONFIG` keys; (2) torn YAML serves the last good result / `fail_closed` raises. `tests/hermes_cli/test_worktree_gc.py::test_untracked_files_archived_under_the_active_profile_home` (patches `Path.home` AND `HERMES_HOME`). Sabotage: skipping the overlay → red; skipping the canon → red; reverting `worktree_gc` → red.

E2E (temp `HERMES_HOME` + `HERMES_MANAGED_DIR`, real files): gateway `_load_gateway_config()` == TUI `_load_cfg()` == `load_user_config_effective()`; cron snapshot, `hermes_time`, `hermes_logging` read the managed-pinned values; torn YAML → gateway keeps the last good dict, `fail_closed` raises; absent user file → managed layer still applies; `hermes send` bridge exports the effective scalars.

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli tests/cron tests/tui_gateway tests/gateway tests/tools/test_code_execution*.py …`: green except `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_head_moved_gate.py::test_update_success_when_head_moves`, which fails identically on `origin/main` (pre-existing, unrelated).

## Summary
- Fix device-lock leak when `screenshot.sh` is wrapped in `timeout N`: `timeout` sends SIGTERM, which bash's `EXIT`-only trap never ran on — the mkdir-based per-device lock leaked forever. Now traps `INT`/`TERM` too, calling the same idempotent cleanup and exiting `128+signal`.
- Give each device (`Agent_Emulator`/`Narrow`/`Wide`) its own fixed Metro port (8081/8082/8083) instead of a hardcoded 8081 + host-wide `pkill -f "expo start"` — two concurrent `screenshot.sh` calls on different, independently-locked devices no longer collide on Metro or kill each other's in-flight capture.
- Investigated the doc's old "`--wait-for` on hall-menu routes always times out" note — could not reproduce (live uiautomator dumps returned 241 populated nodes including the target text, `MealTabPager.test.tsx` already asserts the accessibility prop is correct). No app code changed. `wait_for_text`'s timeout message now names the known uiautomator/accessibility-service flake class specifically when the accessibility tree never populated (tracked via a max-node-count high-water mark), instead of a generic message — still a hard failure either way.
- `docs/agents/emulator-pool.md` updated to match, including two corrections made during review (see Test plan).

## Test plan
- [x] `bash -n mobile/scripts/screenshot.sh`
- [x] `timeout 8 bash mobile/scripts/screenshot.sh home --device Agent_Emulator_Narrow` — lock directory confirmed gone immediately after timeout fired
- [x] Concurrent `screenshot.sh` on Narrow (8082) + Wide (8083) — both captured correct, distinct PNGs; a live third-party Metro on 8081 (unrelated worktree) confirmed untouched throughout

author: kendrick
body:
Builds the route at the site root: the Task list, the expandable Citation behind every Task, the held-back section, the model's advisories, and check-off that survives a reload. This is what remained of #12 after #26 carved out the shell, the loader, the staleness bands, and the error state.

One decision shapes the rest. Every component below the route is handed the Rule it needs, already resolved, rather than a rule set to look one up in. The same resolution that comes back empty is what renders the "not in the current rule set" line, so completion and presentation cannot disagree about a Task: there is no path where a Task reads as checked while also reading as unresolvable.

Closes #12.

## Where To Start

Read `src/components/citation.tsx` and `src/planner/completion.ts` first. The first is the feature the product is actually about, and the second is the only non-UI file in the diff.

`src/components/this-week/this-week.tsx` is where the wiring lives, and `src/components/this-week/fixtures.ts` is worth reading before any spec, because every component test feeds off it.

## What I Am Least Sure About

**The de-emphasis treatment.** #12 asks for the Task list to be "visually de-emphasized" once the Artifact is over a week old, and the mechanism I picked overrides `--foreground` for the subtree so every nested `text-foreground` resolves to `--muted-foreground`. That keeps the whole thing on tokens the app already uses and known to pass contrast, where a raw `opacity` value would have been an unverified contrast claim. It is also a slightly unusual thing to do with a CSS variable, and a reviewer who hates it would not be wrong.

**Prop threading.** `rulesById`, `plantsById`, `narrationById`, `completedIds`, `window` and `onComplete` travel together through `ThisWeek`, `DeferredSection` and `TaskItem`. That is a render-context type wanting to be born, and #14 will feel the same pull when it reuses `rule-summary`. I left it as plain props because contract 11 fixes the component boundaries and inventing a context object at review-fix time is the wrong moment.

**A scoped ESLint suppression.** `rule-summary.tsx` exports four constants for `citation.tsx` to share, and `react-refresh/only-export-components` refuses any non-component export from a component file. The suppression is scoped to those four and carries its reason. The rule's own answer is a third module, and the symbol that most wants one is `MONTHS`, whose home is `src/planner/dates.ts`, frozen for this ticket.

## Testing

```sh
CI=true pnpm lint && pnpm lint:css && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build && pnpm test:e2e --project=mobile-chrome --project=desktop-chrome
```

55 test files, 688 tests pass, 7 skip. The build exports `/`, `/rules` and `/yard` as static routes. Playwright passes 4 tests across mobile-chrome and desktop-chrome, including zero axe violations on the home page.

The e2e run is the one worth keeping in the loop. It drives the built export, so a change to page structure passes lint, typecheck and the unit suite and still fails there.

Checked by hand: `grep` on `out/index.html` finds no `--muted-foreground` override and no `<time>` carrying a clock reading, so neither the staleness band nor the de-emphasis reaches the prerendered file. Both wait on the mount flag, for the reason the banner already established.

Reload survival is proven by mounting, ticking a box, unmounting, and mounting again against the same fake Store. That test fails if the checked state is ever held beside the Task instead of read back out of the Store.

## Glossary Proposals

`CONTEXT.md` is frozen for this run, so these are proposals for the commit that lands after the wave rather than edits in this branch.

**Evidence start**: The earliest `completedAt` that counts as a Task's current cycle rather than the last one, derived per Citation kind: a Window Rule's `start` in the planned year, a Threshold Citation's `from`, a Cadence Task's `asOf`, and nothing at all for an Approaching Task. It is computed on demand and never stored.
_Avoid_: Cutoff, since, deadline, threshold (Threshold is a Rule kind), anchor (an Anchor is the Occurrence a Cadence Rule counts its interval from)

**Completed Task**: A Task the yard already holds an Occurrence for, dated on or after that Task's Evidence start. It is computed on every render from the Occurrence history, never written onto the Task, and never true for an Approaching Task.
_Avoid_: Done, ticked, checked off (the checkbox is the control, not the state), finished

That second entry needs a ruling rather than just an entry. The Occurrence entry's `_Avoid_` line currently lists "Completion", and this branch ships `src/planner/completion.ts` exporting `isCompleted`. Contract 7 in the plan specifies that exact path, and `Occurrence.completedAt` is pre-existing frozen vocabulary, so the collision is real and was not introduced casually. The proposal is to narrow that `_Avoid_` entry: "Completion" stays banned as a name for the Occurrence *record*, and is allowed for the derived question of whether one covers a Task. If you would rather keep the ban absolute, the rename is `occurrence-evidence.ts` and `hasCoveringOccurrence`, and it touches one file plus its spec.

## Deviations From The Plan

**Contract 7 gained a fourth parameter.** `isCompleted(task, occurrences, asOf, rule)`. The contract named a Window Rule's `start` as the evidence start, and the three arguments it listed cannot reach it: a window Citation is `{ kind: 'window', date: asOf }`, so it carries the day the Plan was generated rather than the Rule's range, and a Task carries no window bounds. Reading `citation.date` instead would walk the evidence start forward every night, and a Task checked off yesterday would come back unchecked this morning, which is this ticket's own reload-survival criterion failing by construction.

The Rule arrives already resolved rather than as a map, and that is the load-bearing half of the correction. Resolving once in the component is what keeps completion and the unresolved-Rule marker from disagreeing; handing the function a map and letting it look the Rule up itself means the day the two diverge, a Task renders as unresolvable while still reading as checked. It also makes the null case meaningful rather than defensive: a window Task whose Rule cannot be found has no resolvable evidence start, so it reads unchecked, and unchecked is the safe direction for work nobody can prove was done.

This is a corrected contract, not a worked-around one.

**The wave table was restructured, 3 waves to 5.** `citation.tsx` imports `rule-summary.tsx` and `task-item.tsx` imports `citation.tsx`, and the original table put all three in one wave. `check-waves.py` proves disjoint file ownership and cannot see an import, so two workers would have been coding against files their peers had not written yet, with no way to run the verification command. Same tasks, same ownership, different wave numbers. The batched `deferred-and-advisories` task split for the same reason: `advisories` depends on nothing and `deferred-section` composes `TaskItem`.

## Findings For Other Tickets

**The Artifact cites two Rules the seed set does not carry.** `src/artifact/fixtures.ts` and the committed `data/artifact.json` both name `deep-water-fig`, and `src/artifact/fixtures.ts` also names a `water-in-after-application` Guard. Neither is in `src/seed/rules.json`. All three files were frozen for this ticket, so the route renders the mismatch rather than reconciling it, and the deployed placeholder page will show the "not in the current rule set" line on the fig watering Task until #11's first real run replaces the Artifact. Worth deciding deliberately: either the seed gains those two Rules, or the placeholder Artifact stops citing them.

**Spaced em dashes are repo-wide.** The house rule chains an em dash flush to the text on both sides, and roughly 80 spaced ones sit in `src/planner`, `src/store`, `src/w

author: anobaka
body:
Three things that stood between a fresh thin client and a working library. The
first two are real bugs — pairing could not succeed, and even when it did the
client could not reach the server afterwards. The third is the screen those two
bugs were hiding behind.

Fixes #1352
Fixes #1353
Closes #1354

## 1. A paired client could not reach its server at all

`UpstreamTransformer` signed the outgoing request while `RequestUri` was still
null — YARP fills the destination URI *after* the transformer returns, and the
comment in that file described the order backwards. The signer threw, YARP
recorded it as `RequestCreation`, and the forwarding layer translated that into
"the server did not respond": a 503.

Because nothing is signed without credentials, everything looked fine right up
until pairing succeeded — and then **every** request failed, across restarts.

Fixed by computing the destination with YARP's own
`RequestUtilities.MakeDestinationAddress` first, then signing against it.

## 2. Approving a pairing request did nothing

`/client/pair/request` returned outcome `Paired`(0) when it had merely *filed*
the request. `connect.html` took that at face value, called `enterApp()`, and
dropped the user into a library with no credentials — **polling never started**,
so the server-side approval was never observed.

Filing now reports `AwaitingApproval`, which is the true state, and the page
keys off `requestId` — the same thing the React settings page already did, which
is why only the client's own page was affected.

The real repair is `ClientToServerForwardingTests`: two real hosts on two real
ports, with requests carried end to end. **No existing pipeline test did that** —
they all exercised the "no server" path, which is exactly how two bugs on the
happy path shipped together. Revert either fix and the corresponding test fails.

## 3. The connect page was never translated

It is the first screen of the thin client and the only one in the product still
hardcoded in English. It carries its own strings precisely because it is shown
before there is a server, and the app's translations live on the server — so the
pairing flow, the one thing a new client user has to get through, was
English-only.

It now ships an en/zh dictionary and reads the locale the web view reports from
the OS, which is the only signal available at that point and the right one for a
screen seen before anything is configured. No dependency and no build step: the
client package carries no web frontend, and an i18n library here would be the
first crack in that. The English in the markup stays as the fallback if the
script never runs.

`ConnectPageTests` is what keeps it honest — nothing else points translation
tooling at this file, so a string added on one side would simply be missing on
the other, quietly, because the lookup falls back to English and the page still
renders. It reads the shipped page back and checks the two dictionaries against
each other, against every key the markup asks for, and against both outcome
enums, so a new C# enum member fails the build rather than showing a raw detail
string.

## 4. Nothing said which of the two downloads you had

They are called Bakabase and Bakabase Client, and neither the names nor anything
on screen said that one of them cannot work alone. App info now names the
edition and what it means, and the client card on the other-devices page — where
someone goes to fetch the second one — says outright that it is not the same
download as the app they are standing in.

## Verification

- Solution build: 0 errors
- `Bakabase.Tests`: 1084 passed, 0 failed, 14 skipped
- Frontend: 349 passed, lint 0 errors, build ok
- Connect page rendered under `en-US`, `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` with no unresolved keys

author: dhannyell
body:
## API

- The package clause is now `b2`; the import path stays `github.com/dhannyell/dbox2d`. A call reads like the reference: `b2MakeBox` → `b2.MakeBox`.
- New generic constructors `F`, `V2` and `Degrees` accept `int`, `float32`, `float64` or `Q`, so a literal needs no conversion: `b2.V2(0, -10)`, `b2.F(0.35)`. They do not allocate. The long forms (`QFromInt`, `QMustParse`, ...) remain.
- The samples module uses the short forms; its string tables became `float64`.

## Robustness

- A panic on a worker goroutine no longer kills the process. It is caught, the other workers finish, and `Step` re-raises it on the caller as `*WorkerPanic` (worker index, value, stack). The world stays locked afterwards. Cost: +1.5% on `joint_grid` with 4 workers.

## Performance

Bit-exact in both modes; float hashes still match the reference under `dbox2d_upstream_pairs`, fixed traces unchanged.

- Manifolds written in place; per-call scalar literals hoisted.
- Exact fast path in `unwindAngle`; null check dropped from the tree query loop.
- `jointSim` overlays the seven joint payloads in one union: 896 → 224 B float, 1608 → 392 B fixed.
- `shape` overlays the five geometries: 432 → 344 B float, 704 → 536 B fixed.
- `RotateVector` and `MulRot` written out so they fit the inliner budget.

Solver time relative to the C reference (AVX2, geometric mean over 7 scenes):

| workers | before | after | with PGO |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.39x | 1.35x | 1.30x |
| 2 | 1.34x | 1.29x | 1.26x |
| 4 | 1.29x | 1.24x | 1.20x |
| 8 | 1.35x | 1.29x | 1.24x |

README and `tools/cbench/README.md` carry the per-scene tables.

## Checks

- `go test` float and fixed, `go vet`, golangci-lint clean on the root module.
- Samples build in both modes; their 24 lint findings predate this branch.

author: davidharrishmc
body:
Issue #1838 item 5.

`jalr` clears the least significant bit of its target. Wally cleared it on the fetch path but `IEUAdrE` carried the raw ALU sum, so `xtval` for an instruction-address-misaligned trap could report an odd address where the architectural target, and Sail, have bit 0 clear.

The mask is applied in `datapath.sv` where `IEUAdrE` is formed — the ALU can't do it, since `Sum` also feeds `FullResult` and the comparator flags. `JumpE` alone suffices: `jal` targets are already even and `JumpE` is 0 for every load/store, so the LSU path is untouched.

Fixing it at the source also repairs the consumers that inherited the odd bit: `BPWrongE` stops firing on a *correct* prediction of an odd `jalr` target, and the BTB stops storing the odd target, which previously re-triggered that flush on every later execution.

Independent of the other three PRs for this issue; they apply in any order.

**Verification:** `lint-wally` and `lint-wally --nightly` clean. All 44 `tests/coverage` ELFs on rv64gc are cycle-identical to `main`.

author: kroticw
body:
## Summary

A session frozen inside a tool call — `ssh` asking about a host key nobody will see, a network call with no timeout, an MCP call that never returns — cannot produce any words, and the daemon keeps describing it as working with no question outstanding. The panel repeated that as "nobody is waiting". Its only fallback, the silence rule, was reset by any message sent to the session, because silence was measured by the transcript's modification time.

A frozen step cannot be told apart from a slow one from outside. This change makes the panel stop claiming more than it knows.

## Changes

- **Silence is what the session said.** It is measured from the last line the session itself wrote (model output or a tool result). Incoming messages, runtime attachments and bookkeeping lines no longer reset it.
- **A move left unanswered is not an answer of "no".** When a session has owed its next move for 16 minutes without a word — a call that has not returned, a result it has not acted on, a message it has not answered — the "waiting" verdict becomes *not known* instead of *no*, the same third answer a source that never reports already gets. Words from the daemon still decide first, and no new banner is raised.
- **The row states the fact, not a cause.** The badge reads "not answering", or "silent inside <tool>" when the transcript shows the open call. A call is named only when it is on disk: some calls, such as `Read`, are written to the transcript only once they return. The badge takes precedence over a flag-only stall, which says less.
- **One threshold, two copies kept equal.** The browser restates the server's rule, and a Go test reads the browser's constant so the two cannot drift apart.
- **Docs.** Protocol section 5 rule 3, the design spec's silence definition, and a new limitations section in English and Russian.

## Why 16 minutes

Measured on local transcripts over 14 days, replayed with multi-call messages written only when their last result arrives: working sessions owed their move for at most 651 seconds before their next line appeared. The worst case the parts add up to — a command at its 601-second timeout ceiling after the model's p99.99 of 338 seconds — is 939 seconds. Sixteen minutes clears that and still comes well before the 30-minute silence notification.

## Not in this change

- The daemon's `detail` carries the last incoming message verbatim, and the panel still shows it as a stopped session's reason. That affects every session that was written to and is tracked separately.

## Testing

- `go test ./... -race -count=1`
- `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues
- `make test-web` — 853 tests
- Acceptance against a genuinely frozen session: a session blocked inside a `Read` on an empty named pipe for 20 minutes, watched through this build's `/api/snapshot` every 30 seconds. `unansweredFor` grew without a break, a message sent to the session five minutes in did not reset it, and at 963 seconds the row showed "not answering" and the header its "+?" mark. The open `Read` never reached the transcript during the run, which is why the verdict does not depend on seeing the call. An earlier attempt was void because the machine slept during it.

author: analisaperlengkapan
body:
Modul pertama dari daftar penukaran di **ROADMAP §16**. Dasbor yang paling sering dilihat, jadi ia yang pertama: **17 penyaring** `student: { unitId }` di `dashboard` dan `dashboard-enhancement` kini bertanya *"saat itu unitnya apa?"* alih-alih *"unitnya sekarang apa?"*.

## Yang diukur, bukan dijanjikan

Skenario di basis data terisolasi: satu santri TK dengan **7 hari kehadiran yang dicatat saat ia masih di TK**, lalu naik ke SD IT — `students.unit_id` berubah, baris riwayat TK-nya tetap tinggal.

| Dasbor | Aturan lama (`students.unit_id`) | Aturan baru (riwayat) |
|---|---|---|
| **TK Qur'an** | **0** | **7** |
| **SD IT** | **8** | **1** |

Dua kerusakan sekaligus: dasbor TK kehilangan seluruh minggu kehadiran anak itu pada detik kolomnya berubah, dan dasbor SD IT mengklaim 7 hari kehadiran yang terjadi di TK. Pengukurannya memakai aturan persis seperti yang dikirim kodenya — termasuk klausa cadangan di bawah — supaya angkanya bukan versi yang lebih bagus daripada yang benar-benar berjalan.

## Potongan `where`, bukan daftar id

`studentInUnitAt(unitId, tanggal)` mengembalikan `{ unitEnrollments: { some: … } }`, jadi kuerinya tetap **satu kueri dengan join**. Mengambil daftar id lebih dulu akan menambah satu kueri dan menghasilkan `IN (…)` sepanjang jumlah santri — di unit dengan ribuan santri itu kueri yang berbeda kelas beratnya. Bentuk relasi `student` sama di setiap model, jadi satu potongan ini cocok di ke-17 tempat.

Penyaring unit-nya terindeks: `student_unit_enrollments` punya indeks `(unit_id, academic_year_id)` dan `(student_id, entry_date)`, dan cabang cadangan (`none`) memakai awalan `student_id`.

## Santri tanpa riwayat tetap terhitung

Secara bawaan potongannya berbunyi: *punya baris riwayat yang mencakup tanggal itu*, **atau** *belum punya riwayat sama sekali dan unit sekarangnya ini*. Itu keputusan, bukan kelalaian — laporan yang diam-diam kehilangan orang lebih berbahaya daripada laporan yang memakai unit sekarang. Laporan historis nanti (akreditasi, angka tahun lalu) menyetel `termasukTanpaRiwayat: false`, karena di sana "tidak tahu" memang jawaban yang lebih jujur.

## Dua lubang jalur tulis ditutup

Supaya "tanpa riwayat" tidak jadi keadaan normal:

- `student.service.create` menerima `classId` sebagai **pilihan** — santri pindahan sering masuk sebelum rombelnya ditentukan.
- Orkestrator onboarding juga bisa dipanggil tanpa rombel.

Keduanya kini memanggil `ensureUnitEnrollment`, yang menyandarkan barisnya pada tahun ajaran aktif. Tanpa tahun ajaran aktif ia diam — dan itu aman, karena penyaringnya masih memasukkan santri tanpa riwayat.

## Tanggal yang dipakai

**Akhir rentang yang dilaporkan**, bukan hari ini. `getAttendanceStats` menerima rentang yang bisa historis; memakai hari ini di sana berarti menanyakan lagi "unit santri ini SEKARANG apa" — persis kekeliruan yang penukaran ini menghapus. Fungsi lain di modul ini rentangnya memang berakhir hari ini.

`prisma.student.count` untuk "berapa santri unit ini" sengaja **tidak** ditukar: itu pertanyaan tentang keadaan sekarang, dan `students.unit_id` adalah jawabannya.

## Verifikasi

- Gerbang lokal **ALL-PASS 10/10**.
- Uji baru di dasbor **dibuktikan merah** dengan mengembalikan satu penyaring ke bentuk lama: ia gagal sambil menyebut penyaringnya `{"unitId":"unit-tkq"}`, bukan riwayat.
- Uji potongan penyaring memastikan bentuk ketatnya tidak menyentuh `students.unit_id` sama sekali (satu kunci di tingkat atas), dan bentuk bawaannya memang punya cabang cadangan.

author: hd6vpgyj85-rgb
body:
## Causa real del bug reportado

El PR #3 corrigió las URLs del CDN del motor OCR y el fix ya estaba en producción, pero el usuario seguía viendo el escaneo colgado. La razón: esta es una PWA con Service Worker para soporte offline, y su estrategia de caché era **"caché primero"** para todo el código propio (`js/*`, `css/*`, `index.html`). Un teléfono que ya había abierto la app una vez (con el `ocr.js` viejo y roto) seguía sirviendo esa copia guardada para siempre, sin importar cuántas veces se corrigiera el archivo en el servidor — el Service Worker nunca volvía a pedirle el archivo a la red.

Encima, `_headers` agregaba una segunda capa del mismo problema: le decía al navegador que cacheara `js/*` y `css/*` hasta 24h sin revalidar con el servidor.

## Fix

- **`sw.js`**: estrategia "red primero" para el código propio — intenta la red, y solo si no hay conexión cae a la copia en caché (mantiene el soporte offline). Se sube la versión de caché (`v1` → `v2`) para forzar que los teléfonos que ya tenían la app abierta limpien lo que quedó guardado de antes.
- **`_headers`**: `js/*` y `css/*` pasan de `max-age=86400` a `no-cache` (el navegador revalida con el servidor en cada carga en vez de asumir que el archivo sigue vigente por un día entero).

## Validación

Reproduje el escenario exacto reportado con Playwright: un navegador que ya tenía cacheada una versión vieja de `ocr.js` (con un marcador falso) recibe el contenido real y actualizado en el siguiente reload, **sin que el usuario tenga que borrar datos del sitio a mano**. Repetí el flujo principal (alta/edición de productos, steppers) y el modo offline (la app sigue abriendo y mostrando datos sin conexión) — sin errores de consola ni regresión.

This pull request introduces advanced filtering and a new Notes Graph feature to Deckard, along with related UI updates and documentation improvements. Several commands and screenshots are added or updated to support these features, and minor bugs and UI issues have been fixed.

**Major feature additions:**

* **Advanced filtering in Entity Overview:** Users can now build complex Deckard queries using `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, parentheses, and field-specific conditions (e.g., `tag`, `text`, `task`, etc.) for more powerful searches. The advanced search UI supports completion and a visual builder. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR7-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R210-R239)

author: centralhardware
body:
A backfill read a chat's history far slower than Telegram hands it over, and nearly all of that was round trips the bot made itself, one after another.

**Two per message went to `peer_names::remember`.** It wrote the chat's and the sender's names whether or not they had changed — the repeats were left to the Buffer and `ReplacingMergeTree` to collapse, which is cheap in storage but is still an insert each, and a chat's whole history is thousands of inserts for one unchanging pair of names. It now remembers what it last wrote for a peer and writes again only when the names actually differ (`updated_at` excluded from the comparison — it is the version, not part of the identity). Live traffic saves the same two round trips per message.

**The rest was building the rows.** A reply target's lookup, a name, now and then Telegram for a topic title — all awaited in turn. A batch now builds up to 16 rows at once through a `JoinSet`, modest enough that the Telegram calls among them stay a trickle. A row that panics on the way is logged and dropped rather than taking the backfill with it.

What is left is the search itself, which is 100 messages per request and Telegram's own limit.
