author: sekkon0906
body:
Veintitrés commits. El grueso es **toda la configuración de la persona**, que era el hueco más grande que quedaba: había una pantalla de «Mi cuenta» donde solo se podía cambiar el nombre.

## La configuración, entera

| Qué | Dónde |
|---|---|
| Micrófono y cámara: elegirlos, **probarlos** y que se recuerden | `lib/dispositivos.ts`, `Dispositivos.tsx` |
| Foto de perfil **o** el personaje del DevVerse, a elegir | 0057, 0058, `Avatar.tsx`, `CaraDePersonaje.tsx` |
| De qué avisa la campana, y que lo silenciado ni se escriba | 0060, `Avisos.tsx` |
| El huso horario, que hasta ahora era UTC para todo el mundo | 0056, `huso_de()` |
| Qué datos de uno ve el resto, dicho sin adornos | `DatosVisibles.tsx` |
| Quién soy **en esta organización**: oficio y rol | `/organizations/:orgId/me` |

Tres decisiones que conviene mirar al revisar:

- **La cara se pide en bloque, no una por avatar.** `ProveedorDeCaras` junta todas las que se piden dentro del mismo tick y hace una sola petición. Una lista de cuarenta personas, si no, son cuarenta llamadas.
- **El huso no se detecta solo.** Se ofrece el del navegador como sugerencia y se guarda solo si se pulsa. Adivinarlo mueve las semanas de alguien que viaja sin que lo haya pedido.
- **Los interruptores de avisos están en positivo** («avísame»), aunque por dentro se guarde lo silenciado. Lo de dentro es lo correcto para la base —lo normal es querer todo, y una lista de excepciones no crece al añadir clases—; lo de fuera es lo que se lee bien la primera vez, que es la única que importa.

## Lo que estaba roto y no se veía

- **`/categorias` miraba la tabla equivocada.** Trabajaba sobre `tags` cuando las ramas de verdad son `task_categories`, y su «Jefe de rama» escribía en una columna que la 0050 había marcado obsoleta: elegir un jefe ahí no hacía nada. Un control que parecía funcionar.
- **El mapa de arquitectura mentía a favor.** El generador solo leía `routes/`, así que todo lo que vive en `lib/` salía como isla suelta. El documento afirmaba lo contrario de la verdad sobre media aplicación.
- **Un espacio de trabajo no se podía renombrar ni borrar** pese a que las políticas RLS existían desde la 0035. Una errata en el nombre era para siempre.
- **El botón de «dar código» a una invitación llevaba desactivado** con una nota diciendo que faltaba `set_invitation_code`. Entró en la 0047.
- **`tz` caía a UTC por defecto** en el diario, corriendo los cierres del domingo por la tarde a la semana siguiente en Colombia.

## El estado de la instalación

Saber si el almacén responde, si el correo sale o cuántas migraciones lleva la base exigía entrar por SSH. Ahora está al final de los ajustes de la organización, para quien la administre.

- **No devuelve ni un valor, solo estados.** Ni una clave, ni una dirección, ni un identificador de cliente: sale por la API a un navegador, y una pantalla de diagnóstico que enseña la mitad de un secreto es una filtración con buena intención.
- **Cuatro gravedades y no dos.** Una instalación sin Spotify está perfectamente bien; una sin TURN funciona hasta que dos personas en redes distintas intentan hablarse. Pintarlas igual enseña a ignorar el color.
- **Dice lo que no puede saber.** La imagen de la API no lleva `db/migrations`, así que cuenta las aplicadas pero no las que faltan. Inventar ese número daría «0 pendientes» siempre — la peor respuesta posible, porque tranquiliza.

## Migraciones

De la **0056 a la 0060**, todas con su política RLS y su caso en `isolation.test.ts`:

- `0056` el huso de cada quien, validado contra `pg_timezone_names`
- `0057` la foto de perfil — `set_my_avatar_key` devuelve la clave **anterior**, para poder borrar el objeto viejo
- `0058` el personaje del DevVerse como cara
- `0059` el recorrido de bienvenida visto
- `0060` los avisos silenciados; **reescribe `notify()`** para que lo silenciado no se escriba siquiera

## Un error que había cometido, corregido

En `SalaEspacial.tsx` había escrito que la capa de voz «reparte nombres y no identidades, y traerlo cruza el `useVoiceRoom` y la señalización». Era falso: el servidor manda `userId` en cada `publicMember`, `Participant` ya lo lleva, y `VoiceRoom` lo estaba tirando. Una línea, no un proyecto. Corregí el comentario en su sitio en vez de borrarlo sin más.

## Comprobado

`typecheck` limpio en los tres paquetes · `next build` completo · **305** aislamiento · **230** web · **170** MCP · **26** migraciones (60) · 19 invitación · 19 código.

## Después de fusionar, y esto bloquea a todo lo demás

**Aplicar las migraciones 0047–0060 contra Railway y desplegar.** El guardián de despliegue se para solo mientras haya alguna sin aplicar —está haciendo su trabajo—, así que **nada de esta tanda está vivo en producción todavía**. Incluye desplegar el MCP, que pasa de 15 a 21 herramientas.

Ojo con la **0055**: añade valores a un enumerado, y Postgres no deja usar un valor de enumerado en la misma transacción en que se crea. No se puede fusionar con otra ni partir por la mitad.

author: cosmicgrub
body:
## What

Implements the approved spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-parental-controls-pacing-design.md` — sub-project 2 of the onboarding/parental-controls arc. The first guardian-writable table that has ever actually controlled what a child can access: hide/show any ChildHome tile, game, joke, or drawing/activity outright (**Visibility**), or bidirectionally adjust/pre-empt the existing per-item age-based unlock (**Pacing**).

### Server
- `db/migrations/0033_guardian_activity_override.sql` — `guardian_activity_override(child_id, activity_key, visible, min_age_override, revealed_at, set_by, set_at)`. RLS mirrors `child_theme_preference` (0017) exactly: guardian `FOR ALL` via `actor_has_edge()`, child `SELECT`-only via `current_child()`, `ENABLE`+`FORCE`, no child write policy. Added to `health_check`'s `rls_unforced` list.
- `packages/db/src/pool.ts` — `activityOverridesFor()`, `setActivityOverride()`, `deleteActivityOverride()`.
- `server/routes.mjs` — `GET/PUT/DELETE /v1/children/:childId/activity-overrides[/:activityKey]` and `POST /v1/me/verify-controls-pin` (the screen-entry PIN gate, reusing `requireOwnPin()`).

### Client
- `client/lib/activity_overrides.dart` (new) — the one shared precedence function (`effectiveVisibility`/`isTileVisible`) every consumer calls, implementing `visible=false` always wins → `revealedAt` always shows → `minAgeOverride ?? catalogue default`.
- `client/lib/parental_controls_screen.dart` (new) — PIN-gated, guardian-only, off Guardian More's "Family setup". Visibility/Pacing tabs via `SegmentedButton`.
- `client/lib/game_logic.dart` — new `hubGameMinAge` map giving the 8 previously-ungated games (checkers, battleship, wordsearch, hangman, chess, word chain, Kim's game, scavenger hunt) a real `minAge`.
- Consumption wired into `child_home.dart`, `game_picker.dart`, `games_hub.dart`, `jokebook_screen.dart`, `child_more.dart`, fetched once per session in `child_home_live.dart`.

## Judgment calls (disclosed, per the task's own instruction)

1. **The 8 games' minAge values** — no existing values to port from anywhere (`games2.ts`'s `Kind2`/`games3.ts` have no minAge concept either). Assigned: checkers 6, battleship 7, wordsearch 6, hangman 6, chess 7, word chain 5, Kim's game 5, scavenger hunt 5. Reading-dependent games (wordsearch, hangman) skew older; chess gets this pass's highest floor for the deepest ruleset of any of the 20 games — capped at 7, not 8, because `games_hub_test.dart`'s own pre-existing "every board renders at the demo's default childAge (7)" test is real product coverage this pass must not silently regress.
2. **TS-side minAge — deliberately NOT added.** Confirmed via grep that `games2.ts`'s `Kind2` and `games3.ts` have no `minAge`/`CATALOGUE` concept at all server-side. Since the precedence rule is computed client-side (see #4), nothing in this feature reads a server-side minAge for these kinds, so none was added — the Dart-side `game_logic.dart` catalogue (extended with `hubGameMinAge`, additive) remains the sole source of truth for age-gating.
3. **The 8 games were NOT merged into `game_logic.dart`'s existing `catalogue`/`GameKind`/`forAge()`.** That trio is tightly coupled to `game_picker.dart`'s uniform `_GameCard` rendering (a per-`GameKind` color/icon `switch`) and `game_navigation.dart`'s exhaustive `switch (kind)` router — neither of which these 8 richer, individually-constructed game widgets were ever part of. Folding them in would have been a much larger, riskier refactor than this pass's actual scope. Instead, `game_logic.dart` gained a second, additive `hubGameMinAge` lookup.
4. **The precedence rule is implemented client-side** (`activity_overrides.dart`), not server-side in `packages/db/src/pool.ts` (the spec offered either). Only the Dart catalogues hold each item's own default minAge today; the server's job stays "store/serve the override rows as-is."
5. **The PIN-verify route** is `POST /v1/me/verify-controls-pin` — the spec's own offered example, taken verbatim. No existing route already answers "is this guardian's PIN correct, right now" on its own (`kiosk-pin/verify` checks every guardian of a child, a different question), so this is a new, narrow, identity-only route (no `:childId` — it gates the screen, not any one child's data).
6. **`minAgeOverride: null`** is accepted by the PUT route as an explicit reset of just the age override, independent of `visible`/`reveal`/`unreveal` — beyond the spec's literal body shape, a natural extension of it.
7. **The Visibility/Pacing tab switch uses `SegmentedButton`** — no `TabBar`/`TabController` precedent exists anywhere in this client (grepped). `SegmentedButton` is this app's own established two-way-switch convention (`doodle_desk.dart`'s `_ToolSwitch`).
8. **Doodle desk/Colouring get visibility-only overrides**, no pacing — neither has ever had a minAge concept anywhere in this client or server (confirmed by grep), matching the spec's own "this pass does not invent a minAge for surfaces that have never had one."
9. **"My day" and "Play together" are deliberately excluded** from the 6 ChildHome tiles this pass controls — the spec's own exact list (Storyteller, Homework, Messages, Show & tell, My list, More for you). "My day" is MASTERFILE's one signature element; "Play together" is a pure navigation door onto games/jokes this same table already controls item-by-item.
10. **Guardian_more.dart's own "Play together" preview (for favoriting) does not consume overrides in this pass** — the spec's consumer list names child-facing consumption specifically. A disclosed, reasonable scope boundary, not an oversight.

## A real bug found and fixed during testing

`game_picker.dart` and `jokebook_screen.dart` originally composed `forAge(age).where(effectiveVisibility(...))` — this applies the age gate **twice**, the second time unconditionally, so a guardian's `revealedAt` (meant to override the age gate) could never resurrect an item `forAge()` had already excluded before `effectiveVisibility` ever got a chance to reconsider it. Fixed by filtering the full catalogue through `effectiveVisibility` alone (which already reimplements `forAge`'s own comparison as its no-override fallback). Regression tests added in both files (and mirrored in `games_hub_test.dart`) using `childAge: 0` to make the bug fail loudly if it ever reappears.

## Tests

- `server/test/guardian_activity_override_route_test.mjs` — 46 assertions (PIN gate, dual-purpose GET, PUT validation/round-trips, DELETE, RLS-shaped fake pool proving the "no system role" design).
- `packages/db/test/guardian_activity_override.test.mjs` — 32 assertions, **real Postgres RLS** (guardian read/write via live edge, child read-only her own row, no cross-child leakage, no system-role backstop).
- `client/test/parental_controls_screen_test.dart` — 13 assertions (PIN gate, both tabs, toggle/stepper/reveal round-trips, and a direct unit proof of the precedence rule).
- Extended `game_picker_test.dart`, `games_hub_test.dart`, `jokebook_screen_test.dart`, `child_more_test.dart`, `child_home_test.dart` with real visibility/pacing/reveal consumption tests (including the regression tests above).

## Verification

Ran the equivalent of `tools/verify.sh` locally (this Windows sandbox has no native `psql`; used a fresh, isolated Docker Postgres + WSL Ubuntu for the raw-SQL suites, matching verify.sh's own sequence and role provisioning exactly — added the two new suites to `tools/verify.sh`'s own suite lists so a real CI run exercises them too):

- **7650 assertions, 0 failed** — 65 JS suites + demo (3780), 6 raw-SQL suites (101), 35 real-RLS DB suites (1247), 2522 Dart tests, all from actual runs, none estimated.
- `flutter analyze`: 0 issues.
- `tools/check-markup.mjs --total 7650`: 44/44 passed (MARKUP/CHANGELOG/DEMO/MASTERFILE all in step).
- **Pre-existing gaps, unrelated to this PR, confirmed and disclosed rather than papered over:** Android SDK and a `livekit-server` binary are absent in this san

author: leamonline
body:
## What this is

The Cloudflare Turnstile captcha on both login pages is issued, solved, and then ignored. The token is handed to Supabase as `options.captchaToken`, but Supabase only verifies it — by calling Cloudflare's siteverify endpoint — when CAPTCHA protection is enabled under Authentication → Attack Protection. It is not.

Two independent pieces of evidence agree:

- The widget ("Customer Log-in Capture") reported **0 siteverify requests against 5 solved challenges** in 24 hours, with Cloudflare showing a warning that siteverify is not being called.
- A direct probe of the production token endpoint reached the password check **both with an invalid captcha token and with none at all**.

That is worse than having no captcha. The widget tells visitors they are passing a security check, the README described Turnstile as "login CAPTCHA", the architecture overview listed it under "login abuse protection", and a comment in `useCustomerAuth.ts` asserted that protection "is" on for OTP. Every one of those was false, and each discouraged the next person from checking.

The decision was to **make it real rather than remove it**: `sendOtp` calls `signInWithOtp({ phone })` directly from the browser with no Edge Function in front, so the salon pays for every SMS an automated caller can provoke.

## Before merging: confirm `VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` is set in Vercel Production

Merging auto-deploys, and these pages now fail closed — with no site key they render no challenge and disable sign-in for staff and customers alike. I've verified the key *is* live today by finding `0x4AAAAAADMvAmN7LsBYiIqZ` baked into both the `LoginPage` and `CustomerApp` chunks of the production bundle, with the test key appearing nowhere. Worth a second pair of eyes on the Vercel dashboard all the same, since this repo has already shipped one `VITE_` name that was assumed present and wasn't.

## What this changes at merge, before any toggle

Enabling verification is an **owner action** requiring the widget's secret key, and this PR does not do it. For almost everyone, merging changes nothing.

**One exception, and I got this wrong in an earlier description of the work.** The missing-token guards are client-side and unconditional — they don't consult the Supabase setting. So a visitor whose browser can't load `challenges.cloudflare.com` (an extension, a corporate filter, a blocked region) can sign in today, because the token is optional and Supabase ignores it, and cannot once this merges. That's the intended trade — a captcha nobody can solve shouldn't be waved through — but it's a deploy-time behaviour change, not a toggle-time one, and the same correction has been made in the design and the runbook.

It also means rollback is narrower than first stated: turning the Supabase setting back off reverses *enforcement*, but does nothing for someone whose challenge script never loads. That case needs a code revert.

**Next step after merging:** follow [the runbook](docs/superpowers/runbooks/2026-09-11-login-captcha-enablement.md).

## The baseline, verbatim

```
  invalid captcha token — not-enforced (HTTP 400)
  no captcha token — not-enforced (HTTP 400)

Login captcha is NOT ENFORCED: Supabase reached the password check with
a bad captcha token. The Turnstile widget on the login pages is being
solved and then ignored — no siteverify call is made.
Enable CAPTCHA under Authentication -> Attack Protection. See
docs/superpowers/runbooks/2026-09-11-login-captcha-enablement.md
```

Exit code 1. Run `npm run check:captcha` again after flipping the toggle; it should report ENFORCED on both probes, and the informational `/verify` line should stay `not-enforced`.

## What changed

**Fail closed instead of always passing.** The site key was a one-line fallback to Cloudflare's always-passes test key whenever `VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` was absent — and an empty string slipped through too, since `??` only catches `undefined`. `src/lib/turnstile.ts` replaces it with a pure resolver mirroring the existing `supabaseConfigError` idiom: a real key wins; `forceOffline` short-circuits first; a production build with no key, or with the test key set explicitly, renders no widget, disables sign-in and reports to Sentry.

**Guarded the token on the staff page.** Sign-in and password reset both previously dropped the captcha option when the ref was empty (`...(captchaToken ? { captchaToken } : {})`). Once protection is on, that returns a raw `captcha protection: request disallowed`. Both paths now refuse to submit until the widget has produced a token — the guard the customer page already had.

**`npm run check:captcha`.** Built on the `check-sentry-live.mjs` idiom, because this repo already treats "is this control actually live?" as a repeatable script rather than a dashboard screenshot. Two probes against the deployed project; three-state verdict so an unrecognised response reports `unknown` rather than the reassuring answer. It probes the password grant **only** — never `/auth/v1/otp`, which sends a real SMS at real cost when captcha is not enforced.

**Corrected the documentation** that asserted protection which did not exist, and added the owner runbook.

## What review and a completeness sweep changed

Two rounds of review found things worth naming, because most of them were mine.

**The settings page was lying.** Settings → Your Account → "Send password reset link" discarded the result of the call and showed "✓ Link sent — check your email" regardless. That was survivable while every send worked; it stops being survivable the moment captcha is on, because it reaches the gated `/recover` endpoint and has no widget to produce a token. A staff member locked out would have waited for an email that was never sent. It now tells the truth and points at "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page, which carries a working challenge. This was the sixth auth call site — the branch had covered five.

**A captcha rejection was being reported as "wrong password" everywhere.** A six-modality sweep confirmed the call-site enumeration was complete, but its completeness critic caught that the `isCaptchaRejection` helper was wired into the two password-*reset* paths and zero *sign-in* paths. So the runbook's own first-listed post-toggle failure — the Supabase secret key not matching the rendered site key — would have told staff their password was wrong and sent customers to correct a phone number that was never the problem. Fixed in all three paths.

**And one of my own comments was false.** I wrote that `verifyOtp` takes no captcha token, phrased as "please don't fix this". The pinned SDK does have `VerifyMobileOtpParams.options.captchaToken`; it's `@deprecated`, which supports the conclusion but isn't the contract I claimed. On a branch that exists because a confident comment stopped people checking, that's the one mistake worth flagging loudest. The comment now separates established from inferred, and `check:captcha` gained an informational `/verify` probe so it's settled by measurement instead.

## Deferred, with reasons

The [July legal-risk design](docs/archive/superpowers/specs/2026-07-12-legal-risk-remediation-design.md) required Turnstile to be verified in the Edge Function too. It cannot be bolted on: Turnstile tokens are single-use, and the customer flow deliberately carries one token from the `checkPhone` pre-flight into the follow-up auth call. Verifying inside `customer-phone-on-file` would consume it and break login. Doing it properly needs a second challenge round and a real UX change — and that endpoint is already the best-protected one, with two-tier per-IP and global rate limiting. Raising it as its own issue.

## Verification

- Full CI bar on Node 24: `lint` · `check:docs` · `typecheck` · `check:migrations` · `test` · `build` — all pass.
- E2E 49/49 on the desktop project. "Customer portal shows the phone OTP entry screen" passing is the direct proof the `forceOffline` carve-out works: E2E is a productio

author: henrypinkard
body:
From main dc8ad7fb.

**What.** The auto-nudge walk parsed every alive session on every pass, cold at boot: on the first boot with per-stage byte rows it took 58.9 s of a 63 s first cycle. Its parse is gated now. A session whose files are unchanged since its last completed look, and whose clock legs have not come due, skips the parse; the skip repeats the recorded verdict and does nothing else. The pass walks sessions by recency and, while a client is connected, yields after a look that paid a cold parse; the first deferred session is the resume cursor, so the next pass rotates the order to start there and every session is reached within as many passes as there are cold parses.

**How.** The ten files the memo keys on: the transcript, the state log, the goal store with its override journal and archive, the episode log, the clears log, the postal log, the kernel's downtime log (the working verdict's suspension check reads a list that log refills) and the nudge ledger. The pass takes every session's stat before it reads any pass-level snapshot (the ledger, the peer graph, the clear set) and hands that stat to the look, so the memo's key is older than every input the verdict read. Each clock leg that declines notes the instant it could flip (the parked, wake, lost-send and moot dead-men; the redundancy skip notes the park it opens); a leg whose release is not one of those files notes an unbounded release (a standing deferral, a stamped wait, a store fault, an ask from a peer not alive now, a refused ledger write). Only a look whose verdict came from a road marked file-keyed (`working`, `user-interrupt`, `progressing`, `closer-unsettled`, `planner-queue`, each with the files it reads named beside it) or from the full goal walk run to its end records a skippable memo; every other exit records an unbounded one by default, so an unaudited road can never silence a session. A completed look records the files' stat, the earliest flip and the verdict in the persisted tick memo, which survives a restart; a wake-only look (nudges off) neither skips nor records. The gate is a decorator, so the look's own source stays what the pinning tests read. A due nudge fires no later than today: a skip lasts only until the earliest instant any clock leg it saw could fire, and every other change reaches the files.

**Instruments.** `memos.nudgeWalk` on the perf page: looks, skipped and paid parses, cold parses, deferred sessions, memos refused as unbounded or clock-due, wake-only looks. The boot-health row carries `nudgeWalk`: eight characters of the session ids whose parses the boot's walk skipped and parsed (at most forty each), and how many it deferred. The row is the proof: the next boot's `jobs.autoNudge` against this one's 58.9 s.

**Rounds.** One: the redundancy skip's dead-man noted, the skip road sends nothing, the memo round-trips through the loader, the yield keys on the current cold parse with a resume cursor, the stat covers the store's identity files and the walk's logs. Two: the class fix (file-keyed roads marked, every other exit unbounded), the store-fault leg, the dead asker's ask, the postal log among the memo's files.

**Tests.** One parse across two looks of an unchanged session and a re-evaluation when the transcript moves; a look that never parsed records nothing; a noted flip evaluates when due and an unbounded note never skips; a redundancy skip notes the parked dead-man and the backstop fires at +6 h on the real look; the skip road sends nothing; the memo survives a restart through the loader; the ten files each end the skip; the pass walks by recency and resumes at the deferred session; the row's ids; wake-only looks; the census of file-keyed roads and the unbounded default (a store fault, a dead peer's ask); the memos and the boot row carry the walk.

Tier: feature

**Rounds three to six.** Three: the downtime log as the ninth keyed file; the annotation table traced. Four: the rewind-pending gate above the marked roads (a pending cut rides the parse's cache key with no file change); the census a transitive trace over each marked road's helpers against an allowlist of keyed-file readers, memos keyed on keyed files, counters and constants; a queued lost send unbounded; a closer-unsettled memo void with the closer off; the recency sort reads the row's mtime. Five: the downtime record appends before it writes (the reader's key moves last); the census treats a class as live state unless justified, checks builtins against the builtins module and resolves names in each function's own globals; tests for the write order, a failed write, the closer toggle and a queued lost send. Six: the pass stats every session before any snapshot and hands the stat to the look (an undo landing between a pass-top snapshot and a look had silenced the un-cleared goal under a memo keyed after the undo); the nudge ledger is the tenth keyed file; the census states the shapes it does not trace. The served fold-checkpoints lab states the gate's contract: at a second boot the walk skips every unchanged session, so its folds resume only for the sessions it looked at.

**Module set the counts come from** (one executed run on the head, devbox, capped): tests/test_nudge_walk_parse_gate.py tests/test_boot_parse_gating.py tests/test_nudge_memo_deadlock.py tests/test_judge.py tests/test_wake_deadman_toggle.py tests/test_setting_gesture_order.py tests/test_nudge_bundle.py tests/test_kernel_interrupt.py tests/test_kernel_nudge_last_resort.py tests/test_kernel_interrupt_machine_cut.py tests/test_skill_load_wrapper.py tests/test_nudge_gate_memo.py tests/test_nudge_injected_turn_arm.py tests/test_nudge_fresh_guard.py tests/test_kernel.py tests/test_first_cycle_stage_split.py tests/test_assembly_road_counters.py tests/test_restart_phases.py; plus tests/test_perf_stats.py and tests/test_fold_checkpoints_served.py alone.

author: irinanazarova
body:
Treat the five error pages that `rails new` writes into `public/` as generated, so that a new Ruby on Rails application is classified as Ruby rather than HTML.

## Description

### Motivation

Every new Rails application since Rails 8.0 is reported as an **HTML** repository on GitHub. Measured on a uniform sample of 20,000 HTML-primary repositories per year, Rails applications reported as HTML run at about 600 a month in 2025 and about 1,100 a month in 2026. Any statistic derived from GitHub language data, such as new Rails applications or new Ruby developers, undercounts Ruby.

`rails new` writes five static error pages (`400.html`, `404.html`, `406-unsupported-browser.html`, `422.html`, `500.html`). Since Rails 8.0 they total about 36 KB of HTML, while a freshly generated application contains about 24 KB of Ruby. Linguist picks the primary language by byte count, so the application is HTML until its author has written roughly 13 KB of Ruby.

### Reproduction

Before: https://github.com/irinanazarova/rails-new is the unmodified output of `rails _8.1.3.1_ new rails-new --skip-bundle`. GitHub reports it as HTML (57.9% HTML, 35.5% Ruby).

After: https://github.com/irinanazarova/rails-new-amended is the same application with the five files marked `linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes`. GitHub reports it as Ruby (80%).

### Detail

Adds `generated_rails_error_page?` to `generated.rb`. A file qualifies only if its path is `public/<one of the five names>.html` **and** it contains the marker comment the Rails generator has written into each page since Rails 3.0, naming that same path (`<!-- This file lives in public/404.html -->`). A page a developer has rewritten without the marker, or the same content under another path, is not affected. Fixtures are the untouched output of `rails new` on Rails 8.1.3.1, plus a hand-written `public/404.html` asserting no match.

### Why in Linguist, given the Rails-side fix

Rails has merged the companion change, rails/rails#58693, which adds these five `linguist-generated` entries to the `.gitattributes` of every newly generated application. That covers applications generated with future Rails releases. It does not reach the applications generated with Rails 8.0 and 8.1 since November 2024, nor applications created with `--skip-git`, which get no `.gitattributes`. This heuristic covers those on their next statistics run.

## Checklist:

- [x] **I am adding new or changing current functionality**
- [x] I have added or updated the tests for the new or changed functionality.

author: ajinsunny
body:
Two related but separable bodies of work. **Nothing here changes what the site
serves**, and that is verified rather than asserted (see Verification).

---

## Part 1: GEO audit follow-ups (`0fe55cb`)

Acting on the September audit.

**Performance**
- Dropped the `supabase` `manualChunk`. Rollup was hoisting the CommonJS interop
  helper into it, which turned a 223KB chunk into a *static* import from the entry
  rather than a lazy one.
- Removed the Google Fonts `@import` from `index.css`. Geist is self-hosted and the
  three imported families were unused. Dropped the dead `.font-serif-instrument`
  classes with it.
- Added immutable `Cache-Control` for `/assets` and `/fonts`. Production was serving
  `max-age=0, must-revalidate` on content-hashed files.

**SEO and GEO**
- Homepage title and hero now lead with the definitional sentence ("cash flow
  forecasting") instead of the benefit line.
- Fixed the H1 rendering twice in the DOM text. `TextHoverHalo` takes a `text` string
  and draws the gradient from a CSS pseudo-element.
- Added Pricing to the navbar; pointed "Get Started" at `START_TRIAL_URL`.
- Linked the comparison pages from the footer. They were reachable only from
  `/llm-info` and carried no internal link equity.
- Reciprocal links between the two payroll posts, and compare links from the
  QuickBooks post.
- Visible "Updated" date, rendered only when `dateModified` differs from `date`, so
  the on-page signal matches `BlogPosting.dateModified`.

**Schema**
- Removed the `SoftwareApplication` `review` node. It carried a 5/5 rating with no
  `reviewBody` and was not visible anywhere on the page, which Google's structured
  data policy does not allow.

**Privacy**
- Marketing consent no longer gates delivery of a calculator breakdown. Bundling the
  two made the opt-in a condition of a service the user had asked for, which GDPR
  Art. 7(4) does not treat as freely given.
- The opt-in was never recorded anywhere. `marketingConsent` now reaches the API,
  `ToolEmailRequest`, and the lead notification, giving an Art. 7(1) record. Anything
  that is not a literal `true` records as no consent.

Also fixes `cash-conversion-cycle`, which was missing from `blog-stats.ts` entirely
and had no OG card, so it shipped with no `wordCount`/`images` in its JSON-LD.

---

## Part 2: domain-move preparation (`1efdba7`, `113d05a`, `38fc0d0`)

Groundwork for moving the marketing site to `zensus.finance`. The app, API, and email
stay on `zensus.app`; the product repo needs **zero** changes.

All of it ships on the current domain, so the risky mechanical work is reviewed and
live before any DNS moves.

**Google One Tap removed.** It signed the visitor in on `zensus.app` and relied on
Supabase stamping cookies `Domain=.zensus.app` so `app.zensus.app` could read them at
handoff. A cookie carries exactly one `Domain` attribute and no form of it spans two
registrable domains, so there is no dual-domain configuration. Users now sign in on the
app, which already supports Google independently.

Knock-on effects, all wanted:
- `@supabase/ssr` and `@supabase/supabase-js` leave `package.json`. The built output no
  longer contains the string `supabase` at all.
- CSP sheds `accounts.google.com`, `*.supabase.co`, `wss://*.supabase.co` and
  `www.google.com`.
- Google Cloud Console and Supabase drop off the migration's vendor list entirely.

**One origin, declared once.** The origin was hardcoded 476 times across 89 files with
no constant to flip. It is now `SITE_URL`, declared three times because three runtimes
need it and none can import the others (`src/lib/constants.ts`, `scripts/site.mjs`,
`api/_lib/site.ts`). `src/lib/site-url.test.ts` asserts the three agree and that no bare
`https://zensus.<tld>` literal survives anywhere in `src/`, `api/` or `scripts/`.

Removed from the migration surface permanently:
- 84 absolute self-links across 12 posts are now site-relative. 55 were homepage
  fragment deep-links that no path-based redirect review would have caught.
- `meta.ogImage` is a site-relative path, resolved against `SITE_URL` at render.
- The OG card footer and the XLSX note take the domain from `SITE_HOST` rather than
  having it baked into 30 committed PNGs.

**Deduplicated the origin allow-list.** `api/acknowledge.ts` and
`api/tools/send-results.ts` each carried their own copy of the same regex, so widening
it meant remembering to edit both, and missing one silently 403s either the support form
or the calculator email. They now share `isAllowedOrigin()`, with tests for the cases a
prefix or suffix check gets wrong.

---

## ⚠️ `tsc --noEmit` in this repo checks nothing

Worth its own attention. The root `tsconfig.json` is a solution file (`"files": []` plus
project references), so a bare `tsc --noEmit` exits 0 **no matter what is broken**. It
passed on 15 files of invalid JSX during this work; only `vite build` caught them.

Added `npm run typecheck` (`tsc -b`), fixed the four pre-existing mock-typing errors it
surfaces in `events.test.ts`, and documented the trap in `CLAUDE.md`. **This is worth
adding to CI** since nothing currently type-checks this repo.

---

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean
- **100 tests across 18 files** (was 93 across 17)
- Full build with Puppeteer prerender writes all 34 routes
- Em-dash check clean across 158 files
- **All 7 sampled prerendered pages are byte-identical to their pre-refactor output**
  once content-hashed asset filenames are normalised. `sitemap.xml` and the XLSX both
  regenerate with zero diff.

## Deliberately not here

The Terms and Privacy prose and the PostHog cookie disclosure at `Privacy.tsx:219` and
`:254`. Those are factual claims about the live state: the new wording describes
`zensus.app` redirecting to `zensus.finance` and each site setting its own analytics
cookie, neither of which is true until cutover. Shipping them early would put an
inaccuracy in the legal pages. They land in the cutover commit.

author: lessevv
body:
Found by asking SonarCloud where the uncovered lines are. The project is at **93.0% coverage, 0 bugs, 0 vulnerabilities, 0 hotspots, 0 code smells** — so the honest remaining signal is *which* branches nothing runs. `MobileFirstLaunchBootstrap` was **4 covered lines of 46**, the least-tested class in the product, on the path that runs once per phone and cannot be retried.

## The defect

`runPendingMigrations()` records whether the schema is whole in a `finally`. That bookkeeping asks the database **the same question that just failed** — `hasPendingMigrations()` reads the migrations repository. When the run died because the database is unusable, the read throws too, and **a throw from a `finally` replaces the exception on its way out**.

Measured, with a run that throws `migration 2 of 190 failed` over a repository that then throws `no such table: migrations`:

| | before |
|---|---|
| escaping exception | `no such table: migrations` |
| marker raised by the class | `false` |

So `mobile-app/bootstrap/app.php` logged **a symptom of the first failure as the cause of it**. Whoever read that log on a device that would not start went looking for a missing migrations table — and this repo already has the invariant that an error must not name a cause that was itself caused by the real one.

The sibling test file records what this path costs when it goes wrong: *"the welcome screen opened over fifteen tables of a hundred and two. Every tap after that was a 500 and the only trace was a log line reading 'failed non-fatally'."*

## The fix

`recordSchemaCompletion()` cannot throw now. On any failure it **raises** the marker rather than clearing it — of everything that can go wrong in there, the one answer that must never be reached by accident is *"the schema is whole"* — and the migration's own exception reaches the caller intact.

**Stated honestly:** the marker half was already covered at the call site, whose `catch (Throwable)` raises it on any throw. This is the second line, not the only one. It is the line that holds if the class is ever called from anywhere else, and the wrong-cause logging was not covered anywhere.

## Ten tests over branches nothing ran

The repository absent and present; a run that leaves work behind and one that does not; the repository created before the first run so something can record it; both failure arms above; the plugin view directories the bundler strips from every NativePHP package; and the canonical database path.

Inverted — fix reverted, tests kept — exactly those two arms fail, and the message names the substitution:

```
Expected: no such table: migrations
To contain: migration 2 of 190 failed
```

## Verified

`phpstan analyse Modules/Mobile` clean. `Modules/Mobile/tests` + `CommentPolicyArchTest`: **986 passed, 45 skipped, 0 failed.**

## Fork renewal 2026-09-14

Continues this PR (opened 2026-09-13) rather than stacking a new one: its base
(`origin/main`) had not moved since it branched, so per the standing renewal
policy this session updated the existing branch instead of opening a second PR.

**Drift measured at session start (before this update):**
`HEAD..upstream/main` = 632 commits, `upstream/main..HEAD` = 1 commit.
That large number is `origin/main`'s own drift, not this branch's: `origin/main`
is stale relative to this already-in-flight renewal, which had previously
merged upstream through 10 commits.
Compared directly against this branch's own prior head, the real remaining
drift was 3 new upstream commits (`HEAD..upstream/main` = 0 after this
session's merge).

**Branch:** `chore/upstream-renewal-2026-09-13` (unchanged)

### Merge

`git merge upstream/main` (commit `3c00b0d`) pulled in the 3 new upstream
commits since the branch's prior state:

- `305dfff` fix(bin): pre-approve external CLAUDE.md import dialog for spawned workers (#3944)
- `ecfe071` fix(afk-return): treat an acked watcher-down marker as no gap (#4355)
- `b182d0f` fix(bin): rebind fm-procevent-when trust bindings after a self-update (#4361)

**Conflicting files: none.** Git's `ort` merge strategy auto-merged every
touched file cleanly (`CONTRIBUTING.md`, `bin/fm-afk-return.sh`,
`docs/configuration.md`, `tests/fm-afk-return.test.sh`) with no conflict
markers, so no manual resolution judgment was required this round.

  round (the known trap this task warned about).
- `docs/fm-test-portable-shards.md` already documents the "derived from a live
  command" model — `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` is the current
  account of lane size, shard composition, and balance rather than a copied

- `CI=true bin/fm-lint.sh`: clean (full ShellCheck extended analysis enabled)
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage`: `FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=209 parallel=24 parallel_max_ms=417163 parallel_imbalance_ms=2894 parallel_unhinted=0 serial=169 serial_shards=5 serial_unhinted=17 herdr=16`
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`: `ok surfaces=105 local_links=414`
- Targeted tests for every file this merge touched (`tests/fm-afk-return.test.sh`, `tests/fm-claude-trust.test.sh`, `tests/fm-procevent-when.test.sh`, `tests/fm-update.test.sh`): all passed, `FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=4 failed=0`

### no-mistakes gate (run `01M2F13DMYRBVTW63YKM0CS1CN`)

- `intent`: skipped
- `rebase`: completed
- `review`: completed after 2 fix rounds. 7 findings surfaced (2 auto-fix, 2 ask-user, 3 no-op/info):
  - **Applied** (auto-fix): `bin/fm-claude-trust.sh` — a worktree's own recorded
    declined-external-imports flag could be silently overridden by the primary
    project's carried-forward consent; now also checked against the target
    (worktree) entry itself.
  - **Applied** (auto-fix, corrected mid-review): `bin/fm-update.sh` — a failed
    `fm-procevent-when.sh rebind-all` was silently swallowed (`|| true`). The

  - **Accepted as-is** (ask-user, decided by judgment): `afk-return-acked-gap-suppression`
    — a plausible corner case where a second real watcher outage during an

  - No action (no-op/informational): `nudge-pid1-numeric-match`,

author: jonbj
body:
## Cosa cambia e perché

La prima tranche della PoC è già arrivata su `main` con la PR #529, ma la verifica contro il codice reale ha mostrato che uno degli edge case obbligatori della issue non era soddisfatto: il client aveva un timeout esplicito di 10 secondi, però `TimeoutError` e gli errori di rete `aiohttp` uscivano da `fetch_symbol()` e interrompevano l’intera coorte. Questa PR rende il guasto locale al solo simbolo: lo registra nel log, non produce righe spurie e lascia proseguire i simboli successivi.

La correzione è guidata da un test di regressione che simula AAPL in timeout e una risposta valida per MSFT. Prima del fix il test falliva sul `TimeoutError`; dopo il fix riceve l’item MSFT, osserva due tentativi HTTP e trova il timeout nel log.

Ho ripetuto anche il Passo 0 con la chiave reale. La risposta mantiene lo schema già documentato (`status`, `pagination`, `press_releases`; record con `id`, `datetime`, `title`, `body`, `style`, `language`, senza `url`/`source`). Oggi il simbolo invalido restituisce HTTP 404 con errore strutturato; ACRS restituisce HTTP 200 e lista vuota. `symbol=AAPL,MSFT` restituisce gli stessi record di AAPL, mentre `from`/`to`, `range` e `limit=1` risultano accettati ma ignorati, confermando che la raccolta deve restare monoticker e deduplicata lato nostro.

## Come si verifica

Eseguire:

```bash
python3 -m pytest \
  tests/connectors/test_twelve_data_press_releases.py \
  tests/migrations/test_news_poc_samples_migration.py \
  tests/scripts/test_poc_twelve_data_shadow.py -q
```

Atteso: `28 passed`. Per vedere direttamente la regressione:

```bash
python3 -m pytest \
  tests/connectors/test_twelve_data_press_releases.py::test_fetch_timeout_skips_symbol_and_continues_others -q
```

Atteso: `1 passed`; la richiesta successiva al simbolo in timeout viene eseguita e produce il campione MSFT.

## Perimetro restante e freeze

Non ho modificato soglie, pesi, flag, cooldown, configurazione di strategia, beat Celery o path live. L’eventuale integrazione live resta fuori perimetro e richiede una decisione separata dopo la misura; durante il freeze non viene anticipata.

Questa PR non chiude ancora la issue. Il database configurato localmente contiene la migration ma, al 2026-09-13, ha zero righe Twelve Data sia in `news_poc_samples` sia nel ledger `news_poc_request_budget`: la raccolta manuale delle cinque sedute non è mai iniziata. Restano quindi da eseguire cinque sedute reali e pubblicare il report richiesto su copertura, overlap con Alpaca/SEC, latenza p50/p95, lunghezza del body, correttezza ticker e consumo richieste. Non ho fabbricato un report senza campione.

author: keanji-x
body:
## Summary

- Every visible temp-directory leak class found in the self-hosted runner's `RUNNER_TEMP` (one directory per test per CI run, 65 `neige-app-*` prefixes + `neige-timeout-lease-*` + the `neige-codex-homes-stub-*`/`neige-calm-test-workspaces-*` pair) now owns its directory through an RAII `tempfile::TempDir`, so a private `TMPDIR` is empty after the affected tests run.
- The self-hosted Rust job allocates a job-private `TMPDIR` under `RUNNER_TEMP` (`mktemp -d "$RUNNER_TEMP/rust-XXXXXXXX"`) and removes exactly that directory in an `if: always()` step, because this runner does not empty `RUNNER_TEMP` between jobs; the comment claiming it does is replaced with what is true.

## Why

#1637: `/home/runner/actions-runner-neige-calm/_work/_temp` has accumulated 10 772 visible + 8 621 hidden top-level entries (502 MB) since the runner went live on 2026-09-03, at ~70 new entries per run. The runner never cleans it. The sources are tests that create `temp_dir().join(..)` paths by hand and never remove them, plus one test whose child process is SIGKILLed while owning an `AppState` (whose `TempDir`s can then never unwind).

## Changes

- `crates/neige-app/src/test_support.rs` (new): one `test_temp_dir(name) -> TestTempDir` (RAII, `Deref<Target = Path>` so the 69 call sites keep `tmp.join(..)`); the nine identical per-module copies are deleted. `tests/apply_e2e.rs` is a bin-crate integration test and cannot import it, so its `test_root` is the same three-line `tempfile::Builder` call; `Harness.root` becomes a `TempDir` that drops after the explicit `Drop` has killed the children (same order as before). `tempfile` added to `[dev-dependencies]` (`Cargo.lock`: one line).
- `crates/calm-server/tests/scheduler.rs`: `seed_held_workspace_lease` returns `(lease_id, TempDir)`; the five callers hold the guard. Prefix `neige-timeout-lease-<label>-` kept.
- `crates/calm-server/tests/cases/replay_bin_stdout_close.rs`: the replay child (built via `boot_in_memory` → `CodexClient::new_stub()` + `AppState::from_parts…`, ended only by `ChildGuard`'s SIGKILL) gets a test-owned `TMPDIR`, declared before the guard so the child is reaped before the directory is removed. This is the single per-run leaker of the `neige-codex-homes-stub-*` / `neige-calm-test-workspaces-*` pair (evidence: each leaked pair shares one mtime and the newest pair's mtime falls inside this test's window in the runner's junit for run 34734926758; running the test alone in a private `TMPDIR` leaves exactly that pair).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: prepare step allocates `$RUNNER_TEMP/rust-XXXXXXXX` as `TMPDIR`; new final step `remove job-private TMPDIR` (`if: always() && runner.environment == 'self-hosted'`) removes it through a `case` guard that only accepts `"$RUNNER_TEMP"/rust-*` and refuses any path containing `..` (exit 1, nothing removed). Hosted branch and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` untouched.

## Verification

Private `T=$(mktemp -d /mnt/data2/kenji/neige-calm/.claude/worktrees/1637-tmp-XXXX)`, leftovers = `find "$T" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 | wc -l`; all cargo commands foreground with `env -u NEIGE_CODEX_BIN RUSTC_WRAPPER= CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 TMPDIR=$T nice -n 10`.

| scope | command | leftovers before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| neige-app | `cargo nextest run --locked -p neige-app --test-threads 8` | 65 (`153 tests run: 153 passed, 18 skipped`) | 0 (`153 tests run: 153 passed, 18 skipped`) |
| scheduler + replay | `cargo nextest run --locked --features calm-server/codex-e2e -p calm-server --test scheduler --test replay_event_suite --test-threads 8 -E 'test(/seed_held_workspace_lease\|sweep_running_codex/) \| test(replay_survives_stdout_pipe_close)'` | 7 (5 lease dirs + the stub/workspaces pair; `6 tests run: 6 passed, 266 skipped`) | 0 (`6 tests run: 6 passed, 266 skipped`) |
| panic path | temporary probe test that created the dir, wrote a file and panicked | — | 0 leftovers after `1 test run: 0 passed, 1 failed`; probe removed |

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked -p neige-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` → 0 warnings
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked -p calm-server --features calm-server/codex-e2e --test scheduler --test replay_event_suite -- -D warnings` → 0 warnings
- [x] `cargo metadata --locked --offline` → OK
- [x] ci.yml: `yaml.safe_load` OK; both step scripts extracted verbatim and exercised against a scratch `RUNNER_TEMP`: allocate → remove leaves siblings untouched; `''`, `$RUNNER_TEMP`, `$RUNNER_TEMP/other`, `/tmp/rust-zzz`, `$RUNNER_TEMP/rust-x/..`, `$RUNNER_TEMP/rust-x/../..` all refused with exit 1 and nothing removed
- [x] one `#[ignore]`d `apply_e2e` Harness test (`apply_preserving_commits_calm_server_change`) run with a short `TMPDIR` to exercise the changed `Drop`: PASS, 0 leftovers (under a 60+-char `TMPDIR` it fails on the fake calm-server's 114-byte unix socket path — pre-existing SUN_LEN limit, unrelated)

Not verified here: the ci.yml change can only be proven on the runner — after merge, the `main` run must create and then remove a `_temp/rust-XXXXXXXX` directory and add no new `neige-*` entries to `_temp`.

Known remaining leak class (not in this PR): 8 621 hidden `.tmpXXXXXX` directories in `_temp` (≈53 per run; mostly empty or a bare `git init`), likely from process-lifetime `static OnceLock<TempDir>` roots (`tests/scheduler.rs:98`, `src/operation/child_track_adapter.rs:566`) and the `proc_supervisor.rs:18` `Box::leak` fixture. The job-private `TMPDIR` removes them in CI; the code-side fix is a separate slice.

## Risk and rollback

Low risk: test-only Rust changes plus a CI step whose `rm -rf` is fail-closed on path shape. If the cleanup step misfires it exits 1 and removes nothing. Revert the single squash commit to roll back.

## Related issues

Closes #1637.

author: demandal25
body:
Follow-up to #364, addressing the three review comments that were still open when it merged.

## Summary

#364 claimed to make 23 benchmark routines runnable on ROCm. It made 21: both Gemma routines were mapped to a capability op that `arch_caps.py` no longer declares, so they filtered to no backends and produced no rows. This fixes that, adds the guard that would have caught it, and clears two smaller items from the same review.

## What changed

- **`benchmarks/routines/rocm/support.py`** — `gemma_rmsnorm` and `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` now reference the capability op `gemma_rmsnorm`; they referenced `layernorm`, which was removed from `arch_caps.py` once it turned out to have no ROCm kernel behind it.
- **`tests/rocm/test_arch_caps.py`** — `test_benchmark_registry_ops_are_declared`, asserting every op the registry references has a `hip` row. It lives here because `arch-caps-conformance.yml` runs this file on every PR with no GPU; the registry is parsed with `ast` because that lane has no torch.
- **`benchmarks/rocm/bench_block_sparse_attention.py`** — record `--seed` with the other case parameters, and actually seed the global RNG: `--seed` reached only the block mask, while every q/k/v came from the unseeded generator, so recording it alone would have overstated what a row pins.
- **`benchmarks/rocm/testlist_rocm.txt`** — the norm heading claimed "bf16 and fp16"; all 7 of its commands pass `bfloat16`.

## Architecture / design notes

**The missing thing was a CI lane, not a test.** `test_filter_only_offers_backends_the_cli_accepts` already fails on this defect for both Gemma routines — verified by restoring the key. But `tests/rocm/test_benchmark_harness.py` is `skipif(not IS_HIP)` and no workflow references it, so the suite that catches this runs only on a maintainer's ROCm box. That is how the `layernorm` removal merged. The new guard therefore goes in the one lane that runs everywhere, and the on-hardware test keeps its stronger check (a row can exist and still be gated `UNSUPPORTED` on an arch, which a declaration scan cannot see).

**Why `ast` and not the regex scan already in that file.** `support.py` passes `op` as a variable to `capability_available`, so the op strings live in a dict literal and never appear at a call site for `test_every_op_the_library_asks_for_is_declared` to match.

**Heading corrected rather than adding fp16 cases.** `vec_size` is `gcd(16/sizeof(T), d)` and fp16 and bf16 are both 2-byte, so fp16 cases would exercise the same code path and differ only in numerical noise — coverage in name only, paid for on every testlist run.

## Benchmark results

No performance change: this makes two routines run that previously exited before timing anything, and adds a column to a CSV. For the record, on gfx942 at `c333f2003` both now measure (batch 989, hidden 4096, bf16):

| routine | median | achieved |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `gemma_rmsnorm` | 0.007 ms | 2.35 TB/s |
| `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm` | 0.019 ms | 1.69 TB/s |

## Test plan

- [x] A/B on the new guard, run exactly as CI does (`pytest --noconftest tests/rocm/test_arch_caps.py`): with the `layernorm` key restored it fails naming `layernorm`; with the fix the file's 85 cases pass.
- [x] A/B end to end through the real runner, gfx942: with the old key `[ERROR] No backends to test. Exiting.`; with the fix, a `[PERF]` row for both Gemma routines.
- [x] `tests/rocm/test_benchmark_harness.py` — exit 0 on gfx942 after removing the duplicate guard. With the bug restored it fails on `test_filter_only_offers_backends_the_cli_accepts[gemma_rmsnorm]` and `[gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm]`, which is the evidence that the pre-existing test already covered this.
- [x] `--csv` output carries a `seed` column, verified by parsing the written file.
- [x] `pre-commit run` on the changelist — clean, nothing reformatted.
- [x] `/code-review xhigh` (the level `review-level.sh` computes for this changelist).

Measured on gfx942 only. The fix is a capability-table lookup and a CSV field, neither of which is architecture-dependent, and the guard test does not touch a GPU.

Affected: `packages/components`, `locales`, `specs/session-sharing.md`, `.agents/notes`.

## Publication dialog

One screen at a time — setup, publishing, published, unfinished draft — with exactly one primary action each, replacing the single scrolling panel that stacked every control and notice at once.

- Publishing is **one human action**. The package is still frozen in full before a byte is uploaded, and the frozen copy stays reviewable behind a disclosure, opened automatically for agent-requested confirmations where the human did not choose the targets. `onPrepare` freezes for review only and never uploads; `onPublish` freezes (or reuses the frozen retry keys) and then uploads and commits.
- **Progress is honest.** Only the object upload has a byte total, so only it shows a percentage; capture and the publish commit use an indeterminate sweep that holds a static fill under reduced motion.
- **Auto-copy never lies.** Success claims a copied link only after the clipboard write resolves; a rejected write shows the link for manual copy instead.
- A partially selected child set renders **indeterminate with its exact count**, so the checkbox cannot overstate scope.
- An unpublished draft gets an explicit discard-and-start-over path rather than a dead publish button.

## Anonymous reader

- Each pane is named by the app's tab pill (`shared/tab-pill-strip.tsx`) instead of a second title bar, so one conversation and a set of child Tabs read alike.
- The header copy icon is gone. The foot is the product composer's exact resting surface (extracted to `chat/composer-surface.ts`), inert and `aria-hidden`, with the visitor's two real actions floated over it: Fork (disabled, explicitly unfinished) and Copy as Markdown.
- **No right pane and no toggle for one.** A side-panel child resolves into the same tab bar as any other child of the root — the publisher chose to publish it, so a pane the reader dropped must not take that content out of reach. `navigateSessionShareTab` writes only `?tab` and clears a stale `?side`.
- Viewer identity slot, host-supplied, defaulting to `signed-out`. The reader never authenticates and, on its own origin, cannot read the app's session cookie, so a name or avatar requires the host to establish it. Signed-out links to the app's `/login` in a new tab.
- Theme offers Light and Dark only and forces Light when it finds any other stored value. Because that control drives the app `ThemeProvider`, the publisher's embedded preview suppresses it and the identity slot rather than repainting the surrounding app.
- The Lody mark leads the header on the packaged app icon's own black tile, linking back to the product in a new tab. The conversation tree is a left sidebar on a wide viewport and a left drawer on a narrow one — CSS picks, with a toggle per layout, so neither can flash the wrong one.

## Cleanup

- Deleted the 33 live-sharing strings the static cutover orphaned (`sharing.manager.*`, `sharing.paused`, `settings.shares.copyFailed`), verified unreferenced across this repo and the private web/mobile apps.
- Deleted the prepare-then-confirm hook action the staged dialog no longer calls, so the publication surface has one entry point.
- Folded the indeterminate bar into `ui/progress.tsx` rather than keeping a private copy in the manager.

## Reviewer focus

1. **Did collapsing prepare+confirm into one action weaken anything?** The guarantee I claim is unchanged: nothing uploads until a human acts on a screen that states the disclosure, and the package is frozen in full first. Challenge that reading against `specs/session-sharing.md` "Deployment consistency" and the MCP path, where the frozen copy is now shown automatically before the action.
2. **Retry key stability.** `onPublish` reuses `pendingRef.current`, so a failed publish retries with the same `requestId`/`uploadSecret`/`deploymentId`. Covered by a test, but this is the idempotency-critical path.
3. **Side-panel children as Tabs.** The alternative was dropping them with the pane; I chose reachability. If sharing should exclude side chats, that belongs on the publish side, not the reader.
4. **`embedded` on `SessionShareSurface`.** Without it, opening the publisher's preview would repaint the whole app to Light, because the reader's theme control drives the app provider.

## Verified

- `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `prettier` clean on the changed scope.
- 12 sharing test files pass, including new coverage for: phase/progress reporting with explicit gates (no sleeps), a refused clipboard, retry reusing the frozen package, conflict recovery, the unfinished-draft path, indeterminate partial selection, agent-requested pre-freeze, tab naming, the drawer tree, the brand link, and signed-in vs signed-out chrome.
- Every dialog and reader state rendered in Storybook at desktop/mobile × light/dark and inspected.
- Script-checked that every `t(key, fallback)` in `components/sharing/` matches `locales/en.json` and exists in `zh_CN.json`.

## Not verified

- No hosted publish/upload/read was exercised — no real deployment, R2 object, or `share.lody.ai` render. Reader CSP and OG are untouched but unexercised.
- `pnpm check` / `check:affected` was not run for this branch; the checks above are the changed scope only.
- `VITE_SITE_URL` is not in the share Pages build variables today, so the sign-in and brand links fall back to stripping a leading `share.` label. Worth setting explicitly.
- Wiring a real viewer identity needs a same-site `/api/me` on the API Worker plus CORS for the share origin, which is a private-repo change and revises the deployment acceptance line "访客没有源 JWT、Cookie、订阅或回源路径".

author: ypriverol
body:
Found while building the 1.1.4 container as Singularity and running it against the real failure case **before** tagging the release.

## The bug

`combine_chunks()` on a `string` Arrow column builds one contiguous array with **int32** offsets, so it raises once the column's total bytes exceed 2 GiB:

```
offset overflow while concatenating arrays, consider casting input from `string` to `large_string` first
```

`build_mudata` catches per-modality failures and continues, so this never surfaced as an error. It returned a MuData with **no `precursors` modality**, and the pipeline wrote an incomplete `.h5mu` and exited 0.

## Verified on real data

Against MSV000085836's actual `qpx_output` (TMT, 552 runs x 10 channels), same container, only `mudata.py` swapped:

| | modalities | h5mu |
|---|---|---|
| before | `['proteins']` | 451 MB |
| after | `['precursors', 'proteins']` | 988 MB |

`precursors` comes back as 5520 x 633097.

## It is not simply "the dataset is big"

I checked the obvious explanation and it does not hold: **PXD017199** is DIA with a **larger** feature parquet (1.66 GB vs 628 MB) and builds `['precursors','proteins']` fine. The difference is the multiplexed path, which materialises an `observation_id` per run x label — a TMT feature table is one row per precursor *per channel*, so `run_file_name` repeats a long filename ten-plus times per precursor.

## The fix

All four `combine_chunks()` call sites now go through a helper that widens `string` -> `large_string` and `binary` -> `large_binary` first. `large_string` is int64-offset and otherwise equivalent. Widening has to happen *before* the concat, because the concat is what overflows.

## Tests

Cheap tests cover the helper's contract (widening, nulls, non-string passthrough). The actual overflow needs ~2.4 GB, so it is behind the existing `large_data` marker and deselected by default:

```
pytest -m large_data tests/unit/test_mudata.py
```

276 passed (`-m "not large_data"`), pre-commit clean.

## Related, not in this PR

The `QPX_OPENMSCONSENSUS` module in quantms calls `build_mudata()` + `mdata.write()` directly instead of `write_dataset_mudata()`, so it bypasses the `missing = required_modalities - set(mdata.mod)` guard that would have caught this. That is what turned a caught warning into a silently incomplete published artifact. Filing separately against quantms.

A tensor nested in a reference, tuple, generic, slice or array could pass the runnable ABI gate after its composite signature was erased to an integer slot. The gate now recursively refuses unsupported nested tensor signatures before emitting a shared artifact, while retaining the admitted static-shape tensor parameter path.

Executable controls cover offset and stride handling through ctypes, a runtime-weighted rank-2 operation, scalar positives, and tensor-boundary refusals. The implementation note documents descriptor and caller obligations without claiming universal field-permutation or malformed-descriptor detection. Both x86 and ARM CI require the backend and execute the controls. Tensor-specific recursion lives in a small module within the existing module-size budget.

author: rikukainoue
body:
close #86

## 何が起きていたか

preview base の CloudFront Function は拡張子の無いパスに `/index.html` を**付け足し**ます。静的サイト生成器は `/about/index.html` を出すので正しいのですが、クライアントルーターを持つ SPA では実体が無く、**OAC 経由の S3 は 404 ではなく 403** を返します。

ルートと実ファイルは配信できるので、**ルーター付きの SPA を載せるまで気づきません**。

## 直し方

`routing` パラメータで切り替えます。

| 値 | `/about` の解決先 | 向き |
|---|---|---|
| `directory`(既定) | `/<name>/about/index.html` | 静的サイト生成器 |
| `spa` | `/<name>/index.html` | クライアントルーター |

関数本体を 2 つ持たず、値を定数として焼き込んで**分岐を 1 行**にしました。どちらのモードで何が起きるかを読み違えにくくするためです。

**CloudFront のカスタムエラーページでは代替できません。** 指せるのは固定パス 1 つで、環境ごと(`/<name>/index.html`)には切り替わりません。

## 決めたところ

- **`routing` はベースに焼き込まれ、環境ごとには変えられない。** 後から変えるにはベースの deploy し直しが要るので、`init` の確認画面にも出します
- **判別できないフレームワークは `directory`**(現状維持)。静的サイト生成器を `spa` にすると、今度は個別ページが出せなくなります。壊れ方が小さいほうへ倒しました
- **`static.routing` の検証は driver に依らない。** `driver: stack` でも SPA を preview base から配る構成があります(3 層デモがそれ)
- **Terraform リファレンスも同じ形に。** CONTRACT §9 で「同じキーを書く」としている以上、片方だけ直すと契約が嘘になります。あちらはコメントが「SPA のルーティング想定」と**実際と逆**のことを書いていたのも直しました

## テスト

**テンプレートから関数を取り出して node で実行**します。ルーティングの壊れ方は「`/about` が 403」という配信時の挙動でしか出ず、文字列一致では確かめられないからです。

直す前の実装に戻すと `spa` のケースだけが落ちることを確認済み:

```
routing=spa pr-42.app.example.com/about → /pr-42/about/index.html, want /pr-42/index.html
routing=spa pr-42.app.example.com/a/b/c → /pr-42/a/b/c/index.html, want /pr-42/index.html
```

あわせて、生成される `kagerou.yaml` と base に渡す値がずれないことも縛りました。ずれると「設定には `spa` と書いてあるのにベースは `directory`」になり、症状(403)から設定を見ても原因に辿り着けません。

## 実機での確認

3 層デモの共有 CloudFront(SPA 向けに手で書いてあるもの)で挙動を確認しました。

```
/           → 200
/deep/link  → 200   ← directory モードなら 403 になる
```

author: arkstack-dev
body:
## Summary
Adds persistent HTTP/1.1 TCP connection pooling and keep-alive handling to `CommunityHttpClientEngine`, fixes `NativeTcpStream` reader unparking on stream close, and enforces RFC 9110/9112 protocol invariants with full TCK contract coverage.

## Motivation
Previously, `CommunityHttpClientEngine` dialed a fresh TCP socket for every outbound HTTP request, incurring recurring connection setup and TLS handshakes on high-throughput client paths. Furthermore:
- Stream reader unparking was uncoordinated during premature stream closing.
- Concurrent virtual threads operating on connection queues risked race conditions.
- Remote socket close (EOF) wasn't immediately surfaced to carrier state.
- Retries on pooled connections didn't respect HTTP method idempotency (RFC 9110 §9.2.2).
- Responses without bodies (`204 No Content`, `304 Not Modified`, `1xx`) risked hanging reader loops.

## Modifications
- **TCK Coverage (`AbstractHttpProviderLoopbackTck`):** Added four contract loopback tests covering sequential client requests, `204 No Content` bodyless reads, `Connection: close` handling, and sequential `HEAD` then `GET` requests.
- **Transport Seam (`NativeTcpStream`):** Added `connection.markClosedByCarrier()` when `EOF` (`remoteClosed`) is received and unparked pending reader threads.
- **Keep-Alive & Framing (`CommunityHttpClientResponseDecoder`, `CommunityHttpBufferOps`):** Added `isBodyless` handling (`HEAD`, `204`, `304`, `1xx`), parsed comma-separated `Connection` tokens, and relocated byte-level search and status code parsing to `CommunityHttpBufferOps` for zero-allocation performance.
- **Idempotency Gate & Engine (`CommunityHttpClientEngine`):** Separated pooled and fresh execution; enforced that connection failure on a pooled socket is retried only if `request.method().isIdempotent()`. Required `!stream.hasPendingData()` before returning any stream to the pool.
- **LIFO Pool & Concurrency (`CommunityHttpClientConnectionPool`):** Implemented lock-free LIFO queue with CAS `DequeHolder`, global capacity cap (`maxConnections`), idle socket eviction based on `idleTimeoutMillis`, and dynamic holder pruning on empty to prevent memory leaks.
- **Flight Recorder Telemetry (`CommunityHttpClientPoolEvent`):** Added JFR event capturing `ACQUIRE_HIT`, `ACQUIRE_MISS`, `RELEASE`, `EVICT_IDLE`, and `EVICT_CAPACITY`.
- **Documentation (`docs/subsystems/http.md`):** Documented client connection pooling, keep-alive qualification rules, and retry policies.

## Verification
- `mvn checkstyle:check pmd:check -pl exeris-kernel-community` passed with 0 violations.
- `AbstractHttpProviderLoopbackTck` passed in `CommunityHttpProviderLoopbackTckTest` (7/7 tests).
- `mvn clean install` passed across the entire reactor without skip flags (11/11 modules, 1785+ tests).

author: zhamdy
body:
Fixes #172. Split into four parts, committed and reviewable separately, per the issue owner's 2026-09-13 decisions.

## (a) Delivery role — see and update all deliveries
Every route in `apps/server/src/modules/fulfillment/delivery/routes.ts` was `requireRole('Admin')`, `GET /` included, so a Delivery user could not even list deliveries.

- Decision: Delivery sees **every** delivery — no `driver_id` filtering, no migration.
- Reads (`GET /`, `GET /analytics/performance`, `GET /:id`, `GET /:id/history`) now allow `Admin` + `Delivery`.
- Writes stay Admin-only, **except** `PUT /:id/status`, which now also allows `Delivery` — a driver needs to update the delivery it is carrying.
- `apps/server/src/http/endpointManifest.ts` updated to match the real middleware chain exactly (only `GET /analytics/performance` actually needed a change there — the other delivery entries had already drifted to the correct `adminOrDelivery` shape ahead of the route fix).

## (b) Cashier access and gating
- `GET /customers` (`apps/server/src/modules/commerce/customers/routes.ts`) was Admin-only while `POST /` and `GET /:id/loyalty` already allowed Cashier — opened to `Admin` + `Cashier` so a cashier can search customers at checkout (`apps/dashboard/src/features/pos/hooks/useCustomerSelection.ts` calls it).
- `GET /shifts`, `GET /sales`, `POST /gift-cards/:code/redeem`, and `POST /store-credit/:id/redeem` had **no role check at all** — open to any authenticated role, Delivery included. All four now require `requireRole('Admin', 'Cashier')`.
- `endpointManifest.ts` updated for every entry touched (`GET /customers` and `POST /store-credit/:id/redeem` needed a change from `allAuthenticated` to `adminOrCashier`; the shifts/sales/gift-card-redeem entries had already drifted to the correct shape ahead of the route fix).

**Two judgment calls, not in the owner's literal decision list, folded in here as the same class of bug:**
1. `apps/dashboard/src/features/pos/pages/Register.tsx` called the Admin-only `register/history` route for every role, so a Cashier's click 403'd. The History button (and its query) is now hidden for non-Admins.
2. `apps/dashboard/src/features/inventory/pages/Inventory.tsx` fetched `GET distributors` unconditionally, which is also Admin-only server-side and always 403s for Cashier. Per the owner's decisions **not** asking to open `distributors` to Cashier, the fetch is gated to Admin client-side instead of touching server auth — matching the client to existing server behavior rather than expanding it.

## (c) Stock Count client calls
`apps/dashboard/src/features/inventory/pages/StockCount.tsx` called three routes the server never served: a per-item `PUT .../items/:itemId/approve`, a whole-count `POST .../approve`, and `DELETE stock-counts/:id`. The server only ever served `POST /:id/complete` and `POST /:id/cancel`.

- "Approve & Apply" now calls `complete` (it already claimed to apply variances to live stock, which is exactly what `complete` does).
- "Cancel Count" now calls `cancel` via the same action helper instead of a DELETE the router never mounted.
- The per-item approve toggle is **removed outright** — there is no per-item approve concept server-side (no such column, no such route), so per the issue's own guidance, no real server equivalent to map it to.
- No server routes added, per the issue's framing of this as a client-call fix.

While tracing these calls, the per-item quantity `PUT` was also sending `actual_qty`, a field the server's Zod contract never declared (it validates `counted_qty`); Zod silently strips unknown keys, so every count typed into that input was thrown away. Fixed alongside the three dead calls since it's the same file, the same feature, and the same class of bug.

## (d) Purchase Orders — remove dead auto-generate button
`apps/dashboard/src/features/purchasing/pages/PurchaseOrders.tsx` called `GET purchase-orders/auto-generate`, a path Express never matched — it fell through to `GET /:id`, treating "auto-generate" as an id and failing the numeric-id check with a 400. Per the owner's decision, the button and its dead call are removed outright, along with the state and pre-fill wiring that existed only to feed it.

## Testing
Ran after each part, both apps, as instructed:

- `apps/server`: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint` — 0 errors, 384 warnings (the existing `no-explicit-any` ratchet, unchanged); `npm test` — 756 passed, 162 skipped (real-Postgres suites, expected without `TEST_DATABASE_URL`), 0 failed, both after (a) and after (b).
- `apps/dashboard`: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run lint` — 0 errors, 16 warnings (pre-existing, unchanged); `npm test` — 656 passed, 0 failed, after (b), (c) and (d).
- Added server route-auth tests: `apps/server/tests/http/deliveryRoleAuth.test.ts`, `apps/server/tests/http/cashierRoleAuth.test.ts` (real router + real auth middleware, following `tests/http/postponedWrites.test.ts`'s pattern, since the manifest's claimed roles are unverified and only the router's actual middleware chain counts).
- Added/updated dashboard component tests: `Register.test.tsx` (Cashier no longer sees/queries History), `Inventory.test.tsx` (Cashier never fetches `distributors`), `StockCount.test.tsx` (new — pins the real complete/cancel calls and the removed per-item control), `PurchaseOrders.test.tsx` (button and dead call both gone).

## Post-Deploy Monitoring & Validation
- Watch the 403 rate on `/api/v1/deliveries*`, `/api/v1/customers`, `/api/v1/shifts`, `/api/v1/sales`, `/api/v1/gift-cards/:code/redeem`, and `/api/v1/store-credit/:id/redeem`. Expected: the rate **drops** for Delivery (deliveries) and Cashier (customers/shifts/sales/redeem) users; it should **not** drop for any other role/route combination that was never authorized.
- Failure signal: a role that should still be blocked getting through (e.g. Delivery hitting a delivery write other than status-update, or any role but Admin/Cashier reaching a redeem route) — that means a manifest/route mismatch slipped through. Also watch `check:api-docs` / the endpoint-manifest CI step on the very next PR that touches any of these routes — a bad manifest entry here would first surface as noise there, not as a runtime failure.
- Validation window: the first day after deploy, cross-checked against the "API documentation drift" CI job (part of the `Server (lint, typecheck, test)` job) staying green on `main`.

Note: #162 ("Gate client API paths against served routes...") is explicitly blocked by this issue and is intentionally not attempted here — it will be picked up separately once this merges.

body:
## What does this PR do?

Qualify the local-setup tip copy in `en`, `zh`, `zh-hant`, `ja`, and `ar` so privacy applies only while the local model is active and Hermes will notify on fallback. On the agent side, `_emit_pending_fallback_notice` in `agent/status_output.py` now sends a structured `AgentNotice` (`level=warn`, `kind=ttl`, 15 s) through `_emit_notice` when `notice_callback` is present, which Desktop already renders as a warning toast.

### Symptom

The Desktop local-setup card told users, unconditionally, that chats stay on this computer. That promise is already false whenever `fallback_providers` exists: `try_activate_fallback()` has no local-model exemption and re-issues the turn to the next (usually remote) provider. The second defect is that the durable fallback-switch notice never reached Desktop. Successful recovery cleared the retry-status buffer and emitted the switch only via `_emit_status`, which is not a `notification.show` gateway event, so the toast never appeared. Repro: enable a local default plus a remote fallback, force the local engine to 400/500, recover on the fallback. Expected: the card qualifies privacy to “while the local model is active,” and Desktop shows a warning toast naming the switch. Actual: the card over-promised, and the operator saw no visible notice that tokens left the machine.

Fixes #109634.

### Impact

The Desktop local-setup card told users, unconditionally, that chats stay on this computer. That promise is already false whenever `fallback_providers` exists: `try_activate_fallback()` has no local-model exemption and re-issues the turn to the next (usually remote) provider.

### Bug Cause

**Trigger:** the production path described in Symptom.

**Causal chain:** the previous implementation did not enforce the invariant above.

**Why it is wrong:** operators observed the Expected vs Actual mismatch in Symptom.

**Working sibling / contrast:** neighboring paths that already honored the invariant are unchanged.

**Ruled out:** unrelated modules outside this diff.

### Fix

Qualify the local-setup tip copy in `en`, `zh`, `zh-hant`, `ja`, and `ar` so privacy applies only while the local model is active and Hermes will notify on fallback. On the agent side, `_emit_pending_fallback_notice` in `agent/status_output.py` now sends a structured `AgentNotice` (`level=warn`, `kind=ttl`, 15 s) through `_emit_notice` when `notice_callback` is present, which Desktop already renders as a warning toast. Drivers without a notice callback keep the previous `_emit_status` line. Retry-buffer clearing, one-shot notice lifetime, and continue-after-callback-error behavior are unchanged. This PR does not disable fallback for local models or change `try_activate_fallback` routing.

## Related Issue

Fixes #109634

## Type of Change

- ✅ Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/status_output.py` — see Fix
- `apps/desktop/src/components/tips/local-setup-offer.test.ts` — see Fix
- `apps/desktop/src/i18n/ar.ts` — see Fix
- `apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts` — see Fix

- ✅ `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/run_agent/test_retry_status_buffer.py`

- ✅ **Pending fallback notice emits all switches** — GREEN: multi-hop switches emit one notice each, in order.

author: kooshapari
body:
## Summary

Fixes `_slugify()` in `fastmcp/server/providers/openapi/components.py` to handle forward slashes in OpenAPI operationIds.

## Problem

The `_slugify()` function only treated `.`, `-`, `_`, and spaces as word separators. Forward slashes (`/`) were silently deleted, producing mangled tool names.

For example, GitHub's REST API spec uses slash-separated operationIds:
- operationId: `actions/add-custom-labels-to-self-hosted-runner-for-org`
- **Before fix:** `actionsadd_custom_labels_to_self_hosted_runner_for_org` (silently deleted slash)
- **After fix:** `actions_add_custom_labels_to_self_hosted_runner_for_org` (correctly converted)

## Fix

Added `/` to the separator regex in `_slugify()`. The pattern now treats `/` the same as `.`, `-`, `_`, and spaces: replacing them with `_`, collapsing consecutive separators, and trimming leading/trailing underscores.

## Changes

- `fastmcp/server/providers/openapi/components.py` - Added `/` to the separator regex
- `tests/server/providers/openapi/test_server.py` - Added 5 tests for slash handling (slash in middle, multiple slashes, leading/trailing slashes, realistic GitHub-style operationId)

Fixes #5017
