author: aeplay
body:
🤖 Draft #2913 trial on #2949. No adopter testing requested yet; no merge before morning approval.

## Before / after

JazzSchema clones copied the full developer-authored source and compiled runtime schema. Production access to both is immutable. Store each private field behind Arc so existing owned schema views retain the immutable contents instead of copying all tables, columns, references and policies.

No new cache, interning table, invalidation rule, version shortcut or per-row wrapper. Separate compilations still produce independent schema contents. Public method signatures and Debug shape are unchanged; equality explicitly compares runtime values, not pointer identity. The testing-only mutable runtime accessor uses Arc::make_mut, and the test-only consuming accessor unwraps a unique runtime or clones a shared one.

## Worked cases / invariants

- Query preparation retains schema V1 across an await while the catalogue later selects V2: its V1 view stays immutable and valid, exactly as the old owned copy did. Selecting V2 still follows existing catalogue/version validation.
- Drop the original schema after cloning: source, tables, canonical bytes and version ID remain available from the clone.
- Two testing views share a runtime, then one mutates its table name: copy-on-write isolates the mutation; the other view and its version ID remain unchanged.
- Consuming a shared test view returns an independent runtime. Consuming the final unique view preserves its table allocation.
- Permission checks, public-source serialization, CATS v1 schema payloads, storage and wire encodings are unchanged. Reviewed SchemaVersion's explicit retained-public-schema serialization: it does not serialize the private Arc representation. Existing byte corpora remain authoritative.

## Evidence / validation

Latest complete cold graph under exact b4c78ccc3b16a0bab426bee4358d4b0a9cff5d94 contains 0.979s of 44.514s beneath the synchronous JazzSchema::clone subtree. Predict 1–2.5% cold improvement and approximately flat todo; no matching clone sample in the update graph, so no universal-win claim.

Full rejected ledger/testing guidance read; searched preserved branches and open/closed PRs for schema clone, schema Arc and JazzSchema. #2813 borrowed individual table schemas at three row sites; #932 borrowed old policy context; #2799 prepared record descriptors. This targets remaining owned whole-application-schema handoffs, not the rejected #2848 universal record-sharing design.

Two new tests use public schema builders, check retained source/canonical identity/lifetime and copy-on-write isolation, plus necessary internal pointer assertions to prove sharing which public row equality cannot distinguish. No existing assertions changed. Formatting and diff checks pass; focused tests, full workspace correctness CI, broad Jazz/canaries and timing follow. No local full-CI-equivalent or independent-review claim.

Tooling-friction: distinguish immutable schema ownership from mutable catalogue selection; sharing the former does not require caching the latter.

## Problem

`cliamp.queue.list()` returns a `queued` flag per entry that is meant to say whether the track sits in the play-next queue. The wiring in `main.go` derived it from `Playlist.QueuePosition(i) >= 0`. `QueuePosition` returns the 1-based position in the queue and 0 for a track that is not queued, so the comparison was true for every track, and plugins saw the whole playlist as queued.

## Fix

Compare against zero with `>`, matching the documented contract. One character, plus a comment stating the 1-based semantics at the call site.

## Testing

The wiring lives in a closure in `main.go`, so no unit test is attached. Verified live by reading the queue from a plugin before and after the change: a one-track playlist with nothing queued now reports `queued = false`.

author: acamposve
body:
## Summary

Implements [specs/restaurant/ordering/close-order.md](https://github.com/acamposve/presenciavirtualplatform/blob/main/specs/restaurant/ordering/close-order.md) (Approved in PR #15): transitions an `Open` order to `Closed`, freeing its table for a new order and blocking further `AddItem` calls against it.

This required fixing two pre-existing defects the spec's own review surfaced (BR6/BR7), not just adding new code:

- **BR6**: `Order.Reconstruct` never accepted a `Status` parameter, and `Order`'s constructor unconditionally initialized it to `Open` — every rehydrated order silently reported `Open` regardless of what was actually persisted. Invisible until a second status value existed. `Reconstruct` now takes and preserves `Status`; both `OrderRepository` read paths pass the row's real value through.
- **BR7**: `AddItem`'s merge checked `Status` once, before its per-line-locked upsert, without re-validating under that lock — a concurrent `CloseOrder` could commit in between and let an item land on an order that ends up `Closed`. Introduced a shared order-scoped advisory lock (`OrderLock`) that both `AddItem`'s merge and `CloseOrder`'s transition acquire first, with the authoritative `Status` check moved under it — deliberately placed *after* the idempotency-claim recheck, so a replay of an already-applied `AddItem` keeps succeeding even after a since-concurrent close (per `add-item.md` BR6).

New `CloseOrder` slice: `Order.Close()` (domain invariant, BR1), a dedicated `close_order_idempotency_keys` table (BR3 — its own table, per `add-item.md`'s established precedent, with RLS + a tenant-consistent composite FK), a migration widening `restaurant.orders`'s status `CHECK` constraint, and `POST /orders/{orderId:guid}/close` gated by a new `restaurant.orders.close` permission. The whole flow — idempotency precedence, existence check, the `Open` invariant, and the atomic transition — is one repository call (`OrderRepository.CloseAsync`), since only the `Order` aggregate itself is involved here (unlike `CreateOrder`/`AddItem`, no separate `Table`/`MenuItem` to resolve).

## Tests

- `OrderTests.cs`: 5 new unit tests for `Order.Close()` and `Reconstruct`'s status fix.
- `CloseOrderEndpointTests.cs`: AC1–AC13 against the real API/database, including 3 concurrency races (concurrent close attempts, concurrent identical idempotency key, and the `AddItem`-vs-`CloseOrder` race).
- `RowLevelSecurityTests.cs`: added a direct RLS read/write-isolation test for the new `close_order_idempotency_keys` table.
- **111/111 tests pass** (up from 95) — re-ran 4x with no flakiness observed in the concurrency tests.

## Test plan

- [ ] Await Copilot automated review and address findings

author: cepseudobe
body:
Closes #56

## What

A time-based harvester opened `[last, last + range)` with no notion of the present. A window ending in the future was harvested early and stored with a future date, so later source records were skipped; a gap in the source longer than the range made the window empty on every run and the harvester never recovered.

The window end is now `min(last + range, now)`; an empty window jumps to the next source record and reopens from there. First tests for the harvester, on SQLite with the local storage adapter.

## Decisions

- After a gap the window reopens at the next source record, not at now, so nothing between the two is lost: it is processed in `source_range` slices over the following runs.
- The clamp lives in `run()`, not in `SourceRangeParser`, which stays a pure function without a clock.
- A result row already dated in the future by the old bug makes `run()` return false until time catches up; no automatic repair of existing rows.

## How verified

- components: 10 passed (5 new; 3 red without the fix). Build and `pnpm lint`: green.
- e2e `harvester.spec.ts` against Postgres and MinIO: 3 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Build, tests and lint pass on every touched package
- [ ] I can explain every line of this diff without help from a tool
- [x] AI tools were used for this PR: Claude Code, most of the code and the tests, reviewed by me

author: teemow
body:
Fixes #429.

## Problem

`kagent.substrateWorkerPool.template.nodeSelector` pins the pool to `kubernetes.io/arch: amd64`, and the values comment, the chart README, the README's "Scheduling" paragraph and UPGRADE.md say an actor's golden snapshot is architecture-specific. The constraint is narrower: the snapshot is a gVisor checkpoint, and gVisor restores it only on a host whose CPU offers every feature the checkpoint recorded — two amd64 nodes of different vendors are not compatible.

Observed on the first 4.x installation (2026-09-13, meta 4.9.4, kagent 0.11.0-gs.8, Substrate 0.0.27-gs.8): Karpenter had mixed AMD `c5a.xlarge` and Intel `r6i.xlarge` / `m7i-flex.xlarge` nodes under the pool; the `sre-agent` golden snapshot was taken on an AMD worker; every restore on the Intel worker failed every 30 s with

```
FATAL ERROR: starting container: starting sub-container [/app]: failed to load kernel:
incompatible FeatureSet: missing features: map[cmp_legacy:{} cr8_legacy:{} sse4a:{} misalignsse:{} topoext:{} mmxext:{} fxsr_opt:{}]
```

(all AMD-only CPUID flags) and the portal turn surfaced as `actor "ai-…" request timed out`. The actor never recovers because it stays placed on that worker.

## Change

Documentation only — no render change (`helm lint` clean, `pre-commit` clean, the chart README regenerated by the pinned helm-docs).

- `values.yaml`: the `template.nodeSelector` comment names the feature-set constraint (one vendor and generation, not just one architecture), the failure signature, and the pin per provider: `kubernetes.io/arch` as the coarse case; on CAPA the vendor `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-cpu-manufacturer: amd|intel` (Karpenter consolidation may replace a node with another vendor's at any time) and, where a generation change must be ruled out too, the family `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family`; on CAPZ and the other providers the node pool (`giantswarm.io/machine-pool`) or `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type` — a node pool there is one VM size. Plus the recognition recipe: `kubectl get nodes -L <the label>` showing two values under the pool.
- `helm/agent-platform/README.md(.gotmpl)`, `README.md` "Scheduling", `UPGRADE.md` (three places): the same, in their register.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Unreleased / Changed, with "Installations act".

The knob stays the existing free-form `template.nodeSelector` map: the right key is provider-specific and the vendor label exists only where Karpenter provisions the nodes, so a dedicated values key or a render-time guard would have to know the provider and the autoscaler — that knowledge lives in the fleet template (shared-configs: `agentPlatform.workerPoolCpuManufacturer`, rendered into the selector for every CAPA installation on the 4.x line; giantswarm/shared-configs PR linked from #429), where the provider is known. The durable fix is Substrate's: a restore placed only on a worker whose CPU covers the snapshot's feature set (giantswarm/giantswarm#37742 row 12; proposal prepared in the Substrate line's `FORK.md`).

## Verification

- `helm lint helm/agent-platform` — clean; `pre-commit run` on the changed files — clean (helm-docs regenerates the chart README to exactly this content).
- Not visible in agentlab: the lab is one kind node on one CPU, so a mixed pool cannot occur there. The runtime proof is the fleet installation: the live `WorkerPool kagent-default` carries `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-cpu-manufacturer: amd` next to the arch pin, all four workers run on `c5a.xlarge` (AMD) nodes, and the portal turn that failed passes (giantswarm/giantswarm#37745).

author: aelamrani
body:
## Portal: Add API Product Pause, Resume and Close Actions

Business context

Consumers need to control an API Product subscription as one access unit. Pausing, resuming or closing the subscription must affect access to the whole product rather than individual included APIs.

Consumer pause and resume use the subscription consumerStatus independently from the publisher-managed subscription status.

Scope

Add Pause, Resume and Close actions to the API Product subscription details view.

Pause an accepted subscription by changing consumerStatus from STARTED to STOPPED.

Resume an accepted subscription by changing consumerStatus from STOPPED to STARTED.

Close an ACCEPTED or PAUSED subscription after explicit confirmation.

Apply actions to the complete API Product subscription and all access granted through it.

Refresh subscription details immediately after a successful action.

Display accessible inline success and error feedback and disable actions while a request is running.

Hide or disable actions that are not allowed by the current subscription state or application permissions.

Disable API access presentation while the consumer status is STOPPED.

Enforce lifecycle eligibility, environment ownership and application permissions in the backend, independently of frontend visibility.

Preserve API Product and application audit records and the existing key pause, resume and revocation behavior.

Add focused Portal API, service/domain and Portal Next component/harness tests.

Existing HTTP contract

No new lifecycle endpoint is planned. Reuse the existing Portal API operations:

POST /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/_changeConsumerStatus?status=STOPPED

POST /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/_changeConsumerStatus?status=STARTED

POST /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/_close

Pause and resume require APPLICATION_SUBSCRIPTION[UPDATE]. Close requires APPLICATION_SUBSCRIPTION[DELETE].

Acceptance criteria

[ ] An authorized consumer can pause an accepted, started API Product subscription.

[ ] Pausing changes consumerStatus to STOPPED and suspends access granted through the whole product.

[ ] An authorized consumer can resume an accepted, stopped API Product subscription.

[ ] Resuming changes consumerStatus to STARTED and restores product access.

[ ] An authorized consumer can close an accepted or paused API Product subscription after confirming the destructive action.

[ ] Closing updates the subscription to CLOSED and applies the existing API key revocation rules.

[ ] The updated state is displayed immediately after each successful action.

[ ] The consumer receives clear inline success or error feedback.

[ ] Invalid actions are unavailable in the UI and rejected by the backend.

[ ] No lifecycle action is available for a closed or rejected subscription.

[ ] API Product and application audit records are created for successful lifecycle changes.

[ ] Existing direct API subscription behavior remains unchanged.

Out of scope

Renewing an expiring subscription.

Requesting or approving a subscription end-date extension.

API key renewal or manual API key revocation.

Publisher-controlled pause and resume.

Lifecycle actions for individual APIs included in the product.

Lifecycle actions from the My Subscriptions list.

Dependencies

Parent story: PORTAL-43

API Product subscription details are provided by PORTAL-44.

Unified navigation from My Subscriptions is provided by PORTAL-49.

author: raykavin
body:
RFC 7519 §4.1.3 allows `aud` in two shapes: an array of strings, or a single bare string when the token has exactly one audience. Keycloak emits the bare string once a client's dedicated scope narrows the token down to one audience.

`Claims.Aud` was `[]string`, so such a token failed to decode with:

```
json: cannot unmarshal string into Go struct field Claims.aud of type []string
```

and — critically — this happened *after* go-oidc had already accepted the token, since go-oidc normalizes both shapes internally. A perfectly valid token came back as a verification error.

Introduces an `Audience` type whose `UnmarshalJSON` accepts both forms and normalizes the single string into a one-element slice. Attempting the array first also absorbs a JSON `null` as an empty audience rather than erroring on it.

`Audience` is `[]string` underneath, so existing code that ranges over `claims.Aud` or indexes it is unaffected.

Covered by `TestAudienceUnmarshalJSON` (both shapes, null, sibling claims survive) and an end-to-end `TestVerify_SingleStringAudience`.

author: lessevv
body:
`Modules/CashBook` was the only one of thirty-five modules with no
`.docs/features/` page. It is not a trivial module — 34 PHP files, the `/cash`
surface, and the write path that turns four typed fields into a canonical
ledger row — and the absence was load-bearing: an agent working on it earlier
had to park two findings because nothing stated the module's intended
behaviour.

Spec: A7-R2, GOV-R12

## The pages

`.docs/features/cash-book/{architecture,code,how-to-test}.md`, in the
`_template/` shape and the register of `pots/` and `transfers/`, plus the row
`.docs/features/00-index.md` was missing. Every sentence is grounded in the
code; where intent is not stated anywhere, the page says what the code does
rather than inventing a why.

## The two parked findings

**1. "Which cash account?" was asked twice, unordered — fixed.**
`ManualEntryAnchors::accountIdFor()` and `CashBookPage::entryCurrency()` were
independent `where(user_id, kind = cash)` reads with no `orderBy`. The amount
box was labelled and parsed off one and the entry booked off the other. They
are now one question: `ManualEntryAnchors::currencyForUser()` resolves the
account exactly as the write does, and the page carries no `kind = cash` query
of its own. The resolution is ordered on `accounts.iban` —
`unique(user_id, iban)`, NOT NULL, and the same value on a paired device, which
an autoincrement id is not.

Two cash accounts remain unreachable, and the PR says so rather than claiming a
save: nine call sites create an `accounts` row tree-wide and only two can write
kind `cash` (this module's own find-or-create, which reuses, and
`DemoAccountsSeeder`, which opens one). `unique(user_id, iban)` also gives the
sync merge a natural key, so a peer's cash create is recognised rather than
re-homed beside the local row. Measured, not assumed: before the fix both
unordered reads in fact returned the *same* row, so the disagreement was never
demonstrable — what was wrong is that nothing made them agree.

**2. `BaseCurrency::code()` where `forUser($user)` was meant — fixed.**
`code()` resolves the ambient reader and falls to the install default wherever
there is none. The two sites here write and read `accounts.default_currency`,
a stored column every later entry is booked in, not a display figure — case 1
of the deliberate `code()` / `forUser()` split. Reachable today only from the
console: `DemoCashEntriesSeeder` runs after `DemoAccountsSeeder` has already
opened the cash account, so the mint branch is not reached in the composed
seed. Fixed anyway, and pinned.

## One more found while reading

**A 25-row page ranked on `t.id`.** The entry list ended on
`orderByDesc('t.id')`, and `paginate()` makes an ordering decide *which* rows
the reader is shown. Six coffees typed on one day filled page one one way on
the desktop and another on the phone. It now ends on
`NewestTransactionFirst::ACROSS_ACCOUNTS`, the clause four other modules
already rank this table with.

`AnOrderingThatPicksNeverEndsOnAPerDeviceIdArchTest` (#794, merged today) does
not see it: the pick is spelled across two methods — `manualEntriesQuery()`
returns the builder, `render()` paginates it — and the scanner follows one
token chain. Inlining the identical query onto one chain makes it report
`CashBookPage.php::transactions (1 found, 0 allowed) — a chain bounded by
paginate`, which is how this was found. **The blind spot itself is left for its
own pass**: 49 files both order by an id and touch `transactions`, and telling
the walks from the picks across method boundaries is a sweep, not an instance.

## Ruled out with the measurement

- **Money via float or a runtime quotient** — none. Zero `float`, `/ 100`,
  `* 100`, `round()` or `intdiv()` in the module's source; the two grep hits
  for "float" are the word in a sentence about a wallet float.
- **A figure read without its currency column** — ruled out. The list selects
  `settled_amount_minor` and `settled_currency` together and formats each row
  with its own; the worked example in the error message is built from
  `MoneyInput::toDecimalString()` at the account's scale.
- **An unbounded read on a growing table** — the entry list paginates at 25 and
  the decrypt and tax-tag reads are bounded by the page. The category picker
  reads the whole tree, which is 29 shipped globals plus the reader's own: it
  is bounded by the category tree, which does not grow with use.
- **Direction carried by colour alone** — ruled out. `Money::format()` goes
  through ICU currency formatting, so the sign is in the text on both layouts;
  the emerald is redundant.
- **An id crossing to JS as a number** — ruled out. Both delete call sites send
  the id quoted and it comes back through `DerivedRowId::fromWire()`;
  `transactions.id` is minted rather than derived, so it is small anyway.
- **A `DATE` compared against a `DATETIME` string** — ruled out. The ordinal
  read compares `posted_at` to `toDateString()` and `booked_at` to
  `toDateTimeString()`, each against its own column type.
- **Locale parity** — 26 locales, 31 keys, no key missing and none extra.

## Verification

Each fix was proved by inversion — reverted, test red, restored, test green.

author: anders-lindstrom
body:
`wt sync undo` had three ways of losing work that was not the run's. Each is one commit here; the fourth commit is the what's-new entry.

## What changes

**1. A rebase that is not the run's is refused, not aborted** (`b3f3e6b`)
A rebase in progress beside the run's sidecar was enough for undo to abort it. The rebase may be a person's own, started after aborting the run's from a commit of theirs. `resume` already refused it through `verifySequencer`; undo threw it away, and nothing pinned the commit because the branch ref never moved. The check moves into `wtsync` as `VerifyLeft`, the twin of `VerifyFinished`, and undo calls it in its first loop. The refusal is not lifted by `--force` (nothing to pin) and tells the person to finish or abort that rebase themselves.

**2. A commit made inside a handover is named and kept** (`5eccfca`)
Resolving the stop and committing it, or running `git rebase --continue` yourself and stopping again, leaves your commit on detached HEAD inside the run's own rebase. Undo aborted it; the commit survived only in HEAD's reflog. The sidecar now records HEAD at handover time (`State.Head`), and `CommittedInside` compares against it, A sidecar written before the field cannot prove anything (a dropped pick and a hand commit cancel out in any count), so it is treated as carrying somebody's work: plain undo refuses, forced pins the detached HEAD. The forced undo's row names the ref the commit was kept under and what puts it back. A plain undo refuses and names the commit and both ways forward; `--force` aborts and pins the pre-abort HEAD under the forced epoch, so a plain undo of that forced undo lands the branch on the commit. Branch moved by hand *and* commits inside is refused even with `--force`.

**3. A forced undo that stops partway leaves no pin for a branch it never moved** (`fd19414`)
`WriteRun` writes the forced epoch's pins before anything changes. A failure after it left those pins for branches the undo never reached; the forced epoch was then the newest run touching them, its safety at their current tip, so every later plain undo said "already at" and the real run was unreachable without deleting refs by hand. The apply phase now tracks what it actually moved (reset, update-ref, or an abort that discarded pinned inside-commits) and every failure return after `WriteRun` drops the other pins through `DeleteSafety`.

Undo's ordering rules are unchanged: every refusal before any write; pins only once every branch has passed; aborts before resets; a failed abort stops everything.

## Review questions

- **Item 1.** Is there any rebase in progress that carries a sidecar, passes `VerifyLeft`, and is still not the run's? (Expected answer: only one restarted from exactly the old tip onto exactly the run's onto, which is the run's rebase in every way that matters; item 2 covers what was committed inside it.)
- **Item 2.** After the forced abort, is the branch at `s.Tip` and the pinned safety at the pre-abort detached HEAD, and does a plain undo of that forced epoch land the branch on the partial picks, not on `s.Tip`? Trace the second loop of `Undo` with the forced epoch's result ref.
- **Item 3.** After every `return` past `WriteRun`, is the set of forced pins exactly the set of branches whose ref this call moved? Walk the seven returns. A move is a reset, an update-ref, or an abort that discarded what the pin keeps: inside commits, or a branch ref moved by hand that the abort put back.

## Notes for the reviewer

- `unabortableHandover` (test fixture) used to delete `orig-head`; item 1 would now refuse that before any abort, so it makes the abort fail with a stale `index.lock` instead, leaving the sequencer intact.
- `TestUndoDoesNotReportARewindItNeverReached` lost its premise (a forced undo no longer aborts a foreign rebase) and became a direct test of `abortedRows`.
- A refusal raised after `TakeOver` leaves the handover without its lock, as the five refusals it joins already did. Not changed here; the sidecar is the durable marker.

body:
## Incident
The seven-stage cloud control plane failed at `MONEY_SCORECARD` for the 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00 UTC control runs on 2026-09-13.

Root cause: the stage-linked scorecard seed explicitly inserted SQL expressions such as `exact_stage_status='T0_CONTROLLED_ENTRY'`. When no exact Money Entry snapshot existed, PostgreSQL evaluated the comparison to `NULL`, violating the candidate table's `NOT NULL` contract for `t0_snapshot_available`, `t1_snapshot_available` and `t2_snapshot_available`.

## Fix
Fail closed by wrapping all exact-stage boolean comparisons with `coalesce(..., false)`, including the frozen evidence claim flag. Missing exact-stage evidence is now represented as `false`, never `NULL`.

author: orhunkok
body:
`REBUILD=1` died with `No managed container named 'streamlit-DO-MS'` while that folder's container was running in front of it, called `streamlit-do-ms`.

`rebuild --name` selects an **existing** container, so the name has to be the one that exists — not the one `devcontainer.json` would create. Those differ whenever `name` has been edited or a folder renamed, which is exactly the state a project is in while being migrated. My previous fix read the name from the config, which is the wrong source of truth for this.

`adevcontainer list` knows which container belongs to which source directory, so it's asked rather than guessed:

```
NAME             STATE    MODE    SOURCE
streamlit-do-ms  running  bind    ~/.../streamlit-DO-MS
```

The leading slash in the match keeps `notpinpoint` from answering for `pinpoint`. With no container for the folder it says so and runs `up`, which is the right thing to do with nothing to rebuild.

**The `|| true` on that lookup isn't decoration.** The test fake exited non-zero from `list`, and `pipefail` with `set -e` killed the script before the fallback could run — silently, no output at all. A failing `list` now falls through to `up`.

## Verification

Against a fake runtime whose container name differs from its folder: `rebuild` selects the existing name, and a folder with no container falls back to `up` with a message. `make test` 353 passed / 2 skipped, lint and types clean.

| 4.12.2 | `pwa-icons` crée son dossier de sortie : viser `--out public/icons` échouait sur un message de `sharp` qui ne nomme pas le dossier manquant |
| 4.13.0 | `pwa-icons` produit `apple-touch-icon.png` par défaut, en 180×180 et **opaque** — iOS ignore la transparence et compose l'alpha sur du noir |

Rien ne change sans une exécution de `npm run icons` : les deux correctifs
d'icônes portent sur le générateur, pas sur le build. La montée est donc sans
effet visible ici tant que les icônes ne sont pas régénérées.

Le `package-lock.json` est régénéré par `--package-lock-only` et non par un
`npm install` complet : sous Windows celui-ci omet les entrées optionnelles des
autres plates-formes et casse `npm ci` en CI Linux.

> **Low Risk**
> Dev-dependency and lockfile-only change; no runtime or application logic is modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> Bumps the dev toolchain package **`@mister-guiiug/dev-pwa-config`** from **^4.11.0** to **^4.13.0** in `package.json` and refreshes **`package-lock.json`** (lock-only regen so Linux CI keeps optional platform entries).
> 
> No app or config source files change. You pick up upstream fixes in **4.12.1** (jsdom/`localStorage` setup for Vitest on Node 26), **4.12.2** and **4.13.0** (`pwa-icons` output dir creation and default opaque **180×180** `apple-touch-icon.png`) only when you run tooling that uses those scripts (e.g. icon generation)—not from a normal `build` alone.

author: tomashpl
body:
PR 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-lab-react-app-design.md` (§10). Stacked on #63 — retarget with `gh pr edit --base main` once that merges.

## What is here

`apps/lab`: Vite 8 + React 19, its own ESLint 10 and Prettier, an Nx project that enters both gates, the design system's fourteen colour tokens and two font tokens, the shell (top bar and a tab strip with the full tablist pattern), three routes, the board-store client behind a Vite proxy, the run slice, one long-lived generation worker with `useGenerator` mounted above the routes, the board drawn through `@lit/react`, and one path walked end to end: Generate, carve, draw, save.

It touches `packages/` in exactly one place: two new keys in the engine's bilingual dictionary (`tabDocs`, `tabsLabel`).

**It has been run by hand against the real store**, not only tested: Generate carves a 25×50 board, draws it, and the status line reads `Board closed 100%. — saved`, with no console messages of any kind.

## It overturns §9.1 of the spec, with a measurement

The spec asks for a `proxyReq` hook rewriting `Origin`. Measured against Vite 8.2.2 with an upstream echo computing `new URL(req.url, 'http://' + host)` exactly as `Deno.serve` does:

| proxy options | upstream `Host` | upstream `Origin` | server's `url.origin` | refused? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{ target }` | `localhost:8796` | `http://localhost:8796` | `http://localhost:8796` | **no** |
| `{ target, changeOrigin: true }` | `127.0.0.1:8795` | `http://localhost:8797` | `http://127.0.0.1:8795` | **yes, 403** |
| `{ target, changeOrigin: true, configure: hook }` | `127.0.0.1:8795` | `http://127.0.0.1:8795` | `http://127.0.0.1:8795` | no |

`changeOrigin` is what *earns* the 403, and the hook only undoes that. It is also a security regression the review caught: with `Host` overwritten, the server's loopback check (`lab-server.ts:74`) becomes a tautology, and a DNS-rebinding GET would reach the store's files because GET returns early at `:75` before the `Origin` comparison. The proxy is therefore a target and nothing else, with both keys ending in a slash so `/boards` reaches the application rather than the store. `boards.node.test.ts` holds both lines against a live Vite server and a live `lab-server.ts`.

## Tests that earn their place

- `tokens.test.ts` pins the sixteen tokens the spec keeps, including the two the mock declares and never uses.
- `parity.browser.test.ts` proves the Vite-transformed worker carves the board the engine carves. Its reach is stated honestly: browser mode serves transformed modules, so rollup and minification never run. **A parity test over the output of `vite build` is a prerequisite of PR 8**, which deletes `lab-bundle.test.ts`.
- `LabRoute.browser.test.tsx` asserts that a route change leaves the *same* `<arrowz-board>` node in the document — node identity, not the run's phase, because a remounted element is a disposed GL context whatever the phase says. Probed: making `/` a route element again fails this test and only this test.
- `fonts.browser.test.ts` measures that the two design-system faces actually render, rather than that they are declared.

## Known, recorded, not fixed here

- `/boards/` prefix-matches the whole subtree, so PR 5's board-detail route would be proxied to the store. Suggested remedy when it lands: move the store's files to `/store/`.
- `wasAborted` is cleared by `started()`'s `EMPTY` spread rather than by explicit clears in `finished()`/`failed()`. The invariant holds today; re-check it if PR 3 adds queueing or a second worker.
- Nine deferred minor findings from the task reviews were triaged by the whole-branch review; the two it marked "fix before merge" are fixed.

## What is deliberately absent

Each with its own PR: the knob console (3); the simple view, the language switch and the report (4); the library (5); the docs content (6); the run filmstrip and the ⌘K palette (7). The old lab in `packages/cli` is untouched and retires in PR 8.

author: tablet-ax3-ops
body:
Punto 5: i collegamenti A, C, D e il Dream Trainer -- e il ciclo di apprendimento che finalmente si chiude.

## Il problema che questo file risolve

Questo progetto ha costruito un modulo corretto e testato, per poi non chiamarlo mai, **sette volte**. `diagnostic_assembly.py` risponde allo schema, non al singolo caso: **un file dove vive il cablaggio**, cosi' "e' collegato?" ha un posto dove guardare invece di una ricerca nel codice.

Nessun componente e' stato modificato per adattarsi. L'assemblaggio li compone e basta.

## Il ciclo si chiude -- verificato attraverso un riavvio simulato

```
SESSIONE 1: archi promossi = 1
   bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy -> sarcoidosis  [0.44, 1.00]  learned:case-001:confirmations=3

SESSIONE 2 (riavvio): archi appresi caricati = 1
   -> l'apprendimento SOPRAVVIVE al riavvio
```

`[0.44, 1.00]` su tre conferme -- **visibilmente non certezza**, che e' esattamente a cosa serve l'intervallo.

## `promote_confirmed` e' deliberatamente una chiamata separata

La promozione cambia la base di conoscenza condivisa: deve avvenire quando qualcuno la esegue, **non come effetto collaterale** della risposta al caso di un paziente. Verificato da un test che asserisce che eseguire un caso da solo non scrive nulla.

## Il gancio del DreamTrainer finalmente utilizzabile

`_enumerated` restituiva `None` a meno che `case_context` non portasse `candidate_conditions` -- e nulla nella pipeline ce le metteva mai. Ecco perche' cadeva sulle etichette segnaposto **su ogni caso reale**. `dream_context_for` costruisce quel contesto con i candidati recuperati dal grafo.

16 nuovi test, **969 totali verdi**, lint pulito.

author: emirhan-karaca
body:
### Why this change is important

According to the **[OpenSSF Scorecard](https://securityscorecards.dev/)** and **[SLSA Framework](https://slsa.dev/)**, referencing third-party GitHub Actions via mutable release tags (such as @v4 or @v5) introduces a supply-chain security vulnerability. If an upstream tag is maliciously moved or modified, arbitrary code can execute in your CI/CD environment.

### What this PR does

- Pins all third-party GitHub Actions to immutable full 40-character commit hashes.
- Preserves the original human-readable version tags as inline comments for easy tracking:
  \\\diff
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  + uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4 [pinned by action-pin]
  \\\
- Zero breaking changes to the build, test, or release pipelines.
- Preserves all existing YAML comments, spacing, and formatting.

*Generated with [action-pin](https://github.com/emirhan-karaca/action-pin).*

author: bourbondog
body:
## What this PR does

A Stage-1 seat whose response carried no parseable findings block gets a bounded repair; because the repair's "same findings, fixed" contract cannot be checked against nothing, `run-stages.js` marks the seat's `runStats` row `findingsUnverified: true` (and `repairRefused: {code, detail}` when a checked contract was broken). Both flags have ridden `tally.json` → `verdict.json` since LC-11 and died at the renderer: `report.html`/`report.md`'s **What was lost** was built from the degrade sink's `degrades[]` alone, and `seatsReviewed {reviewed, of}` counted such seats as full reviewers. Study run D0 (2026-09-11): three narration stubs, three repairs, `3 of 3` reviewed, exit 0, nothing shown.

1. **Report rows, both formats.** `src/council/report-lost-rows.js :: lostRowsOf(runStats)` derives `makeDegrade` records when the report is built — one per flagged seat (channel `unverified-repair`: *seat X's findings came from a repair of a response with no findings block — nothing verified them*) and one per refused repair (channel `repair-refused`, naming the code). `report.js :: toModel` appends them after the sink's records, so both renderers print them through `formatDegrade` untouched, and `amicus council report` on an older `verdict.json` shows them too. Nothing is written to `run.json` or `verdict.json`; the exit code and the degrade sink do not move. The wording never says "stub" (study run B2 carried the flag on a real 19,064-byte review with a malformed trailing block).
2. **The census gains a third number (and, after council round 2, a fourth).** `verdict.json` now carries `seatsReviewed: {reviewed, unverified, refused, of}` — `unverified` counts bench seats whose findings came from a repair of a response with no findings block; always written with the census (0 is a measurement); the schema declares it without requiring it, so older documents still validate. D0 reads `{reviewed: 3, unverified: 3, of: 3}` where it read `{reviewed: 3, of: 3}`.
3. **The publish gate sees it.** The council-review check title prints `seats R/O (N unverified)` and the sticky-comment footer `seats reviewed: R of O (N unverified)` when `N > 0`; byte-identical otherwise (jq orders `null` below every number, so a pre-4.9.8 verdict and a clean run both print exactly as before).

Docs: `docs/council.md` (the report's "What it renders", the `seatsReviewed` key note, the repair-contract paragraph, the `runStats[]` row shape); CHANGELOG `### Fixed`.

## What this PR does NOT do — two rulings the council should weigh explicitly

- **P3-R1 (amended by P3-R13 after council round 1) — no sink note and no exit-code change; one stderr line.** The rows are derived when the report is built; `run.json`, `verdict.json.degrades[]` and the degrade sink are untouched, and the exit code does not move. Since round 1 (commit 80fbb56a, kept by the owner) a run whose census count is non-zero prints ONE stderr line at the end — `Notice: 1 of 4 seats' findings came from a repair nothing could verify (glm) — see "What was lost" in report.html` — read off the census the verdict already carries. What is still silent, stated plainly: the exit code (0), `run.json`, and the Workspace GUI's lost-seat panels (which read `run.json.degrades`). The spec's "no new computation" and the exit-code contract are why; a sink `info` note on the (now registered) channels is the recorded follow-up if the owner wants those surfaces to say it too.
- **P3-R3, superseded by P3-R17 after council round 2 — a refused repair has its own census number.** A `repairRefused` seat (`REPAIR_CHANGED_FINDING_COUNT`) has `conformance: unstructured`, `findings: []`, `status: complete`: it tallied no findings at all. It is NOT folded into `unverified` (a seat with no findings has no unverified findings); since round 2 (commit 3f452f60) the census is `seatsReviewed: {reviewed, unverified, refused, of}`, the check title and footer print `(N refused)` when non-zero, and the end-of-run stderr line names those seats — so a seat that contributed nothing never reads as a full reviewer on any gate surface. This extends spec §5's "a third number"; the owner may veto it.
- #242 item 1 (writing repair output back to `review-<seat>.md` / the Stage-2 bundle) stays on the issue, per spec §5.
- `report.js` sits at exactly 300/300 lines; its next edit needs a split.
- Also bundled (round 2): a one-line pin of a pre-existing CI flake in `tests/doctor-alias-check.test.js` (the 24-hour freshness-boundary test read `Date.now()` twice; run 34772368371 failed on ubuntu/node 22 when the readings straddled a millisecond) — unrelated to this feature, test-only.

## Verification

- Fixture: study run D0, verbatim (`tests/council/fixtures/study-d0/`), three flagged seats. Its on-disk `verdict.json` is the pre-4.9.8 document — the report tests prove the rows come from `runStats`, not from a rebuild.
- Byte-identity: a verdict with no flagged row renders exactly as on `main` (av-receiver; the flag-stripped D0 at md 2007 / html 12560 bytes, content pinned by the report snapshots).
- Named mutants, each measured red on the committed tree: **ROWALWAYS** (every row becomes a loss) 10 tests; **REFUSEDDROP** 4; **CENSUSZERO** (`unverified: 0`) V10 + V12; **TITLEBLIND** (the jq clause deleted from the title) 1.
- Gates on the head (`afe6eaae`): `npm run lint`, `check:sizes`, `generate-docs:check`, `npm test` (630 suites / 10054 passed / 8 skipped, `.test-passed` = head), keyless `npm run test:integration` (13 suites / 79 passed / 24 skipped). Zero spend.
- Review trail: per-task opus reviews (Task 1: one fix round — the row's `effect` softened so it is true on a pre-4.9.8 re-render, P3-R8; Tasks 2 and 3 approved first pass), a whole-branch review on the most capable model ("ready to merge", no defects; rulings P3-R3/P3-R10 confirmed and stated above), one fix wave of six prose/docblock edits, scoped re-review clean.
- `jq` is not installed on the dev machine; the workflow edit is pinned by the workflow test and reasoned from jq's ordering — this PR's own council run is its first live execution (watch the title and footer).

## Rulings made while implementing (each with what it costs if wrong)

- **P3-R1** render-time derivation in `toModel`, no sink note — spec says "no new computation"; a sink `degrade` would flip the exit code. Cost: stderr/Workspace do not show the rows.
- **P3-R2** `unverified` always written inside the census, order `reviewed / unverified / of`; schema declares, does not require. Cost: every verdict with a census changes by one key.
- **P3-R3** `unverified` counts `findingsUnverified === true` bench rows only. Cost: a reader wanting refused repairs in the number reads the row instead.
- **P3-R4** seat label = `seat || model` (the street-cred rule).
- **P3-R5** tests in `report-unverified.test.js` / `verdict.test.js` / `council-review-workflow.test.js` (the spec's named files do not exist).
- **P3-R6** fixture = study run D0 (glove-breakin-01's artifacts are not on the dev machine; same brief and seats, 3 flagged of 3).
- **P3-R7** Ajv must be `ajv/dist/2020` (draft 2020-12 schemas) — a plan defect fixed before dispatch.
- **P3-R8** the row's `effect` does not name the census (it must be true on a pre-4.9.8 re-render): *the tiers they were given rest on the repair alone; the seat still counts as reviewed*.
- **P3-R9** the md renderer's guard comment names its second source.

body:
Increasing a later source trace's minimum width on a shared net can leave the routing cache key unchanged. Reordering the same traces can change it instead.

Use the maximum explicit minimum for a connected net, matching the router's [named-net handling](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/de45abb008764235acc2799c0730c9c66b5dedd2/lib/utils/autorouting/getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson.ts#L686). Direct branches retain their own constraints: when one width cannot describe the whole net, include each branch's width and normalized endpoints in the key. This also distinguishes swapped branch widths. Apply the default only where an explicit minimum is absent.

Added 14 tests covering named-net minima, direct branches, defaults, independent nets and normalization; nine fail before the fix. All 27 tests and 13 unchanged snapshots pass, plus types, build and formatting. Existing uniform-width fixture keys remain unchanged; affected multi-width keys intentionally change. This does not change route generation itself.

author: carlelieser
body:
Notion: ["Get it on GitHub" banner classified as screenshot](https://app.notion.com/p/3dae5d90500680619a2cc161ff7e7b7b) (Bug, Scraper)

## Root cause

`STORE_WORDS` in `apps/scraper/src/mapping/readme-images.ts` lists `fdroid`, `izzyondroid`, `googleplay` and `obtainium`, but not `github`. A README image named `get-it-on-github.png` therefore passed every gate in `isRejected()`:

- it is a raster image,
- it carries no `badge` or `shield` substring,
- it is not served from an `/api/` path or a known badge host,
- it holds no `CHROME_WORDS` word,
- and `isStoreBadge` had no store word to match.

It then reached `extractReadmeImages`, where the fallback `preferred.length > 0 ? preferred : resolved` promotes every surviving image when the README has no screenshot-named one. The button became a screenshot. Until now it was only caught by accident, when the filename happened to also contain `button` or `badge`.

## Why the obvious fix was rejected

Adding `'github'` to `STORE_WORDS` looks like a one-word change, but `isStoreBadge` collapses the filename to letters and does a **substring** test. That would also reject legitimate screenshots:

- `docs/github-issues-screen.png`
- `docs/github-actions-dashboard.png`

`github` shows up in ordinary screenshot filenames far more often than `fdroid` does, so this would have traded a visible bug for a quieter one — screenshots silently disappearing from listings.

## The fix

Two predicates wired into `isRejected()`, both built on the existing `wordsOf` word list rather than substring matching:

- `isGetItOnButton` matches the `get`/`on` filename convention shared by every store download button. It generalises to stores nobody has listed yet — `get-it-on-codeberg.png` is now rejected even though `codeberg` is in no word list.
- `isStorefrontName` catches the bare `github.png` case using whole-word semantics, scoped to filenames that are *only* the storefront name.

Because both live in `isRejected()`, this fixes the screenshot path and `findBannerUrl` in one edit.

Word-based matching is what keeps the false-positive rate down. `widget.png`, `budget-overview.png` and `gadget.png` all contain the letters "get" and are all kept; `target-on-map.png` has an `on` but no `get` and is kept too.

## Making the fix retroactive: mapping version

A classification fix alone is not retroactive. `refresh.ts` recomputes `bannerUrl` and `screenshots` only when the README came back `fresh`, so a listing whose README has not changed keeps the store button it stored earlier.

This repo already has the mechanism for exactly this, so no new one was invented:

- `MAPPING_VERSION` in `apps/scraper/src/mapping/version.ts` is the version the mapping logic owns.
- `scrape_sources.mapping_version` persists the version each cached ETag was written under (added back in migration `0003`).
- `readEtag` in `apps/scraper/src/persistence/sources.ts` returns `null` when the stored version differs from the current one.

A null ETag means the conditional request carries no validator, so GitHub answers `200` instead of `304`, the resource arrives `fresh`, and every derived field is recomputed under the current logic. **This PR bumps `MAPPING_VERSION` 9 → 10.**

This is the established convention here — `2a75df7 fix(scraper): bump the mapping version so icons are remapped` did the same thing for an icon change. It is general by construction: any future classification change is made retroactive by bumping the same constant.

**No schema change or migration is required** — `mapping_version` already exists on `scrape_sources`.

The version gate itself had no test coverage, since the comparison was written inline in a database query. It is now named `isEtagUsable` and asserted directly: current version reuses the ETag; an older version, the `0` default on pre-versioning rows, and a newer version (as after a rollback — the check is `!==`, not `<`) all discard it and force a refetch.

## Operational cost of the bump — worth a look before merging

Invalidating every ETag means the next runs refetch rather than getting cheap `304`s. Concretely:

- Invalidation is **global, not scoped to affected listings**. The version lives per *resource*, and there is no join from a listing to its source rows, so all four resources per listing (`repo`, `releases`, `readme`, `git/trees/{branch}`) are refetched — roughly **4 requests per listing** against the authenticated limit of 5,000/hour.
- It is **self-limiting, not a stampede**. `listListingsForRefresh` caps each run at `DEFAULT_MAX_REFRESH = 500` listings (`main.ts:18`) ordered by `last_scraped_at asc nulls first`, so a run costs on the order of **~2,000 requests** and the backlog drains oldest-first over successive nightly runs rather than all at once.
- The practical effect is a **temporary loss of 304 efficiency**: `notModifiedCount` drops and `requestCount` rises for as many runs as it takes the corpus to cycle through, then returns to baseline. Listings recover their correct screenshots as they are reached.

I don't have the production listing count from here, so the total number of runs to fully drain depends on corpus size — at 500/run, a corpus of N listings needs about N/500 runs. **If the corpus is large enough that this is a concern, the bump can be landed separately from the classification fix.** Flagging it rather than assuming it is acceptable.

## Tests

Written first, confirmed failing before the fix. Each predicate was then disabled independently to confirm both are load-bearing; the same was done for the version gate.

Rejected: `assets/get-it-on-github.png`, `assets/get_it_on_github.png`, `fastlane/get-it-on-github.png`, `.github/resources/github.png`
Kept: `docs/github-issues-screen.png`, `docs/github-actions-dashboard.png`

`bun run test` (477 passing), `bun run check` and `bun run lint` all pass at the repo root. No existing assertion changed, including the no-screenshot fallback case and the platform-mention case.

## Summary

Fixes two issues surfaced while triaging Google Search Console reports for ab.dk.

### Rich Results — missing SportsEvent fields
GSC's structured data report flagged the `SportsEvent` schema on `/kamp/{id}` and `/en/match/{id}` as incomplete:

| Issue | Count | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Missing `performer` | 15 | Added home/away teams as `SportsTeam` performers — was never emitted |
| Missing `address` (in `location`) | 3 | Was only emitted for home fixtures; now always present, falling back to `addressCountry: DK` for away grounds where we don't hold a street address |

Not changed (flagged as warnings, not errors, and intentionally accurate rather than fabricated):
- `offers` on away fixtures — AB doesn't sell tickets for away matches, so omitting `offers` there is correct.
- `price`/`priceCurrency` — no real price data is available from the billet.ab.dk scrape; publishing an invented number would be worse than the warning.

### Soft 404s
Every content detail route (`nyheder`, `en/news`, `spiller`, `en/player`, `stab`, `en/staff`, `partnere`, `en/partners`) redirected (302) an unknown slug to its parent listing page instead of 404ing — the classic soft-404 pattern GSC's Page Indexing report flags.

Unknown slugs now `Astro.rewrite()` to a real 404 response. Curated redirects are unaffected:
- canonical-slug 308s (legacy name-only player URLs → `{id}-{slug}`)
- `EXCLUDED_PLAYER_SLUGS` legacy exclusion list
- `hideFromSquad` Strapi override

Adds `src/pages/en/404.astro` — `getLocale()` reads the *rewritten* path, so rewriting an English route to `/404` would have rendered the Danish 404 page instead.

## Verification

- `npm run check` — 0 errors
- `npm run build` — passes
- Manual dev-server checks: all 8 unknown-slug routes return 404 with correct locale; known content and curated redirects still resolve correctly

## Related

The other GSC finding from this triage — 4 leftover Astro-template ("LaunchPad") demo pages (`homepage`, `pricing`, `faq`, `contact`) live in Strapi and polluting the sitemap — was resolved directly in Strapi admin (unpublished), not in this PR.

## Contexto

Requisito de observabilidade da Fase 3: além de métricas/traces de infraestrutura, o desafio pede **eventos de negócio** que permitam construir dashboards e um alerta sobre o processamento das Ordens de Serviço. Este PR entrega a **instrumentação no código** — a metade que faltava para que qualquer requisição (Postman/API) passe a gerar dados no New Relic.

## O que muda

- **Porta `eventRecorder` + `EventoOS`** na camada de aplicação (`ports.go`) — inversão de dependência, no mesmo padrão do `notifier`.
- **Adapter New Relic** em `internal/infra/observability` — publica `OrdemServicoEvent` via `RecordCustomEvent`. É **no-op** quando não há transação New Relic no contexto (ambiente local sem licença), então o caso de uso nunca é afetado.
- **Instrumentação** em `CriarOS`, `AvancarStatus`, `AprovarOrcamento` e `RejeitarOrcamento`:
  - emite `resultado: "sucesso"` na transição concluída (com `duracao_status_segundos` para o dashboard de tempo médio por status);
  - emite `resultado: "falha"` **apenas** em erro de persistência/infra (`persistencia_os`, `deducao_estoque`, `atualizacao_status`). Validações de cliente (4xx) **não** emitem — assim o alerta de falha continua significativo.
- **Injeção via functional option** (`ComEventRecorder`), preservando todos os callers existentes; wiring no server HTTP.

## Segurança / LGPD

O evento **não carrega CPF nem e-mail** — só identificadores da OS e metadados de status. Inclui `trace.id`/`span.id` para correlacionar o gráfico com traces e logs da mesma requisição.

## Testes

- Use case: sucesso, falha na persistência, validação-não-emite, sem-recorder-não-panica.
- Adapter: no-op sem transação no contexto.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet` e testes dos pacotes afetados passando.

## Próximo passo (fora deste PR)

Definição dos **dashboards + alerta como código** (NRQL sobre `OrdemServicoEvent`): volume diário, tempo médio por status, erros de integração, e alerta em `resultado: "falha"`.

author: shivamagw06-dev
body:
Reading the fifty claims NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 filing produced. **Most are the material content of the quarter:**

> "supply and capacity commitments from $119 billion last quarter to **$279 billion**"
> "Data Center revenue was $89.0 billion, **up 117%**… driven by the ramp of our Blackwell Ultra infrastructure"
> "**Three direct customers** accounted for 25%, 18%, and 13% of our accounts receivable"
> "guarantees, capped at a total of **$105 billion**… with affiliates of SB Energy Corp"
> "a **$4.5 billion charge**… associated with H20 for excess inventory, as the demand for H20 products diminished"

Four were not.

## A theme belongs to the business that has it

The freight theme matched the bare word `export`, so NVIDIA's **semiconductor export controls** were tagged as railroad volumes.

The plural is what means cargo. It keeps Berkshire's *"higher grain **exports** and petroleum fuel shipments"* and drops four of Berkshire's own false positives about pipelines and tariffs.

## Two more pieces of boilerplate

| sentence | why it is not a risk |
|---|---|
| "**Any of these risks** may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows." | refers back to the risks above and names none of them |
| "**You should read this Quarterly Report** on Form 10-Q completely and understand that our actual future results may be materially different" | an instruction to the reader |

Both were published as risks.

## A cover page's checkbox ballot

NVIDIA's 10-Q opens with Yes/No ballots, and the first real fact on the page arrived welded to one:

> "**Yes ☐ No ☒** The number of shares of common stock, $0.001 par value, outstanding as of August 21, 2026, was 24.1 billion."

## A cross-reference reports nothing

A sentence ending in `Item 2.` is an index entry — and that one arrived with a **whole lease table flattened in front of it**. The annual-report side has refused these since it was built; the chain did not.

## On the evidence for the two new boilerplate rules

They are **weaker than the rest and the fixture says so**: judged wrong on review, rather than rejected by the person working the queue. Two real NVIDIA risks in the same register are asserted alongside them — *"Any regulatory control or other restriction that limits our ability to provide products and services…"* — because telling those apart is the whole difficulty.

## Measured

Berkshire 746 → **745 claims**, the one lost being a cross-reference. Risks 29 → 28.

Suite 1,584 → **1,593 passing.**

body:
## Summary

Phase 10 Security Audit Task 10.3 (#566) — pin the audit acceptance that `Wallet::as_keypair` is NOT reachable from external crates.

`Wallet::as_keypair` was narrowed from `pub` to `pub(crate)` in commit `abb123c6` (merged via PR #570 / squash `461773ac`). An external crate (FFI consumer, downstream library) trying to call it should hit a compile error: `E0624: method 'as_keypair' is private`.

The narrowing itself was already shipped; this PR pins the acceptance contract via a gated negative compile-fail test + CI job.

## Changes

**`Cargo.toml`** (+12 lines):
- `[lints.rust] unexpected_cfgs = { level = "allow", check-cfg = ["cfg(negative_test)"] }` — registers the custom cfg name so clippy's `-D warnings` (via the `rust-lint` CI job) doesn't reject the gated test file.

**`tests/wallet_as_keypair_external_reach.rs`** (new, 52 lines):
- Negative compile-fail test, gated behind `#![cfg(negative_test)]` + `#[cfg(negative_test)] fn attempt_external_as_keypair_call`.
- File-level doc-comment explains the contract: under the regular `cargo test` run (cfg OFF) the file is inert; under `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg negative_test"` the file calls `wallet.as_keypair()` from an external-crate namespace, which MUST fail with `E0624`.
- If the build ever succeeds under `--cfg negative_test`, the audit acceptance has been violated.

**`.github/workflows/rust-sol-core-ci.yml`** (+48 lines):
- New job `rust-test-negative-as-keypair` between `rust-test` and `rust-deps`.
- Runs `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg negative_test" cargo test -p sol-wallet-core --test wallet_as_keypair_external_reach` and asserts:
  1. Exit code != 0 (compile failure expected)
  2. `grep -q 'E0624'` against stderr (expected error pattern)
- `continue-on-error: true` because the negative test SHOULD fail to compile — a non-zero exit here is the audit passing.

## Verification

```
cargo clippy -p sol-wallet-core --all-targets -- -D warnings   # GREEN
cargo test -p sol-wallet-core --lib --tests                     # GREEN (gated file inert)
RUSTFLAGS="--cfg negative_test" cargo test -p sol-wallet-core --test wallet_as_keypair_external_reach
# error[E0624]: method `as_keypair` is private
```

## Commits

1. `4ec7db40` chore(sol): register negative_test cfg in Cargo.toml lints
2. `6d500bbf` test(sol): negative compile-fail pin for Wallet::as_keypair visibility
3. `862033f3` ci(sol): rust-test-negative-as-keypair — assert E0624 on gated negative test

## Related

- Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-09-sol-wallet-core-v0.1.md` Phase 10 Security Audit / Task 10.3
- Issue: #566
- Prior audit series: PR #570 (Task 10.1), PR #571 (Task 10.2 + H1 follow-up)

body:
## Summary

Eligible local factory work can continue under one bounded operator authorization, with delivery artifacts checked for staleness before they are reused. This adds the candidate-stage continuation and evidence checks needed for Gaia's unattended delivery loop; it does not activate that loop or automate publication and merge.

## Boundaries worth reviewing

- One repository, finite run budget, one active job in a local SQLite registry. Revocation blocks future starts; uncertain completion retains the slot instead of rerunning work. Separate registries and manual runs are outside this exclusion guarantee.
- Restricted Claude subscription workers render bounded provider activity. A non-TTY host refuses before consuming authority. This is not an OS sandbox.
- Artifact chains pin content digests across intent, candidate, test, independent-review and publication stages. Required dependency changes invalidate downstream freshness; advisory/reference changes do not. Missing stages remain missing and payload claims remain unverified.
- Candidate sidecars are immutable derived files, not authority or a second terminal-state ledger. A sidecar failure cannot rerun a completed worker.

## Related

Related: #53, #141, #145

## Prior full-scope validation

Subject: `26e564af8930882e6b99184439ac0c591ad8290f`; base: `cd98875b4d6145916320af858c421ca668229797`.

- Node 26.8.1 on Windows: 82 focused tests pass twice in each independent review subject.
- Full default-concurrency suite: 2,146 passed, zero failed, one skipped in the Spec subject and coordinator rerun.
- The Standards subject's first full run failed an unchanged dashboard abort timing test. That file passed isolated reruns; the full serial rerun passed 2,146 tests with one skip. The original failure is retained, not discarded.
- `npm run verify` exits zero; three local bus-evidence checks remain advisory and do not establish live inter-agent delivery.
- Architecture drift passes against the pinned base.

Two independent Claude Fable 5 reviews approve this exact subject: Spec session `cdbb3c84-5822-4511-8006-c470921f8001` and Standards session `f9c97b6e-7fc6-4658-915a-94286e6b3a92`. Their source copies remained clean and byte-identical before and after review; the coordinator verified their fixed points and consumed both reports.

Non-blocking review notes are retained: the focused npm alias omits newer suites (the full test command includes them), some failure codes and freshness labels could be clearer, and one canonical encoder is duplicated for a flat internal value. No review claims live operation or grants merge authority.

## Latest reviewed delta

Current head: `354c0e1b269fa1e7caa5ce00faed128b7a2acc64`. Delta base: `26e564af8930882e6b99184439ac0c591ad8290f`.

- `75f3c7d` selectively adopts SlashForge instruction coverage, visible investigation handoffs and explicit review coverage into existing guidance. No package, new workflow or authority change.
- `354c0e1` fixes missing/non-string diagnostic codes at the factory and CLI boundaries. [P2 repair and test evidence](https://github.com/GuitarAlchemist/gaia/pull/146#discussion_r4000083767).
- Two fresh independent Claude Fable 5 contexts approve this seven-file delta: Spec `b5717850-946e-4b03-9ddd-8dbe279d2f94`; Standards `69f154aa-a530-453c-9786-dfada3ccfad2`. The Standards reviewer fully read all seven files; Spec recorded full changed-hunk coverage and its partial context reads. Both review subjects remained clean at tree `a4d4afec11a4195047f5dff712ed5ceb91df4bd5`.
- Each reviewer ran 22 new regressions twice, 27 adjacent tests and the full suite: 2,168 passed, zero failed, one environmental Playwright skip. Independent old-mechanism controls reproduced the defect. Verify retains its three non-gating bus-evidence shape advisories.
- Bare delta architecture checks refused absent impact declarations; declared probes passed. Coordinator replay using this PR's actual impact declaration and main base `cd98875b4d6145916320af858c421ca668229797` passed at the current head. The writer's pre-commit architecture PASS is not used as evidence for the committed delta.
- Non-blocking notes: README's test-count explanation could distinguish loop registration; the ASCII regex lacks a behaviorally unnecessary unicode flag. No blocker was reported on either axis.
- Review artifact SHA-256: Spec `203e2eb45c08471c61957def0aacc90b4ee402fc99e7bdce06cb7f27ec6825c5`; Standards `2f3d785e6a5c51592bc731f62464a23f7310b3d88db41fb244a9408419126fcf`.

One new #53 candidate is authorized after verification, but none has been started. The old registry remains revoked with zero used runs. Intake still needs a source head and an explicit disposition of historical reviewer assignments in the sealed normal-admission policy. No policy change, workflow dispatch, merge or deployment was performed.

## Operational limits

The prior bounded activation produced no candidate and its policy was revoked. wmux screen capture remains intermittent; passing controlled display probes is not proof that the live pump is observable. The canary source still lacks an unambiguous eligible head. No authority reset, activation, hosted-policy change, deployment or merge is included here.

author: akadlec
body:
## What

`RouterTest` and `WidgetsRepositoryTest` in `Module/Ui` carried a `.phpt` extension, which made them **invisible to every gate at once**:

- `tools/phpunit.xml` `<directory>` entries set no `suffix`, so PHPUnit's default of `Test.php` excluded them
- PHP_CodeSniffer and PHPStan only scan `.php`

Pointing PHPUnit at the directory directly rejects both with `InvalidPhptFileException` — they are ordinary test classes, not PHPT fixtures. They weren't merely unrun, they were **unrunnable**.

Renaming them adds **5 tests and 7 assertions**, and surfaced three dormant problems.

## 1. A test asserting the opposite of its three siblings

`RouterTest::testPrefixedRoutes` expected the module prefix to be the *valid* path, and omitted `/api` entirely. Devices, Triggers and Accounts all run the same test against the same `apiPrefix: false` config:

| | Devices / Triggers / Accounts | Ui (before) |
|---|---|---|
| valid | `/api/v1/<resource>` → 200 | `/<module-prefix>/v1/dashboards` → 200 |
| invalid | `/api/<module-prefix>/v1/<resource>` → 404 | `/v1/dashboards` → 404 |

Now aligned with its siblings; all 13 tests in the two files pass.

**How it hid is the interesting part.** Its `readAllInvalid` case expected 404 and got 404 — but so did the supposedly-valid path, because neither route existed at that prefix. A test that passes because *everything* 404s is indistinguishable from one that passes for the right reason.

## 2. 16 coding-standard violations

Fixed by `make csf`.

## 3. Two missing `@throws` tags

For `Uuid::fromString`. I initially over-applied the fix to three doc blocks; PHPStan's `throws.unusedType` caught the third immediately.

## CLAUDE.md

Two traps recorded:

- **Test files must be named `*Test.php`** or they slip past all three gates simultaneously.
- **`composer install` does not refresh the `vendor/fastybird/*` mirror.** `COMPOSER_MIRROR_PATH_REPOS=1` copies path repos rather than symlinking, and Composer skips a package already installed at the same version — so an edit under a package's `src/` has no effect on anything loading the production namespaces until `composer reinstall <package>`. This once produced a confident "Nothing to update" from `orm:schema-tool:update`, which would have shipped an entity change with no migration.

## Verification

```
lint 0   cs 0   phpstan 0
tests 0  OK (1415 tests, 5678 assertions)    (was 1410 / 5671)
```

body:
The `Verify and publish release` job failed at release artifact verification because `.SRCINFO` was missing from downloaded release assets. The publish workflow uploaded `signed-assets/*`, which does not include dotfiles, so `.SRCINFO` was excluded from the GitHub release.

- **Root cause**
  - Release verification expects `.SRCINFO` in the published asset set.
  - Shell glob `signed-assets/*` omitted `.SRCINFO`, causing `verify-assets.mjs` to fail with `Missing .SRCINFO`.

- **Workflow change**
  - Updated release upload logic to:
    - start from `signed-assets/*`
    - conditionally append `signed-assets/.SRCINFO` when present
    - upload the assembled list via `gh release upload`

- **Regression guard**
  - Added a focused workflow contract assertion in `src-tauri/tauri-workflow.test.ts` to ensure hidden `.SRCINFO` handling remains in `release.yml`.

```bash
assets=(signed-assets/*)
if [ -f signed-assets/.SRCINFO ]; then
  assets+=(signed-assets/.SRCINFO)
fi
gh release upload "$TAG" "${assets[@]}" --repo "$REPOSITORY"
```

body:
Fixes NER-304

Projekt z `tracker: github` przechodzi całą oś pluginu (issue-writer → plan → start → implementacja → review → close-out) przez nowy adapter `adapters/trackers/github.md`, z fazami kanonicznymi niesionymi przez strategię `label` (domyślnie) albo `comment`; nowa operacja kontraktu `issue.create-branch` (Linear: `git checkout -b`, GitHub: `gh issue develop`).

## Review

`review-verify` (4 osie, `main...HEAD`): mapped 2, verified 1, rejected 1, unverifiedOverflow 0, gaps 0. Zweryfikowane (security, major): filtr `authorAssociation` OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR w strategii `comment` nie gwarantował prawa zapisu wymaganego przez `adapters/statuses.md` — poprawione: autor markera sprawdzany przez `gh api repos/<REPO>/collaborators/<login>/permission` (`admin`/`write`).

## Weryfikacja

Lokalnie: `node --test 'scripts/**/*.test.ts'` 222/0; `validate-workflow-graph.ts` (5 adapterów), `validate-platform-config.ts` (2 domyślne mapy adapterów + konfiguracja `tracker: github` z mapą domyślną i ze strategią `comment`; `native` odrzucone), `validate-cli-dependencies.ts`, `validate-manifests.ts` (0.27.0) — zielone. Kontrakt: `issue.create-branch` dodane najpierw w `workflow-graph.json`, walidator czerwony dla `linear.md`, potem zielony.

End-to-end na prywatnym repo testowym `nerd4rent/n4r-github-tracker-sandbox` (`gh` 2.100.0), operacja po operacji według receptur adaptera z tej gałęzi:

| Krok osi | Operacja / receptura | Wynik |
|---|---|---|
| bind-statuses | `label.list` → brak `status::*` → `label.create` ×3 | etykiety utworzone |
| issue-writer | `issue.create` + `issue.create-child --parent` | #7, #8; `subIssues` [8], `parent` 7 |
| odczyt fazy | `label` read, otwarte bez etykiety | `backlog` |
| plan | `issue.comment` + `issue.set-status todo` | `todo` |
| zatwierdzenie (symulacja człowieka) | etykieta `status::in-progress` | `in-progress` |
| issue-start | `issue.read-branch` (slug ASCII), `issue.create-branch`, pusty commit, draft PR `Fixes #7` | gałąź `7-e2e-os-github-issues` powiązana z issue; PR #9 `closingIssuesReferences` [7] |
| create-branch na istniejącej gałęzi | receptura z kontrolą `show-ref`/`ls-remote` | exit 1 „already exists” (sam `gh issue develop` zwraca 0) |
| resolve-from-branch | wiodący numer + `gh issue view` | `#7` |
| review | `issue.set-status in-review` (zdjęcie `in-progress`) | `in-review` |
| issue-close | `pr ready`, `pr merge --merge`, checkout `main` + pull, `issue.set-status done` | merge commit; issue zamknięte przez `Fixes #7` (COMPLETED), `gh issue close` idempotentne; faza `done` |
| odrzucenie PR | `issue.read` na #9 | `url` z `/pull/` → odrzucone |
| label: przejścia | closed → `status::todo` (reopen), → `open` | `todo`, potem `backlog` |
| comment | brak markera / `Status: todo` / marker w 2. linii / `Status: in-progress` | `backlog` / `todo` / ignorowany / `in-progress` |
| comment: autorzy (po review) | nowsze markery od `octocat` (`permission: none`, association `MEMBER` w fixture) i od usuniętego konta (404) | pominięte, liczy się marker autora z `admin` |
| comment: brak weryfikowalnego markera | jedyny marker od autora `none` | `backlog` |
| comment: wywołujący bez push | endpoint uprawnień na `cli/cli` (403) | stop, phase unknown |
| comment: wartość spoza mapy | `Status: cancelled` | phase unknown |

Nie zweryfikowane live: uprawnienia tokena fine-grained (sprawdzony tylko klasyczny `repo`), `Fixes owner/repo#123` między repozytoriami, uruchomienie skilli jako pluginu 0.27.0 (receptury wykonane ręcznie; zainstalowany plugin 0.26.0).

Odkryte gotchas zapisane w adapterze: `gh issue view` przyjmuje numer PR; `gh issue develop` nie zwraca błędu dla istniejącej gałęzi, a `--list` przestaje ją pokazywać po otwarciu PR; domyślna nazwa gałęzi zachowuje polskie znaki; `--remove-label` na etykiecie nieistniejącej w repo zwraca błąd; `gh issue list` opóźnia się o kilka sekund po zmianie etykiety.
