author: mafarrag
body:
# Description

`cleopatra.basemap.tiles` could only talk to an XYZ slippy-tile template, so a service published as OGC **WMS** or
**WMTS** — which is how most national and institutional imagery is served — could not be drawn at all.

The interesting part is how little had to change. `tiles` reaches a provider through exactly one call,
`build_url(x=, y=, z=)` returning an http(s) URL. Everything downstream of it is already service-agnostic: the fetch
returns opaque `bytes`, the mosaic is stitched from `dict[Tile, bytes]`, and the composite is drawn with
`ax.imshow`. The gap was entirely in URL construction, so the bulk of this PR is one new module. It does make one
change next door, described under "What this changes in `tiles.py`" below.

`WMTSProvider` and `WMSProvider` are frozen dataclasses satisfying that one-method contract, which means they work
through the unchanged public entry point — `add_tiles` already accepts a non-string provider object:

```python
from cleopatra.basemap.ogc import WMSProvider, WMTSProvider
from cleopatra.basemap.tiles import add_tiles

add_tiles(ax, WMTSProvider(url="https://example.org/wmts", layer="TrueColor"), crs=3857)
add_tiles(ax, WMSProvider(url="https://example.org/wms", layers="ortho"))
```

The two service kinds reach the same place differently, and that difference is the whole design:

- **WMTS is a tiling scheme.** A `GetTile` request is a `(TileMatrix, TileRow, TileCol)` triple, which *is*
  `(z, y, x)`. On the `GoogleMapsCompatible` matrix set that is exactly the grid `_lonlat_to_tile_xy` already
  computes, so the mapping is the identity. Both encodings are supported: a `url` containing `{TileMatrix}` is
  treated as a RESTful template and substituted, anything else as a KVP endpoint.
- **WMS is a single-image request.** A `GetMap` takes a `BBOX` plus `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`, not a tile index. It fits by
  asking for *one `GetMap` per tile*: `_tile_xy_bounds` already returns precisely the EPSG:3857 bounds a `BBOX`
  needs. Pinning every request to EPSG:3857 also sidesteps the WMS 1.3.0 axis-order trap — 1.3.0 orders `BBOX` by
  the CRS's own axis order, and it is EPSG:4326 that flips to latitude-first, a CRS never requested here.

Two things come for free because the renderer already reads them defensively: the **attribution** line
(`add_tiles(attribution=True)` picks up the dataclass field) and **credentials**, since a keyed service is just a
query parameter — which also closes the keyed-provider gap that existed for XYZ, where `build_url` is called with
no way to supply a key.

Service descriptions are validated at construction rather than per tile mid-render, so a bad endpoint, an empty
layer or an unknown WMS version names the field it came from instead of surfacing much later as an unreadable
tile. `extra_params` is copied behind a read-only view, so a caller mutating their own dict afterwards cannot
rewrite the URLs of an already-built provider.

**Deliberately not included.** The tile-matrix-set generalisation (phase 2 in the issue) — a WMTS on a grid that
is *not* GoogleMapsCompatible needs five geometric call sites to take the scheme as data, which is an extraction
across `tiles.py`, not an addition beside it. Doing it first would block the common case behind a refactor. The
limitation is stated in the module docstring and on the docs page rather than left to be discovered. Also skipped:
a `GeoMixin.add_wms` / `add_wmts` convenience, which `add_tiles(ax, WMSProvider(...))` already covers.

**What this changes in `tiles.py`** (+118/−3). Two review rounds turned up one defect that could not be fixed
from the new module: `fetch_single_tile` wrote the full request URL to the debug log on every failed attempt, and
this PR documents `extra_params` as the place to put an API key — so a flaky service persisted the credential
wherever the logs go. That was already true for a keyed XYZ template. `_redact_url` masks credential-shaped query
values and userinfo while keeping the OGC/XYZ parameter names that say *which* tile failed, so the retry log stays
diagnosable. `add_tiles`'s and `world_texture`'s docstrings also learned the providers exist. **This is a
behaviour change for existing XYZ users: the debug log line is now redacted.** Nothing else in the render path
moved.

No new runtime dependency — `urllib.parse.urlencode` and `decimal.Decimal` are stdlib — and no lockfile change.
Importing the module touches neither `xyzservices` nor `pyproj`; the `[tiles]` extra is still required only to
render, enforced by `add_tiles` as before.

# Issues

- Closes #355 — Serve WMS and WMTS basemaps through the existing tile fetch-and-stitch path

## Type of change

Check relevant points.

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] This change requires a documentation update
- [ ] Dev changes (CI/pyproject.toml/docs/examples/testing)

Additive apart from one deliberate change in `tiles.py`: a failed tile fetch now logs a redacted URL instead of
the full one. Every existing XYZ caller sees that difference, at DEBUG level only. The two new provider classes are
opt-in and nothing that works today renders differently.

# How Has This Been Tested?

Full suite, run against the worktree:

```bash
VIRTUAL_ENV="C:/python-environments/uv/cleopatra" PYTHONPATH="<worktree>/src" \
  python -m pytest "<worktree>/tests" -q -p no:cacheprovider
# 3143 passed  (2968 before this branch, + 175 new in tests/test_ogc.py)
```

`src/cleopatra/basemap/ogc.py` and `src/cleopatra/basemap/tiles.py` are both at **100 %** line and branch
coverage. Doctests across the two modules: **24 passed**. `ruff@0.15.22 format --check` and `check` are clean
on every file this branch touches.

- [x] **Test A — URL construction, no network and no optional dependency.** `TestWMTSProviderBuildUrl` and
  `TestWMSProviderBuildUrl` pin the tile-triple mapping, the fixed service parameters, the RESTful substitution,
  `extra_params` merging/escaping/overriding, and preservation of an endpoint's pre-existing query string. The WMS
  `BBOX` is asserted against `_tile_xy_bounds` itself over three tiles rather than a copied literal, so the two
  cannot drift apart.
- [x] **Test B — the 1.1.1 / 1.3.0 axis trap.** `test_crs_parameter_follows_the_version` checks all four supported
  versions send the right key *and* not the wrong one; sending the wrong spelling would make a service silently
  answer in its own default CRS and misplace every tile.
- [x] **Test C — validation and immutability.** Every rejected construction is covered, including `tile_size=True`
  (an `int` subclass a bare `isinstance` check would wave through as a 1-pixel request), plus that mutating the
  caller's `extra_params` dict afterwards does not change the provider.
- [x] **Test D — end to end through the real pipeline.** `TestProvidersDriveAddTiles` patches only the HTTP opener
  and lets the genuine `fetch_single_tile` → `fetch_tiles` → `stitch_tiles` → `imshow` path run, asserting a mosaic
  is drawn, that *every* request carries `REQUEST=GetTile` / `REQUEST=GetMap` (so a silent fallback to a default XYZ
  provider could not pass), and that the attribution reaches the axes. Patching `fetch_tiles` instead — as some
  existing tile tests do — would never call `build_url` at all, which is exactly the seam under test.

## Review

Two full `/review-rounds` passes, each in an isolated reviewer with no obligation to fix what it found.

- **Round 1** — 20 findings (1 High, 7 Medium, 7 Low, 5 Nit), all fixed. The High: an endpoint ending in `?` got a
  second one, renaming the mandatory `SERVICE` parameter to `?SERVICE` and failing every tile of a
  MapServer/GeoServer-style endpoint.
- **Round 2** — 16 findings

author: nikkikom
body:
## What

Milestone 1 of the zoned DAS thermal plan: `src/aqua_bridge/sim/das.py`, a DAS truth plant that later milestones (zones, PI-DAS, estimator, MPC-DAS, identification, hot-swap and noise regression tests) run against, plus `--sim-plant {basic,rich,das}` in `__main__`.

### Truth model
- Per zone air node: inlet (ambient + per-zone offset), leak, misc heat, symmetric inter-zone leakage `kappa` (declared pairs; the `rich` preset also adds small undeclared leakage).
- Per bay latent drive node: class (hdd / ssd_sata / nvme) heat idle/active driven by `heat_schedule` activity or seeded bursts, `h = g0 + k * Qn_z`.
- Per sensor lag node: roles inlet / zone_air / drive_proximal / exhaust, placement offset, air fraction `beta` for proximal sensors, lag, per-type quantisation (thermistor 0.01, DS18B20 0.0625), optional noise and dropout.
- SMART per drive with serial: internal offset, internal lag, 1 degC quantisation, seeded 30-60 s cadence. Stale entries of removed drives keep ageing, and the truth bay is never exposed (no SES).
- Fans per PWM output: dead band, airflow exponent, 1-2 fans (splitter; only fan 0 drives the tach), tach-less outputs (rpm key absent, as in the hwmon adapter), stall per fan, spin-up lag, fouling drift, resonance bands, and a truth noise index from rpm.
- Hot swap via `bay_schedule` (remove/insert with class, serial, model, temp) or `remove()` / `insert()`.
- Integration: backward-Euler substeps on the per-tick linear system. It is unconditionally stable for the stiff air nodes and conserves energy exactly in the discrete sense; `plant.energy` records that balance and the tests check it.
- Deterministic per seed. Generators are keyed by purpose and name, so results do not depend on dict order, and `observe()` is idempotent.

### API for later milestones
- `build_das_params(topology, preset=, seed=, dt=, heat_schedule=, bay_schedule=, **overrides)` / `build_das_plant(...)` from a plain `{zones, bays, fans, sensors}` dict (optional `inlet`, `heat_schedule`, `bay_schedule`). Controller-side keys (`zones.channels`, `fans.model/group`, `sensors.redundant`) are accepted and ignored.
- `default_topology()`: 4 zones, 15 bays, 8 outputs, 25 sensors (8 thermistors).
- `DasPlant`: `observe`, `observe_smart`, `apply`, `advance`, `step`, `steady_state(pwm)`, truth accessors (`t_air`, `t_drive`, `sensor_truth`, `margins`, `airflow`, `noise_db`, ...), `stall`/`unstall`, `remove`/`insert`.
- `run_das_closed_loop(plant, cfg, controller, ticks, observe_hook=, smart_hook=, on_tick=)` returns `DasRun(records, series)`. The series are JSON-serialisable truth time series, and `DasRun` adds `array()`, `worst_margin_c()` and `violations()`.

### `__main__`
- `basic` (default) builds exactly the legacy RC plant, so legacy behaviour is unchanged.
- `rich` is the legacy RC plant with 1 tick of actuator delay and 0.02 degC noise.
- `das` builds the truth plant from a top-level `sim.das: {topology?, preset?, seed?}` section. Without that section, or when `mpc.temps` / `mpc.channels` are not in the topology, it fails with a clear `ConfigError` (exit code 2).

`sim/plant.py`, the legacy goldens and PROJECT.md/README.md are untouched.

## Tests
`tests/test_sim_das.py` (57 tests, about 5 s): topology validation, preset and override rules, energy balance through transients and hot swap, steady state and heat balance, monotone cooling (uniform and per output), dead band and exponent, quantisation and DS18B20 plateaus, first-order lag, SMART cadence and offset, splitter and tach-less outputs, fouling and inlet drift, activity bursts, hot swap, closed loop with `checked_step`, determinism per seed, lie injection hooks, and `--sim-plant` wiring. Full suite: 927 passed.

## Deviations
- `run_closed_loop` (legacy) keeps its signature. The DAS loop is a separate `run_das_closed_loop`, because it returns truth time series.
- Schedules (`heat_schedule`, `bay_schedule`, inlet steps) are in plant seconds, not tick indices, so they do not change with `dt`. Bay events take effect at the first tick boundary at or after `t_s`.
- `--sim-plant das` reads its topology from an interim top-level `sim.das` section (kept in `AppConfig.extra`), because the zoned `mpc` config does not exist yet. Once it lands, the zoned config maps onto the same topology dict.
- `rich` for the legacy plant is defined as delay + noise. The plan only says basic/rich keep today's plant.
- Until `PlantObservation.inputs` exists (estimator milestone), SMART is exposed through `observe_smart()` and recorded in the series. It is not passed to the controller.
- The `rich` preset leaves sensor dropout at 0 so that later closed-loop tests do not get unintended zone faults. `dropout_prob` is available per sensor.

author: drehtuer
body:
Four defects you found on the phone. **Stacked on #59** — merge that first.

None of them could have been caught by a test as written, which is its own finding; each now has one.

## The walls were not drawn

`light()` added a key light and a fill and **no ambient at all**. Every surface facing away from both is then exactly black — and the surfaces facing away from both are the inner walls. What you saw was the lit top of the wall, a shadow cast across the floor, and nothing in between casting it.

A tray is lit by a room, not by two lamps in a void. There is now an `IndirectLight`: one spherical-harmonic band, which is the constant term and nothing else. A sky-above/ground-below gradient would want three bands and this file being right about which axis Filament's harmonics run along — invisible when wrong, and not worth being clever about for a tray lit by a room.

## The camera closed in on the dice

Which took the table away with it. `2d12` looked like one d12 because the other was outside the frame — both dice were always there.

It now frames the whole tray and stays there, start to finish. Looking closer is yours to do by pinching, and that is written down as a task rather than guessed at — so `framingTheDice` and `eased` are **deleted** rather than left as dead code. Their tests are replaced by the two claims that are left and now matter more: the whole tray is in shot at every shape of phone, and a die against the far wall is wholly inside it.

## A settled roll vanished when the screen blanked

`LiveRoll.close()` ended the renderer, and the tray closes a roll the moment it lands — so the scene was torn down while you were still reading it. It survived only as the last drawn buffer, so anything that took the surface away and gave it back left a black tray until the next roll. That is exactly "recovers after rolling".

Closing a roll now gives back the physics world and nothing else. The picture outlives the simulation that made it; the tray ends it when there is nothing left to look at. The regression test is your sequence: land a roll, lose the surface, get it back, dice still there.

## The screen blanked at all

The roll screen now holds it on, on the view rather than the window flags — undone by leaving the screen rather than by remembering to undo it.

## Found while verifying, not fixed here

**A d12 is simulated and drawn at about 45 mm.** `ShapeGeometry.boundingRadiusPerSize` holds each solid's circumradius **per edge** (`√3/2` for a cube, `(√3/4)(1+√5)` for a dodecahedron), but it is multiplied by `DieMaterial.sizeMm` — documented as the die's nominal size *across*, and read as a diameter by `DieMaterial.boundingRadiusMm` (`sizeMm / 2`). They disagree by 2.8× for a d12; a cube only looks right because its edge and its size across are the same number.

Everything is internally consistent — hull, mesh and capacity rule all use the one formula, so the physics and the picture agree — they agree on a plum-sized d12. Fixing it means deciding which `sizeMm` means and re-recording the golden cases, so it is written down in `docs/TODO.md` rather than changed unilaterally.

## Still open from your list

**Shake.** Separate branch — it is a behaviour change, not a fix: spawn on shake *start* and drive the dice live, rather than throwing when the shake ends. The sensors are not dead (checked `dumpsys` on the phone: our PID is an active client on the linear-acceleration sensor).

## Verified

`2d12 + 5` now shows two dice on a lit tray with the whole table in shot. Coverage 93.6% functions, 82.2% branches — unchanged. Emulator and Pixel 10a green.

author: dantheman1991
body:
Two reports off the running app. Both right, both about the same screen.

## "It didn't find the animal"

Your screenshot showed an empty dropdown and *"Which animals is not one of the choices"*. **Three separate faults** behind one symptom:

1. **The build you tested predated #533.** The search seam had merged minutes earlier.
2. **A searched field was still drawn as a dropdown** — and one with no list renders *empty*, with no way out of it. Worse: a field that had resolved **correctly** looked identical, because its id matched no entry either.
3. **The validation disagreed with itself across the network boundary.** The server's field carries `find`, a function. The browser's carries `searched`, a boolean — because a function can't cross into a client component. The same check runs on both and only understood the server's spelling.

So even when it found the animal, the browser rejected it — **with the answer sitting on the card in front of you.**

Searched fields now draw their shortlist, always, with the chosen one filled in. The candidates are kept even once it's decided, so it shows its working and changing its mind is one tap. Nothing found says so in words instead of offering an empty list.

## "Shouldn't it also fill out the what you saw field?"

It should, and it couldn't — and the reason is a design flaw I'd have left in.

`livestock.check` derived its status from *whether there were notes*. So "she is doing well" couldn't be written down without flagging Bluebell as needing attention. The model was explicitly told to drop it instead. That's why the field came back blank.

**A note is a note. Whether it needs somebody is a different fact.** Now it's a different field.

Driven on dev, side by side:

```
Bluebell   normal      "doing well"
Rosie      attention   "wound on her left foreleg"
```

The first of those was impossible before.

## Verified

`I checked on Bluebell and she is doing well` →

- **Which animals:** `Bluebell — Cattle · 1 head`
- **What you saw:** `doing well`
- **Anything wrong?:** `All fine`
- recorded as `normal`, note kept

No migration.

author: pixnop
body:
Seven of the nine unchecked boxes on #411, one commit each. The two fr-FR boxes are the parallel translation PR's, untouched here.

## What the player sees

**The Mod filters say when a lookup fails.** Opening the Author box with the mod database unreachable used to show an empty suggestion list, which is exactly what "nobody has published a Mod" looks like. It now says so. Versions and Tags carry the same three-line fetch and had the same silence, so all three say it.

![Author filter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StratumServer/RiftLauncher/pr-assets/contrast-pass/mods-pass/411-mods-author-filter-lookup-failed.png)

**Add Installation points at the field that is missing.** With no game version installed, saving is refused with "Fill in every field before saving." and nothing on the form moved. The Version block now wears the border and fill an invalid input gets, with the warning icon and the error colour on its headline.

![Add Installation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StratumServer/RiftLauncher/pr-assets/contrast-pass/mods-pass/411-add-installation-version-required.png)

**A deleted Installation stops being the last used one.** `lastUsedInstallation` follows the sidebar: the first remaining row, or nothing at all when the last Installation is the one going.

**A backup's name and its row agree.** The archive made during the live run below is `Solo-Play_2026-09-13_16-30-31.tar.gz`, and the row reads 13/9/2026, 16:30:31. Under the old UTC stamp that name would have said 14-30-31. The list itself does not render file names (the path lives on the row's open-folder tooltip), so the shot shows the time and the name is quoted here beside it.

![Backups list](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StratumServer/RiftLauncher/pr-assets/contrast-pass/mods-pass/411-backups-list-local-time.png)

**Background captions keep their descenders.** The y in "Valley Ruins" and the g in "Lava Springs" are whole again.

![Config backgrounds](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StratumServer/RiftLauncher/pr-assets/contrast-pass/mods-pass/411-config-background-captions.png)

**Six sentences stopped shouting.** "Welcome to RiftLauncher", "No Installations found.", "No VS Versions found.", "Install one on the VS Versions page.", "Downloading VS Version 1.19.8." and Debug info's copy line. The extraction task description went with the download one it sits next to, since a task that downloads with a period and extracts with an exclamation mark reads worse than either. A second commit in this PR went past those seven and swept the other 40 en-US strings that still ended on an exclamation mark, so every string value in en-US.json now reads as a plain sentence.

**Both install folder fields are read-only now**, next to their Browse button, which is the shape "Add an already installed VS Version" has always had.

## Why

The three ModDB filter lookups shared one hook that caught a rejection, logged it at debug and returned an empty list, so the failure never left the hook. The hook now carries a `failed` flag out with the entries.

The Version picker's empty state was written as an information block, not as a field state, so the only thing the refused save had to point at looked like a normal notice.

`DELETE_INSTALLATION` rebuilt the installations array and left every other key alone. ConfigContext has a repair effect for a dangling selection, but it only fires when there is another Installation to move to, and only after a render, so deleting the only Installation left the id on disk.

`formatTimestampForFilename` was UTC and `ManageInstallationBackups` renders `toLocaleString`, so one archive read two hours apart in the two places a player looks at it.

The caption is a direct child of the tile button, so it takes `.text-trim-children` from styles.css: `padding-block: 0.3em` with a matching negative `margin-block` that cancels it in normal flow. This one is not in normal flow. Absolutely positioned against `bottom-0`, it is placed by its margin box, so the negative bottom margin pushed 3px of it past the tile's own `overflow-hidden`. Measured on the packaged build: the caption's text ended 3px below the tile before, and 0.59px above it after.

`assertManagedPath` only admits a path under a configured root or one the native dialog just granted, so a typed folder anywhere else was refused, and the refusal was mapped to a message about permissions on one form and about the download failing on the other.

## Decisions

**The backup stamp goes local, not the list UTC.** The list is what a player reads, and it already shows local time everywhere else. Nothing reads the stamp back: pruning walks the records newest first off the epoch millis in the config, restoring opens the path recorded with the backup, and the list sorts by insertion order. So neither pruning nor sorting depends on how the name sorts. What local time costs is a file manager sorting a folder by name across the hour a daylight-saving change repeats, once a year, in a view the launcher does not own. That is cheaper than a name nobody can match to a row.

**Line 12 of the issue, read-only versus a dedicated message: read-only, on both forms.** The issue names "Add an already installed VS Version" as the consistent shape and it was already read-only plus Browse. The picker is what grants the path, so making it the only way in removes the refusal instead of rewording it. It does cost something real: a player could type a subfolder of the managed root and that worked, since a configured folder grants its whole subtree. The suggestion already puts the Installation's name there, and Browse reaches anywhere else, so I took the consistency.

One thing from that item is not fixed. Electron still prints `Error occurred in handler for 'query-url'` on stderr, because the handler has to reject for the renderer to know anything went wrong. Turning that into a returned result would touch every caller of the channel and belongs in its own change.

## Testing

Each commit carries a test that fails without its change. Reverting the source with the test in place, one item at a time:

- Filter lookup, `tests/renderer-dom/modsFilterLookupFailure.test.tsx`, "tells the player in the suggestion box when the author lookup fails": red on revert, green restored.
- Version picker, `tests/renderer-dom/installationFormVersionRequired.test.tsx`, "wears the invalid-field treatment when no game version is installed": red on revert, green restored.
- Last used Installation, `tests/renderer/configReducer.test.ts`, "moves lastUsedInstallation to the first row left when the selected one goes" and "clears lastUsedInstallation when the last installation goes": both red on revert, green restored.
- Backup stamp, `tests/domain/naming.test.ts` "reads the same clock the backups list shows" plus the two others, and the four archive-name assertions in `tests/domain/installations/backup.test.ts`: seven red on revert, green restored. Also green under `TZ=UTC` and `TZ=America/New_York`, since the expected stamps are built from local date fields rather than from a fixed instant.
- Caption, `tests/renderer-dom/configPageBackgroundCaption.test.tsx`: class pin, red on revert. jsdom has no layout engine, so the measurement is the packaged run above.
- Wording, `tests/copy-tone-locales.test.ts`: all seven keys red on revert. `splashLoader` and `modsBrowseActions` assert the new strings too.
- Folder fields, "refuses a typed folder and keeps following the name" and "takes its install folder from Browse only": both red on revert.

`git status` after each restore showed only the expected modified files.

Gate on Node 22.22.0: `npm run typecheck` 0, `npm run lint:ci` 0 errors and 14 warnings (14 on `origin/dev` too, none new), `npm run format:check` 0, `npm run test:coverage` 198 files, 2735 passed, 2 skipped, statements 94.74%, branches 91.53%, functions 95.13%, lines 96.17%.

Live check on `npm run build:unpack`, headless with a throwaway profile. The ModDB failure

body:
Follow-up to #17: attach archive snapshots to the event citations that had none, and replace the default `F` reliability on the 14 sources added in #17 with reasoned Admiralty ratings.

## 1. Archives

For each unarchived citation the Wayback availability API was checked first; Save Page Now was only called when no snapshot existed (≥20 s between requests, backoff on 429/5xx, max 3 tries per URL). 9 of 10 URLs already had a Wayback capture, so no new Save Page Now captures were created. Four captures (Sofia Globe, Armenpress, SANA, Al Jazeera) are timestamped 2026-09-13 02:15–02:41 UTC, inside the #17 session, so SPN likely completed those despite returning HTTP 500 at the time.

| Event | Source | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Air-policing agreement | BTA | Wayback, existing capture `20260807031154` |
| Air-policing agreement | The Sofia Globe | Wayback, existing capture `20260913021535` |
| Batyl Toitarys-2026 | TASS | Wayback, existing capture `20260804060901` |
| Batyl Toitarys-2026 | Caspian Post | **Failed** (see below) |
| Armenia–India | Armenpress | Wayback, existing capture `20260913023405` |
| Syria–Russia (Hmeimim/Tartus) | SANA | Wayback, existing capture `20260913023545` |
| Syria–Russia (Hmeimim/Tartus) | The Moscow Times | Wayback, existing capture `20260810020102` |
| Syria–Russia (Hmeimim/Tartus) | Arab News | Wayback, existing capture `20260811153951` |
| Syria–Russia (Hmeimim/Tartus) | Al Jazeera | Wayback, existing capture `20260913024104` |
| Burebista 26 | București FM | Wayback, existing capture `20260911233243` |

**Failed: Caspian Post** (`https://caspianpost.com/kazakhstan/kazakhstan-launches-nationwide-troop-deployment-for-military-drills`). No existing Wayback capture; Save Page Now returned HTTP 500 on all 3 tries. archive.today fallback: the submit endpoint answered HTTP 429 with a reCAPTCHA page, so it was abandoned (CAPTCHAs are not solved). The citation stays without `archives`; the event stays `unverified`.

**Content spot-checks** (raw `id_` captures, decompressed and grepped):
- BTA `20260807031154`: title "Bulgaria, Romania and Spain Sign Agreement for NATO Cross-Border Air Policing Operations", dated 06.08.2026, body mentions Romania/Spain/air policing.
- The Sofia Globe `20260913021535`: title "Romanian, Bulgarian, Spanish air forces sign air policing agreement", article body present ("…cross-border Air Policing operations by on-duty fighter jets of a third country, in this case Spain, the Defence Ministry said."). The "CAPTCHA"/"not found" strings in the page are a comment-plugin i18n blob and an ad-inserter console message, not a challenge wall.

## 2. Source ratings

Ratings follow the handbook (tr/05) and match the existing registry: official government/military = B; established international outlets/agencies = B; state-controlled agencies of parties to conflicts = C with attribution; local outlets with a track record = C; unknown = F. Each `description` now carries a one-sentence TR/EN justification (the "pending maintainer review" text is removed).

| Source | Rating | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Al Jazeera | B | International broadcaster, own correspondents, long track record; Qatari state funding → Qatar/Gulf characterizations attributed |
| Jewish Telegraphic Agency (JTA) | B | Established US news agency with own reporting; relayed Israeli official statements attributed |
| Hellenic Navy Hydrographic Service (NAVTEX) | B | Official military primary source for factual notices; area/jurisdiction characterizations attributed to the Greek side via `claims[]` |
| Bulgarian News Agency (BTA) | B | National agency, statutorily independent public body, long track record; republications of BTA copy are not independent |
| TASS | C | State-controlled; Russia is a party to armed conflicts → claims always attributed via `claims[]` |
| Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) | C | State-controlled; Syrian government is a party to conflicts → claims attributed via `claims[]` |
| Armenpress | C | State-controlled; Armenia is a party to the conflict with Azerbaijan → contested claims attributed via `claims[]` |
| Qatar News Agency (QNA) | C | State-controlled → used for Qatari official statements, claims attributed to the Qatari government |
| Cyprus Mail | C | Local English-language paper with a track record; relays Greek Cypriot official statements, attributed to that side |
| The Sofia Globe | C | Local English-language site with a track record; largely relays Bulgarian official statements and BTA |
| Arab News | C | Long-running Saudi daily, owned by a group close to the Saudi state → Saudi-related characterizations attributed |
| The Moscow Times | C | Independent, long track record, publishes from exile; relays Russian officials/media, anonymously sourced reports attributed |
| București FM | C | Bucharest regional station of public broadcaster Radio România (SRR); military items mostly relay official announcements |
| Caspian Post | **F (unchanged)** | Ownership, location and editorial policy are not disclosed on the site → no basis to judge |

**`terms`**: left as `attribution` for all 14. We only link, summarise in our own words and archive; no text or data is copied. Several sites' terms (e.g. Al Jazeera, Caspian Post "all rights reserved") forbid reproduction, which is the same situation as AP/AFP already registered as `attribution`; none is a data licence of the ACLED type that would call for `restricted`.

## 3. Status — proposed for maintainer confirmation (NOT changed)

No `assessment.status` was changed in this PR.

- **Proposed `verified`: Syria–Russia memorandum on Hmeimim/Tartus** (`evt_01m2c7m48afz99pwc2she8h7ps`). Now meets every rule in tr/05: credibility 2; EN title and summary; all 4 citations archived; ≥2 independent sources — the Syrian Foreign Ministry statement (SANA) and the Russian Foreign Ministry statement (reported by The Moscow Times) come from the two parties to the agreement through separate official channels (tr/05: parties confirming the same fact count as independent). Al Jazeera and Arab News may relay those same statements, so they are not counted as extra independent sources. The validator's mechanical check (≥2 distinct publishers) also passes. Maintainer: please confirm the independence judgement before flipping the status.

author: emadmokhtar
body:
Closes #40

## Why

Dependabot PR #32 bumps `pydantic-core` 2.46.5 → 2.49.0 and its `check` job fails on the contract snapshot test. The bump is the problem, not the test:

- `pydantic-core` is a direct dependency of the reference service, so Dependabot bumps it on its own.
- Every `pydantic` release pins one exact `pydantic-core`; the only `pydantic` that pins 2.49.0 is the pre-release **2.14.0b2**.
- Dependabot runs `uv lock --upgrade-package pydantic-core==2.49.0` with `uv` 0.12.7. Since `uv` 0.12.3 the default pre-release mode falls back to a beta when no stable version fits, so the lock silently moved `pydantic` to 2.14.0b2 (`uv` 0.11 refused the same command).
- `pydantic` 2.14 drops the `pattern` from the JSON Schema of an unconstrained `Decimal` (`MoneyOut.amount`), so the committed `openapi.json` drifts by one line.

Verified locally: same code, `pydantic` 2.13.5 passes; 2.14.0b2 fails.

## What — two independent layers

1. **`.github/dependabot.yml`**: the `uv` entry ignores `pydantic-core`. The `pydantic` bump carries it (the pin is exact), so nothing is lost.
2. **`tool.uv.prerelease = "explicit"`** in the template's `pyproject.toml` (rendered into `examples/reference-service/`) and the root's. `uv` now resolves to a pre-release only where a first-party requirement names one, so any future path to a beta — a Dependabot bump, a hand edit, a transitive pin — fails `uv lock` with the package named in the hint instead of landing in the lock. The permanently beta-versioned OpenTelemetry instrumentation packages are named: the direct ones by their existing `0.65b0` floors, the four transitive ones (`opentelemetry-instrumentation`, `-instrumentation-asgi`, `-semantic-conventions`, `-util-http`) by `constraint-dependencies` next to the setting.

Both locks change by their options/manifest sections only; no version moves. ADR 0014 records both exceptions.

Verified under Dependabot's `uv` 0.12.7 and local 0.11.12: both locks pass `uv lock --check`; Dependabot's exact `pydantic-core==2.49.0` command is now refused; `pydantic` and `opentelemetry-instrumentation-*` bumps still resolve; `just regen-check` matches; root and reference-service `just check` pass.

PR #32 should be closed, not merged — it installs a beta `pydantic`. `main` already has stable `pydantic` 2.13.5 / `pydantic-core` 2.46.5.

### Motivation

- Allow host apps to route Places search/details and forward/reverse geocoding through their own authenticated endpoints, caches, or map providers without mimicking Google's HTTP API shape.
- Make the picker extensible so consumers can provide custom implementations while retaining the existing HTTP-based behavior by default.

### Description

- Added abstractions `PlacesDataSource` and `GeocodingDataSource` and implemented `CallbackPlacesService` and `CallbackGeocodingService` to back all Places and Geocoding operations with host-provided callbacks (`PlacesSearchFetcher`, `PlaceDetailsFetcher`, `ReverseGeocodeFetcher`, `ForwardGeocodeFetcher`).
- Updated `PlaceProvider` to accept optional `placesDataSource` and `geocodingDataSource` and default to the existing `PlacesService`/`GeocodingService` when callbacks are not supplied.
- Extended the public package exports in `maps_place_picker.dart` to surface new models and services and exported the callback-backed service implementations and data-source interfaces.
- Added new `PlacePicker` constructor parameters to accept callback fetchers (`placesSearchCallback`, `placeDetailsCallback`, `reverseGeocodeCallback`, `forwardGeocodeCallback`), injects `CallbackPlacesService`/`CallbackGeocodingService` into the provider when supplied, and asserts that search/details callbacks are provided together.
- Ensured the picker session token is forwarded to distance-ranked searches by passing `sessionToken` into `searchTextRankedByDistance` usage in autocomplete.
- Bumped package version to `1.1.0` and updated `CHANGELOG.md` with the new features.
- Added unit tests in `test/callback_services_test.dart` covering delegation, error mapping to network status, session token forwarding, and forward/reverse geocoding behavior.

author: jyh
body:
Desk LQ: census D #2 and #3. One author and one PR per repo. `.githooks/{pre-push, gate_scan.py, prove_pre_push.sh}` are **byte-identical** to saltworks #43 (merged `339de92`) and salt #121.

## What was wrong
- **#2:** `pre-push` grepped its own two-shape copy of the session-trailer pattern. Three of five shapes went red in CI, after the push, and passed the hook: a lowercase key, a space before the colon, and a chat-service link that is not a session link. jas's `commit-msg` was never affected, because `commit_msg_scrub.py` already imports the gate. That is the shape this PR gives `pre-push`.
- **#3:** `pre-push` ran `check_private_paths.py --range`, a net diff. A path added then removed inside one push reached the remote with the hook green. This is the same population `--history` was ported here to catch (#150).

## The change
- **`gate_scan.py` (new, 100644):** loads `FORBIDDEN` and the matching functions from both gate scripts and types no pattern. A gate it cannot load exits 2, and the hook refuses on that.
- **`pre-push`, arm 1:** walks the pushed range one commit at a time. Messages are scanned with the trailer gate. The lines each commit introduces are scanned with both gates, using the paths gate's own `commit_introduced` and `history_key`. Arm 2 (`--range`) is unchanged.
- **`prove_pre_push.sh`:** the five shapes, each first shown to be one gate finding; path and link add-then-remove arms, each with a net-diff control; a fail-closed arm for a missing scanner; and remote restore after every red arm.
- **`README.md`:** the table names the new module and arms.
- **Unchanged:** `commit-msg`, `commit_msg_scrub.py`, `prove_commit_msg_scrub.sh` (10/10 locally). The module docstring's "the pre-push and commit-msg hooks" describes salt and saltworks; here only `pre-push` had the copy.

## Evidence
- **Red first,** measured in saltworks with the same prover: 20 failed arms against the unfixed hook, which lets shapes 3/4/5 and both add-then-remove pushes land. The fixed hook passes, here too (36 expect lines fired).
- **Parity with CI on this repo:** over all 3,610 commits, the per-commit paths arm accepts exactly the **23** findings `--history` accepts, and reports 0 new.
- **5 historical file lines shaped like a trailer:** 4 fixture lines in the scrub prover's early history and 1 in the gate's self-test, all placeholder ids and none real. They are reachable only by a root-commit push. No CI arm reads that population. Recorded, not acted on.
- This branch's own push ran the new hook: `pre-push OK [per-commit trailer+paths + private-paths --range]`.

## Declared
- One shape loosens by construction: the key mid-line with no link already passed the gate. The harm is the link, which the gate matches anywhere.
- jas is dark. Nothing here waits on its seat, and the row carries it.

author: bunsdev
body:
Implements `X Comms v2.dc.html` (Claude Design project *Comms Operations Console Redesign*) as a new role surface, `x-comms`, registered beside Comms Operations.

Closes the design handoff for bead `cave-2enyt`.

## Where it sits, and why not inside Comms Operations

The design project's file lineage runs *Comms Operations (current)* → v2…v5 → *X Comms* → *X Comms v2*, narrowing to X along the way. Comms Operations (`messenger-surface.tsx`) stays channel-agnostic — email, discord, slack, sms, teams — and keeps its `XPublishPanel`. This room is X end to end, so it can be shaped around the single decision it exists for: a person releasing one write, once, at a slot they chose.

Registration is one `registerRoleSurface` call. No shell code changed.

## Nothing here reaches X

Approving moves a local record and schedules a slot no dispatcher reads. The live publish path remains `/api/x/publish` driven by `XPublishPanel`, and this room deliberately does not call it — a behavior test asserts no `fetch` leaves the room. A banner above the header says so and points at where the real path lives, because a console this faithful would otherwise read as live.

`room-flags.ts` classifies it known-but-not-production for the same reason.

## What changed on the way in from the prototype

| The frame | What shipped | Why |
|---|---|---|
| its own `xlen()` | `weightedPostLength` + `X_POST_WEIGHTED_LIMIT` from `x-publish-composer.ts` | two rooms disagreeing about what fits in 280 is the failure a second copy produces; the link-counts-as-23 rule layers on top, since the server counts the text it is handed |
| fixed `PT = -7` | `Intl` in `America/Los_Angeles` | a fixed offset moves every "6:10 PM PT" by an hour for four months of the year, and the slot is a claim about follower activity |
| frozen `NOW` | fixtures seeded from a `now` the room passes in | the room reads live whenever it opens; tests pin the clock and get identical strings |
| every value inline | type/space/radius scale in a component-imported sheet | never the `globals.css` facade — the root bundle has no headroom |
| local `--cream` | `--x-cream`, mixed from `--text-primary` and `--color-warning` | the warm serif cast survives all 42 theme/mode combinations instead of being one palette's constant |
| `CovenCave.Segmented` | a local `Segmented` radiogroup | there is no Segmented primitive here, and `Tabs` announces panels these controls do not own |
| its own agenda dock | `SurfaceRoom`'s drawer | not a second implementation of what the chrome already does |

### The responsive rail is the room's own

Worth calling out because I got it wrong first. The three columns are the room's own elements, not the chrome's named rails — the queue is drag-resizable and the dispatch rail is a fixed 376px, neither of which the shared template expresses. So `.role-surface-rail--right`'s container-query collapse never applied to them, and `[data-rail="collapsed"]` was styled but never set: below 1280 the third column simply wrapped. The room now measures the viewport at the frame's own 1280 break, renders the 44px tab strip and opens the rail over the canvas, anchored to the columns box rather than the viewport (it was `position: fixed; top: 40px`, which assumed exactly one banner — the room can carry two). Commit `86eb7fe7e`, with a test that fails against the one before it.

## Reaching all thirteen frames

Eleven follow from data. Three did not, and now do: `post-failed` and `slot-passed` are seeded drafts, and the two account-level states (`x-disconnected`, `rate-limited`) hang off a switch in the demo banner — the one place already saying the data is not real. Both are states where approving still works and nothing moves, so each says what holds and what drops rather than only that something is wrong.

## Design-system gates

- `eslint` (no-raw-px-text / no-static-inline-style / no-render-hex-color): clean. The seven remaining `style={{}}` sites are per-record state colour, the operator's dragged queue width, and the 80%-budget border.
- `check:tokens:defined`, `codemod:design:check`, `tokenize-css.mjs`: clean, codemod is a no-op over the sheet.
- Drift ratchets: spacing **banks 1617 → 1616** (main alone measures 1607, so the old figure carried 10 of stale headroom); radius +3 and inline styles +7, both justified in the baseline notes against the existing short-solid-mark and runtime-derived precedents.

## Tests

- `src/lib/x-comms-model.test.ts` — 32 cases over the rules: what blocks approval and in what order, the room rules, DST-correct slots, media affordances, the queued API cost.
- `src/components/role-surfaces/x-comms-surface.behavior.test.tsx` — 18 cases over the wiring: approve, undo, the inline confirm before a discard, thread conversion, preview honesty, keyboard resize, the three account states, and the load-bearing one — **Trends writes to `notes` and never to a post body**.

Both registered in `run-tests.mjs`; the model file needs the alias loader because it imports `x-publish-composer` as a runtime value, which is the point.

## Review round (c73db6410)

The automated review returned 11 findings and all 11 were real — including two that contradicted the description above as originally written. Each thread has a reply naming the commit. The substantive ones:

- **The room disagreed with itself about a disconnected account.** The banner promised approvals keep working while posts hold locally; the gate disabled both approve paths, so nothing could ever be queued *waiting* for the reconnect. `approvalBlocker` no longer takes a connection at all — `connectionAdvice()` says what each state means without enforcing it. The test that pinned the contradiction now pins the promise.
- **`1 link max` was counted across the whole thread**, so a four-post thread with one link each — every post satisfying the rule its chip states — was reported as failing.
- **Destination URLs were prefix-matched**, letting `…/status/123/trailing-junk` through the room and into a write the server rejects. Both validators now delegate to `parseXPostUrl`, the publish path's own parser.
- **`merge ↓` silently destroyed content** — `slice(0, 4)` on media, `a.poll ?? b.poll` on polls — and could assemble combinations the add buttons refuse individually. It now refuses by name and loses nothing.
- **The post editor and preview restated `280`/`10_000`**, which is precisely the drift the shared-counting design exists to prevent. Both derive from `limitFor(draft)`.
- **Inline article image ids came from `inline.length + 1`** (delete one, the next collides), and an image whose `[img:n]` marker was cut from the body warned in amber while approval succeeded anyway.
- **The slot dialog declared `aria-modal` without honouring it** — Tab escaped, focus never returned. Now uses `useFocusTrap`, the repository's stated contract.

## Reviewing

The room is gated on `xPublishEnabled` and a messenger-role familiar, and is dev-only. Worth a look: the approval card's six states, the constraint footer's rule chips (each names its source and whether it blocks), and the slot picker's heatmap.

author: suestecreative
body:
Requested by Pedro on 13/09: choose newsletter recipients individually, from a searchable list of all clients (name + customer number) with a selector each, and add addresses that have no account yet.

**Clientes (picked by hand)**
- New block under the filter chips: search input (name, `RIO-` code or email, accent-insensitive), dropdown with a checkbox per client, picked ones shown as removable chips + "Limpar".
- A pick is the key `user:<id>`, one group like the others: alone it is exactly those clients; with chips it is the picked clients that also match them.
- SQL: `u.id IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(?))`, one bound parameter however many are picked. An id failing `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` still opens the group, so it selects nobody, never everybody. Picks cannot reach outside `CUSTOMERS` (no staff, no invited seats).

**Emails manuais**
- Textarea, one per line or comma-separated; shows how many are valid and which were ignored.
- Each address is the key `email:<address>`. They are **added** to what the filters resolve, deduped by address. With nothing else chosen they go **only** to those addresses; if every typed address is invalid, the result is empty, not the whole list.
- Chosen without a consent confirmation, by Pedro's decision.

**Why keys and not a separate list**
The simulation signature, the `confirm_count` check on send and `newsletter_campaigns.filters_json` already cover `filters`, so both features ride on them with no new plumbing. `GET /api/admin/newsletter` returns `clients` for the picker, from the same base query the empty filter uses.

**Known limitation**
A typed address has no contact name, so a template that greets with `Olá{{GREETING_NAME}},` reads "Olá ," for those recipients. Use a template without the greeting for them.

**Checks:** `newsletter-audience.test.ts` + `newsletter-template.test.ts` 29/29 (8 new: exact pick, AND with chips, no reach past the customer base, malformed pick selects nobody, 300 picks bind as one parameter, typed-only, typed + filters deduped, all-invalid stays empty). `tsc --noEmit` on backoffice clean.

## What changed

  `issue_comment`, and `push`-to-`main` triggers, the `mitchellh/vouch/action/check-user@v1`
  call, and the label sync).
- Delete `.github/VOUCHED.td`, the trust list that was the workflow's only input.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: the "Read This First" paragraph no longer promises a `vouch:*` status or
  a `vouch:unvouched` label and no longer links the trust list. The adjacent sentence about
  automatic `size:*` labeling stays, since PR Size still runs.

Deliberately untouched: `.github/workflows/pr-size.yml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
(independent validation), `.github/pull_request_template.md`, and the `vouch:trusted` example
in `apps/web/src/components/pullRequest/pullRequestList.logic[.test].ts` — that one tests
generic colon-namespaced label search, not this workflow.

## Verification

```
$ test ! -e .github/workflows/pr-vouch.yml && test ! -e .github/VOUCHED.td   # both gone
$ rg -n "VOUCHED\.td|recheck-vouch|mitchellh/vouch|vouch:(trusted|unvouched|denounced)" CONTRIBUTING.md .github
(rg exit 1 — no matches)
$ python3 /tmp/vouch_verify_workflows.py
parsed 14 workflow files
failures: []                 # every remaining workflow still parses
pr-vouch present: False
$ git diff --exit-code HEAD~1 -- .github/workflows/pr-size.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml
(unchanged)
$ git diff --check           # clean
```

The change touches no application code, so the test suite, typecheck, and lint have no scope
here; the worktree has no `node_modules` (the t3.json worktree-setup script has not run), so
those checks were not attempted rather than claimed.

No regression test is added: the approved plan for this card (kanban `t_1e886f2a`) determined
that workflow/data deletion plus a docs edit warrants none, and the "check is not invoked"
property is structural — GitHub cannot schedule a workflow file that does not exist — which
the commands above assert directly. A repo-layout test asserting a file's absence would be
new machinery that duplicates those greps.

## Compatibility notes

- The check will still fire on **this** PR: `pull_request_target`, `issue_comment`, and
  `push` workflows are read from the base branch, so `main`'s copy runs until this merges.
- Historical `vouch:*` labels on existing PRs are not removed by this change — that is
  external cleanup via the API, not a code change.
- `.macroscope/check-run-agents/*.md` list `vouch:trusted` under `labels:`. Once this lands
  those checks will no longer see that label on new PRs. Left unchanged on purpose: it is a
  separate review-bot configuration and changing it is a different concern.

## Issue

There is no GitHub issue for this in `wilsonwan/whaleshark` — `gh api
search/issues?q=repo:wilsonwan/whaleshark+vouch` returns `total_count: 0` across all states.
The work originates from the Kanban card `t_812f1832` (root `t_9855b41a`), so nothing closes
on merge.

body:
## Summary

Full admin → storefront builder config integration for the Eukolakis SBS builder. Every admin KIT Builder control is now truthful and fully connected to real storefront output. The flow is: **Admin setting → persisted product builderConfig → Admin reload → storefront SBS render** as a reliable 1:1 pipeline.

### What changed

**Asset upload/remove/preview (Sections A & B)**
- All 4 builder image fields (logo, mobile logo, banner, mobile banner) have Upload/Remove buttons with inline preview thumbnails
- Server-side `builderAssetUpload` multer (5MB, png/jpg/webp) with old-file cleanup on replace
- `POST /admin/builder/asset-upload` and `POST /admin/builder/asset-remove` endpoints with field allowlist validation
- `imageVersion` counter incremented on every upload/remove for cache-busting
- Reuses existing admin media upload infrastructure — no duplicate upload routes

**Cache-busting (storefront + preview)**
- Banner and logo `src` appended with `?v=bcVersion` using `bc.imageVersion`
- Preview panel also applies cache-busting to match storefront behavior

**Benefits reorder (Section C)**
- Move up/down buttons on each benefit item in the admin editor

**Trust items enable/disable + reorder (Section D)**
- Enable/disable toggle per trust item (parity with benefits)
- Move up/down buttons for reordering

**Live preview panel (Section E)**
- Mini SBS branding area preview in admin that updates in real-time
- Shows: banner background, logo (with position/size), slogan, secondary slogan, title, subtitle, helper text, benefits strip, trust row, video CTA
- Logo positioned in dedicated wrapper for clean left/center/right placement
- Images use `onerror` handlers to hide gracefully on load failure
- Logo uses `object-fit:contain` with max-dimension constraints — never stretched
- Preview defaults open for immediate visual feedback

**Unsaved indicator (dirty-state fix)**
- "Unsaved builder changes" badge shown when builderConfig differs from last loaded/saved state
- Uses JSON snapshot comparison — no separate model/state
- **Fixed**: `markBuilderClean()` removed from form submit handler — dirty state now persists until server confirms persistence via page reload
- Cleared on panel open (`syncBuilderConfigPanel`) which runs after page reloads with persisted data
- `checkBuilderDirty()` called from `refreshLivePreview()` on every change
- Failed saves (network error, validation error) correctly preserve the dirty indicator

**Option group & choice display**
- Groups without customer-facing label show "raw ID" warning badge
- Bilingual labels show both EL and EN when different
- Choice cards show price source (linked product vs custom delta) and image source (custom/variant/product/none) indicators

**Visual fixes (prior commits)**
- Builder logo CSS: scoped to `.sbs-banner-bg` only, logo constrained
- Raw ID filtering: `looksLikeRawId()` guard in storefront step labels
- Completion step: full recap with per-step status rows

### Audit matrix

Para alguien que entra desde Instagram con datos moviles, eso es el sitio entero. - Script npm run imagenes (sharp): genera AVIF y WebP en varios anchos y deja en src/lib/fotosLanding.js el manifiesto de lo que existe, para que el srcset nunca apunte a un archivo que no se genero. - Las fotos pasan a con srcset/sizes. 4061 KB -> ~138 KB en celular. - El hero deja de ser background-image de CSS y pasa a con fetchpriority=high mas preload en index.html: el navegador ya no espera al bundle para descubrirlo. - robots.txt, sitemap.xml, canonical y titulo/descripcion por ruta (src/lib/seo.js), mas JSON-LD LocalBusiness con las seis comunas donde opera Howria. El panel y las pantallas de reserva quedan noindex. - Dos paginas nuevas, /paseos y /adiestramiento, con estructura problema-solucion-resultado y JSON-LD de tipo Service. - Header, footer y boton de WhatsApp se extraen a src/lib/publico.jsx, ahora que hay tres paginas publicas que los comparten. - Accesibilidad: contraste del copyright a AA (3.96:1 -> 4.82:1), anillo de foco visible y alto tocable en el menu de celular. author: felixtechgiti
body:
**The patch worked — Spotify DJ plays.** Measured on hardware 2026-09-13 14:27:53:

```
[librespot] context resolved empty; following lexicon_context_url
[librespot] lexicon context response (64610 bytes): {"uri":"spotify:playlist:37i9dQZF1EYkqdzj48dyYq", …
[librespot] Loading <SOMMERNACHT 2> with Spotify URI <spotify:track:2pjvFlsY66hTK3seefBQHJ>
[music]     plane owner: spotify
```

The lexicon session provider answers with **exactly the same `Context` JSON the ordinary path returns** — 64610 bytes, 60 tracks — so the guess in #168 was right. The AEC far-end reference has carried real audio continuously since (rms 1000–1800, peaks to 14731), and not one `has no tracks` since.

## What this changes

The question the raw dump existed to answer is answered, and the line becomes the problem: **64 KB per DJ selection, on one line**, into a log already at 1.2 MB.

The firmware's own log filter does not catch it, and correctly so: it folds *indented continuation lines* of a Rust `{:#?}` dump, and this is a single very long line.

So INFO now carries only the **shape** — bytes, pages, tracks on the first page. The full body appears only when parsing fails, which is the one case where the bytes are the diagnosis.

**The general form, because it will recur: output that is right for one measurement is almost always wrong as a standing state.** The comment at the site now says what the dump was for and why it is gone — otherwise the next person adds it back to answer the same question again.

## Verification

**In CI verifiziert** — `cargo check --no-default-features --features rustls-tls-webpki-roots,with-libmdns` across the workspace, i.e. the device build's exact feature set: clean. The patch applies cleanly to `v0.8.0`.

**Am echten Gerät verifiziert** is the finding that prompts it: the 64737-byte body in the log, and DJ playing.

## Not in this PR

The DJ's *voice* is still missing, and that is a separate thing entirely: the narration is not audio in the context but SSML plus TTS parameters (`tts_provider: SONANTIC_LARGE`, `voice: VOICE81`) per track, with no media reference anywhere in its 14 fields. #160 carries the detail.

author: ivanskainet
body: Closes #350. ## Что нашлось Issue я завёл по находке фаззера как «500 на непарные суррогаты». **Диагноз был неверен**: суррогаты уже отвергаются с 400 — защита стоит с #286. Воспроизвести исходный 500 на чистом состоянии не удалось; вероятно, он зависел от состояния, накопленного предыдущими запросами фаззера. Зато нашлось другое, серьёзнее. Читатель и писатель расходились во мнении об одной и той же строке. `mission_dir()` (`arena/resources/mission_catalog.py:30`) с самого начала отвергал `..`, разделители пути и ведущую точку. `create_mission_from_draft()` не проверял ничего. Через публичную ручку `/v1/mission/create`: ```python rt.mission_create_sync({"goal":"pwn","title":"pwn","mission_id":"../../secrets","overwrite":True}) # -> {'ok': True, ...} # victim/mission.json: {"id": "../../secrets", ...} <- перезаписан ``` `mission.json` и `PLAN.md` пишутся в любой каталог, докуда дотягивается относительный путь, `overwrite=True` затирает то, что там было, ответ — `ok: True`. Замер по одним и тем же именам, до фикса: | имя | писатель | читатель | |---|---|---| | `../escaped` | accept | refuse | | `a/b` | accept | refuse | | `a\b` | accept | refuse | | `.hidden` | accept | refuse | | `..` / `.` | accept | refuse | | `a..b` | accept | refuse | | `sub/../ok` | accept | refuse | | `ok-name` | accept | accept | Писатель принимал **всё**, что читатель отвергал. После фикса расхождений 0. ## Второй дефект из той же щели Он срабатывает без всякого злого умысла. `_slug()` сохранял серии точек, поэтому обычный заголовок порождал id, который система потом не принимала: ``` title "Ship v2..final" -> id 20260913T142604Z-ship-v2..final-d918d6 -> created ok: True -> mission_dir(): ValueError: invalid mission name ``` Миссия на диске есть, прочитать её нельзя и в `list_missions()` её нет. Запись «успешна», объекта для API не существует. Достаточно двух точек в названии. ## Фикс 1. Общая функция `not_a_single_directory_name()` рядом с существующей `unusable_directory_name()`. Разделены намеренно: вторая отвечает, **может ли файловая система удержать** имя (NUL, суррогаты, длина, устройства Windows — это #286), первая — **адресует ли имя один каталог** под корнем. Разные вопросы, разные причины отказа. 2. Писатель и читатель зовут её же. Инлайновое условие из `mission_dir` убрано — именно наличие двух независимых мнений и было корнем. 3. Проверка контейнмента после сборки пути (`resolve()` + `is_relative_to`). Строковой проверки мало: симлинк внутри `missions_dir` уводит наружу, не содержа ни `..`, ни разделителя. Проверено тестом, который без этой части падает. 4. `_slug()` схлопывает серии точек и срезает ведущую — писатель больше не изобретает имя, которое сам же отверг бы от вызывающего. `..` отвергается в любом месте имени, а не только как отдельный компонент. Это строже, чем требует контейнмент (`a..b` никуда не ведёт), но ровно так вёл себя читатель, и миссия, которую писатель создал, а читатель не открывает, — это и есть второй баг выше. ## Проверки Полный прогон: `1 failed, 11174 passed, 53 skipped` — единственное падение pre-existing `test_openapi_error_contract_89.py::test_the_served_document_is_valid_openapi`, красное и на master. Мутационное покрытие, 42 теста в `tests/test_mission_id_containment_350.py`: | мутация | падает | |---|---| | M1: писатель не проверяет имя | 12 | | M2: убрать проверку контейнмента | 1 | | M3: вернуть прежний `_slug` | 4 | | M4: валидатор пропускает `..` | 2 | Ключевой тест — `test_the_writer_and_the_reader_agree`: он параметризован обоими наборами имён и требует, чтобы ответы двух сторон совпадали. Именно такой проверки не было, поэтому расхождение и жило незамеченным; он же не даст им разойтись снова. Отдельно проверено, что строгость не задела рабочие имена: `scenario-`-префиксы, генерируемый формат `--` и одиночная точка в имени принимаются по-прежнему. Четыре ратчета и `lint-imports` зелёные, ruff чист. author: mandubian
body:
## What

Completes the anti-confabulation design from the session-76a8d5c6 postmortem (companion to #1332/#1333). The gateway now re-presents a bounded **session-facts block** every turn — in the trim-proof trailing gateway state notice — containing:

```
[session facts — gateway-observed; authoritative over memory; do not reply to this block directly]
Task: <first 200 chars of the spawn/initial message>
Artifact refs: ar.abc123, ar.def456
Workflow tasks (most recent first): task-1 coder.default succeeded; task-2 packager.default failed
```

## Why this closes the loop

#1332's guards are boundary checks: a fabricated `artifact_ref` is rejected, and the true refs ride along at each wake. But the postmortem identified a residual gap: **pull-based truth requires knowing what to pull**. After `trim_history` evicts the early turns, the model doesn't know there was ever a task summary to fetch — the goal itself lives only in the oldest prose, which is exactly what trimming eats first. This tail makes the goal, the artifact identity, and the child-task picture standing facts that survive any amount of history trimming, because the block is rebuilt fresh each turn at the newest position (`append_volatile_state_message` — the same cache-stable mechanism the Ri-0.1 state attestation and degradation notice use).

## Design properties

- **Gateway-observed only.** Every line is a store read (artifact-ref store, workflow store) — never parsed from the model's own prose, so it cannot drift from what actually exists. Same discipline as the attestation it sits beside.
- **Bounded.** Hard cap 900 chars with whole-line truncation (`SESSION_FACTS_MAX_CHARS`); task preview capped at 200 chars; at most 8 most-recent tasks. The layer stays ratchet-shaped even though its content is dynamic.
- **Free when empty.** A fresh session with no store pays only the task line; no task and no store pays nothing (`None`).
- **Two render sites.** The pre-loop compose (`execute_loop`) and the per-turn compose — both already rebuild volatile tails each turn and drop stale ones.

## Tests

Four unit tests in `context.rs` (in-crate `AgentExecutor` construction with a NoopDriver): empty-session `None`; task preview + 900-char block cap; session-scoped ref listing with the global universe excluded; workflow-task listing via `ensure_workflow_for_root_session` + `save_task_run`.

## Verification

Full gateway suite: 4875/4877 — the only failures are the two known pre-existing ones on `main` (allow_set, loopback).

## Follow-up

Update `docs/internals/prompt/context-map.md` (PR #1334) to list the session-facts tail as a measured volatile layer once this merges.

author: wangbo981016
body:
## Summary

- Replace admission's full cache scan and heap construction with on-demand epoch traversal, stopping once enough capacity is found.
- Remove full-cache deduplication-set insertion and repeated candidate metadata hash lookups; deduplicate only request-reclaimable blocks and carry cached metadata directly.
- Stop Host free-slot scans once batch demand is met. Host victim selection still scans the target group, but uses `partial_sort` without repeated metadata lookups. Preserve eviction policy and prefix protection.

## Performance

Historical comparison: baseline `c3576050` versus branch `0246dc41c`, before merging the newer main. 100k cached entries, one group, packing 1, distinct epochs, one eviction per cycle. All rows measure the same probe/admit/check/free/replenish cycle.

| Variant | µs/cycle |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline | 7,753.51 |
| Baseline: no deduplication | 2,903.26 |
| Baseline: dense metadata instead of hash lookup | 5,150.32 |
| Baseline: no heap construction | 7,621.50 |
| Baseline: no parent scan | 7,462.74 |
| Baseline: no deduplication + dense metadata | 1,068.52 |
| Above + no heap construction | 1,053.65 |
| Above + no parent scan | 615.37 |
| Branch before merge | **1.51** |

Deduplication and repeated metadata lookup dominate the baseline's overhead. Lazy traversal also avoids full candidate collection through early stopping. Ablations are fixture-specific and their deltas are not additive; larger same-epoch batches or pinned prefixes still require more traversal.

## Test Plan

- 479/479 C++ tests passed after merging main; cache scan benchmark completed.
- Historical benchmark variants verified identical victim sequences and checksums.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed.

author: petarzarkov
body:
Also moves `@dunx/*` to **3.9.0**, which is where the email area landed.

Net **-514** (**-70** excluding the lockfile). 356 unit + 33 e2e green.

## We do need email, and dunx now ships what we wrote

Four templates go out: welcome, password reset, account suspended, invite - the reset one is better-auth's `sendResetPassword` enqueueing onto the notifications queue. That stays. What goes is the transport around it, because this app had independently written most of `@dunx/infra/email`:

| was here | is dunx's |
|---|---|
| `EmailService` over Resend, 83 lines | `EmailService` + `EmailTransport` seam |
| two renders, `plainText: true` for the text body | `ReactEmailRenderer`, same trick |
| guard because `new Resend(undefined)` throws | absent transport -> `LogTransport` |
| checked Resend's `{ data, error }` by hand | `@dunx/infra/email/resend` -> `EmailSendError` |
| `email dev --dir ... --port 3035` | `dunx-email preview`, same default port |

## The two invariants this app cared about

Both hold, and both are the framework's own reasoning rather than something I had to configure back in:

- **HTML and plain text on every message.** `ReactEmailRenderer` renders the tree twice, once with `plainText`, for the same spam-filter reason the old service gave. Verified on a real template through `MemoryTransport`: 529 characters of text alternative beside the HTML.
- **No retry inside one send.** The old comment was explicit that the queue owns the attempt and a second loop would multiply against `QUEUE_MAX_RETRIES`. dunx defaults `retry: { maxRetries: 0 }` and says why: *"the cost of guessing wrong is a second email in a real person's inbox."* Nothing to set.

## Dependencies

`@react-email/render` and `resend` **stay** as `dependencies`. They are *optional* peers of `@dunx/infra`, so nothing installs them for us - the same trap `swagger-ui-dist` is, and the image installs `--production`. What does leave devDependencies is `react-email` and `@react-email/ui`, replaced by `dunx-email preview`.

## Tests

`email.test.ts` goes 164 -> 66. It keeps what belongs to this app - that a reset link and an invite code survive into the plain-text alternative - and drops the three that tested Resend's wire behaviour, which `@dunx/infra` tests now.

One assertion I did not carry over: "sends nothing, and does not throw, with no api key". It tested a branch that is now three lines choosing a transport, and the failure mode it guarded against is a loud boot error rather than a silent send, since `ResendTransport` refuses an empty key in its constructor.

## Overview
Promotes the continuous deployment (CD) workflow to `main`, establishing an automated, zero-downtime deployment pipeline to Azure Container Apps (`aca-mechanicshop-api`).

## Key Changes
- **Workflow Restructuring:** Renamed `ci.yml` to `ci-cd.yml` and established a three-tier pipeline architecture (`build-and-test` -> `push-image-to-ghcr` -> `deploy-to-azure`).
- **Continuous Deployment Job:** Added the `deploy-to-azure` job using official `azure/login@v2` and `azure/container-apps-deploy-action@v2`.

author: thanasiskostaras
body:
## Summary
- Adds `CC_LANGFUSE_REDACT_SECRETS` (default `true`): scans every string span attribute at export and redacts PEM private keys, labeled credential assignments (`api_key`/`token`/`password`/`secret`/`credential`/`auth` = value, quoted or bare), and unlabeled high-entropy tokens — replacing each with a `[REDACTED:...]` marker.
- Leaves the SDK's own structural attributes untouched: `langfuse.observation.{type,level,model.name,model.parameters,usage_details,cost_details}`, `langfuse.{environment,release,version}`, and `langfuse.internal.*`.
- Masks each attribute independently: a value that raises during redaction becomes `[REDACTED:masker-error]` rather than propagating, since an unhandled exception in `mask_otel_spans` drops the *entire* export batch per the SDK's contract — this keeps a single bad value from taking the whole batch down.
- If `CC_LANGFUSE_REDACT_SECRETS` is on but the installed SDK predates `mask_otel_spans` (<4.9), `create_langfuse_client` refuses to create a client at all rather than send unmasked content (fail closed). Bumped the script's pinned floor to `langfuse>=4.14.3,<5` for langfuse-python#1803 (a duplicate span id used to silently drop the whole batch).
- Motivation: with `CC_LANGFUSE_MAX_CHARS=0`, only *string* tool inputs get truncated — dict-shaped ones (e.g. a Bash `command`, a Write/Edit `content`) ship unredacted today, and tool-error text built by `build_status_message` is never truncated at all. This masker is meant to be the actual gate for turning content capture on, rather than relying on `MAX_CHARS` alone.

## Test plan
- [x] `uv run --group dev pytest -q` — 293 passed (271 existing + 22 new in `tests/unit/test_masker.py`): PEM (full + truncated with no END line), labeled credential (quoted/bare), the `max_tokens`/`input_tokens` false-positive guard, entropy fallback + a low-entropy negative case, the structural skip list, per-attribute error containment, and fail-closed client creation.
- [x] Verified against the real SDK (4.15.2), not just the test stubs: constructed a live `Langfuse(mask_otel_spans=...)` client, and round-tripped real `MaskOtelSpansParams`/`OtelSpanData` objects through the masker.
- [x] Measured ~1.7ms per call on a 24KB attribute value.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

New .NET 8 Web API that records post office data into the existing `pec.PostOfficeData` MSSQL table, structured as Model / Service / Controller with EF Core, protected by per-request HMAC signatures since it will be exposed to external data providers.

**API**
- `Models/PostOfficeData.cs` — entity mapped to `[pec].[PostOfficeData]`, columns typed to match the DDL (`varchar(n)`, `decimal(18,3)`, `decimal(18,2)`, `datetime2`).
- `Models/Dtos/PostOfficeDataRequest.cs` — client payload exposes only the `PO_*` fields; `PO_TrackingNo` and `PO_MobileNo` required (NOT NULL in the table), other columns (NID, receiver, status, Mcs*) stay owned by back-office processes.
- `Services/PostOfficeDataService.cs` — DTO↔entity mapping, insert (single + bulk), lookups by id and tracking number; `PO_CreatedAt ??= DateTime.UtcNow`.
- `Controllers/PostOfficeDataController.cs` — `POST /api/post-office-data`, `POST /api/post-office-data/bulk`, `GET /{id}`, `GET /by-tracking-no/{trackingNo}`.
- `Data/PostOfficeDbContext.cs` — declares the 9 existing indexes (including filtered ones) so the model matches the database; no migrations are applied, the table must already exist.

JSON naming policy is disabled (`PropertyNamingPolicy = null`) so payload keys stay `PO_TrackingNo` rather than camelCased `pO_TrackingNo`. The connection string lives in user secrets / env vars, not `appsettings.json`, and startup throws a descriptive error when it is missing.

**Authentication** (`Authentication/`, fallback authorization policy — every endpoint requires it)

```
stringToSign = app_number \n user_token \n call_datetime \n METHOD \n path+query \n base64(sha256(body))
X-Signature  = base64(hmacsha256(app_secret, stringToSign))
```

Headers `X-App-Number`, `X-User-Token`, `X-Call-DateTime`, `X-Signature`; `app_secret` never leaves the caller. Callers are registered in the `ApiClients` config section (`AppNumber`, `AppSecret`, optional `UserTokens` allow-list). Requests are rejected with 401 for an unknown app/token, a `call_datetime` outside `AllowedClockSkew` (default 5 min), a signature mismatch (which also covers body tampering, as the body hash is signed), or a replayed signature (`IMemoryCache`, retained for 2× the skew window).

Verified against a SQL Server 2022 container: unsigned, tampered-signature, stale-timestamp and replayed requests all return 401; a correctly signed POST returns 201 and the row reads back via the tracking-number lookup.

`postman/PostOfficeApi.postman_collection.json` signs each request in a pre-request script; `db/schema.sql` holds the provided DDL for reference.

author: rasuvaeff
body:
Fixes #34

## What

`ClickHouseSqlFilterVisitor::buildComposite()` and `ClickHouseQueryBuilder::buildWhere()` merged sibling parameters with `array_merge()`. Two `ClickHouseRawFilter`s reusing one name — under one `AndX`/`OrX`, or one in the mandatory filter and one in the user filter — kept both `{name:Type}` tokens in the SQL while only the last value was bound; a raw name equal to a builder key (`p0`, …) or to the keyset boundary (`ck0`, …) lost the builder's value the same way.

Both merge points now go through a new `@internal` `PlaceholderRemap::merge()`: a name already collected becomes `name_0`, `name_1`, … and its token in the fragment is rewritten in one pass over whole tokens (whitespace inside `{ v : UInt64 }` is kept — the server accepts that form), whichever sibling comes second. A nested composite returns a self-consistent fragment, so its parent re-namespaces it as a unit; no state is shared between frames besides the existing `$index`. The `ClickHouseFilterVisitor` interface is untouched; a custom visitor keeps merging its own composites and gets the builder-level isolation only. `ck0`/`ck1` are no longer reserved names.

## Tests

- `PlaceholderRemapTest` (new): verbatim without collision, prefixed sibling, parametric types, whitespace in the token, repeated token, two-stage collision, next free suffix, foreign tokens untouched.
- `ClickHouseSqlFilterVisitorTest`: raw-vs-raw, raw-vs-`p0` in both orders, nested `OrX`, `Not` passthrough; property `everyPlaceholderIsBoundExactlyOnceAndNoValueIsLost` over random `AndX`/`OrX`/`Not` trees with raw leaves that deliberately share names — tokens == keys and the multiset of leaf values equals the multiset of bound values, with `Classify::cover` gates on the collision paths.
- `ClickHouseQueryBuilderTest`: mandatory raw vs user raw; colliding params from a custom visitor renamed at the builder.
- `ClickHouseKeysetReaderTest`: base filter using `ck0`.
- `ClickHouseIntegrationTest`: renamed tokens bind on a live ClickHouse 24.8.

All new tests are red on the previous `src`.

## Gates

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `composer build` (Unit 325) | PASS |
| Integration on ClickHouse 24.8 | 19 passed |
| `composer rector` | PASS |
| `make bc-check` (from `v1.8.0`) | No backwards-incompatible changes |
| `make mutation` | MSI 96% (minMsi 95); no escaped mutant in the changed code |
| `bin/package-audit` | 0 errors |

body:
**Blocked on an upload: `tauso_score_v1_clean_exp_med.ubj` has to be added to Zenodo record 22688592 before this can merge.** `setup-model` fetches by filename, so CI will fail until it is there. Draft for that reason.

1. `MODEL_FILES["v1"]` points at `tauso_score_v1_clean_exp_med.ubj` (md5 `8dcff7f537013d51080a2d8479567a25`) instead of the JSON. `load_model` needs no change; `Booster.load_model` picks the format from the file.

Loading 9,829 trees from 265 MB of JSON builds a document tree of roughly ten times the text, which XGBoost frees and glibc then keeps. The booster itself is 358 MB, about 78 bytes per node over 4,591,081 nodes.

`design_asos` over 40 candidates:

| | wall | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| JSON | 12.8 s | 4.52 GB |
| UBJSON | 8.5 s | 1.90 GB |

The rankings are byte-for-byte identical, and the conversion is lossless:
