author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord and OpenAI voice still load the older Opus WebAssembly package, which can exhaust its stack when encoding supported 40 ms and 60 ms stereo frames and corrupt subsequent codec operations.

## User Impact

Both voice integrations receive the repaired codec and the encoder validation and cleanup fixes introduced since 0.2.0. Both production encoders continue to emit 20 ms frames. Their existing audio formats and configuration remain unchanged. The library requires Node 22 or newer, which is below OpenClaw's current supported minimum.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pin both plugin-owned dependencies to [libopus-wasm 0.4.0](https://github.com/openclaw/libopus-wasm/releases/tag/v0.4.0), including [the upstream stack fix](https://github.com/openclaw/libopus-wasm/pull/18). This changes no stored data, database schema, migration, retention, or OpenClaw runtime configuration. The pnpm workspace setting controls package installation only. Keep a temporary dependency-cooldown exception for this exact reviewed version so fresh installs can resolve it; remove the exception after September 21.

## Evidence

The released npm tarball matches the tested publication artifact byte for byte; upstream Node 22/24/26 CI, 30 tests, and a 720-packet codec matrix passed. [npm version](https://www.npmjs.com/package/libopus-wasm/v/0.4.0) · [registry tarball](https://registry.npmjs.org/libopus-wasm/-/libopus-wasm-0.4.0.tgz)

Upgrade compatibility: the existing task workspace had both plugins installed against 0.2.0. Updating its lockfile and running a frozen pnpm install succeeded; both consumers now resolve to the same published 0.4.0 module. Through each consumer resolution, 40/60 ms stereo encoding followed by 20 ms frames succeeds without corrupting later operations. All 83 focused cases pass: 55 Discord codec, resampling, playback, and receive-recovery cases, plus 28 OpenAI media-peer cases covering actual Opus RTP round trips, reordering, packet loss, timing, cancellation, and Bun construction.

The Discord npm lock mirror, pinned-dependency check, extension production types, formatting, and diff checks pass. Independent review is clean through P2. Required [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34763151816) for `243f135f804510a9fcaef40cccde822312ca35d1`; the canonical watcher reports GREEN with no pending checks. These are codec/transport boundary tests with synthetic audio, not a live Discord-room or OpenAI voice-service session.

author: bwbensonjr
body:
## Why

Every existing command stops at aggregates. None can show you a **filing** — the CPF 102 a candidate actually submitted, with its reporting period, balances and schedules.

That gap is widest where the existing commands go blind: a **special election**. The depository year-to-date feeds behind `ocpf race` carry one cumulative figure per filer per calendar year and are never segmented by election, so a February-to-March special window does not exist in them. The filing covering that window does, and until now the only way to read it was the OCPF web UI.

## What changed

- **`ocpf reports <filer>`** — the index of what a committee has filed, with `--type`, `--year`, `--since`/`--until`, `--limit`, `--include-superseded`, `--json`.
- **`ocpf report <report-id>`** — one filing in full: header, schedule totals, amendment lineage, canonical link, and `--schedule` (repeatable) for line items.
- **`src/ocpf_cli/reports.py`** — the endpoint client, hiding four hazards verified against the live API (see the `feat` commit).
- **Docs** — a report-endpoints section in `CLAUDE.md`, plus two corrections: `reports/reportList/{cpfId}` is not broken (it requires `BaseReportTypeId`), and free-text name search is not entirely dead (`reports/log?Name=` works).
- **Specs** — `openspec/specs/report-list` and `openspec/specs/report-detail`.

## Verification

144 tests pass (92 before, 52 new); no existing test needed changing. Every commit passes its own suite, so a regression is bisectable. Verified live: `ocpf reports 14819` returns 21 current / 47 with `--include-superseded`; `ocpf report 170378` renders the 2013 special-election filing with balances $7,953.94 to $1,430.30 and 43 expenditure items totalling $10,036.61.

## Issues

`Refs #3` — **this does not close it.** #3 asks for a district-scoped roster (district plus date to cpfIds); this delivers the filer-to-report path, which is the open question #3 poses ("there may be a filer-to-reports path that does not depend on a roster" — there is: `reports/baseReportTypes/{cpfId}` plus `reports/reportList/{cpfId}`). The roster itself needs cross-filer `reports/log` search, deliberately deferred. #2 and #4 are untouched.

author: lamy210
body:
## Purpose

Fail closed when Foundation cannot establish whether the destination volume is read-only.

## Root cause

`FoundationDropFileSystemInspector` computed writability with `values.volumeIsReadOnly != true && fileManager.isWritableFile(...)`. Because `volumeIsReadOnly` is optional, `nil` was treated like explicit `false`.

Production execution does not independently re-read the volume read-only state: `DestinationDirectoryLeaseRegistry` requires the authoritative plan to be writable, then the production copy accessor's `isWritableDirectory` only proves that the exact descriptor-bound destination directory is active. Therefore an unknown Foundation volume read-only state could be promoted into an executable plan whenever the path-level best-effort check returned writable.

## Fix

- isolate destination writability classification in a small internal classifier
- require `volumeIsReadOnly == false` explicitly before advertising the destination as writable
- keep `FileManager.isWritableFile` as an additional conservative path check, not as evidence that an unknown volume state is writable
- unknown `volumeIsReadOnly` -> not writable
- explicit read-only -> not writable
- explicit writable volume + non-writable path -> not writable
- explicit writable volume + writable path -> writable
- keep source/destination descriptor authority, exclusive no-overwrite commit, Recovery, persistence, entitlements, dependencies, and release workflows unchanged

## TDD

### RED

Bootstrap CI #523 on test-only head `ebd404c1c5fa9f658002ef88958eebec58c2f151` failed in Swift package tests because `DestinationStorageWritabilityClassifier` did not exist. This proved the conservative classification contract was not already implemented.

### GREEN

Bootstrap CI #525 on head `8c0d8ce553843147aed5d12df8b00cdaf1577e1b` completed successfully.

Regression coverage verifies:

- unknown volume read-only state is rejected as writable authority
- explicit read-only volume is rejected
- explicit writable volume with a non-writable path is rejected
- explicit writable volume with a writable path is accepted

Verified in CI:

- Public repository guard ✅
- Architecture guard ✅
- File safety guard ✅
- Release metadata guard ✅
- App icon guard ✅
- Production release preflight ✅
- Swift package tests / Xcode 26.6 ✅
- Visual snapshot regression ✅
- AddressSanitizer package tests ✅
- Xcode project validation ✅
- Debug app build ✅
- Release app build ✅
- App bundle / Sandbox baseline ✅
- Unsigned CI artifact packaging/upload ✅
- Swift package tests / macOS 15 ✅
- macOS 15 app compatibility build ✅

## Scope

One conceptual destination capability hardening change only. No copy primitive, descriptor identity, no-overwrite commit, persistence schema, entitlement, dependency, Recovery, source-file handling, or release workflow changes.

author: arist12
body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39311

Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/3690

## What I did

Investigated the prepared `main` implementation for the reported DeepSeek-V4 routed-expert FP8 / float-block-scale accuracy issue. The checkout already contains an issue-specific candidate correction: `Fp8MoEMethod` requantizes serialized 128x128 block-FP8 routed-expert weights from float32 block scales to UE8M0 only when the selected runner is a compatible DeepGEMM BF16 path.

I therefore did not duplicate or broaden the source change. This PR records the evidence, the existing regression coverage, an independent one-GPU numerical boundary fixture, and the limitations.

## Reproduce

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-fb1fcfe3152f/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_deepgemm_ue8m0_requant.py
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-fb1fcfe3152f/venv/bin/python reports/j-fb1fcfe3152f/validate_fp8_requant_gpu.py
```

The focused suite passes 7 tests, including the MoE w13/w2 call site and negative boundaries for non-DeepGEMM runners, non-BF16 output, incompatible shapes, unsupported block size, and repeated processing. The gfx950 fixture used exactly one visible MI350X and measured 0.0249255 relative RMSE for float-scale checkpoint values requantized to UE8M0-compatible scales, with finite output.

## Uncertainty and limitations

The source issue itself was not reproduced. The reporter's private DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT weights are unavailable, and this job has one AMD gfx950 rather than eight NVIDIA H200 GPUs. Consequently this does not execute CUDA/SM90 DeepGEMM, TP=8, the full model, or the 480-sample AIME25/vLLM comparison. The result is `candidate_verified`, not a claim that the full-model quality gap is confirmed fixed. The tiny Llama transport fixture was intentionally not substituted for DeepSeek-V4 quantization or semantic accuracy.

No native library was changed or rebuilt.

author: dbn1972
body:
### Summary

Fixes **DOM-016**: `metadata-service`'s rule-expression evaluator (`services/metadata-service/src/modules/rules/domain.ts`'s `resolveField`) resolved field names via a bare `data[fieldName]` lookup with no own-property check. Referencing a name like `constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString` or `hasOwnProperty` in a rule expression resolved a value off `Object.prototype` instead of correctly reporting "field not found". Added an `Object.hasOwn` own-property guard, added regression tests proving both the fix and that legitimate same-named own fields still resolve correctly, and verified no regression against the full `metadata-service` suite.

### Business impact

Tenant-defined validation-rule expressions are meant to be a safe, restricted grammar — the module's own header comment states "NO eval(), no arbitrary JS — safe by construction." This bug broke that guarantee at one specific point: a rule expression referencing a non-existent "field" that happens to share a name with something on `Object.prototype` got a non-null, non-data-driven result instead of the correct "not found" behavior. That undermines the integrity of rules that gate whether data is accepted (a rule meant to reject bad records could be made to always pass, or the reverse) and can leak a stringified internal (e.g. `String(Object)`) into the evaluation.

### Findings resolved

DOM-016 (P3) — Rule evaluator resolves prototype keys.

### Technical changes

- `services/metadata-service/src/modules/rules/domain.ts`: `resolveField` now returns `null` immediately when `!Object.hasOwn(data, fieldName)`, before ever touching `data[fieldName]`.
- Read the tokenizer in full (lines 48-93) to confirm field names are always flat identifiers (`[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*`) — there is no dotted-path contract this guard could break.
- `resolveField` is module-private, only reachable through the exported `evaluateExpression`/`validateRecord`; no API/schema/migration changes.

### Tests performed

All commands run in an isolated worktree (`~/wt/dom-016`) on `cloudsphere-ec2`, never the primary checkout.

- `pnpm --filter @civitasone/metadata-service exec vitest run tests/metadata-engine.test.ts -t "DOM-016"` — reproduced the bug first: 3/4 new tests failed against the unfixed code (bare `constructor`/`__proto__` reference evaluated truthy; `ISBLANK(constructor)` returned `false` instead of `true`; a rule referencing `ISBLANK(constructor)` fired when it shouldn't).
- Applied the fix, re-ran the same file: 26/26 passed (22 pre-existing + 4 new).
- Sabotage check: `git stash push -- .../rules/domain.ts` (keeping the new tests), re-ran — same 3 failures reproduced identically; `git stash pop` restored the fix — green again.
- `pnpm --filter @civitasone/metadata-service test` (full service suite): 222/223 tests passed across 15 files, 6 files failed to resolve `@civitasone/auth`/`@civitasone/observability` workspace-package entries. Ran the identical command against pristine `origin/main` for comparison: 218/219 passed, same 6 files failing the same way. The only difference is this PR's 4 new passing tests — zero regressions.
- `pnpm --filter @civitasone/metadata-service exec tsc --noEmit`: same pre-existing unresolved-workspace-package errors on this branch and on baseline `origin/main` (compared directly); nothing new introduced.

### Security impact

Closes a prototype-chain read path in a rule-expression evaluator: `constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf`, etc. now correctly resolve to `null` ("field not found") instead of an attacker-influenceable non-null result. This resolver is read-only — no prototype-pollution *write* occurs anywhere in this file — but the missing guard let expressions get inconsistent, non-data-driven pass/fail behavior from names that aren't real fields, a correctness/integrity issue for a component whose entire purpose is deciding whether data is valid. No auth/tenant boundary is touched.

### Database impact

None.

### UX impact

None directly. A tenant admin authoring a validation-rule expression that happens to reference a name colliding with a JS prototype member now gets consistent, honest "field not found" behavior instead of unpredictable engine-internal behavior.

### Deployment considerations

None — pure application-code change, no config/flag/migration/restart sequencing implications beyond the service's normal deploy.

### Remaining risks

- Found the identical unguarded pattern in a sibling module while checking for other callers: `services/metadata-service/src/modules/formula/domain.ts:156`'s own `resolveField` (used by the formula engine, a different module from the rules engine this gap named). Deliberately **not** fixed here to keep this PR scoped to DOM-016's filed evidence — filed as new gap **DOM-031** in `docs/ENTERPRISE-GAP-REPORT-2026-09-07.md` (included in this PR) rather than silently fixed or ignored.
- Pre-existing, unrelated: 6 `metadata-service` test files fail to resolve `@civitasone/auth`/`@civitasone/observability` workspace-package entries in a fresh worktree (needs a workspace `pnpm build` first) — confirmed present identically on unmodified `origin/main`, not introduced or worsened by this change.

### Checklist

```text
[x] New branch created from latest origin/main (worktree on shared hosts)
[x] Scope limited to requested module and required dependencies
[x] No unrelated user changes overwritten
[x] No secrets committed
[ ] Formatting / lint / typecheck pass for touched packages -- lint not wired for a bare --filter invocation in this fresh worktree (pre-existing env gap, unrelated); tsc --noEmit shows only the same pre-existing errors as baseline, nothing new
[x] Build passes for touched packages (n/a for this module; tsc --noEmit checked, no new errors)
[x] Unit / service tests pass (222/223, matching baseline's 218/219 exactly plus the 4 new tests)
[ ] Integration / contract tests run when cross-service behaviour changes -- n/a, no cross-service behavior change
[ ] Critical e2e workflows considered or executed -- n/a for this scope
[x] Security and tenant-isolation tests pass where applicable (the new DOM-016 regression tests are exactly this)
[ ] Database migration validated -- n/a, no migration
[ ] Accessibility-critical paths checked when UI changes -- n/a, no UI change
[ ] Performance smoke considered for hot paths -- n/a

body:
Supersedes #78 and #79, which carried these two changes separately. Both commits are preserved here unchanged, including @Varuas37's pill-composer commit. ## What this changes for a consumer Purely additive on the new module; the pill-composer half changes behaviour of an existing component without changing its API. No export, import path, registry target, token, or file layout moved or changed meaning. - **`@nessalabs/ui` (npm):** new public exports — `MessageApproval`, `ContactChoices`, `MessageDigest`, and their prop/entry types (`MessageApprovalProps`, `MessageApprovalStatus`, `ContactChoice`, `ContactChoicesProps`, `MessageDigestEntry`, `MessageDigestProps`). `PillComposer` and `ChatComposerEditor` keep every prop they had; what changes is how the composer expands and lays out multiline input. - **`@nessalabs/agent-stream` (npm):** no change. Neither entry (`.`, `./transcript`) is touched. - **shadcn registry (`shadcn add `):** a new item, `shadcn add nessalabs/nessa_ui/message-actions`, installing eight files under `components/ui/message-actions/` and pulling `button`, `nessa-base`, and `utils`. The existing `pill-composer` and `chat-composer-editor` items keep their files and targets; only their copied source changes. `nessa-base` gains nothing — the new components use tokens that already ship. - **Storybook:** a new `Conversation/MessageActions` entry with 18 stories, all with play tests, plus additions to `PillComposer`'s stories. - **`assets/brand-marks/`:** new, outside every published surface. Provenance for the two channel marks; not a build input. ### Before and after ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph before["Before"] B1["@nessalabs/ui"] --> B2["Message, ChatBubble
transcript pieces"] B3["a send-confirmation card"] -.->|"assembled by hand
from Card + Button"| B2 end subgraph after["After"] A1["@nessalabs/ui"] --> A2["MessageApproval
ContactChoices
MessageDigest"] A3["shadcn add …/message-actions"] --> A4["components/ui/message-actions/
index.ts + 7 files"] end ``` ## The three message-action surfaces **ContactChoices** asks which of several same-named people was meant. **MessageApproval** is the confirmation before the message goes: recipient, the app it travels over, the draft, and the two decisions. **MessageDigest** is the reading half — what the agent found in an inbox, drawn the way a mail app draws it, quiet tiles by default and buttons the moment `onValueChange` says a row can be opened. All three measure their own container rather than the viewport, so one element works docked in a narrow rail — where the approval's actions stack with **Send** on top — and in a full-width panel, with no size prop to keep in sync. Delivery, selection, ordering, and filtering stay with the host. ## Decisions worth reviewing - **The editable draft draws no focus ring.** The caret shows where focus is, and browsers match `:focus-visible` on editable fields for pointer focus too, so an outline there reads as a permanent border around the message rather than as focus. This is the call `ChatComposer`'s textarea already makes and documents. The read-only draft (`editable={false}`) keeps the ring — it has no caret and takes a tab stop while it scrolls. The focus inventory in `validation/nessa/focus-treatments.ts` records exactly that split. - **The live region is mounted for the card's whole life**, empty while the decision is open. A region inserted at the moment its text appears is a mutation most screen readers never announce, so "Sending…" and the outcome would be silent. The visible status line is not the live region. - **Channel marks are trademark-scoped.** iMessage and Mail marks are traced from the public-domain SVGs recorded in `assets/brand-marks/` (`PD-textlogo` on Commons, plus their standard trademark warning). A card badges one only when its own `channel` names that service; every other channel gets no badge until the host passes `channelIcon`, because a wrong logo claims something untrue about where the message is going. - **Corner markers sit on the avatar's ring, not its bounding box.** A circle's bounding-box corner is outside the circle by `0.29r`, so `-bottom-0.5 -right-0.5` leaves a marker floating diagonally clear of the edge. Both the channel mark and the unread dot centre on the circle's own edge at 45°. - **Unread rides the avatar rather than a leading column**, which would cost every row that indent for a mark most rows do not carry. The dot is `aria-hidden`; the word "Unread." is in the row's text. ## What it looks like Storybook captures, light and dark. The images live on the orphan branch `assets/pr-80-screenshots` rather than in this diff, because the repository keeps no binaries on `main` — delete that branch when this PR closes. | MessageApproval | Editable draft | | --- | --- | | | | | Resolved, dark | Narrow rail, dark | | --- | --- | | | | | ContactChoices | Told apart by their badge, dark | | --- | --- | | | | | MessageDigest | Digest in a narrow rail, dark | | --- | --- | | | | ## Review round The automated review raised three findings on `3c3b433`, all fixed in `ba845b5`, each with a play test asserting the end state: - **A badge that carries meaning now says so in words.** `ContactChoice` and `MessageDigestEntry` take a `badgeLabel`, rendered after the name so a row reads "Clark Kent on Mail". The marks stay decoration; MessageApproval still needs no label because it writes the channel out beside the avatar. - **Corner markers mirror with text direction**, using the logical `start` inset with a direction-aware centring shift instead of a physical `left`. - **PillComposer collapses when expansion is withdrawn.** `expanded` is derived from `expandable`, so flipping the prop off while expanded cannot strand someone in a full-pane overlay whose only exit was Escape. ## Checks `pnpm typecheck` clean and `pnpm validate` 0 failures on the combined tree. `pnpm build:registry` regenerates byte-identical output, so the two branches' `registry.json` edits merged cleanly rather than textually. `pnpm test`: 974 of 974 passing, including the three new regression stories. ## Summary

Reject incompatible Windows Vulkan worker process paths before launch, preserving verified canonical-path execution and CPU-safe selection. This is a narrowly scoped stack on #160; it does not merge or alter that parent.

## Why

Fixture-signed diagnostics on physical NVIDIA hardware (driver 616.92) found two complete Vulkan SCIF/transcription passes at a 255-unit ordinary DOS worker path and two pre-Hello FAST_FAIL_INVALID_ARG failures at 256. CDB observed ordinary versus verbatim CreateProcessW path representations. These captures used the pre-guard build; they are diagnostic evidence, not production-pack or release qualification. Rust 1.96's path conversion corroborates this boundary, but the driver's internal cause is not established.

## Changes and invariants

- After signed-pack, reviewed-loader, and worker-file verification, the shared Windows Vulkan probe/execution resolver permits only standard local drive paths with a projected DOS length of at most 255 UTF-16 units.
- Reuse the existing strict Windows path parser to reject normalization-sensitive components, reserved names, UNC, and device namespaces. Accept short canonical VerbatimDisk paths without rewriting them.
- Preserve exact-path Command launch, retained handles, immediate identity revalidation, loader hashes, inventory verification, and IPC authority.
- Propagate a typed, path-free incompatibility diagnostic through discovery and route planning. No device binding/generation is created and the deterministic rejection is not recorded as a GPU crash/quarantine event.
- Preserve strict explicit GPU behavior and Auto's other qualified GPU routes/CPU fallback. CPU, CUDA, Metal, and non-Windows launch behavior are unchanged.
- No signing changes, qualification entries, calibration, driver changes, downloads, aliases, reparse indirection, or DLL trust relaxation. The Auto manifest remains empty/default-deny.

## Verification

Using Rust 1.96.0 and the validated pinned MSVC/SDK environment, a fresh isolated local Cargo target, reviewed native archive, and private test TEMP/TMP:

- Clean parent baseline: `cargo test --locked --offline --all-targets --features ui-harness,inference-worker -- --test-threads=1 --quiet` — 1,642 passed, 11 intentionally ignored.
- Changed full suite: same command — **1,648 passed, 0 failed, 11 intentionally ignored**; six additional tests.
- Focused `windows_vulkan` suite — **23 passed, 1 hardware-evidence test intentionally ignored**.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — passed.
- `scripts/test-windows-vulkan-evidence.ps1` — passed, including four pack-target and three CPU-digest harness mutations.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- CI-matching lint: `cargo clippy --locked --offline --all-targets --features ui-harness,inference-worker,vulkan-acceleration -- -D warnings` — passed.
- CPU-safe application: `cargo check --locked --offline --bin local-transcriber --features ui-harness` — passed.
- Supplemental CPU-only lint attempt (without `vulkan-acceleration`) failed on five unchanged Vulkan-only helper dead-code warnings; no warning suppression or unrelated source changes were made. The CI-matching Vulkan-enabled lint above passed.
- Clean-head Vulkan-enabled suite: `cargo test --locked --offline --all-targets --features ui-harness,inference-worker,vulkan-acceleration -- --test-threads=1 --quiet` — **1,648 passed, 0 failed, 12 intentionally ignored**, on `4920b6174de368f44c36cce146ecd5e23e0ab70f`.
- Independent security/correctness review: code-level GO after adding DOS-normalization and route-propagation coverage.

New coverage includes Disk/VerbatimDisk 255/256 boundaries, UTF-16 surrogate-pair accounting, NUL/namespace/normalization rejection, unchanged canonical paths, the shared verified-launch boundary, typed discovery propagation, no generation/failed probe-cache state, strict GPU errors, and Auto CPU route availability.

## Fresh-head fixture hardware diagnostic

On exact clean `4920b6174de368f44c36cce146ecd5e23e0ab70f`, a freshly built **release Vulkan fixture worker** and matching **CPU-only debug parent harness** were tested on NVIDIA RTX 4080 SUPER / driver 616.92. This is targeted guard validation, not production or release/performance qualification.

- At an actual 255-UTF-16-unit immutable worker path, the existing verified Vulkan smoke passed challenge-bound SCIF Hello, expected stable GPU identity, transcription/expected-phrase assertions, warm reuse, and its zero-CPU-launch assertion. The two reconstructed `CreateProcessW` worker application strings exactly match that path (probe and inference).
- At an actual 256-unit verified worker path, the test returned the exact typed compatibility rejection before any observed worker-launch call. No copied worker module, Vulkan loader, NVIDIA module, or native fast-fail marker appeared. The expected failing smoke exited 101 without timeout.
- The original diagnostic wrapper incorrectly required exit 0 before its expected-rejection assertions and looked only in stdout for an error emitted on stderr. Its wrapper result remains failed. An independent, hash-pinned post-capture validator passed the paired raw evidence, reconstructed paths, and exact retained pack inventory without modifying or rerunning the originals.
- Independent security/evidence review confirmed these narrow conclusions. The 256 Rust assertion is not the previous NVIDIA native fast-fail. Counts refer to worker-launch calls, not all OS/debugger descendants.
- Removed only the verified duplicate pack and empty case roots after review (98,881,825 file bytes). Original fixture pack, logs, and matching binaries/symbols remain locally retained.

author: chelseakr
body:
## The premise, stated accurately

**The publisher is fine and this PR does not touch it.** `pages.yml` fires on `push: branches: [main]` with no path filter, plus `workflow_dispatch`. That trigger is correct and nothing here changes it, dispatches it, or touches publishing policy.

What is missing is anything that notices when a firing did not land. This repository has no `live-integrity.yml` and no scheduled job that reaches https://chelseakr.github.io/perimeter/ at all — unlike `cairn`, `chalkline`, `plumbline`, `disclosed`, `gauntlet`, `sprout`, `nearmiss`, `homeroom`, `id-churn-sentinel` and `tods-validate`. `ci.yml` reads the working tree, `codeql.yml` reads the source, `pages.yml` publishes, and none of them asks what a visitor receives.

Measured over the 75 commits on `main` since `pages.yml` was added on 2026-08-07:

| | |
|---|---|
| main commits since `pages.yml` landed | 75 |
| of those, with **no** `github-pages` deployment | **23** (31%) |
| of those 23, `publish-site` run finished `cancelled` | 13 |
| of those 23, no `publish-site` run at all (batched push / pre-Pages-config) | 10 |
| of those 23, commits that changed files under `site/` | **2** — `4385957b9`, `edbfb9bd7`, both 2026-08-29 |

The `pages` concurrency group is `cancel-in-progress: false`, which holds exactly one pending run: a second push while a publish is in flight evicts the first. (Counted over `--event push` runs only; the ten with no run at all arrived inside a push whose tip was another commit, and have no `ci` push run either.)

The sharpest single case is `edbfb9bd7`, one of the two that changed `site/`: its `ci` push run finished **success** and its `publish-site` push run finished **cancelled**. `main` got a full green verdict on a commit whose bytes never went out, and nothing said so — a cancelled run is not a failed one, and nothing was asking.

Three published states of `site/` were therefore never served by any deployment: `d7c40cbf2` (2026-08-07, before Pages was switched to Actions), `d4d346a9d` and `a3aa215dc` (both 2026-08-29). The last two were superseded within minutes, so no visitor was wrong for long — but nothing in this repository could have said so either way.

## What this adds

`tools/deploy_staleness.py` + `.github/workflows/deploy-staleness.yml` + `tests/test_deploy_staleness.py`.

### The comparison: the published subtree, not the deployed commit

`gh api repos/ChelseaKR/perimeter/pages` reports `build_type: workflow`, which invites "deployed SHA versus `main` head". That comparison would be wrong here.

`pages.yml` does not render the site. It cannot: `site/` is built from CAL FIRE's acquired files, which are never in git and never in CI — the workflow's own header says so. Its build job *checks* the committed bytes (determinism from fixtures, `tests/test_published_site.py`, `html-validate` and axe-core over `site/` itself) and then hands `actions/upload-pages-artifact` exactly one thing: `path: site`.

So this is a **committed-tree publisher**, and the visitor-visible path set is the published directory itself:

```
git rev-parse <deployed_sha>:site   vs   git rev-parse <head>:site
```

Equal tree object ids mean the visitor holds exactly the bytes `main` holds, however many commits and days separate the two. The derivation, spelled out in the module docstring:

- `src/perimeter/render.py`, `artifacts.py`, `coverage.py` and the field registry *produce* `site/`, but a change to any of them alters no published byte until somebody runs `make site` against `data/raw/` and commits the result. `make site-check` exists because that gap is real.
- `.github/workflows/pages.yml` decides *whether* the upload happens, not what is in it. A change there that broke publishing shows up as a missing or unsuccessful deployment, which this module already refuses on.
- `tests/`, `docs/`, `README.md`, `fixtures/`, the lockfiles and every dependabot bump change `main` constantly and change nothing a visitor receives.

Concretely: a SHA comparison would have cried wolf on 21 of those 23 undeployed commits and said nothing useful about the two that mattered. It would also call a change plus its revert permanently stale; tree ids do not.

### The source: the deployment record, not `publish-site`'s run history

Thirteen of those runs finished `cancelled`. Count a cancelled run as a publish and the site reads as fresh every time; filter cancellations out and the newest surviving run may be days from the commit it is credited with. A `github-pages` deployment exists only because bytes were published, it names the commit they came from, and its newest status must read `success` before its commit may be treated as live — a deployment row on its own is a *request* to publish.

### It publishes nothing

No `pages: write`, no `id-token: write`, no deploy credential, no `workflow_dispatch` of anything, no publish-enable variable read or set. Workflow-level `permissions: {}`; the one job takes `contents: read`, `deployments: read`, `issues: write`. `persist-credentials: false`, `fetch-depth: 0`, `timeout-minutes: 15`, `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, `actions/checkout` pinned to the same 40-char SHA already used in `ci.yml` and `pages.yml`. Weekly, Mondays 06:29 UTC, plus `workflow_dispatch` with a `max_age_days` input.

### The verdict is an issue, not a permanent red

Overdue files or updates one issue and closes it when the site catches up. The run goes red **only when the measurement cannot be made**: no `github-pages` deployment in the history, none reporting a successful status, a deployed commit this clone does not contain (shallow checkout), a diverged history, a `site/` that is not where `pages.yml` says it is, or two readings that contradict each other. Every one of those raises and exits 2. None returns a comfortable zero.

Age alone is never the verdict: a site nobody republished because nothing it publishes changed is correct, not stale. The clock starts at the **oldest unpublished commit that touched `site/`**, not at the deploy — an old deploy plus a change made yesterday is one day of waiting, not two hundred.

## Current reading

```
Published build:  874107fca  (2026-09-13, deployment 6423957323)
main:             874107fca
Published bytes:  site/ tree 36e172463 served, 36e172463 on main
Since the deploy: 0 days, 0 commits, 0 of them touching site/

Up to date: the served site/ tree is byte-identical to main's.
```

The site is correct today. The point is that nothing could have said so, and nothing would have said otherwise.

## Negative controls

Each sabotage was applied to `tools/deploy_staleness.py`, its landing proved by a changed `git hash-object` and a non-zero occurrence count, the full pytest output read, then restored and the hash confirmed byte-identical (`9712934352b08279eaf7432f6691674f7c7568e4`). `__pycache__` cleared between runs.

| # | Sabotage | hash before → after | tokens | Fired | Assertion |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A deployment row counts as a publish regardless of status | `9712934…` → `8a736e5…` | 1 | yes, 3 tests | `Failed: DID NOT RAISE StalenessUnknown` |
| 2 | Trust the checkout depth (drop the absent-commit refusal) | `9712934…` → `587b8ff…` | 1 | yes, 1 test | `Regex pattern did not match. Expected regex: 'not in this clone'; Actual message: 'git merge-base aaaa… failed: fatal: Not a valid commit name aaaa…'` |
| 3 | Compare commit ids instead of `site/` tree ids | `9712934…` → `acfadc2…` | 1 | yes, 3 tests | `AssertionError: assert False … .serving_current_bytes` |
| 4 | The deploy's own age is the verdict | `9712934…` → `a329fcc…` | 1 | yes, 4 tests | `AssertionError: assert not True … deploy_age_days=200, unpublished_commits=0 … .overdue` |
| 5 | A refusal returns 0 | `9712934…` → `b4a93ba…` | 1 | yes, 1 test | `assert 0 == 2` |
| 6 | `PUBLISHED_PATH` drifts from what `pages.yml` uploads | `9712934…` → `ae8e87c…` | 1 | yes, 11 tests | `AssertionError: pages.yml publishes 'site' and deploy_stalene

author: marquescoding
body:
`ghcr.io/marquescoding/valence` holds **52 tags**: `latest`, `main`, and **50 `sha-*`** tags. `publish.yml` adds one per merge to `main` and nothing has ever removed any.

## What it deletes

Only `sha-*` tags, older than **8 weeks**, keeping the **20 most recent**.

```yaml
image-tags: 'sha-*'
tag-selection: tagged
cut-off: 8w
keep-n-most-recent: 20
```

That single pattern is the entire guard. `latest`, `main` and every version tag are unreachable because none of them begins with `sha-`. I first wrote thirteen explicit exclusions (`!latest !main !v* !0*`…) and removed them: they would read as load-bearing protection while protecting nothing the selector could reach anyway.

## Why tag-driven and not version-driven

This is the part that matters. A package *version* can carry several tags, and I checked the registry rather than assuming:

    latest            sha256:2bf0158b…
    main              sha256:1b9e6ef9…
    sha-d41262ef…     sha256:1b9e6ef9…   ← same version as main

`actions/delete-package-versions` is the official action, but its inputs are all version-oriented (`num-old-versions-to-delete`, `min-versions-to-keep`). It has no way to express *delete this tag but keep the version, another tag needs it*. Once `0.1.0` is pushed it will share a digest with the `sha-` tag from the same commit, and a version-level delete would take the release image with it.

## Two things worth knowing

- **The first run deletes nothing.** Every `sha-` tag on the registry is weeks old, so `8w` + `keep-n-most-recent: 20` matches none of them today. A green run that removes nothing is the expected result, not a failure. It prunes as history ages.
- **This needs the repository granted the Admin role in the package settings.** It uses `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` so no secret has to be created, but a temporal token cannot list packages — hence `image-names: valence` exactly rather than a pattern — and without that role the scheduled run will fail on a Sunday where nobody is looking.

Manual runs default to `dry-run: true`, so the first execution can be a listing rather than a deletion.

author: rvanguita
body:
## Contexto

O portfólio apresentava bem o trabalho, mas não respondia às três perguntas que
um headhunter de Engenharia de Dados faz nos primeiros dez segundos: **quão
sênior, disponível como, e o que a experiência comprova.** A trajetória mostra
doutorado e engenharia elétrica — nenhum emprego formal em dados — e o site
silenciava sobre isso, o que transforma a lacuna em objeção.

O redesign visual já está em `main` (#58). Esta PR é a passada de **copy**
orientada a triagem, num único commit.

## O que muda

- **Assume a transição de carreira** na abertura, em vez de silenciar sobre ela.
- **Publica a ficha de triagem que faltava** — cargos-alvo, contratação, alcance
  e idiomas — como ficha técnica no bloco de contato, reusando a gramática da
  `.spec` de um projeto em vez de inventar um componente novo.
- **Promove o currículo em PDF a ação da abertura** (antes só no rodapé).
- **Reescreve quatro resumos de competência e quatro de projeto** para liderar
  pela capacidade transferível, não pelo domínio: o FastF1 agora abre em
  "lakehouse medalhão em Delta Lake com DAG semanal no Airflow", não em Fórmula 1.
- **Carrega `title`, `description` e JSON-LD** com os termos que headhunter
  pesquisa, em pt e en (`Data Engineer`, `lakehouse`, `ETL`, `MLOps`), com
  `jobTitle`, `knowsLanguage` e `seeks`. A interface segue 100% em português.
- **Sincroniza o dossiê em PDF**, que duplicava a copy do perfil, e libera
  `"Cientista de Dados"` no `check_dossier.py` — agora é um cargo-alvo
  declarado, não resíduo de versão antiga.

## Honestidade preservada

Nenhuma ressalva foi removida. O modelo do FastF1 segue **experimental**, o
artigo da INDUSCON segue **submetido** (nunca aceito ou revisado), o
fraud-detection segue **em desenvolvimento** e a ressalva de viés do dataset do
bank-churn continua na ficha. **"Pleno" aparece só como cargo procurado**, nunca
como cargo exercido ou tempo de casa.

## Verificação

- `npm run format:check`, `npm run build` (14 páginas) e `npm run check` — 0 erros.
- `dist/` servido na base `/portfolio/`: sem overflow horizontal a **360 / 768 /
  1440 px** (viewport real medido em iframe, não `--window-size`).
- Contraste ≥ 4.5:1 nos elementos novos, **nos dois temas**; três botões da
  abertura a 49 px de altura.
- `npm run dossier:generate && npm run dossier:check` — 3 páginas A4, 7 links.
- Preservados: **9 projetos, 28 itens de competência, 24 certificados, 14
  páginas** e a ordem do catálogo.

author: andrianm28
body:
Opsi **M2** dari [`2026-09-13-kamboja-design-language.md`](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-13-kamboja-design-language.md) §7 — panel teks + CTA naik di atas pita foto, **hanya di mobile**.

## Judulnya jujur: ini memperbaiki 256px, bukan menyelesaikan masalahnya

Rencana menyebut posisi CTA sebagai *"temuan UX terpenting dari seluruh pemeriksaan ini"* — aksi utama produk berada 1,4 layar di bawah lipatan, pada produk yang menurut brief sering dibuka dalam keadaan darurat, satu tangan, oleh orang yang sedang terguncang.

**PR ini memindahkannya dari 1,4 layar di bawah lipatan menjadi 0,14 layar.** Ia **tidak** menaikkannya ke atas lipatan, dan tidak boleh dideskripsikan begitu di mana pun.

| Viewport | | CTA atas | CTA bawah | Lewat lipatan 740? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 360×740 | sebelum | 1048 | 1100 | tidak — 360 lebih |
| | **sesudah** | **792** | **844** | tidak — 104 lebih |
| 320×740 | sebelum | 1116 | 1168 | tidak — 428 lebih |
| | **sesudah** | **860** | **912** | tidak — 172 lebih |

Tidak ada elemen yang terdorong ke bawah lipatan: yang di atas foto tidak bergerak sama sekali, yang di bawahnya naik 128px. Tidak ada yang berpindah sisi.

## Desktop tidak berubah — dibuktikan, bukan dilihat sekilas

1280×900: CTA di 808 sebelum **dan** sesudah. Screenshot halaman penuh **byte-identical**, md5 `97827f0705809bc6a4478fcd173e66a5`.

## M1 dicoba, diukur nol, dikembalikan

Saya perintahkan menumpuk M1 (perkecil pita foto) di atas M2. **Itu ruling saya yang salah.**

M2 sudah memindahkan foto ke **bawah** CTA — pada 360px, foto mulai di y=868, yaitu **76px di bawah** CTA. Memperkecil sesuatu yang dirender setelah CTA dalam aliran blok hanya memendekkan halaman di bawahnya. M1 diimplementasikan penuh (`h-64`→`h-32`, `md:h-96` utuh, CSS di-rebuild pada pin 4.3.3), diukur, dan hasilnya:

| | pita foto | CTA atas | CTA bawah |
|---|---|---|---|
| M2 | 256 | 792 | 844 |
| M2+M1 | **128** | **792** | **844** |

**Nol piksel**, dengan biaya memotong separuh satu-satunya foto besar halaman itu jadi strip 2,8:1. Dikembalikan, tidak di-commit.

**Konsekuensinya untuk rencana:** §7 berbunyi *"M1 dan M3 tetap tersedia bila pengukuran ulang menunjukkan CTA masih di bawah lipatan."* Itu keliru — **M1 adalah alternatif M2, bukan penerusnya.** Jatah ~96px M1 habis begitu M2 mendarat. Koreksi dokumen menyusul terpisah.

## Sisa tuas, diukur — dan keputusannya milik pemilik

Diukur lewat CSSOM pada build M2 yang ter-commit, tanpa mengubah kode. Lipatan = 740.

| Tuas | 360px | 320px |
|---|---|---|
| `h1` → `text-3xl` | 752 (12 lebih) | tidak lewat |
| `h1` → `text-2xl` | **740 — lewat tepat 0px** | 808 (68 lebih) |
| panel `p-6` → `p-4` | 796 | tidak lewat |
| banner → `text-sm` | 836 | tidak lewat |
| **banner dihapus** | **500** | **lewat** |

**Di 320px, tidak ada satu pun tuas yang lewat kecuali menghapus banner.**

Dan satu peringatan yang mudah hilang dalam ringkasan: **740px adalah tinggi viewport, bukan tinggi yang benar-benar terlihat di tangan.** Chrome browser memakan sebagian. Margin 0px dan 8px pada baris `text-2xl` kemungkinan besar **negatif di perangkat nyata.** Hanya opsi "banner dihapus" yang marginnya selamat.

Tiga pilihan tersisa, masing-masing berbiaya yang hanya pemilik bisa timbang:

1. **Banner** — satu-satunya yang lewat di 320px, tapi ia pengakuan jujur tentang apa yang situs ini belum bisa lakukan, dan §2.8 menyebutnya sudah benar. Memperkecilnya menukar keterbukaan dengan konversi, pada layanan pemakaman.
2. **M3 sticky CTA** — bekerja tanpa menyentuh banner; menambah elemen persisten di halaman pemasaran.
3. **`h1` → `text-2xl`** — mengamandemen skala tipografi `design-system.md` §1.4, dan lolosnya nol piksel.

Tidak ada yang dipilih di sini.

## Dua koreksi pengukuran terhadap audit

- Banner ketersediaan yang audit catat "~136px" sebenarnya **360px — 49% viewport**, lebih besar dari pita foto yang M2 geser. Total tetap rekonsiliasi di 1048, jadi salahnya di atribusi. Siapa pun yang merancang perbaikan berdasar 136px akan salah hitung.
- `<h1>` hero membungkus jadi **lima baris** (200px) di mobile.

## Verifikasi

`ci/verify-docs.sh` 18/18 PASS. Lewat image CI-parity PHP 8.5.8: `pint --test` PASS (1791 berkas), `blade:verify-content-survival` PASS (106 berkas, 0 rusak), `design:verify-filament-palette` PASS, tes hero/beranda + seluruh `tests/Feature/View` 0 gagal (204 asersi), `php -l` bersih. Tes regresi baru **mutation-checked** — gagal terhadap komponen sebelum perubahan.

Pengukuran menuntut build CSS: Tailwind v4 JIT, dan **tidak ada bundle lama yang memuat `order-last`** — percobaan pertama mengukur perubahan ini sebagai no-op literal karena itu. Dikompilasi dengan Tailwind CLI pada pin persis `package-lock.json` (4.3.3) di scratchpad saja, lalu dihapus. Bukan `npm run build`, bukan install penuh.

author: xizhuomengcontin
body:
Adds `integrations/orcareplay.md`.

### What it is

[OrcaReplay](https://github.com/Continuum-AI-Corp/OrcaReplay) (Apache-2.0, npm, Node 20+) records a Haystack run at the HTTP boundary to the model provider — **from outside the process** — and serves the recording back so the same run happens again with no provider contacted and no key needed.

There is nothing to register and no component to add, because `OpenAIChatGenerator` leaves `api_base_url=None` and the OpenAI SDK then falls back to `OPENAI_BASE_URL` — the variable the recorder sets for the child process it launches, and only for that process.

### Verified before submitting

`haystack-ai` 3.1.1 on Python 3.12, both a standalone `OpenAIChatGenerator` and a full `Pipeline` (`ChatPromptBuilder → OpenAIChatGenerator`), each recorded and then replayed with **the origin process killed**:

```console
$ orca replay last
info replaying exchanges=1 egress=blocked
info replay.done reused=1/1 exact=1 divergences=0 unmatched=0 exit=0
```

`exact=1` is a byte-for-byte match against a deterministic local origin standing in for a provider, so it is a real comparison rather than a model happening to repeat itself.

I filed the same result as a [Show and tell in the main repo](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/discussions/12729) — mentioning it here so the overlap is visible rather than discovered.

### Type and limits

I filed it under `type: Monitoring Tool` as the closest existing category — it is really a record/replay debugger, so if you would rather see a different type (or a new one), say the word and I will change it.

The page has an explicit **Limits** section, because two things here are easy to overstate and one is a genuine gap:

- blocked egress is **model-provider** egress, not network isolation — retrievers and custom components still run for real, so it is not a sandbox;
- a matching replay is **not** a determinism result, since the model is not re-asked;
- **`/v1/embeddings` is not captured.** I measured this rather than assuming it: embedding traffic is passed through to the live provider and is absent from the recording, so a replay refuses it with a named error instead of serving a wrong vector. A pipeline that embeds at query time cannot be fully replayed today. I would rather say that on the integration page than let someone find out at replay time.

No PyPI package — it is an npm CLI that launches your Python process, so only `repo` is set, which the README allows. No logo included; happy to add one if you would like.

Disclosure: I maintain it.

author: harol-reina
body:
## Why

`VoiceAiPipeline.PipelineLoop` sorted an `OperationCanceledException` from a synthesis into one of two clauses:
- the caller's clause, filtered on the caller's token;
- a barge-in clause with no filter at all.

A synthesizer that cancelled itself, while nobody had asked it to stop, therefore landed in the barge-in clause. Two ways that happens are an elapsed `HttpClient.Timeout` and a connect deadline the synthesizer links over the token it was handed. The caller heard nothing for that turn, yet the pipeline reported a successful synthesis:
- `tts.syntheses.completed` went up;
- it published `SynthesisEndedEvent`, and no `PipelineErrorEvent`;
- nothing was logged at Warning;
- the synthesis activity stayed `Unset`.

Both inputs below were measured on `b973e994` while the caller's token was still live:
- a real `HttpClient.Timeout`, which raised `TaskCanceledException` with an inner `TimeoutException`;
- `DeepgramSpeechSynthesizer`'s own connect deadline, which raised `TaskCanceledException` with an inner `IOException`.

Both exceptions carry a cancelled token of their own. Cartesia, LMNT, Speechmatics and Azure can raise the same kind of input, but that comes from reading the code, not from running them.

## What changes

### Code (CHANGELOG entry, BREAKING for telemetry)

The barge-in clause is now filtered on the synthesis's own source: `when (ttsCts.IsCancellationRequested)`. Only a barge-in or a disposal cancels that source.

Every other cancellation now reaches the existing failure clause, which:
- counts `tts.syntheses.failed` instead of `tts.syntheses.completed`;
- publishes one `PipelineErrorEvent` with source `Tts`, carrying the exception, instead of `SynthesisEndedEvent`;
- logs `PipelineError` at Warning;
- sets the `voiceai.tts.synthesis` activity to `Error`.

The failure is not rethrown. The session goes on to the next turn and still counts as completed.

Unchanged: a barge-in, a disposal and the caller's own cancellation, including when one of them lands while a synthesizer's own cancellation is still unwinding. In that race the requested ending wins, because `await foreach` awaits the enumerator's `DisposeAsync` before the exception reaches the filters.

### OpenSpec change `tts-own-cancellation-is-a-synthesis-failure` (decision_ref `Sdk/ADR-0050`)

- Adds a requirement to `streaming-session-lifecycle`. A synthesizer's own `OperationCanceledException` is reported as a synthesis failure. A synthesis ended by a requested cancellation is not.
- Does not require the current `tts.syntheses.completed` accounting for barge-ins and disposals. ADR-0050 E9 records that accounting as debt.
- Task 4.1 (the CHANGELOG entry) is checked in this PR. Tasks 3.6 (CI green) and 4.2 (archive) close after the merge.

## Verification

All runs are on `b973e994`, for the final commits: `37e2163b` (docs) and the fix commit.
- `dotnet build`, Release, of `Verbara.Sdk.VoiceAi.Tests` and `Verbara.Sdk.Governance.Tests`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `Verbara.Sdk.VoiceAi.Tests`: 87 of 87 pass, 62 of them in the pipeline namespace. `Verbara.Sdk.Governance.Tests`: 129 of 129.
- `tools/audit-test-asserts.sh`: 0 violations. `openspec validate --all --strict`: 10 passed.
- The full unit lane with coverage ran on the previous head, which had one test fewer. All 30 assemblies passed, line coverage was 83.23 % (band [83, 86]), and patch coverage was 100 % (1 of 1 changed line).

**Tests** (in `VoiceAiPipelineCancellationAccountingTests`)
- **Regression theory.** A synthesizer cancels itself in one of two shapes, either before any audio or after one chunk. The first shape is a `TaskCanceledException` with an inner `TimeoutException`; it carries the token of a source the synthesizer owns and has cancelled, as both measured inputs did. The second is a plain `OperationCanceledException`. The theory asserts the failure accounting and that no `SynthesisEndedEvent` is published.
- **Next-turn test.** After that failure the caller speaks again, and the test waits for the second response cycle.
- **Three controls.** A barge-in, a disposal and the caller's own cancellation during a parked synthesis are not reported as synthesis failures.
- **Precedence theory.** Each of those three endings lands while a synthesizer that cancelled itself is parked in `DisposeAsync`.

**Failing-first.** With `origin/main`'s `VoiceAiPipeline.cs`, 5 tests fail for the defect's reason: the four own-cancellation cases and the next-turn test.

**Mutations.** Each of these fails at least one committed test:
- removing the filter, or filtering on `!ct.IsCancellationRequested`;
- inverting the filter;
- deleting the barge-in clause;
- narrowing the filter by the exception's shape (`InnerException is not TimeoutException`);

author: johnnyt
body:
The placeholder a read-only mount draws in an empty slot shipped as an
`aria-hidden` decoration, so a screen reader heard the slot header and then
nothing. An editing mount announces the gap's "+"; the one mount that draws no
"+" said nothing at all about an arm being empty.

The operator's ruling of 2026-09-12 (RQ-SF041-5) is to NAME the empty arm -
"empty" together with the arm's own label. The span is now a labelled
`role="img"`: `aria-label={"#{@label} is empty"}`, with `label` threaded from
the slot to the gap the way `empty?` already is. Only the gap a slot draws
before its first child can be empty, so the interleaved gaps keep the
attribute's default and pass nothing.

The mark stays a mark - no event, no `phx-` attribute, no tab stop, no
`button` - which is ADR-0005's Note of 2026-09-08 item 7b's other half; the
existing non-interactivity test is unchanged and still green.

## Provenance

- Files: `lib/statifier_blocks/editor/slot.ex`,
  `test/statifier_blocks/editor/profile_test.exs`, `changelog.d/sb-z6vv.md`.
  All three are in the dispatch's file map, with one correction: the brief and
  the bead note name the file `lib/statifier_blocks/slot.ex`; the real path is
  `lib/statifier_blocks/editor/slot.ex` (re-located by anchor
  `class="sb-gap__placeholder"`).
- The `aria-hidden="true"` attribute is REMOVED from the placeholder. The
  dispatch asked for a test asserting the placeholder "and its aria-hidden";
  an `aria-hidden` element has no accessible name to give, so naming the arm
  and keeping `aria-hidden` on the same element are mutually exclusive by
  spec. The ruling (name the arm) wins and the test asserts the name, the
  `role="img"`, and the absence of `aria-hidden`. Flagged in the worker return.
- No sibling PR was rebased over: `origin/main` was `229a560` at branch time
  and unmoved at push.
- No `docs/adr/` change (`git diff origin/main --stat -- docs/adr/` is empty);
  the blocks editor keeps "run" for fixture replay - no rename.

## Gate

`mix quality` green on this exact tree (`git write-tree` =
`90b4de3b2d280c21e829ed0a4ebc3d278113d03c`, the tree this commit carries):
`Format`, `Compile` (warnings as errors), `Dependencies`, `ADR cites`
("Every record citation resolves and is unmoved", 57 advisory), `Credo`,
`Tests: 3,248 of 3,248 passed, 94.9% coverage`, `Dialyzer: No warnings`.
`gate=green`. The gate lock and machine slot were held across the gate and the
commit; the commit tree is byte-identical to the tree the gate ran on, so the
commit was taken bare citing this run (SF037 retro d shape).

## Sabotage

`aria-label` dropped from the placeholder in `Slot.gap/1` (the span keeps
`role="img"`): `mix test test/statifier_blocks/editor/profile_test.exs` went
`29 tests, 1 failure` - only the new test - and the pre-existing
non-interactivity test stayed green. Reverted from a `cp` copy taken before the
mutation, not by `git checkout`; the suite is green again on the restored file.

## Firewall

Terminology scan from the umbrella's `docs/terminology-firewall.md` over the
full outbound diff and over this body: `hard=0`, `soft=0`. Positive control
constructed by injecting a known-hit term into a COPY of the diff; the control
run printed the injected line, and the copy was deleted when the scan was read.

## Acceptance

| Line | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A read-only mount's empty arm carries an accessible name | checked | `slot.ex` placeholder span: `role="img" aria-label={"#{@label} is empty"}` |
| The name is "empty" together with the arm's own label | checked | Rendered for the fixture's arm as `When "variant_b" is empty` |
| A test asserts it | checked | `profile_test.exs` "an empty slot's placeholder is named for its arm" |
| The mark stays non-interactive | checked | Pre-existing test "an empty slot draws a non-interactive placeholder" unchanged and green |
| Sabotage red | checked | See Sabotage above |

author: edenbd1
body:
Four things, none touching a contract.

## 1. The deferred claim is settled

Claim 41, 1 USDC, owner bob, had been skipped by the queue head and left counted in `outstanding_liabilities`. bob was given a trustline, claimed it, returned the cash to the admin who funded him, and had the trustline dropped again, which is the state `smoke-review2` needs him in. Liabilities are 0.

## 2. The suites get the book they assume

They walk end to end against one shared deployment and every one assumes a book roughly at rest. None established that, so the first suite in a run got what it expected and the rest got whatever the one before left.

`lib-baseline.sh` settles the queue and brings home anything an adapter still holds against its booked exposure. A written-down position is left alone: the adapter holds nothing and its exposure is already zero.

Patching assertions one at a time was making each suite tolerate one more shape without fixing the class. Several were also still sized on the basis the Engine stopped using; those move onto accounted free reserves and `floor_base`, with each leg bounded by its own pool remaining room.

## 3. Where the Vault equity can go

Nowhere, and that is worth stating. USDC leaves through exactly two calls: `settle_allocation`, to an adapter whose only outbound path returns to the Vault it stores, and the payout behind `claim_withdrawal` and `settle_withdrawal`, bounded by the agUSD burned to make the claim. There is no third, deliberately: a Vault that can pay equity to an admin is a Vault an admin can empty.

This Vault holds `133640000` above agUSD supply, recovered principal booked without minting against it. It is permanent.

## 4. That number changes the redeployment trade

Closing the `contractspecv0` divergence means a new Vault generation, and a replacement has no way to take that capital either, so it would be stranded. A doc comment is not worth `133640000`. The `pendingRedeployment` reason says so now.

## Not finished

Run one at a time on a normalised book all eight suites pass. Chained they do not yet, and the remaining failures are the same kind: assertions that predict a number the contracts compute from state that moved underneath.

196 tests pass.

author: brunojet
body:
> Empilhado sobre #3. Depois dos merges de #2 e #3, trocar a base para `develop`.

## O que muda

O fallback copiava de forma síncrona e respondia `302` a quem pegava o lock — o tempo de cópia ficava amarrado ao timeout de integração do API Gateway (29 s). Agora a PoC simula o desenho assíncrono da ADR 0001:

- **Requisição do API Gateway:** checa o path direto → pega o lock → confere a origem (`404` só em `NotFound`; outros erros viram `500`, não `404` cacheável) → dispara a cópia com `InvocationType: Event` → responde `202` + `Retry-After`, **inclusive a quem pegou o lock**.
- **Invocação assíncrona:** fica dona do lock, copia `origin/{key}` → `{key}` em streaming e libera o lock. É uma invocação separada da Lambda (não goroutine após o retorno), então roda até o fim dentro do timeout da função.
- **Terraform:** timeout 300 s e TTL do lock 360 s, com `precondition` exigindo TTL ≥ timeout; permissão de autoinvocação; `maximum_retry_attempts = 0` na invocação assíncrona (um retry rodaria sem lock).
- Docs: diagramas de sequência (cache-miss e concorrência), ADR, SPEC e architecture.

Também inclui o rebuild com a correção do lock expirado do `go-infra-adapters` (`feature/storage-ranges`, commits `101da07`/`2fbc199`).

## Validação (AWS real, stage `dev`)

| Cenário | Resultado |
|---|---|
| Lock vencido plantado na key (antes deste PR, com a correção do adapter) | chamada 1 detecta a expiração, apaga o lock e responde `202`; chamada 2 pega o lock e resolve |
| Cache-miss, objeto pequeno | winner recebe `202` em ~1,1 s (com cold start); cópia em background; próxima chamada `302` → `206` |
| Cache-miss, origem com 109 MB, via `scripts/download_range.py` | cliente recebeu `202` (`fetch started`) e `202` (`already in progress`); cópia de 7,1 s em background (log `COPY OK`); download completo com SHA-256 idêntico |
| `precondition` com `fallback_lock_ttl_seconds=10` | `plan` falha com mensagem clara |

Estado de teste restaurado ao fim (objeto de 73 bytes na origem).

## Observações

- `go.mod`: adiciona `aws-sdk-go-v2/service/lambda` e sobe o núcleo do SDK para versões compatíveis.
- `go build`/`vet` foram rodados com um `-modfile` temporário, porque o `replace` relativo do `go.mod` não resolve a partir de worktrees.

author: zsomborrajki
body:
Two rounds of the same problem: `.github/copilot-instructions.md` describing a CloudKit state that had moved on. The first commit fixes the claims #319's review pass flagged; the second was written after the schema was promoted to production **while this PR was open**, which made part of the first commit wrong in the other direction.

Documentation only — no code, no tests. Nothing was written to CloudKit: `export-schema` and `validate-schema` only.

## What the live container says now

A read-only `cktool export-schema` of **both** environments returns byte-identical files (`md5 3b0e2dfa48759da3c9d53de98007eb48`). Compared field-for-field against the code:

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `CommunityHike` vs `CommunitySchema.Listing` | matches — no missing or extra fields |
| `CommunityHikeSubmission` vs `CommunitySchema.Submission` | matches — no missing or extra fields |
| Listing indexes | `location` QUERYABLE+SORTABLE, `title` SEARCHABLE, `publishedAt` SORTABLE, `submission` QUERYABLE, `authorID` **unindexed** — as the schema header requires |
| Submission indexes | **none at all**, `___recordID` included — the enumeration control holds |
| Grants | listing `_world` read + create/write to `reviewer`; submission `_creator` **read** |
| `CD_HikeWalk` vs `MirroredCloudKitSchema` | complete |
| `CD_Hike` vs `MirroredCloudKitSchema` | **missing `author`, `importedAuthorName`, `keywords`, `trackDescription`** |

## The promote answered an open question

This file said nothing had established that a deploy *can* drop an index or downgrade a `GRANT` rather than only add things — production's submission type had every field indexed and `GRANT WRITE TO "_creator"`, and whether the button could take those away was unknown. It can, and the file now says so, with the standing instruction to re-export and check kept intact: one promote is not a guarantee about the next.

## The four-field gap survived it

Development did not have those columns either — all four are `String?` never exported with a non-nil value, so SwiftData never created them and the promote had nothing to carry. The warning this file used to give about promoting with that gap is now the live situation, so it is written down as one, along with the recovery: *adding* a field to a promoted type is allowed where deleting, renaming and retyping are not, so a non-nil value for each of the four in development, re-export, promote again.

That is the remaining blocker on #275, and it is worth knowing it is now a production blocker rather than a pre-deployment one.

## Also in the first commit

- `routeOutline`'s development index: both places that still told a reader to strip it now record that #272 did, confirmed by the export.
- Line 155 no longer says no production deployment has been recorded while the Community section describes production's shape in detail.
- `MirroredCloudKitSchemaTests` missing the four-field gap now says *why*: it compares two local descriptions and never reads a live database.

## Verification

`cktool` 1.0.23001, read-only, container `iCloud.tappium.com.OpenHikes`. The environment flag was checked rather than trusted: a bogus value is rejected, a bad container returns `authorization-failed`, and `validate-schema --environment production` still fails with `BadRequestException: endpoint not applicable in the environment 'production'` while the same file validates clean against development. Record-level queries were not run — those need a user token, not the management token. No suite or build was run for this change; CI has no markdown check.

Pinned by the new **integrations-linkedin-unipile-reconnect.test.ts** "POSTs /v2/auth/link with { providers: [\"linkedin\"] } and NO account_id on a fresh connect (no prior external_id)" test.
- [x] **Unit test pins the reconnect request body; integration test pins the callback behaviour on a changed `account_id`.** — Unit: **client.test.ts** — the reconnect body test above. Integration: **integrations-linkedin-unipile-reconnect.test.ts** covers same-id round-trip (no DELETE, no reconnect-orphan warn, external_id unchanged), different-id (warn log naming both ids + **DELETE /v2/accounts/{priorId}** best-effort + new id lands), different-id + Unipile 404 (log-and-continue, local landing still commits), different-id + Unipile 503 (log-the-error, local landing still commits). Every branch runs against the real in-process Unipile mock so the exact wire path is exercised, not a spy.

## What this PR does
Adds Unipile v2's RECONNECT form of the hosted-auth link to the LinkedIn-unipile provider. The Unipile v2 schema for **POST /v2/auth/link** is an **anyOf** between:
- **link new account** — **{ providers, expires_on, redirect_uri, state, ... }**
- **re-authenticate existing account** — **{ account_id, expires_on, redirect_uri, state, ... }** where **account_id** matches **^acc_.*$**

(Confirmed against **api.unipile.com/v2/docs/json** on 2026-09-13 via the **createAuthLink** operation — the schema uses **anyOf**, and the reconnect branch drops **providers** entirely: "Generate a link to re-authenticate or reconfigure an entire existing account.")

**Wire changes:**
- **client.ts** — **createAuthLink** now accepts a discriminated union (**CreateAuthLinkFreshRequest** | **CreateAuthLinkReconnectRequest**). The body sent to Unipile omits **providers** on reconnect and vice versa — sending both together is a 400 on the live API (schema is **anyOf**, not **oneOf**-ish-in-practice), so the client must not co-send.
- **routes/integrations-linkedin-unipile.ts `/connect`** — reads **existing[0]?.externalId**. If set (the row has been connected before, whether currently active or previously disconnected), the connect handler asks Unipile for a reconnect link with that account id. Otherwise fresh.
- **routes/integrations-linkedin-unipile.ts `/callback`** — captures **pending.externalId** BEFORE the credential-landing transaction and compares it to the returned **account_id**. On mismatch: warn-level log naming both ids AND **deleteUnipileAccountForReconnectOrphan** (best-effort DELETE of the orphaned id). Runs AFTER the local landing commits so a Unipile hiccup on the delete cannot leave the local row half-updated. On match: nothing extra happens (the row's **externalId** stays the same across the landing UPDATE).
- **disconnect.ts** — new **deleteUnipileAccountForReconnectOrphan** wrapper delegates to **deleteUnipileAccountBestEffort** (P3-B's exported helper) with **reason: 'reconnect-orphan'** and the same test-overridable client builder as the disconnect hook. Zero duplication — the log-and-continue / 404 / 5xx / network-fault semantics are exactly the disconnect ones.
- **mocks/unipile-server.ts** — the **POST /v2/auth/link** handler now inspects the body and returns 400 if both **providers** and **account_id** are present (or neither), matching Unipile v2's live 400. Same **{ object: 'HostedAuthLink', link }** envelope for both branches on success. This is the load-bearing part per **.claude/rules/live-verification.md**: a mock that answered 200 on the both-fields case would let a client regression pass a green suite while every real reconnect hit a 400.

## What this PR deliberately does NOT touch
- **Delete-on-disconnect** — that's **P3-B** (PR #1607), which this PR stacks on. The exported **deleteUnipileAccountBestEffort** helper is what makes reuse work.
- **The account.reconnect webhook path** — the webhook's job is registry sync on **account.updated**, not orphan cleanup. Orphan cleanup lives at the connect-callback layer because that's the ONE place we know we just watched an account_id change through the wizard.
- **Detecting a dead LinkedIn session** and flipping **needsReconnect** — out of scope per the task body (filed separately; the 2026-09-11 "503 no_client_session" reports weren't from this integration per P3-I).
- **Retry logic / dead-letter queue** on the orphan DELETE — best-effort means one shot, same as **P3-B**.

## Feature flag
No flag needed (non-user-visible) because the change is a backend behaviour swap: the Settings > Integrations reconnect button already existed and already fires **/connect**; this PR only changes WHICH Unipile v2 endpoint variant that call takes. No new UI, no visible state change to the user. Flag policy in this repo is visual-layer only per **.claude/rules/feature-flags.md**.

## Screenshots (UI only)
N/A — no UI in this PR.

## How to verify locally
- Type-check: **pnpm --filter @maskin/dev type-check** — clean this session.
- Lint: **pnpm lint** — Biome + billing-cap script both clean this session.
- New reconnect suite: **cd apps/dev && pnpm exec vitest run src/routes/__tests__/integrations-linkedin-unipile-reconnect.test.ts** — **6 tests pass this session** (72ms).
- Every existing LinkedIn suite still green: **cd apps/dev && pnpm exec vitest run linkedin** — **231 tests pass acro

author: xgboosted
body:
## Problems

1. **`df.ta.adjusted` had no effect.** `docs/dataframe_api.rst` documents `df.ta.adjusted = "adj_close"` as switching the default close column, and #143 made the setting persist under pandas 3 — but nothing ever read it: every indicator wrapper passed the literal `"close"` to `_get_column`, which only consults `adjusted` when given `None`. `df.ta.adjusted = "adj_close"; df.ta.sma(length=10)` averaged `close`. Identical before #143.
2. **Accessing `df.ta` mutated the caller's DataFrame.** `AnalysisIndicators.__init__` did `attrs.setdefault("_ta_last_run", …)` on every access, so `df.attrs` went from `{}` to `{'_ta_last_run': ...}` without anything running; `attrs` propagate to derived frames and pandas ≥ 2.1 writes them to Parquet metadata. `last_run` also reported the accessor's construction time as if a run had happened.
3. **Test gap.** The #143 worker-payload test only called `_worker_columns()`. Replacing `self._df[self._worker_columns(...)]` with `self._df.copy()` in `strategy()` passed every test while restoring the 1244 MB task payload.

## Fix

- New `AnalysisIndicators._default_column(name)`: `"close"` resolves to `adjusted` when set. Used for required column params and `series_a`/`series_b` defaults in `_make_ta_wrapper`, and in `df.ta.ichimoku()`. An explicit `close=` (name or Series) still wins; `high`/`low`/`open`/`volume` are untouched; `adjusted = None` restores `close`.
- `__init__` writes nothing. `last_run` returns `attrs.get("_ta_last_run")` — `None` until `df.ta(kind=...)` or `df.ta.strategy()` runs (direct method calls never recorded a run, before or after).
- `TestStrategyWorkerPayload` spies on `_worker_columns` through a real multiprocessing `strategy()` run.

## Verification

- Behaviour matrix on pandas 2.3.3 and 3.0.5: `sma`/`atr` (high/low + adjusted close)/`ichimoku` accessor/`percent_return`/`sub` (`series_a` default) all read the adjusted column; explicit `close="close"` and `close=Series` win; reset restores `close`; `strategy("Volatility")` with `adjusted` is identical serial vs multiprocessing and differs from the unadjusted run; reads leave `attrs` empty; derived frames of an untouched frame have empty `attrs`.
- Mutation checks (pandas 3): reverting each fix fails its new test (worker slice, adjusted default, attrs write).
- `pytest tests/` (both oracles): 2465 passed. pandas 3.0.5 non-oracle: 2345 passed. Every test module passes standalone. Fixture rebuild: no diff. NaN-prefix sweep: 0 regressions.
- `black --check pandas_ta_classic/`, `ruff check pandas_ta_classic --select E9,F63,F7,F82` clean.

Found by the adversarial review of the 2026-09-13 merge batch (D3, D4, T1).

author: adamstallard
body:
Two trivial, already-diagnosed bug fixes, kept out of the OpenSpec proposal machinery per the discussion in #agent-workroom (no design decision to record, no capability added).

## `consensus/receiver.py`: `update_num_sealers` stack overflow

Reported by Philip: a transient RPC error during an IDChain reorg made this retry itself with no delay and no depth bound, ~1,347 frames deep, segfaulting the interpreter (exit 139) — invisible to any Python-level `try`/`except`. With no restart policy (that's `#37`, still unmerged), the receiver stayed down 9 hours.

Reproduced safely in a subprocess (so a real crash can't take the test run down with it) — confirmed it dies by `SIGABRT`, matching the reported segfault exactly. Fix drops the recursive retry: the caller already re-invokes this every 100 blocks and at startup, so a transient failure just leaves `NUM_SEALERS` at its last known value until the next successful call.

## `updater/seed_groups.py`: PoA middleware gated on hostname

Same hostname-substring pattern `#38` already fixed on the `consensus/receiver.py` side (`if url.count('rinkeby') or url.count('idchain')`) — flagged by that PR's review as an unfixed sibling instance. A self-hosted PoA node under any other hostname silently got no PoA middleware, breaking header decoding on a Clique chain. Fix makes the injection unconditional, matching `#38`'s fix.

Both proven red→green with a regression test before the fix landed.

author: millyinvr
body:
Follow-on to #454. `ConsultThreadCopy.planSeeAll` — "See the whole plan" — has been shipping as a **dead string since P5a**. Behind it, on the web, is `/client/consult/[id]/results`. On iOS there was no destination and no screen.

## What was rendered nowhere

All of this was already **decoded on the device** and had no home:

- **What you shared** — her own answers, in her words, and deliberately *first*, before anything a model observed
- **What the photos suggest** — base and lightest level, shade, condition, density, texture, each with its **confidence range**
- **Safety and history to discuss** — always drawn, *including empty*: an empty section is a statement ("nothing specific was found, and your pro still has to check"), and hiding it would read as a clean bill of health nobody gave
- **What may be achievable** — assessment, context, direction
- **The full recommendation list with each one's reason** — the thread card shows three titles and nothing else
- **The locked Me-card teaser** — the tap records interest and unlocks nothing, and says so

## How it's built

`ConsultResultsView` walks `ConsultResultPresentation.sections` rather than hard-coding a sequence beside it — render order has been a declared contract in the flow machine since it was written, and the test asserts the list *and* that every enum case has a branch.

The thread keeps its summary. A chat message is not a report, and the web makes the same split: its thread card carries `ConsultProfileDetails` and the page repeats it in full.

`ConsultResultsCopy` mirrors `lib/brand/defaultClientConsultResultsCopy.ts` the way `ConsultBookingCopy` mirrors its twin — this screen is composed on the device, not served. A hair level renders as a **colour** ("medium brown"), never "Level 5"; that is the web's own wording out of `attributeShortNames`, and rule 2 of the voice is no jargon before its picture.

`ConsultFeatureProfile.clientEntries` now carries each entry's confidence, so this screen and the thread's disclosure read **one** list — the twelve fields aren't typed a third time.

## Two defects the render caught that no assertion did

🔴 **`ImageRenderer` draws a `ScrollView` as its background and nothing else.** The first render came back 780×5200 pixels of **exactly one colour** — and the test **passed**, because it asserted the width. The content is split out of the scroll view now, and the test counts distinct pixel values.

🔴 **Long sentences truncated instead of wrapping** — the page's own title read *"Directions to discuss with your pr…"*. In a `VStack` the children negotiate width and the longest `Text` loses. Every sentence now goes through one `para` helper carrying `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)`.

## Verified

App target **619 / 85**, TovisKit **1501 / 189** (release toolchain via `DEVELOPER_DIR`, fresh derived data). Screen rendered and inspected in light and dark.

## NOT verified

Not driven on a simulator or a phone — the push transition and the Me-card tap have not been exercised against a live server. No build-number bump.

author: jonathanjoelneptune
body:
## Purpose
Finish the Priority 1 ownership consolidation identified by the Media Audit architecture review while preserving the already-landed Priority 2 and Priority 3 behavior.

This final branch is replayed directly on the current `main` head `19446960523d74803418475161d60fb2f6dc3da9`. It preserves the adjacent-day startup ribbon and read-only playback-follow fixes unchanged.

## Priority 1 completed in this slice
- Replace the direct installer chain in `sbb/__init__.py` with explicit startup registration and inspectable startup diagnostics.
- Preserve the legacy pre-import/install phases rather than changing startup timing implicitly.
- Introduce a shared exact GET route table with legacy fallback and install it last as the top-level route authority.
- Migrate Backend Inspector to that route table as the first live service migration.
- Extend the v5 playback adapter boundary to own pause, resume, and recovery.
- Route early-pause recovery through the adapter instead of directly retuning through the public playback facade.
- Adopt Browse's existing `handlePlaybackFailure` and `onPlayerError` compatibility policies into one architecture-owned top-level failure owner. Browse's same-game alternate / next-game behavior is preserved; its delayed retry markers are retained so it cannot construct another wrapper chain.
- Add ownership regression coverage, including load-order and non-recursive activation checks.

## Priority 2 preserved
Current main already contains SQL-side audit filtering/pagination, cached audit status, hidden-tab polling reduction, serialized persistence, persisted probe evidence, and explicit deferred handling. Regression guards protect these behaviors rather than duplicating them.

## Priority 3 preserved
Current main already keeps healthy fallback/alternate media associated with the event and separates preference from validity, quarantining only hard-failed alternatives. Regression guards protect that behavior.

## Merge safety
- Parent: current `main` `19446960523d74803418475161d60fb2f6dc3da9`.
- No ticker, canonical timeline, Game Center, adjacent-day ribbon, playback-follow, release-version, or deployment files modified.
- No deployment is part of this PR.
- Shared route fallback remains in place for backend modules not yet migrated to explicit registration, allowing incremental dependency cleanup without a big-bang server rewrite.

(#57's own bug, not in the audit). One commit per issue — see
