author: sgladstein
body:
**What this does.** The lab can now draw its zoomed-out bed at up to sixteen times as many dots, so a stem that was drawn four cells wide is drawn one cell wide again. **It requests x4 — the same as the sandbox**, because consistency between the two games is a requirement.

**Where it sits.** The half that was missing. #389 gave the sandbox this; the lab had the identical 15-in-16 discard and none of the fix.

## What the owner has actually seen is x2, not x4

The lab-bar card (`20260913T170211133Z-af41c9`) came back *"I think this is fine. If there are other better looking options, we can explore them"* — the block-drawn glyphs are accepted.

**But the decode carries a fact worth stating plainly.** `blind_was: [1, 0]` puts the **x2** arm in front of him as pane A, because the card was rendered at the **1024x640 default window**, where `pixel_scale_cap` resolves a request of x4 down to x2. So: **the default asks for x4, the cap gives x2 at that window, and x4 arrives only if the window grows.** Reporting "the lab ships at x4" would be a claim about a picture nobody has looked at.

The same qualification applies to consistency, in both directions: both games **request** the same budget; what either **displays** depends on its window. That is the honest position, and the right one — but they are identical in intent, not pixel-identical.

## A refused request now says so on screen

That fact exposed a real defect: the refusal was **silent**. A budget can be refused two ways — the window is too small, or the zoom rung cannot divide it — and a player who set x4 and saw x2 had no way to know which, or that anything had been refused.

A line under the clock now names the request, what it resolved to, and which of the two refused it — verified live, reading **`PIXELS X4 -> X2 (WINDOW)`**. Drawn only when the request is *not* met, so the usual case costs one integer comparison. This is `time::PRESETS`' own principle applied to a second dial: *"the dial is a request, and a request the machine cannot meet is how the readout earns its keep."* Under the clock rather than on the bar, because row 0 measures 508 of 508 pixels at its tightest spacing.

**Its guard took two attempts, and the first is the instructive one.** It counted opaque pixels in the notice's band and compared x4 against x2 — which measured the **buffer size**, because the world is drawn behind the notice so every pixel in the band is opaque either way. It read 14,336 against 57,344 and said nothing about the notice at all. The version that works is a **paired diff at one buffer size**: both arms at scale 2, one meeting the request and one refused, asserting the notice band differs and everything else is byte-identical. Confirmed red with the notice removed.

## "Even when pixels are off screen, they are being simulated, why does making them visible affect performance?"

**The simulation half does not move at all** — those cells were always being stepped, visible or not. What grows is the **drawing**. `Renderer::draw` does its per-**output-pixel** work — colour, depth shade, per-cell grain, sky lighting — once per buffer pixel: 164k of it at 512x320, 2.6M at 2048x1280, plus a larger buffer to the GPU each frame.

**That is also why the whole-frame figure is 1.66x and not 16x**: the simulation is untouched (`frame::step` reads 13–14 ms at every budget), and **cell reads are constant by construction** (`pixels x stride²` is the same product at every budget), so the only thing that grows is per-pixel colour work — a minority of a frame that also holds the simulation, the HUD and the particles. In the lab the same work appears in a different **unit**: it competes with the tick budget, so it shows as fewer simulated seconds per real second.

## What it costs

The brief reasoned the render would be amortised away by the speed dial. **Measured, it is not.** `examples/labzoom_cost.rs` drives the real loop and reports **`achieved`** — simulated seconds per real second, render included.

**1024x640 bed** (rung 2, so x2 and x4 both spend scale 2):

| dial | x1 | x2 | x4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.0x | **1.00x** | **1.00x** |
| 16 | 5.4x | 0.47x | 0.45x |
| 256 | 4.4x | 0.57x | 0.53x |
| 1024 | 3.5x | 0.65x | 0.64x |

**2048x1280 bed**, 48 founders, 4 colonies (rung 4): x2 reads **0.73–0.78x**, x4 **0.40–0.44x**.

`TimeControl` gives each pass one wall-clock budget and the render comes out of it, so the render **competes with the dial rather than being amortised by it**: free at dial 1, costing most exactly where it was expected to cost least.

**This is expensive on a large bed at fast-forward — roughly half the achieved rate — and I have shipped the x4 request anyway**, because that is his pick and the alternative re-creates the divergence he objected to. If that trade is wrong it is his call with this number in front of him.

Why it is safe where most people will meet it:

- **The shipped 512x320 bed cannot zoom out at all**, so the budget buys nothing and costs nothing — **1.00x** at every budget and dial, measured.
- On any bed reaching only **rung 2, x4 and x2 are the same thing**.
- **Free at dial 1**, and one key to step down.

## The bug, which is #389's bug wearing different clothes

`zoom_within` derived the scale from the renderer's pushed copy while its `viewport` came from the caller's authoritative pair, so a bed reaching rung 4 at budget 1 **stopped at rung 2 at budget 2**. It did not panic — **the tell was a number that could not be true: the bigger buffer measured *faster* (1.09–1.24x)**. It was showing half as much world.

Fixed by deleting the ambiguity: the camera is about *cells*, so `follow`/`pan`/`set_camera`/`zoom_within` take the **logical** viewport and touch `pixel_scale` nowhere. `visible_span`'s contract moves with them (logical viewport, ladder stride); `draw`, the one caller holding a buffer, divides by the scale on the way in.

**That guard also had to be written twice** — the obvious `Renderer`-level one passed with the fault reinstated, so it was replaced rather than widened, per `CLAUDE.md`. The working one is at `Lab` level and pushes the budget first, because that is the order the app runs in.

## The other half, which is not in the renderer

The lab bar is **interactive**, which the sandbox HUD is not. The cursor arrives in buffer pixels and the bar is laid out in logical ones, so the conversion happens once at the window boundary (`Lab::to_logical`); hit tests, hover, `press`/`drag` and world lookups via the new `Renderer::logical_to_world` are all logical. Rack thumbnails are pinned to budget 1 for their own off-screen draw.

~175 call sites in `src/lab/ui.rs` went through a mechanical `hc: render::Hud` parameter — a big diff in a contested file, worth landing promptly.

## Follow-up, named rather than done

The one cheaper-looking option for the bar: at scale ≥ 2, draw HUD text from a **real 2x glyph set** instead of block-scaling the 5x7 one. Cost is a second font table in `hud.rs`, used only at grown buffers. Not done here — the current look was accepted, and this lane's time went to the measurement.

## Also

Beds up to **2048x1280** show whole at one cell per pixel; `MAX_BOX` is 4096, so the top of the range does not. `PIXEL_PHYSICS_LAB_BOX` / `_ZOOM_OUT` / `_PIXELS` make this checkable headlessly — all three are needed together, because the budget is only ever spent at a rung that can divide it.

## Gates

**`cargo test --release`** (not `--lib` — it cannot reach `tests/*.rs`): lib **1,714 passed / 0 failed / 85 ignored**, `tests/worldgen.rs` **44 passed / 0 failed**, `tests/determinism.rs` 3 passed, bin 10 passed. `cargo clippy --all-targets --release --locked -- -D warnings` clean. `bash scripts/docscheck.sh` clean. Verified live under xvfb on the merged tree.

**On the red trunk:** `generated_terrain_is_already_at_rest` was failing here on inheritance, naming **druid seed 2** — this branch touches no `src/sim`, no `src/worldgen` and no assets. The fix is **

author: towhead
body:
Follow-up to #1990. **Blocks the `v0.39.0` tag** — `VERSIONING.md` step 3 requires `--assert-empty` to pass on the commit being tagged.

## What fired

Running the mandatory cut-time assertion on #1990's merge commit:

```
$ scripts/assemble-changelog.sh --assert-empty HEAD
assemble-changelog: FAIL — unassembled fragment(s) still present at HEAD:
  - changelog.d/1982-review-diff-relay.fixed.md
```

## Why it happened — the cut-vs-sibling omission race

Exactly the failure `--assert-empty` exists to catch, described in `VERSIONING.md` step 3:

- #1990 assembled 55 fragments and deleted them.
- While #1990 sat in the merge queue, `07d43fda` ("make the review-diff content checksum position-sensitive") landed a **56th** fragment.
- The two commits touched **disjoint files** — #1990 rewrote `CHANGELOG.md` and deleted 55 files; the sibling added one new file. Git merged them **clean**: no conflict, no queue ejection, no gate failure.
- Result: the #1982 entry is on `main` but **absent** from the section about to be tagged. A *missing* entry, not a wrong one — which is why nothing else in the pipeline sees it.

## What this PR does

Folds the fragment's bullet into the existing `## [0.39.0] - 2026-09-13` → `### Fixed` section and removes the consumed file. The fragment merged **before** the tag, so it belongs in this release rather than being deferred to `[Unreleased]`.

**Not deleted to silence the assertion** — `VERSIONING.md` is explicit that the file *is* somebody's entry.

## Verification surface

**The assertion, before and after.** Before (on #1990's merge commit) — see the FAIL above. After, on this branch:
```
$ ls changelog.d/*.md | grep -v README | wc -l
0
```
so `--assert-empty` has nothing left to find, and the tag can proceed.

**Placement — the bullet landed inside 0.39.0, not in `[Unreleased]`.** Headings after the fold:
```
15:## [Unreleased]
17:## [0.39.0] - 2026-09-13
431:## [0.38.0] - 2026-08-27 — BREAKING
```
and the tail of 0.39.0's `### Fixed`, showing the new bullet as the last entry before the 0.38.0 heading:
```
427|  over a name only the check's author had chosen.
428|
429|- **The `/build` pre-push review's reviewer-routing table can now be corrupted in transit …
430|
431|## [0.38.0] - 2026-08-27 — BREAKING
```

**No version movement.** `VERSION` is untouched at `0.39.0`; `test_version_embedding.sh` still passes:
```
PASS: VERSION file present and well-formed: 0.39.0
PASS: temperloop version reports the embedded VERSION, not 'dev'
OK: version-embedding contract holds (temperloop#677)
```

**No BREAKING signal change** — the folded entry is a `.fixed` fragment with no `.breaking` marker, and it lands under the existing `### Fixed`, so 0.39.0 stays a clean minor and v0.38.0's own marker is untouched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01PG9BHymQjXTZu6Mmjpn5jt

Changelog: amend - VERSIONING.md step 3's sanctioned remedy for the cut-vs-sibling omission race. [0.39.0] exists on main but is NOT yet tagged, so folding the stranded #1982 fragment into it is completing the in-flight cut, not rewriting a shipped release. The alternative the gate suggests — leaving the entry under [Unreleased] — would ship v0.39.0 with a hole and defer a fix that landed before the tag to the next release.

author: playfaster
body:
## [3.3.23] - 2026-09-13 - Release: Asynchronous SMS Deletion Verification and Send Outcome Tracking

### Summary

- **Asynchronous SMS Deletion Verification**: Updated post-deletion verification to poll until router inbox state settles (up to a 15-second window), preventing completed deletions from being prematurely flagged as failures on routers with asynchronous storage processing.
- **SMS Send Outcome Tracking**: Added pre- and post-send counter comparisons (`sms_nv_send_total` vs `sms_nv_draftbox_total`), accurately reporting when a router saves an outgoing message to drafts instead of transmitting it.

### Fixed

- **Premature Deletion Failure Reporting**: Fixed false-negative deletion errors where routers acknowledge command acceptance immediately but require several seconds to purge message records from flash storage.
- **Draft SMS Misclassification**: Prevented stored/drafted outgoing SMS messages from being misreported as successfully delivered transmissions.

### Added

- **Diagnostic Deletion Timings**: Captured detailed per-attempt re-list timings and `sms_cmd_status_info` metadata in diagnostic exports to track firmware deletion latency.
- **Observational Send Counter Verification**: Logged sent and draftbox counter transitions surrounding SMS transmissions in diagnostic downloads without triggering unwanted session re-authentications.

author: davidmycodeguy
body:
Fixes #1863.

## The problem

`Rs2TileObjectModel.isReachable()` returns a hardcoded `true` whenever the object's world view id matches the player's — which is every object in the top-level world view, i.e. essentially all overworld objects. The real check runs *only* when the ids differ:

```java
if (objectWorldView.getId() == playerWorldView.getId()) {
    return true;
}
return IEntity.super.isReachable();
```

Consequences: `query().where(m -> m.isReachable())` filters nothing, and `nearestReachable()` / `firstReachable()` degrade to `nearest()` / `first()` for tile objects, since both filter with `source.filter(IEntity::isReachable)` and dispatch to this override.

## Inverting the condition is not the fix

Worth stating, because it is the obvious patch and it is wrong.

`IEntity.super.isReachable()` delegates to `Rs2Reachable.isReachable(getWorldLocation())` — *"is the object's own tile walkable?"* A solid object's own tile never is. You interact with a booth, a tree or a rock from an **adjacent** tile.

So simply routing to the default makes every bank booth, tree and rock report unreachable. I built that version and measured it: all eight bank-related objects at Edgeville reported `false`, including booths that bank perfectly well in game. That is arguably worse than the constant, because a permanent `false` silently removes objects from consideration, where a permanent `true` at least fails visibly at the click.

It also seems the likelier reason for the original short-circuit: delegating to a tile test was never going to be right for tile objects, so `return true` was bolted on rather than the delegation corrected.

## The fix

`Rs2GameObject.isReachable(GameObject)` already asks the right question — it builds the object's `WorldArea` from its `sizeX`/`sizeY`, collects the interactable tiles around it, and looks for one that is walkable and reachable. `Rs2TileObjectModel` already retains the underlying `TileObject`, so this delegates to that helper rather than reimplementing the geometry, which keeps the two paths from drifting:

```java
if (objectWorldView.getId() != playerWorldView.getId()) {
    return false;                                                 // no walking between views
}
if (tileObject instanceof GameObject) {
    return Rs2GameObject.isReachable((GameObject) tileObject);     // adjacent-tile question
}
return IEntity.super.isReachable();                               // single-tile objects
```

The `instanceof` split is load-bearing rather than defensive: `WallObject`, `GroundObject` and `DecorativeObject` carry no `sizeX`/`sizeY`, so the area helper does not apply to them, and for a single-tile object the tile test is the honest answer.

## How it was tested

Built the client from source three times — unmodified, with the naive inversion, and with this patch — and ran each logged in at the same spot (Edgeville bank), same account, same character position. For each build I recorded `isReachable()` for two populations: every bank-related object within 25 tiles, and a 2000-object sample of the loaded scene within 60 tiles, drawn in five slices so it was not only the nearest objects.

| Build | Bank booths | Scene sample (2000 objects) |
|---|---|---|
| unmodified | all `true` | 2000 `true` / **0** `false` |
| naive inversion | all **`false`** | 894 `true` / 1106 `false` |
| **this patch** | all `true` | **1050 `true` / 950 `false`** |

Only the third result satisfies both requirements at once: objects that can genuinely be used report `true`, while roughly half the scene still reports `false`. A riverside location with building interiors and far-bank objects in range should produce a large minority of unreachable objects, and the unmodified build reporting not one `false` in 2000 is what makes the current behaviour visible.

I would encourage verifying this independently rather than taking the numbers on trust — the effect is large enough to be obvious in any setup where object reachability is inspected.

## Not covered

- The cross-world-view branch (`return false`) is reasoned, not measured. I did not test inside an instanced area such as a house or a raid.
- No unit tests are included, as there appear to be none for this class to extend.
- `Rs2Reachable.isReachable` remains hardcoded to `Client.getTopLevelWorldView()`. That is why the cross-view case cannot simply be delegated, and making it world-view aware would be a larger, separate change.
- Scope appears limited to tile objects: `Rs2NpcModel`, `Rs2ActorModel`, `Rs2PlayerModel` and `Rs2TileItemModel` declare no `isReachable` override, so they inherit the default.

author: fil-donadoni
body:
Closes #3533. Parent PRD #3526.

## What changed

At `expert` the search is already handed the human seat's real decklist
(`convex/gre/deckKnowledge.ts`, `DIFFICULTY_KNOWS_OPPONENT`). The opponent
colour-demand estimate issue #3532 built could not see it, so a deck that is
40% black said nothing about what denying black costs while two Swamps did.

The decklist now **sharpens that one derivation** rather than bypassing it:

- **`deckColorEvidence`** (`deckKnowledge.ts`) lowers a decklist into the SAME
  per-colour mass the board classes already speak — **one unit per coloured
  card**, counted once per colour the card is (a gold card demands each of
  them). Deliberately the `POTENTIAL_MANA_WEIGHT` tier: a card in a deck is the
  purest form of potential, it may never be drawn. Its weight comes from its
  COUNT, which is why a deck's colour identity outweighs two lands without any
  special pleading and without a second scale.
- **`observedOpponentColors`** folds it into the existing
  `ObservedColorEvidence` map, so every consumer of that derivation —
  `colorCoverage`, `colorModePrior`, `colorModeTiebreak` — sharpens at once and
  none of them grows a decklist branch of its own.

### How it reaches the leaf — the ROOT carries it

`evaluate(state, playerId, weights)` is called at every leaf and its signature
is called by the whole engine; threading a fourth argument would have meant
~8 new signatures in `search.ts` alone, and the second feed is exactly what
"the estimate has one home" forbids. So the evidence rides on the state:
**`GameState.deckColorKnowledge`**, listed in `TRANSIENT_KEYS` (never persisted
— `compactState` drops it) and explicitly named `undefined` in BOTH projections
(never on the wire).

It is stamped **once, on the ROOT**, by `searchWithTrace` — not per
determinized world. Two reasons. It is constant for the whole search, so
re-deriving it per iteration is waste; and, decisively, the root rules and the
trace read `evaluate` / `observedOpponentColors` against the ROOT, not against
a world (`colorModeTiebreak`, `buildTrace`'s `evaluateBreakdown`). A stamp that
lived only on the worlds would have left `colorModePrior` reading informed
evidence while the tie-break its own doc-comment says it can never disagree
with read blind evidence — and the Debug panel reporting the blind
`colorCoverage` for a decision taken informed. `cloneGameState` walks keys
generically, so every world inherits it for free; `determinize` only CLEARS it
under the ladder's `blind` opponent model, so the invariant holds from both
ends.

The same stamp is applied by **`buildVerdictState`** (`ai/verdicts/position.ts`),
and that is not cosmetic: an Eval Pair is a snapshot of what `evaluate` saw
when the decision was judged. Rebuilding blind does not lose precision, it
makes the two candidates an informed entry separates **structurally
identical** — the fit's own report called both new entries BLIND pairs and
carried them as constraints no weight could ever satisfy. `Verdict` therefore
gains a `deckKnowledge` field in the blade entry's own vocabulary (card names
per seat), and `registrySource` carries it through.

### The gate — absence, and it is stricter than "a decklist exists"

`deckColorsForSearch` lowers every seat **other than the search observer**.
That exclusion is the gate, not tidiness: the client hands the bot its OWN
decklist at every difficulty (`useVsAiDriver`'s `blind` shape), so "a decklist
exists for this seat" is as true on `easy` as on `expert`. What is true only at
`expert` is that one exists for a seat the searcher is not sitting in — and
`evaluate` runs from BOTH seats' viewpoints inside one search
(`materialMargin(state, moverId)`, `policyValue(fired, pid, …)`), so a gate
that missed this would have sharpened the estimate of the BOT's own colours at
every difficulty. Tests pin exactly that, on both seats.

Still **no hand read at any difficulty** — a decklist says what the deck
contains, never what the opponent is holding.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC 1** — the estimate reads the decklist only at `expert`: gated by the
  stamp, which `determinize` writes only for a non-observer seat with a
  decklist. Four `determinize` tests pin the gate (informed / observer-only /
  none / `blind` model).
- **AC 2** — `easy`/`medium`/`hard` byte-identical on a position where
  `expert` visibly differs: the estimated seat holds one untapped Plains and a
  mono-black decklist. Blind reading `{ W: 1 }`, coverage **1**; expert reading
  `{ W: 1, B: 20 }`, coverage **1/21**. Pinned per difficulty through
  `knowsOpponent` and the client's own two knowledge shapes, on BOTH seats.
- **AC 3** — blade `must`, a discriminating twin pair (below).
- **AC 4 — a refit WAS owed, and NOT because the term's magnitude changed for
  the non-expert levels.** It did not: `colorCoverageWeight` is untouched BY
  THIS MECHANISM and the non-expert reading of the estimate is byte-identical.
  The refit is owed by the other rule — **the registry IS the verdict corpus,
  so two new `moves` blade entries are two new verdicts**
  (`weightFit.bot.test.ts` reds and names `bun run fit:weights`). Because
  `DEFAULT_EVAL_WEIGHTS` is used at EVERY difficulty, the refit does move what
  the bot plays at `easy`/`medium`/`hard`; the fit always restarts from
  `FIT_BASE_EVAL_WEIGHTS`, so nothing compounds. Movement off the base:
  `colorCoverageWeight` 24 → 29.640823 (+23.5%), `tappedManaWeight` +15.5%,
  `manaDevWeight` −11.7%, `boardRemoval` −27.4%, `disruption` −26.2%,
  `tokens` −39.3%. Loss 0.9424 → 0.9059, pairs satisfied 144 → 147, **blind
  pairs 28 → 24** (the four the new entries used to inject are gone — the
  review's first finding). Two scry pairs slipped just under the δ=100
  separation margin (Δ 101.8 → 96.2) while staying correctly ordered; the full
  `must` tier is green after the refit.
- **AC 5** — proof-of-failure for every new guarding test, below.

## Blade — `must`, a discriminating twin pair

`informed colour denial: the decklist, not the board, picks which land dies`
and `… the same board demands the OTHER land on the mirrored decklist`.

Identical board on both halves: the bot holds two Stone Rains off three
Mountains; the opponent has an untapped Plains, an untapped Swamp, and a
**colourless** Obsianus Golem as the clock. Both lands are their own only board
evidence, so destroying either one takes the demand away with the supply and
coverage stays 1 — **on the board alone the two targets are identical to the
last decimal, and a blind search picks between them by rollout noise**. The
only difference between the halves is that the twenty-card decklist is
`Scathe Zombies` ({2}{B}) or `Pearled Unicorn` ({2}{W}) — exact functional
twins, same 2/2 vanilla body, same mana value, equally uncastable off two
lands, so "it kills the land that stops a spell" is ruled out. The expectation
flips with the decklist. Five seeds each, green.

The golem is colourless on purpose (CR 105.2a): the position needs a clock —
with nothing happening, holding the card outranks every denial and the position
stops being about colour — but a coloured body would put board evidence back on
one of the two colours and reopen the discrimination the pair exists to close.

## Tests + proof-of-failure

New: `convex/gre/__tests__/deckColorKnowledge.bot.test.ts` (18), one
`serialize.test.ts` drift-guard line, the blade pair.

| Break | Red |
| --- | --- |
| `searchWithTrace` stops stamping the root | the trace test — the two land targets price identically again |
| `deckColorsForSearch` stops excluding the observer | 8 tests: the gate, the per-difficulty estimate on BOTH seats |
| `determinize` stops clearing on `opponentModel: "blind"` | the blind-clearing test |
| `registrySource` stops carrying `deckKnowledge` into the verdict | `weightFit.bot.test.ts` — the corpus is blind again and the committed vector is no longer its fit |
| `observedOpponentColors` stops folding the decklist | 3 unit tests + **b

author: delowar01
body:
**DO NOT MERGE — for review.** Live data-loss defect found while mapping the upload architecture for Batch 3. Split out as its own hotfix; contains no Batch 3 private-storage code.

Two files: one filter in `attachment-persist.ts`, plus the regression suite that proves it. No schema, no migration, no dependency, no accounting change.

## Root cause

`persistDocumentAttachments` accepted only URLs starting `/uploads/attachments/` — the **pre-Blob, local-filesystem shape**. Since storage moved to Vercel Blob, `storeBlob()` has returned:

```
/uploads/organizations/{orgId}/attachments/{orgId}-{ts}-{16 hex}.{ext}
```

The filter matched nothing, `rows` came out empty, the insert was skipped by the `if (rows.length)` guard, and the action returned success. **Every attachment staged on a creation page was discarded in silence** — no row, no error, no log — on create *and* update, across all ten call sites (quotation, sales invoice, sales order, proforma, purchase order). It is the only insert into `document_attachments` in the application.

## Failing-before evidence

Reproduced through the real action path — `createInvoiceAction`/`updateInvoiceAction` driven over the wire with a genuine owner session, asserted against the real table. Against unfixed `main` (`45c914e`):

```
PASS  control: an invoice saved with no attachments has 0 attachment rows
FAIL  an invoice created with 1 attachment persists 1 attachment row  -> got 0
FAIL  the persisted row keeps the file name the client sent           -> undefined
FAIL  an invoice created with 3 attachments persists all 3            -> got 0
2/7 checks   (exit 1)
```

The control passes, so the assertions were satisfiable — it was the attachments that vanished. Only the Blob upload itself is synthesised (it needs a live store); the fixture supplies the exact string `storeBlob()` returns, which is what the client holds in form state and posts back.

## Fix

Build the accepted prefix from the **caller's `orgId`** instead of a constant, and check the filename against the same server-generated pattern the upload route enforces. Smaller than it looks, but a strictly stronger guarantee: the old constant prefix could not bind a row to a tenant at all, so it never checked that a posted path belonged to the acting org.

## Regression results — 14/14

| Assertion | Result |
|---|---|
| 0 attachments → save → 0 (control) | ✅ |
| 1 attachment → persists 1 row | ✅ |
| row keeps file name / path / content-type / size | ✅ |
| 3 attachments → all 3 persist | ✅ |
| existing attachment survives an unrelated edit | ✅ |
| existing + new on edit → both preserved (1 → 2) | ✅ |
| two further saves add nothing (no duplication) | ✅ |
| path under **another org's** folder refused | ✅ |
| hand-written filename under the right prefix refused | ✅ |
| every persisted row carries the acting organization | ✅ |

## Mutation proof

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| restore the original `/uploads/attachments/` prefix | **5/14** — the whole persistence set fails |
| remove the tenant binding + filename check | **12/14** — and exactly the two security assertions fail (foreign-org path accepted, 1 row; forged filenames accepted, 2 rows) |

Both reverted; `git diff` is the fix alone.

## One acceptance criterion not met, and why

`remove an attachment that was saved earlier` — **not possible, and this PR does not add it.** Nothing in the application `SELECT`s from `document_attachments`: there is no read path, the form's attachment state always starts empty (`invoice-form.tsx:146`), and no page displays saved attachments. That is a missing feature, not this regression, and building it would be the upload-subsystem redesign this hotfix is scoped out of. Reported rather than quietly skipped.

## Production impact — read-only, nothing repaired

**Blob objects still exist.** `storeBlob` completes its `put()` before returning and nothing deletes them, so every dropped attachment left an orphaned object under `organizations/{orgId}/attachments/`.

**The references are not deterministically recoverable.** `uploadDocumentAttachmentAction` writes no DB row and logs no activity or audit entry; `file_access_logs` records reads, not uploads; and the document association existed only in browser state. An orphan's name yields its org and its upload instant, never the document it was meant for. Timestamp correlation against document `created_at`/`updated_at` could produce *candidates* for a human to confirm — that is not deterministic reconstruction, so no recovery script is included.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | 0 errors |
| `eslint src --max-warnings=0` | clean |
| crypto-policy | 18/18 |
| access-control | 17/17 |
| `verify:static` | 9 suites / 414 |
| `verify:server` | 24 suites / 966 |
| `verify:browser` | **40/40 suites / 1,032** |
| `db:push` (disposable PG16) | exit 0 |
| `build` | exit 0 |
| `npm audit --audit-level=high` | exit 0 |

**New browser baseline: 40 suites / 1,032 checks** (was 39 / 1,018) — the new suite contributes 14. The runner discovers suites by directory scan, so no registration was needed. Disposable local PostgreSQL only; nothing pointed at production.

author: johnnyt
body:
Resolves `sb-6ykd` (campaign SF044, the ruled fill for RQ-SF041-5).

## What changed

ADR-0005's three-way chain - the type's own line, else the author's title,
else the type's label falling back to the type name - was written twice.
`ViewModel`'s private `sentence/5` drew all three rungs;
`Compiler.writer_sentence/2` asked `BlockType.sentence/2` and stopped at the
type's label. RQ-SF041-5 rules that the writer half reads the view model's
chain.

`StatifierBlocks.SentenceChain` (new, `@moduledoc false`, internal) is that
chain written once. The chain and the title-override reader move into it
verbatim from `view_model.ex`; `ViewModel` and `Compiler` both call it. The
compiler cannot call `ViewModel.sentence/1` itself - it holds no view model,
and building one to name a single block would be a second answer to a
question the chain already answers.

No new public surface: the new module is internal, and no public function
was added, removed, or widened.

## Finding: the bead's premise does not hold at this SHA

The bead says a composite declaring no `sentence/1` and carrying a `label`
string param is named by its type's label in a `:type_mismatch` sentence and
by the author's title on its card. Verified against the code at `229a560`,
the first half is right and the second is not, for a reason that makes the
divergence unreachable from the writer half:

- `writer_sentences/3` names the block `anchor/2` resolves a minted member
  to, which is always a block whose type is a COMPOSITE.
- `StatifierBlocks.Composite`'s `use` macro always generates `sentence/1`
  (`composite.ex`, the `@impl StatifierBlocks.BlockType def sentence(config)`
  clause), and `Composite.render_sentence/2`'s first clause answers the
  palette label for a declaration that composed no template.
- So `Palette.declares?(ref, :sentence, 1)` is true for every composite, the
  chain takes its FIRST rung every time, and the author's-title rung is
  reached on neither surface. `ViewModel.sentence/1` answers the type's line
  for such a block too - which the new test asserts directly.

What the card draws as its author title is `ViewModel.title/1`, the card's
FIRST line, and ADR-0005 says in as many words that `sentence` is "a fourth
thing a node carries, not a re-spelling of the third". That distinction
survives this PR by design and is now pinned by a test.

Two consequences, both reported to the conductor rather than decided here:

1. **Behaviour is unchanged.** This PR removes the second copy of the rule,
   not a live divergence.
2. **No changelog fragment.** `changelog.d/README.md` says not to write one
   for "internal refactors with no visible effect", and the invariant block's
   own clause says a brief never asks for a fragment the repo forbids. The
   brief asked for `changelog.d/sb-6ykd.md` under Fixed; the repo rule wins
   and none is written.

## Tests

`test/statifier_blocks/compiler/minted_writer_sentence_test.exs` gains a
`TitledSection` composite (no `sentence:` template, a `label` string param)
and two cases:

- *names the composite exactly as its card's line does* - the writer finding
  and `ViewModel.sentence/1` answer one string. Sabotage: have
  `writer_sentence/2` answer the bare `type` instead of calling the chain -
  RED (`"myapp.titled_section"` in the message).
- *the author's title names the card's first line and not either sentence* -
  `ViewModel.title/1` is the author's title while neither sentence is.

The title rung itself stays covered where it is reachable:
`test/statifier_blocks/view_model/sentence_test.exs:206` ("is the author's
title where the type declares no sentence"). Sabotage: drop the `title ||`
from `SentenceChain.sentence/5`'s non-declaring arm - RED there, which is
the evidence the chain moved intact.

Both sabotages were run from a `cp` copy of the file and reverted from that
copy.

## Provenance

- Files touched: `lib/statifier_blocks/compiler.ex`,
  `lib/statifier_blocks/view_model.ex`,
  `lib/statifier_blocks/sentence_chain.ex` (new),
  `test/statifier_blocks/compiler/minted_writer_sentence_test.exs`.
- `lib/statifier_blocks/sentence_chain.ex` is outside the brief's file map
  ("the lib file named + its test file"): the bead's own acceptance asks for
  the chain to be written once where both callers can reach it, and neither
  existing module is reachable from the other. Reported as
  `[brief-corrected]`.
- Rebased onto `origin/main` at `229a560` ("Withholds refused card controls
  when read-only", the sibling sb-7n1h PR). No conflict; disjoint files.
- No LiveView test file was touched: the fill is not rendered anywhere new,
  and the file this PR extends is a pure test.

## Gate

`mix quality` green on the rebased HEAD:

    ✓ Format ✓ Compile ✓ Dependencies ✓ ADR cites (unmoved, 57 advisory)
    ✓ Credo ✓ Dialyzer ✓ Tests: 3,249 of 3,249 passed, 94.9% coverage
    ✓ All quality checks passed!

gate=green (`mix quality`, full profile, on this exact tree).

## Firewall

author: cadenlast
body:
The weekly pool email usually lands early Sunday afternoon, but the scan only ran on a fixed slow interval (default 4 hours) regardless of day - could easily miss the actual send time by hours. Replaced the plain setInterval with a self-rescheduling timer: once past 11:30am Sunday with no email received yet that week, it checks every minute; otherwise it falls back to the normal interval, capped so it never sleeps past the upcoming Sunday cutoff (landing exactly on it rather than drifting past). Reverts to the normal cadence as soon as that week's email is actually found.

Verified the delay computation across the key transitions: mid-week normal cadence, landing exactly at the Sunday cutoff from earlier that morning, switching to 1-minute polling once past it unreceived, and reverting to normal the moment it's received.

author: robobun
body:
### Problem - `comment.text = s` rejects `-->` only. The HTML tokenizer also ends a comment at `--!>`, and ends an empty comment at `` and ``. So `--!>` anywhere in `s`, or a leading `>` or `->`, is accepted, and the rest of `s` becomes markup: `"x--!>"` gives `

-->

`. - The cause is lol-html `Comment::set_text` (`vendor/lolhtml/src/rewritable_units/tokens/comment.rs:70`). It checks only `text.contains("-->")`, with the error ``Comment text shouldn't contain comment closing sequence (`-->`).`` Upstream fixed it in cloudflare/lol-html@ba25359 (v3.0.0, a security fix). Bun's fork is on v2.7.2. ### Fix - Pin `oven-sh/lol-html` at `ef9f6fd` (oven-sh/lol-html#6), a cherry-pick of that commit onto the `bun` branch. The setter now also throws for `--!>`, a leading `>` and a leading `->`: `Comment text shouldn't contain a comment-closing sequence.` - Correct because these four are the only ways the tokenizer leaves a comment before the serializer's own `-->`. Near misses (`--!`, `x--`, `a->b`) stay accepted and read back unchanged. - The pin also picks up `ea6125b` (#41479): the fork branch is linear. - Verified: `test/js/workerd/html-rewriter.test.js` (8 of 19 new cases fail on bun 1.4.3). Also the other `html-rewriter*` suites and `bundler_html`. ### Background - `HTMLRewriter` is a binding over lol-html, built from the `oven-sh/lol-html` fork (`bun` branch: v2.7.2 plus handler suspension). `scripts/build/deps/lolhtml.ts` pins the commit. - lol-html serializes a modified comment as ``. A comment has no escape syntax, so the setter can only reject text that would end it. - `comment.before()`, `after()` and `replace()` escape text, so they are not affected.
Notes Repro on bun 1.4.3-canary.1 (b99371011). Main at 09bb5463 pins the same lol-html commit. ```js const set = s => new HTMLRewriter().on("p", { comments(c) { c.text = s; } }).transform("

"); set("x-->"); // throws set("x--!>"); //

-->

set(">"); //

-->

set("->"); //

-->

``` With this PR all four throw. Why four forms: after `` cases in the new test fail on 1.4.3 only because upstream reworded the error. The other six fail because the setter does not throw. lol-html checks on the fork commit: `cargo test --features=integration_test` 172 + 3 + 32 + 2 pass. The cherry-pick had two mechanical conflicts: `set_text` keeps the v2.7.2 `BytesCow::from_str_without_replacements(..)` plus `into_owned()`, and the `CHANGELOG.md` hunk is dropped because the branch has no v3.0.0 section. This pin conflicts textually with #41479 and #41968 (same line in `lolhtml.ts`). Whichever lands first, the others move their pin to the head of the fork's `bun` branch.
--- **no test proof** · iteration 0 · platform-specific test(s) that do not run on this machine, deferring to CI, which covers all platforms: test/js/workerd/html-rewriter.test.js

author: villebro
body:
## Summary

A component Service with `service.type: NodePort` or `LoadBalancer` that does not pin `service.nodePort` gets a node port auto-allocated by the apiserver on create. The component reconciler rebuilds the desired Service spec from scratch each reconcile (with `nodePort: 0`) and did not preserve the allocated value, so the apiserver re-allocated a **different** node port on every reconcile. The externally reachable node port (and the LoadBalancer target) therefore changed continuously, causing Service update churn and intermittently broken external access.

This affects a supported, common configuration and is silent — there is no error, the port just keeps moving.

## Details

`preserveServiceAllocatedFields` already carries apiserver-allocated fields (`clusterIP`, `clusterIPs`, `ipFamilies`, `healthCheckNodePort`) from the existing Service into the rebuilt desired spec. This extends it to also preserve per-port `nodePort` for `NodePort`/`LoadBalancer` Services when the user has not pinned one (matching the existing port by name + protocol — the operator names its single port `http`). A user-pinned `nodePort` still wins, and `ClusterIP` Services are deliberately left untouched so a node port is never set on a type that rejects it.

### Tests

Extended `TestPreserveServiceAllocatedFields` with cases for: preserving an auto-allocated node port when unpinned, keeping a user-pinned node port over the existing one, and not carrying a node port onto a `ClusterIP` Service.

author: amir-arad
body:
## Summary

- **Replaced operation queue model with per-protocol priority slots**: Instead of a serial queue of `RepairOperation` objects with statuses (QUEUED/ACTIVE/DONE/CANCELLED), the repair system now uses fixed `RepairProtocolSlot` objects (one per catalog protocol) with priority levels (OFF/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/RUNNING/CANCELLING). This eliminates queue-length caps, reordering logic, and terminal-state display timers.

- **Simplified scheduling**: At most one slot is ever RUNNING at a time; when neither RUNNING nor CANCELLING exists, the highest-priority pending slot is promoted (ties broken by catalog order). No pre-emption: raising a pending protocol to HIGH never interrupts what's already running.

- **Unified command interface**: Replaced three separate commands (`enqueueRepair`, `cancelRepair`, `reorderRepair`) with a single `cycleRepairPriority` command that raises or lowers a protocol's priority. Pressing the hotkey on a RUNNING protocol initiates a wind-down (CANCELLING state) rather than instant cancellation.

- **Energy cell refund logic**: Added `refundEnergyCell` parameter to `revertRepairSlot` (renamed from `revertOperationSideEffects`) so normal completion keeps the cell spent, while self-abort or wind-down refunds it.

## Tests

- Updated `repair-manager.spec.ts`: Rewrote 10+ tests to use the new priority model (raise/lower helpers, slot queries, RUNNING/CANCELLING states).
- Updated `repair-queue-sync.spec.ts`: Verified that fixed-size slot array survives Colyseus encode/decode.
- Updated `armor-plate-renewal.spec.ts`, `reactor-jump-start.spec.ts`, `radar-traverse-servo-alignment.spec.ts`, `tube-repair-protocol.spec.ts`: Migrated test helpers to use `cycleRepairPriority` and slot queries.
- Updated `engineer-screen.spec.ts`: Verified hotkey display (raise/lower keys shown, no click buttons on Engineer screen) and priority state transitions.
- Updated `energy-starvation-visibility.spec.ts`: Adapted to new slot-based queries.
- All existing unit and e2e tests pass.

author: x-nihil0
body:
Five changes, all Python-side. Nothing here touches the worker, the protocol on the wire, or how the picture looks by default.

Measured on an RTX 5080 / 4K desktop / the bundled runtime — a different card from the 5070 Ti your numbers come from, though the figures below are CPU- and memory-bound, so the card isn't what they're measuring.

## 1. `read_out()` copies into a reused ring — ~10.8 ms per recorded frame

`SharedFrameBuffer.read_out()` called `.copy()`, so every recorded frame mapped a **fresh 33 MB array** and paid ~8000 first-touch page faults on it. At 4K with four frames held alive (the encoder's queue depth):

|  | per frame | throughput |
|---|---|---|
| `.copy()` (before) | 13.2 ms | 2.5 GB/s |
| reused ring (after) | 2.4 ms | 13.7 GB/s |

The memcpy was never the cost. And this runs on the reader thread *inside* the recv the main loop is blocked on, so it was frame time rather than background work.

I think this is also where the leftover in TECHNICAL.md went. The recording section explains the `OUTS` channel as removing "~7 ms of pushing 33 MB down the pipe", but the "after both fixes" column still shows `recv 17.5 → 24.5 ms`. `OUTS` removed the *transport* and left the *allocation*.

The ring is **scanned rather than simply advanced**, and that's the part worth reviewing: a returned frame travels by reference into the encoder queue and lives until the encoder has written it, so a slot is only handed out when its refcount shows nobody else holds it. With every slot in flight the answer is a fresh array — slower for that frame, always correct. Slots are created on demand, so a session that never records allocates none of it.

## 2. The feature-18 verdict dies with the worker that gave it

`st.gpu_ok` is latched (that's what keeps `refresh_gpu_ok` off the per-frame path), but only `rebuild_pipeline` cleared it. The four restart paths — a lost worker, a silent worker, the auto-revive, and `do_restart`'s fallback — inherited the dead worker's answer.

So a card that started working kept the red dot, and, worse, **a pipeline that came back broken kept the green one** — while TECHNICAL.md tells the user that dot is the thing to trust ("it goes green only when the worker actually created feature 18").

`forget_verdict()` is deliberately **not** called for a live RNSZ resize: `resize_window_live` keeps the same process, so its verdict still stands. `test_verdict_forget.py` asserts both halves of that.

## 3. Bypass no longer computes a motion field nobody reads

In NR OFF the worker skips the NGX evaluate, so nothing ever reads the field — but DIS ran anyway: **2.9 ms per frame**, on the mode that runs fastest (121–133 FPS), about half a core spent filling a buffer that gets thrown away.

`previous_gray` is cleared with it, so the first frame after NR comes back reports a scene cut instead of correlating against a screen that may be minutes old.

## 4. The flow preset is a setting — `flow_preset`

**Default unchanged.** `dis.calc` on the same 320×180 pair, with endpoint error against synthetic ground truth (a known pixel shift, in flow-grid px):

```
                     ms      EPE mean over 1..16 px    p99 @1px   max @32px
FAST / finest 1    2.85          0.001 - 0.029           0.10       8.5
ULTRAFAST / 1      0.34          0.0003 - 0.076          0.49      31.6
```

`ultrafast` is **8.4×** faster, and its mean error stays under 0.08 flow px — inside the 0.5 px noise floor `guides.py` already zeroes, so on average it cannot even reach the motion field.

Its **tails** are why I did not make it the default: p99 0.49 px at a 1 px shift, and a 31.6 px maximum at a 32 px shift against 8.5 px for `fast`. Tails are what a temporal network shows as smearing, and I can't judge that without the GPU pipeline and real moving content in front of a person. So it ships as a switch with its numbers attached, the way `nr_small` did before it became the default — and the before/after wipe is how to judge it. You have the hardware and the eye for this in a way a synthetic benchmark doesn't.

## 5. Two smaller ones

- **The fallback resize stops using Lanczos.** `INTER_LANCZOS4` measured **11.76 ms** for 2560×1440 → 4K against 1.53 ms (`INTER_AREA`) and 1.64 ms (`INTER_LINEAR`). It only runs when dxcam is grabbing and its frame disagrees with the configured size — i.e. on the slowest hardware in the fleet, the path that exists *because* the fast one was unavailable. AREA when shrinking, LINEAR when growing.
- **Recording waits one frame for queue room, not a quarter second.** `write()` runs on the main loop, so `PUT_TIMEOUT_S = 0.25` made a full encoder queue a quarter-second freeze of the picture — ~14 frames at 55 FPS — which is the opposite of the policy stated two lines above it ("the user looks at the screen, not at the file"). The clock-based pts keeps the file's duration correct either way.

## Verification

27/27 green on the tests covering the changed code, including **`test_out_shm.py` and `test_bypass.py`, which drive the real worker on the GPU** — so the changed read-back path is validated byte-for-byte, not just unit-tested:

```
test_out_shm, test_pixels_after_resize, test_out_status, test_bypass,
test_gpu_alert_path, test_verdict_classifier, test_gpu_mark, test_gpu_rollback,
test_hard_failure_window, test_revive_race, test_revive_warmup, test_live_resize,
test_rebuild_warmup, test_recorder_thread, test_recorder_fallback, test_recorder_audio,
test_mv_validation, test_motion_small, test_nr_small, test_skip_static,
test_state_contract, test_module_layers, test_config, test_silent_spots,
test_stdout_noise, test_out_ring, test_verdict_forget
```

New: `test_out_ring.py` (the ring is reused, bounded, and never overwrites a frame still in use) and `test_verdict_forget.py`. `test_live_resize.py`'s guides stub was widened by one `**kw` — it stood in for the generator, it wasn't pinning its signature.

`autocheck.py`'s git-clean check passes. Its other two failures here are environmental: no release zip in a clone (gitignored) and the release-tag lookup.

I did not run the full suite or the GUI/smoke stages — those take over the screen for a long time each, and I'd rather you ran them on your own machine than have me report a number I got on someone else's display.

## Not done, on purpose

- **The 2.0 s sleep in `restart_worker`.** It's documented as required because "initialising a new process concurrently on the same GPU hangs or kills it" — but `teardown_pipeline` → `rebuild_pipeline` starts a new worker with **no sleep at all**, and `shutdown_worker` has already waited for the old process to exit. Both can't be right. Either the sleep is two seconds of frozen picture on every settings-fallback restart and every auto-revive, or the rebuild path is racy. Deciding needs a GPU-init race I couldn't reproduce on demand, so I left it alone — but it seemed worth flagging.
- **The worker-side wins**, which have the higher ceiling and need MSVC (not installed here): hardware optical flow on the NVOFA engine would delete items 3 and 4 outright *and* the `GRAY` channel; returning NV12 instead of RGBA would halve the `OUTS` payload (33 → 12.4 MB) and delete the RGBA→yuv420p conversion in `recorder.py`; a multi-slot `OUTS` section would delete item 1's copy entirely rather than optimise it.
- **`TECHNICAL.ru.md`.** The English one is updated (the `flow_preset` row, the recording-cost correction, and a "What the guides cost" section). I left the Russian to you rather than machine-translating into your own documentation.

One documentation note in passing: TECHNICAL.md says `grab` and `guides` "drop to 0.1 ms" in DDA mode. That holds on a **static** screen — `process()` sees a scene score under 0.001 and returns a cached zero field without calling DIS (I measured 0.03 ms). On moving content the DIS call runs and the stage is 3.9 ms. I've noted that inline rather than replacing the original claim, since keeping the correction next to it seems to be the conventi

author: mrdannyclark82
body:
The Daily Empire report was printing `News scraping temporarily unavailable` because `gatherNews()` scraped Google News HTML (`article, .xrnccd`). That page is JS-rendered and blocked from GitHub-hosted runners, so cheerio always came back empty or threw.

## What changed
`daily-analysis.cjs` now pulls headlines from sources Actions can actually read:
- Google News **RSS** (not the HTML search page)
- Hacker News Algolia JSON
- TechCrunch AI RSS
- The Verge AI RSS

Each source fails independently. Results are deduped, scored, and written with source + link + published date. The unavailable placeholder only appears if every source dies.

## How to verify
1. Merge this PR (or run the workflow from this branch).
2. Actions → **Daily Empire Report** → Run workflow.
3. Check the job log for `Google News RSS` / `Hacker News` item counts instead of the scrape warning.
4. Open the `report.md` artifact — News Intelligence should list real headlines.

No new secrets or dependencies. Same axios + cheerio already installed in the workflow.

## Summary by Sourcery

Make Daily Empire news gathering reliable in GitHub Actions by using accessible feeds and resilient multi-source processing.

Missing terrain stays optional, and invalid or unreadable terrain reports a diagnostic without making the map unusable. The native sidecar resolver and leaked source bytes are removed. Peak View keeps its independent worker and cache.

TerrainTables reuses the existing parser and sampling implementation. Existing device reader layout, format, sampling rules and callsites are unchanged. Public architecture and simulator instructions are updated in a separate `docs:` commit; no protected prose changed.

author: xhelliom
body:
La PR décrivait son premier commit — l'ETL Ciqual. Elle en porte 26. Titre et
description remis à jour pour qu'on sache ce qu'on relit.

## Ce qu'il y a dedans

**V1 et V2** — les trois algorithmes du §11, le share target Jow, les
templates et « Restes de… », l'accueil à 5 barres, la saisonnalité, l'historique
et la vue semaine. Toutes les cases du §15 passent sauf la saisie de
`seasonal_produce`, qui est une collecte humaine.

**Les repères nutritionnels.** Des quatre macros de la V1, seules les fibres
sont publiées en grammes par l'ANSES. Les trois autres sont des intervalles en
% de l'apport énergétique : elles sont **dérivées** de trois termes sourcés,
marquées `derived = true`, avec la chaîne de calcul complète dans leur
`source`. Aucune valeur n'a été inventée — les 0-3 ans n'ont donc aucun repère,
et les barres affichent « indisponible ».

**Comptes individuels et foyers multiples** (§7 renversé, §16 tranché).
L'erreur de fond n'était pas dans l'auth mais dans le mot « membre » : une
seule table portait à la fois le coefficient de portion et l'identité de celui
qui saisit. Les enfants sont des convives sans compte, une nounou serait un
compte sans convive. D'où `member` → `eater`, et better-auth pour l'identité
seule.

**L'étanchéité entre foyers** descend dans la base : Row-Level Security en
`force`, plus un garde-fou qui **empêche le serveur de démarrer** si elle n'est
pas effective. Ce n'est pas de la prudence décorative — 178 tests sont passés
au vert avec une RLS entièrement contournée, parce que le rôle Postgres était
superutilisateur et qu'un superutilisateur les ignore en silence.

**La mise en service** : image publiée sur ghcr.io par GitHub Actions après les
tests, manifestes Kubernetes, et `docs/deploiement-kubernetes.md`.

## Ce qui est vérifié, et ce qui ne l'est pas

197 tests, typecheck vert, front qui compile. L'image a été construite et
lancée pour de vrai : elle sert, elle migre, elle s'arrête proprement sur
`SIGTERM`, et son garde-fou fonctionne.

Trois choses n'ont pas pu l'être, et sont consignées dans
`docs/dette-technique.md` :

- **la PWA n'a jamais tourné sur un vrai Android** — c'est le chemin critique
  du produit, et `docs/mise-en-service.md` en donne la séquence ;
- **les manifestes Kubernetes n'ont jamais été appliqués** dans un cluster ;
- **pas de SMTP**, donc ni vérification d'adresse ni réinitialisation de mot de
  passe. La plus gênante des trois.

## Trois tables livrées vides, volontairement

`unit_default` et `seasonal_produce` attendent des collectes humaines (§17),
chaque ligne exigeant une source ou une pesée. `nutrient_reference` est
remplie, mais partiellement : rien pour les 0-3 ans.

Une valeur manquante est écrite `NULL`, jamais `0`, et l'UI dit
« indisponible » plutôt que d'afficher un zéro qui serait faux (I1).

body:
## Scope
Switch GET-Passes 2.0 production launcher and Windows package to PySide6 while retaining `GET-Passes-Legacy.exe` as a temporary Tkinter rollback until workstation/printer acceptance is complete.

## Implemented
- `pass_generator.py` is the PySide6 production launcher; normal runs keep single-instance and crash-log behavior.
- `legacy_pass_generator.py` preserves the previous Tkinter launcher.
- project/installer version is `2.0.0`.
- Windows packages contain `GET-Passes.exe` and `GET-Passes-Legacy.exe`; Inno Setup installs and smoke-tests both.
- selected internal signing route is **TM5 Private PKI**:
  - `TM5 Root CA` is the private trust anchor;
  - leaf code-signing certificate has subject `CN=TM5, O=TM5` and Code Signing EKU;
  - public root is committed as `certs/TM5-Root-CA.cer`;
  - root SHA-256 fingerprint is `86742AE7A08246595855655EB5961417BE75A553521947CD8A26933C0B55C95C`;
  - `tools/install_tm5_root.ps1` validates the fingerprint before adding trust to `Cert:\LocalMachine\Root`;
  - `tools/create_tm5_private_pki.ps1` provides controlled PKI regeneration;
  - build/release workflows use `TM5_SIGN_CERT_BASE64` + `TM5_SIGN_CERT_PASSWORD` and sign production EXE, rollback EXE and installer.
- private root key is never committed, shipped in installer, or uploaded to CI.
- `.gitignore` blocks `*.pfx`, `*.p12` and private-key files to reduce accidental key disclosure.
- Azure Artifact Signing `TM5-CodeSign`, Azure Key Vault and generic PFX remain optional fallbacks; Azure Public Trust is no longer a blocker for the internal release.
- `docs/SIGNING.md` and `docs/PHYSICAL_ACCEPTANCE_2_0.md` document trust deployment and physical acceptance.

## Trust model
TM5 Private PKI is trusted only on managed Windows machines where `TM5 Root CA` is installed, preferably via GPO/Intune. It is **not** globally trusted on arbitrary internet-connected Windows PCs. GET-Passes Setup intentionally does not install the root automatically.

## Final verification — head `cde6770d6d30e009fd9994df68a2cfe986247424`
- Python 3.13: 496 tests, strict flake8/C901, pip-audit and Bandit GREEN.
- Python 3.14: 496 tests, strict flake8/C901, pip-audit and Bandit GREEN.
- gitleaks GREEN.
- CodeQL GREEN.
- Windows PR smoke GREEN:
  - full Windows tests;
  - PySide6 production source self-test;
  - Tkinter rollback source self-test;
  - production EXE build + packaged self-test;
  - rollback EXE build + packaged self-test;
  - Inno Setup build;
  - install + self-test of both installed EXEs + uninstall.
- TDD hardening RED was observed separately: 495 tests passed and only the new private-key-ignore contract failed until `.gitignore` was fixed.

## Diff audit
PR changed filenames contain only public root certificate/configuration, production/rollback launchers, Qt runtime identity, packaging/workflows, version/installer contracts, signing/bootstrap docs/scripts and tests. No `.pfx`, `.p12`, `.key` or root private key is committed. There are no changes to `getpass_core`, SQLite schema/migrations/storage, renderer, blanks, fonts or assets.

## Remaining external gates before merge/tag
1. Configure repository secrets `TM5_SIGN_CERT_BASE64` and `TM5_SIGN_CERT_PASSWORD` from the generated signing PFX. The connected GitHub interface used here does not expose repository-secret writes, so this remains an account-level action.
2. Deploy only `TM5-Root-CA.cer` to target workstations via GPO/Intune or `tools/install_tm5_root.ps1`, then confirm `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` is `Valid` and signer subject contains `CN=TM5`.
3. Complete `docs/PHYSICAL_ACCEPTANCE_2_0.md` on the target workstation/printer.

No stable `v2.0.0` tag/release is created before those gates are complete. PR remains draft intentionally until physical acceptance.

author: octaviowebdev
body:
## Summary

`server/food.ts` previously proxied USDA FoodData Central live on every search with almost no sanitization: nutrients silently defaulted to `0` if missing from a result, and the serving unit wasn't even captured (liquids were mislabeled as grams). This is the "lighter incremental caching" approach discussed as a first step toward "your own verified nutrition database" (the message already shown on the nutrition page).

## What changed

- New `food_cache` table, searched first on every food search — fast, and still works if USDA's API is down or rate-limited.
- Live USDA results are now **sanitized** before being shown or cached: entries with no usable macro data, negative values, or implausible calorie counts (e.g. an obvious misplaced decimal) are rejected outright.
- Every valid live result gets upserted into the cache, with a `searchHits` counter so frequently-searched foods rank higher in local results over time — the database gets more complete and reliable the more it's used, with no big upfront bulk-import project needed.
- Fixed the nutrition page's food search UI to show the real serving unit (e.g. "355ml") instead of always assuming grams.

## Migration note

Added `scripts/migrate-add-food-cache.ts` rather than using `drizzle-kit push`. Production's `users` table predates using drizzle-kit at all (inline `UNIQUE` on `username` produces an unnamed `sqlite_autoindex` instead of the named index drizzle-kit expects), and `db:push` re-diffs the *entire* schema on every run — so even adding one new, unrelated table trips over that old drift and fails outright. Confirmed this by reproducing it against a sandboxed replica of production's exact schema before writing the migration script.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` passes
- [x] Reproduced production's exact schema (including the `users` table drift) in a sandbox and confirmed `drizzle-kit push` fails on it even for this unrelated change
- [x] Confirmed the new migration script applies cleanly and is idempotent
- [x] Exercised `upsertCachedFood`/`searchCachedFoods` against the sandbox — create, re-upsert increments `searchHits`, search ordering by popularity all work
- [x] Unit-tested the sanitization logic against edge cases (missing description, no nutrients, all-zero macros, negative values, implausible calories, a liquid item with a non-gram unit) — all filtered/handled correctly
- [ ] Run `npm run db:migrate:food-cache` on production

author: connor-grady
body:
`pyproject.toml` sets `fix = true` under `[tool.ruff]`, and the only ruff invocation this repository makes already passes `--fix` on its own command line. The setting therefore changes nothing on any path that enforces anything, and its one live effect is on a bare `ruff check` typed at a prompt, where it rewrites source files during what the runner believes is a measurement.

**Where ruff actually runs here.** `prek.toml` declares the `ruff-check` hook from `astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit` at `rev = "v0.16.1"` with `args = ["--fix"]`. That is the whole surface: `grep -rn 'ruff' .github/workflows/ scripts/ package.json` returns nothing, so no workflow, no script and no npm script invokes ruff directly. CI reaches it through `j178/prek-action@v2` in `linters.yml`, and `scripts/lint.sh` runs the same hooks locally, so the CI path and the local path are the same invocation carrying the same explicit flag. `scripts/lint.sh` already documents the consequence in its header comment: "Hooks that support automatic fixes may modify files."

**Ruff's own default, and its own note on precedence:**

```text
$ uvx ruff@0.16.1 config fix
Enable fix behavior by-default when running `ruff` (overridden
by the `--fix` and `--no-fix` command-line flags).
Only includes automatic fixes unless `--unsafe-fixes` is provided.

Default value: false
Type: bool
```

So this is not a setting that restates a default. It is a genuine difference from ruff's default that is unreachable on every path that gates anything, because the command line overrides it precisely where it is used.

**What the deletion moves, measured rather than asserted.** `ruff check --show-settings backend/` at `v0.16.1` is 1565 lines before and after, differing on exactly one:

```diff
-fix = true
+fix = false
```

**Negative control.** On a scratch copy carrying a known-fixable `I001`, with the setting deleted a bare `ruff check` reported the violations and left the file byte-identical by `sha256sum`, while `ruff check --fix` on the same file still repaired it. Restoring `fix = true` to the scratch config turned the bare `ruff check` back into a rewrite, so the probe is not a no-op. That third arm is also the clearest statement of why the current behaviour is easy to miss: the bare check printed `Found 2 errors (1 fixed, 1 remaining)` and silently rewrote the file, and the confirming re-run then printed `All checks passed!`, which is indistinguishable from there having been no violation to begin with.

**The cost, stated rather than hidden.** Deleting `fix = true` means a bare `ruff check` at a developer's prompt reports instead of repairing, and getting repairs becomes `ruff check --fix`. That convenience is a deliberate choice rather than an oversight, so the alternative to this PR is a real one: keep the setting, and remember `--no-fix` at every site where ruff is run to count something rather than to change something. The argument for deleting is that the repository already states the autofix intent where it is enforced, one file away, so the second statement of it can only take effect somewhere nobody declared it should. The two mistakes are not symmetric either. Forgetting `--fix` prints a list of violations and costs one retype; forgetting `--no-fix` today produces a corrupted measurement that looks exactly like a clean one.

**Files touched.** `pyproject.toml`, one line deleted. No backend, frontend or documentation changes are needed: `git grep 'ruff check'` returns nothing tracked, so no documented developer step names the bare command, and `AGENTS.md`'s Validation Commands section routes through `./scripts/lint.sh`.

**Validation.** `./scripts/lint.sh` passes all 18 hooks, `ruff check` among them, which is the direct evidence that the enforced path is unchanged. `./scripts/test.sh` passes both surfaces: backend pytest 212 passed at 52.8% lines and 38.6% branches, frontend Playwright E2E at 59.8% and 43.6%.

No user-visible behaviour changes, and no deployment or data-compatibility notes.

author: mpge
body:
## What broke

`includes/Services/NotificationService.php` was never instantiated. `Escalated::boot()` registered every other service, but nothing referenced this one. As a result:

- **No emails:** no new-ticket or reply email was ever sent.
- **Dead webhook setting:** the **Webhook URL** and **Webhook Secret** settings did nothing.
- **Unsafe fetch:** had `send_webhook()` been reachable, it used `wp_remote_post`, which does not refuse loopback, private or link-local addresses.

## Reproduction

1. Set **Webhook URL** in Escalated settings.
2. Create a ticket.
3. Reply to it as an agent.

No request reaches the webhook, and neither the admin nor the requester gets an email.

## Red

`tests/Test_Notification_Wiring.php` before the fix: 9 tests, 6 failures.

```
1) Test_Notification_Wiring::test_creating_a_ticket_posts_one_signed_webhook
Failed asserting that actual size 0 matches expected size 1.

2) Test_Notification_Wiring::test_ticket_lifecycle_posts_each_event_to_the_webhook
Failed asserting that two arrays are identical.
-Array &0 (
-    0 => 'ticket.created'
-    1 => 'reply.created'
-    2 => 'ticket.assigned'
-    3 => 'ticket.status_changed'
-)
+Array &0 ()

3) Test_Notification_Wiring::test_webhook_to_a_loopback_address_is_refused
Failed asserting that two strings are identical.
-'A valid URL was not provided.'
+'cURL error 7: Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 80 after 0 ms: Could not connect to server'

4) Test_Notification_Wiring::test_creating_a_ticket_emails_the_site_admin
No new-ticket email was sent to the site admin.
Failed asserting that null is not null.

5) Test_Notification_Wiring::test_agent_reply_emails_the_requester
No reply email was sent to the requester.
Failed asserting that null is not null.

6) Test_Notification_Wiring::test_emails_use_the_notification_sender_settings
Failed asserting that null is not null.
```

Failure 3 shows the old `send_webhook()` actually opening a connection to 127.0.0.1.

## Fix

`NotificationService::register()` is called from `Escalated::boot()`. It hooks at priority 100: after the product handlers and workflows, and after `Email_Threading` has set the threading context.

- **Emails:**
  - `escalated_ticket_created` sends `notify_ticket_created()` when `notification_new_ticket` is on.
  - `escalated_reply_created` sends `notify_reply_created()` when `notification_ticket_reply` is on.
  - Both default to on, matching the checked boxes the settings screen shows for an unsaved setting.
  - The From header now uses `notification_from_name` and `notification_from_email`, falling back to the site name and admin email as before.
- **Webhook events:** `webhook_url` receives `ticket.created`, `ticket.updated`, `ticket.status_changed`, `ticket.assigned`, `ticket.unassigned`, `ticket.department_changed`, `reply.created` and `sla.breached`.
  - **Payload:** `{event, payload, timestamp}` as before. `payload.ticket` carries the ticket's id, reference, subject, status, priority, type, channel, department, assignee, requester and timestamps. Guest tokens and contact details are left out.
  - **Signing:** the existing `X-Escalated-Signature` HMAC is sent when `webhook_secret` is set.
  - **Internal notes** are never posted.
- **Failures:** a mail or webhook failure is caught and never escapes into the ticket operation that fired the hook. Failed webhooks still fire `escalated_webhook_failed`.
- **Safe requests:** `send_webhook()` uses `wp_safe_remote_post`, which refuses loopback, private and link-local addresses (cloud metadata included), including after redirects.
- **Robust handlers:** they accept loosely typed arguments and ignore non-ticket payloads, as `WorkflowListener` does. Existing tests fire these hooks with `null`.

## Tests

`tests/Test_Notification_Wiring.php` (9 tests) uses the real services and the hooks registered at boot:

- **One signed webhook per ticket:** creating a ticket posts exactly one `ticket.created` webhook, with the right ticket, event header and HMAC, sent with `reject_unsafe_urls` on.
- **No URL, no request:** with no webhook URL, nothing is requested.
- **Lifecycle events:** create, reply, assign and change status post `ticket.created`, `reply.created`, `ticket.assigned` and `ticket.status_changed`, in that order and with the right agent and status fields.
- **Loopback refused:** a webhook to `http://127.0.0.1/` is refused before any connection is made.
- **Emails honour the settings:** creating a ticket emails the site admin, and an agent reply emails the requester. Each stops when its setting is off.
- **Sender settings:** the notification sender name and address are used.

**Full suite:** 426 tests, 1160 assertions, 4 skipped (the existing skips). It ran in Docker on PHP 8.2 with MySQL 8.0 and the WordPress 7.1 test library, set up as `run-tests.yml` does. `vendor/bin/pint --test` passes.

## Not in this PR

- **Three notification settings still do nothing.** `NotificationService` has no email for assignment or SLA events, so `notification_ticket_assigned`, `notification_sla_warning` and `notification_sla_breach` remain without effect.
- **SLA warnings would repeat every minute.** `SlaService::check_warnings()` runs every minute from cron and fires `escalated_sla_warning` again on every run while a ticket is inside the warning window. An email or webhook on that hook would repeat every minute, so it needs an "already warned" marker first. That is also why `sla.warning` is not posted to the webhook.
- **Webhooks are synchronous.** Each event waits up to 15 seconds for the receiver. The timeout can be changed with the existing `escalated_webhook_args` filter.

author: cartagogit
body:
Every pull request ran **all eleven test zones** whatever it touched, because `plan-tests` built the matrix from the zone list and never looked at the diff.

The machinery to do better **already existed and nothing called it**. `affected.script.ts` computes the transitive closure of affected workspaces; its own header says the tier workflows consume it — and those workflows were deleted. No workflow ran it, no package script named it, and `lint:lints-reach-ci` does not catch it because it only watches `lint:*` scripts.

**Wiring it revealed why it would not have worked anyway.** Its `affected` field unions upstream *and* downstream, because it answers a **build-ordering** question: to build X, first build what X depends on. Test selection asks the opposite — *what could this change have broken* — and the answer never points at a dependency.

Measured: a four-file change to a CI script that **nothing depends on** marked **51 workspaces** affected, which is the same as running everything. Following downstream only, the same change reaches **one zone**.

| Candidate touching | Test jobs before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tools/scripts/ci/` only | 11 | **3** |
| root config / workflow | 11 | 11 (unchanged, deliberately) |

Two properties are pinned, because getting either wrong means a false green:

- **It fails OPEN.** A file changed outside every workspace, or a graph that cannot be built, runs everything — nothing can say what a root config reaches.
- **An unreachable zone stays in the matrix** and reports `skipped` rather than vanishing. A zone missing from the checks list is indistinguishable from one that was forgotten, which is the same principle the empty-zone rule already states.

author: matiasmacera
body:
# Proposed Changes

Follow-up to #663, addressing the review comments left on it about signalling
stale PIDs and hanging on shutdown. This app runs in the host PID namespace, so
signalling a PID that is no longer our child can hit an unrelated host process.

## Problems in the current shutdown handling

1. `terminate_processes` decides that a PID is alive with `kill -0`, which also
   succeeds for a PID that exited and was reused by another host process, and the
   SIGKILL fallback sends `kill -9` to the whole original list.
2. After SIGKILL, every PID is waited for without a limit.
3. The stop trap of the main script is set after both children are started, and
   `stop_exporter` relies on a variable assigned right after `glances &`. A stop
   request that arrives in either window can leave the exporter behind.
4. The 10 s pause before restarting the exporter runs in the foreground, so a
   stop request is only handled once it finishes.

## Changes

- **Only running children are signalled.** A PID is checked against the job
  table of the shell (`jobs -pr`) right before each signal, SIGKILL included.
  The job table only lists our own children and drops one once it has been
  reaped, unlike `kill -0`.
- `wait -n` gets both PIDs explicitly. This is defensive: on the bash 5.3.9 of the
  base image the call without IDs already returns for a child that exited
  earlier, but older bash releases could keep waiting on the other child.
- The timeout is a `SECONDS` deadline; after SIGKILL, processes get 5 more
  seconds, and one that is still running is logged instead of waited for.
- The stop trap is set before any child is started, and both stop handlers take
  the children to stop from the job table instead of from variables.
- The restart pause runs in the background and is waited for, so a stop request
  interrupts it.

**Known limits:** the window between checking a PID and signalling it is reduced
to almost nothing, but closing it entirely would need a pidfd, which bash does
not offer. If the exporter supervisor subshell itself is killed with SIGKILL from
outside, its exporter is not reachable from the parent; that would need a
different supervision layout and is out of scope here.

## How it was tested

- `shellcheck -s bash glances/rootfs/etc/services.d/glances/run` (ShellCheck
  0.11.0): clean.
- Bash 5.3.9, the whole script with bashio stubbed and `glances` replaced by a
  fake that records its PID. After each scenario, check for leftover processes:

| Scenario | Before (#663) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SIGTERM to the script | exits 0, nothing left | exits 0, nothing left |
| SIGTERM right after start (5 runs, 10-50 ms) | exporter left running in one run | nothing left in all runs |
| Web server dies | exits 1, nothing left | exits 1, nothing left |
| Exporter ignores SIGTERM | SIGKILL after ~20 s, nothing left | SIGKILL after ~21 s, nothing left |
| SIGTERM during the 10 s restart pause | exits after ~8 s | exits after ~2 s |

- The helpers on their own:

| Scenario | Before (#663) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A live PID that is not our child is passed in | receives SIGTERM and SIGKILL | never signalled |
| A process that survives SIGKILL (simulated) | waits forever | returns after timeout + 5 s, logs it |

# Related Issues

- Follow-up to #663.
