author: ksquared-16
body:
`vac operating-report [--kind daily|weekly] [--date] [--json] [--write]` derives every figure from authoritative platform state — the governed action store, execution runs, lanes, health, toolkit convergence. Nothing is inferred from prose or logs. A number that cannot be derived is **null, never estimated**.

Identity is the **window, not the clock**, so the same day yields the same `report_id` and a cadence that fires twice cannot create a second today.

**Operator time is never added to system time.** The measured end-to-end P50 was 13.63s and the max 256s, and almost all of the difference was a person deciding. Reported as one figure it would send the next mission to optimise a queue that already answers in 70ms.

## Notification latency needed no new instrumentation

It was carried as UNMEASURED on the assumption a stamp had to be invented. The notification store already records `created_at`, `delivery.at` and `seen_at`:

```
run terminal -> notified   P50 0.116s  P95 0.149s   (n=28)
created -> delivered       P50 0.570s  P95 12.137s  (n=351)
```

A parallel pipeline would have added a second source of truth to answer a question the first could already answer.

## Three defects found by reading the output rather than trusting it

- joining notifications on request id alone matched the **approval** notification, created *before* the thing it announces: **P50 minus 58 seconds**. A negative latency is not a fast system; it is a join that matched the wrong row.
- anchoring a run terminal moment on `updated_at` measured from the last time anything touched the record, which for a resumed run is after its own notification: **P50 minus 33 seconds**.
- classifying governance refusals with a regex over failure codes scored **0 of 19** — the codes that occur contain none of the words a person would guess. Now enumerated, with an unknown code counting as a failure rather than quietly as the system working.

## Also here

`trusted-host-open-pr.mjs` and `trusted-host-merge.mjs` used `err.split('\n')[0]` — the blank-first-line defect already closed on the push path, on the two calls every promotion makes. Both now use `firstMeaningfulLine`.

NC12 asserted merge delegation was disabled. `certified_staging_merge_v1` has since been promoted deliberately and is enabled with eleven gates — the test was stale, not the product. It now asserts what must stay true: staging only, never on weaker evidence.

10 report tests; housekeeping back to 18/18.

author: coreyphillips
body:
Closes #837

An owed held-forward fail on an ERRORED inbound channel is now dropped along with its shared secret, instead of being retried every block.

`retryOwedHeldForwardFailures()` only drops an owed fail on a CLOSED or FORCE_CLOSED channel. `Channel.failHtlc()` also refuses ERRORED, and a channel failed by a BOLT 1 error never returns to NORMAL. When recovery safety blocks the automatic close (data loss, uncertain state, unproven restore), `handleChannelErrored()` leaves the channel ERRORED until the peer closes it. Until then, every block retried the fail, got it refused, and emitted a channel error, while the ledger entry and shared secret stayed in memory.

## What changed

- `retryOwedHeldForwardFailures` treats ERRORED like CLOSED and FORCE_CLOSED. It deletes the owed entry and its shared secret without calling `fail`.

## How to test

- `npx mocha --exit --timeout 20000 -r ts-node/register tests/lightning/hold-invoice-snapshot.test.ts`: 14 passing.
- The new case is 'drops an owed late-part fail and its secret on an errored channel left for the peer to close (issue #837)'. It sets `dataLossDetected` and ERRORED, calls `handleChannelErrored`, then processes two blocks. It checks that the channel is still ERRORED, nothing is owed, the secret is gone, and no channel error fired.
- Run against the unfixed source, the new case failed (owed count 1, expected 0).
- `npx eslint` on both changed files: 0 errors. The 22 warnings are elsewhere in lightning-node.ts.
- `npm run tsc:check`: clean.
- `npm run tsc:check:tests`: 13 errors, all in `wallet`, `transaction` and `receive` tests. They import the package root, which needs a `dist` build that this worktree lacks. None are in the changed test.
- `npm run test:lightning` was started but had not finished when this report was written, so it has no result.

## Notes

The node_modules in this worktree is a gitignored symlink to the main checkout, used to run the gates. It is still there because `npm run test:lightning` is using it.

author: baekpica
body:
Continuation of the 14 September Qwen campaign. Fused QSA is still 10% of 8K GPU time. This PR attempts the remaining analysis items and keeps production on the existing 12×1 fused path.

**Attempted, not adopted**

- QSA PV 6×2 (six heads × two dims per thread): bit-identical to 12×1. Unprofiled 8K/64K medians +0.07% / +0.08% prefill, −0.28% / +0.24% decode. Below the 2% bar. `DS4_QWEN_QSA_PV6X2=1` keeps the mapping for diagnosis.
- Selected-K/V two-row gather reuse: unit-fixture overlap Jaccard ~0.98 and bit identity, but full-model 8K logits drifted (max abs 0.73–1.37, tokens differ at 39/53) with no prefill gain. Kernel not in the default binary.
- HC shared mix_down/inject: not implemented. Those GEMMs are already cublas/cutlass on shared BF16 rows (~97 ms of 8403 ms GPU). Combining them cannot hit 2% e2e.

QSA Tensor Core and the PLE descriptor pool stay rejected as recorded in the 14 September report.

**Shipped**

- `DS4_QWEN_QSA_NO_FUSED` is read per dispatch so fused vs split tests actually switch kernels.
- Native QSA tests poison the score scratch to prove the fused path, then compare split and opt-in 6×2 against it.
- Campaign numbers, clocks (2190 MHz, 300–2200 range) and limits: `docs/qwen38-perf-2026-09-14.md`.

No production default speed path changed. Verify/batch/HTTP serving gates are unchanged because no adopted kernel is on the default path.

body:
## What

Three corrections to the setup documentation, all found while getting l8git running on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 machine:

- **README says Linux installers are not published.** They are — `v1.0.7` ships `l8git_1.0.7_amd64.deb`, `l8git-1.0.7-1.x86_64.rpm` and `l8git_1.0.7_amd64.AppImage`. The release matrix in `.github/workflows/release.yml` has had an `ubuntu-22.04` entry for a while; the README text predates it.
- **The same stale warning sits in `packaging/aur/PKGBUILD`** ("Solange kein ubuntu-Runner in der Matrix steht, existiert das unten referenzierte .deb im Release NICHT"). The `.deb` it points at exists, so the note now sends Arch packagers off a cliff that isn't there. Removed. The per-release `pkgver`/`sha256sums` reminder above it is untouched.
- **Node is not listed as a prerequisite at all**, in either README or CONTRIBUTING. `bun run build` shells out to Vite, Vite runs on Node, and Vite 7 requires `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`. On Ubuntu 24.04's default Node 18 the build dies with `crypto.hash is not a function` — an error that gives no hint about the Node version. CI does not hit this because `setup-node` pins 20.

Both prerequisite lists also got the concrete Debian/Ubuntu package list instead of only a link to the Tauri docs. It is copied verbatim from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so it is the list that is known to work.

## Why

Linux is a supported and released target, but the documentation reads as if it were not, and the two things that actually block a first build there — the dev packages and the Node version — are the two things not written down.

## How tested

Followed the corrected instructions end to end on Ubuntu 24.04: the apt list installs cleanly, and with Node 22 the full CI sequence passes locally — `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run test` (1192 tests), `bun run build`, `cargo test --all-targets`.

## What the reader gets

- `/help/transcribe-a-file/` (order 8): the two ways in, the file formats, the six steps, the two engines and the six polishers as tables quoting the cards' own words, the time estimate and its basis, Stop, what Done offers (three views, Times, Copy/Save/Share and their Marked up relabels, New transcription), where the transcript goes, where the recording goes.

## How the claims were checked

The drafts were written read-only by another session; every factual claim was re-verified against main 3d45306f before shipping, and the review narrowed sixteen of them across four Codex rounds (`.codex/2026-09-13-help-transcribe-a-file-r{1..4}-out.txt`, round 4 CLEAN). The one substantive correction: Stop during the cleanup writes EVERY speaker turn raw and disclosed, not only the turns it had not reached (`writeSpeakerFields(cleanupOutcome: .stopped)` passes no parts); both articles say so and point at Clean it again. The rest: labels need the voices told apart and the words matched to them; no unbound "no length limit"; the engine article compares language counts, not lists; Ollama locality stated only when Ollama reports it; the estimate names its basis; "exactly what was said" became "the original transcription"; History saving confirmed by the chip, not promised; the footer sentence described as changing with step and polisher; the notices carry no frequency claims. Table cells that quote the on-screen cards sit under a column headed "What the card says".

**Cloud gate rounds 1 to 3, and the class round.** The three cloud passes returned seven findings of one class: a sentence stating as always-true what a setting or a surfaced failure path makes conditional (Both as an unassigned-words label; space-free scripts failing at the timing mapper; a turn's time only when it exists; a Not fully polished turn keeping the pre-polisher words, not raw speech-engine output; History rows carrying the file name, not a title; the automatic fixes and their switches separate from the polisher; the History save the app can report as failed). All seven fixed. Then the class was enumerated locally from the producing code rather than from the findings (`.codex/2026-09-13-help-transcribe-a-file-r6-out.txt.last`: every behaviour sentence in both articles, 148 rows, 106 TRUE, 42 OVERSTATED, 0 FALSE). The rows narrowed in the last commit are the ones a setting or a state the app shows makes false in ordinary use (the Enable Dictionary switch, the polish-settings link's appearance, the four polish credits, the view picker's appearance and what Cleaned holds, Times, a long turn cleaned in pieces, Continue's setup, the no-timings notice's scope). The remaining OVERSTATED rows are of one shape, "the write could fail" or "an earlier gate could refuse", for failures the app reports with its own message and the articles describe in their notices sections; those sentences stay as written, because hedging each with "when the save succeeds" describes the failure instead of the feature. author: ajstrick81
body:
## Fixes #167 — Disney+ fails to patch on v26.16.0+ (fingerprint mismatch)

### Root cause
v26.16.0 refactored and R8-obfuscated the MEL pause-ad layer. The clear class `com.disneystreaming.nve.player.mel.MediaXPauseSession` and the `"pauseData"` string are gone (`MediaX/NVE` + `pauseSessionEnded=` strings survive under obfuscated class names), so `PauseAdStartedFingerprint` no longer resolves.

Because **a single unresolved fingerprint aborts the entire patch**, Disney+ failed to patch at all on 26.16+ — even though the pre/mid-roll ad-block (`Insertion`/`DMP` `getPoints()` + `getRanges()`, Patches 1&2) still matches cleanly. That's exactly the reporter's "26.15.2 works, 26.16+ fails" symptom.

```
SEVERE: FAILED: Disney+ Android TV
app.morphe.patcher.patch.PatchException: Failed to match the fingerprint: PauseAdStartedFingerprint
    at ...DisneyPatch.kt:93
```

### Fix
- Wrap the pause-ad injection (Patch 3) in `try/catch` so a missing render seam **degrades gracefully** — mirrors the existing optional-fingerprint idiom in `HBOAdsPatch`. Pre/mid-roll ad removal is unaffected; pause-ad blocking is simply skipped until the seam is re-anchored. On ≤26.15.2 the fingerprint still matches and applies exactly as before.
- Declare the validated `26.16.0+rc2-2026.09.08` compat target.

### Verification (Onn 4K, .211)
- ✅ Patch **applies cleanly** on 26.16.0 (`INFO: Applied: Disney+ Android TV`, no abort)
- ✅ Patched build **installs and boots** with **no VerifyError / crash** (injected ad-block bytecode is valid)
- Core `getPoints()/getRanges()` empty-list mechanism is unchanged from the shipped, previously-verified v1.12.0 patch — only the pause-ad sub-feature is affected.

### Follow-up (not in this PR)
Re-anchor the pause-ad render method for 26.16+ (now an obfuscated synthetic in the `MediaX/NVE` package). Needs on-device pcap verification of the new Glide-into render call, as the original v3 seam was — doing it blind risks breaking playback, so it's deferred rather than guessed.

author: firemanxbr
body:
**Found today** while building an Omarchy reference system from `stable`: pacman refused OPR packages as *corrupted*. A scan of stable x86_64 (229 OPR objects): **69 have a `.sig` that is not a signature of the stored bytes**, and **5 are pinned by an index row whose bytes the pool does not hold**. Cause: the OPR rebuilds the same version per channel with different bytes; before the pool refused a signature for bytes it does not serve (2026-09-12), a later channel's `.sig` landed beside the earlier channel's object, and a second index row for the same filename got pinned while the object stayed the first build's.

**This PR**
- `verify` — `crates/pkg-repo/src/verify.rs`, a job kind (weekly, Saturday 03:00 UTC; `pkg-repo job verify`, `pkg-repo verify --repair` by hand): downloads every OPR object a ring serves (per arch), checks the bytes against the index and the `.sig` against Omarchy's key; with repair, fetches the right signature from the upstream channel that still serves those bytes, re-pins the ring to the object the pool actually holds (indexing the bytes if the index never saw them) and renders; what no channel serves any more is reported in a `verify` event for a replacement. Dry run against production reproduces the scan exactly (69 + 5, 0 unfixable).
- **GC**: an object shared by two index rows is never deleted while another row names it (this would have deleted served bytes once the stale row aged out).
- **Sync**: on a filename collision the stored object is pinned whether or not the index knows the upstream sha, and the colliding sha is never pinned; `POST /packages/known` names the *first* row behind a filename — the one whose bytes are stored.
- **Health check**: a sample per repository (first, last, a few at random; eight for the OPR) downloaded and signature-verified instead of one package — a wrong signature becomes evidence the day it appears.
- Scopes for the job (`pool:write`, every ring's release and artifacts), `JOB_KINDS` gains `verify`, e2e: verify finds the local pool clean, then a signature of other bytes planted beside zlib is found and reported. Docs: RUNBOOK (the incident and the job), ARCHITECTURE, TESTING.

author: leejmorel
body:
Phase **H2c** of `history/auth-identity-assurance-design.md` §15 — the last `[1.0]` item that was not release-gated.

## Problem

The backend has held several addresses per account since #1582, across four merged PRs. The account settings page showed this:

```tsx
<Label>{t("profile.emailLabel")}</Label>
<Input value={user.email} disabled readOnly />
```

One address, disabled, read-only. On every deployment the feature existed and nobody could reach it.

## Changes

**`useAddresses.ts`** — wraps the four generated operations in the `useSecurity` pattern, with one invalidation for the list.

**`AddressManager.tsx`** — the list (primary and unconfirmed badges), add, make-primary, and remove behind a confirmation.

**`UserSettingsAccountPage`** — the section goes above the existing form rather than inside it. Each address action commits on its own, so there is nothing for that form's Save button to collect — and a nested `<form>` is invalid HTML besides. *That reparenting reindents the form body, so most of this file's diff is whitespace; `git diff -w` shows the real change is 10 lines.*

## The section agrees with §6.2 rather than discovering it through an error

Each of these is a rule the service already enforces. Stating them in the UI is the difference between a button that is visibly unavailable and one that looks fine and answers 400:

| Rule | In the UI |
|---|---|
| 6 — never remove the last confirmed address, nor the primary without promoting another | Remove is disabled on both, with a `title` saying which |
| 3 — exactly one primary, always confirmed | "Make primary" appears only on a confirmed address |
| 7 — synthetic addresses are hidden | `source === "synthetic"` rows are filtered out |
| 5 — adding never reveals whether an address is taken | One success message, and it describes the letter rather than the outcome |

## Testing

Six specs, and two are worth calling out:

- **The "last confirmed address" case is reachable and is tested on its own.** My first version asserted it against an account whose primary was confirmed — where the primary check already disables the button, so the assertion proved nothing. The real shape is an account that signed up before confirming and proved a *second* address instead: the primary is unconfirmed and the only address that can sign them in is not the primary. That is exactly what the backend's `LAST_VERIFIED_ADDRESS` refusal is for.
- Verified load-bearing: replacing `isOnlyProvenAddress`'s body with `false` fails that spec and nothing else.

```
vitest run src/components/settings/AddressManager.test.tsx   # 6 passed
vitest run src/pages/user/settings src/components/settings   # 27 passed
vitest run src/__tests__/locale-keys.test.ts src/lib/tools.test.ts   # 395 passed
biome lint ./src && tsc --noEmit   # clean
```

## Strings

New `settings:addresses` block in **de/en/es/fr**, matching the wording already used for the address error codes ("confirmed" / "bestätigt" / "confirmada" / "confirmée"). Added `ADDRESS_TAKEN` to `errors.json` in all four — it was the one reachable address code with no mapping, raised when somebody proves an address while your claim is pending. Removed `profile.emailLabel` / `profile.emailHelp`, which the old field was the only user of.

No backend change, no schema change.

author: qnjoly
body:
## What

The chrome of the default theme brought to the reference design, across every page and the three widths:

- **Mode switch**: a 40 px square drawing the glyph of the current scheme (◐ automatic, ☀ light, ☾ dark) in place of the bordered text button; the name of the control and the scheme are written for assistive technology alone (`aria-label`, `title`, visually hidden text). The island updates the glyph and the names as the choice cycles.
- **Trail**: no longer a line under the bar. The island stands in the bar before the mode switch; once the trail holds a page its script renders a square bookmark button whose disclosure unfolds the trail as a popover under the bar. An empty trail leaves the island empty and hidden. Storage, URL fragment and pinning are unchanged; the `trail.empty` message goes with the line that showed it.
- **Breakpoints**: 700 px (`43.75rem`) and 1100 px (`68.75rem`) instead of 768 and 1180, replaced mechanically in every media query of the split stylesheets, the tests that name them, the gallery state descriptions and the guides. Gallery widths unchanged.
- **Phone**: the bar carries the menu button as a 48 px bordered square (✕ in the ink once open), the mark, the name cut with an ellipsis and a 40 px magnifier button that unfolds the search field under the bar (the field was reachable through the drawer alone). The folded sections go "On this page N", "Properties N", "Related pages N" (open, three entries as title, count and excerpt, the others behind their count, no filter), "Neighbourhood map · N" with the number of pages the map draws; headings in sentence case; the legend of the marks leaves the foot.
- **Tablet**: the search button reads as a small field after the name; the panel takes a narrow column (`11.625rem`) with the values of the properties, three related titles and "N others", the table of contents left out, the map at the foot.
- **Table of contents**: its own module and island, counted after its heading; the entry of the section being read carries the accent rule and the ink (`aria-current="location"`), moved by an `IntersectionObserver` over the top third of the viewport; the served markup marks the first entry, which stays without a script or an observer.
- **Centre column** padded 30 by 40 px on the desktop, 20 px on the tablet, 18 by 16 px on the phone.

## Why

The audit of the generated site against the reference design listed these deviations of the chrome; the boards are the specification.

`pnpm build`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm -r typecheck`, the site, i18n and cli suites (1358 tests), 100 % coverage on every file of `packages/site/src`, `scripts/hygiene.mjs`, `scripts/validate.mjs`, the wiki parity script, and `concordance gallery` (0 accessibility findings, 0 contrast pairs). Blocking teptris-py Windows wheels: the shared library exports
nothing when built with MSVC — no __declspec annotations means a DLL
with zero exports, so no import library is generated and link.exe
dies with LNK1181 (cannot open teptris.lib). Every run so far

consumers (teptris-ruby) never saw it because mingw exports all
symbols by default.

functions, no exported data).

(CMakeLists + version.h said 0.1.0 through v0.1.1), and the version
unit test asserts against TEPTRIS_VERSION_STRING instead of a
hardcoded literal.

Emit.EmittedTomlAlwaysReparses fail identically on current main —
needs a separate investigation.

No mobile, os 5 cards de `.conciliar-resumo` (Registros conciliados / Valor conciliado / Valor projetado / Diferença / Status) ficavam todos numa única linha de tabela, sem caber na tela. ### 3. Modal "Conciliar com o Extrato" — "Vínculos já confirmados"
Cada `<td>` herdava um `style="width:X%"` usado só para dividir colunas no desktop (`table-layout:fixed`), que sobrevivia à virada para "card" no mobile e espremia rótulo+valor numa fração da largura do card. Corrigido com um reset genérico (`.tabela-cards-mobile td{width:auto!important}`) que beneficia qualquer tabela deste padrão com o mesmo resíduo, sem tocar em nenhuma função de render individualmente.

### 4. Backup e Restauração — fechamento do menu
Clicar em "Backup e Restauração" dentro do `menu-arquivo-painel` só fechava o próprio painel, deixando o `mais-sheet` (bottom sheet "Painéis") aberto por cima, escondendo a página de Backup recém-aberta. Agora fecha os dois níveis de menu antes de abrir a página, igual ao atalho equivalente já existente na bottom-nav.

Não fazia nada quando já havia uma conta conectada — chamava `loginOneDrive()` diretamente, que pula o popup de login quando `msalConta` já está preenchido, só recarregando os arquivos da MESMA conta. Nova função `trocarContaOneDrive()` reutiliza os dois fluxos já existentes na ordem certa: `desconectarArquivos()` (mesmo "Sair da conta" de sempre, com a checagem de alterações não salvas) e só então `loginOneDrive()` (que agora abre o popup de verdade, com `msalConta` já `null`) — nenhum mecanismo de autenticação novo. Corrigido nos dois pontos de acionamento (menu-arquivo-painel e card "Conta Microsoft" da Início).

author: bimalthanet5
body:
## This is not meant to be merged

It is a **backup**, and it should be closed without merging once `bimalthanet5/foveo` exists.

This repository holds an unrelated Unity WebGL build. The Foveo scaffold was committed here — under `foveo/`, touching nothing that already existed — only because the session that produced it runs in an ephemeral container and had no other writable destination at the time.

## Why it ended up here

Foveo was built to live in its own repository. Two things blocked that:

- `POST /user/repos` returned 403 — creating a repository needs the GitHub App's *Administration* permission, which the Claude app does not request. This is unlikely to ever work.
- `git push` to this repository also returned 403 at the time, since the app was not yet installed.

Installing the app fixed the second problem, which is why this branch now exists. The first is unchanged: the `foveo` repository has to be created by hand.

## What is in `foveo/`

Hands-free scrolling driven by eye gestures and voice, for RSI and carpal tunnel relief. Milestone 0: architecture, safety model and test harness.

Pipeline, with a typed seam at every arrow:

```
Frame → FaceLandmarks → FaceFeatures → Command → SafetyGate → OS
```

`FaceFeatures` is the narrow waist — images and models above it, plain numbers below. That is what lets the gesture layer be tested with literal floats, and why the suite runs headless with no camera, no model file and no MediaPipe wheel.

Safety model, since this program holds a camera handle and injects synthetic input:

- dry-run by default; `--no-dry-run` required on every run, and a config file alone can never enable injection
- `SafetyGate` starts disarmed and is fail-closed: no recent face, low confidence, a blocklisted foreground window or a tripped token bucket all mean refuse
- event-rate governor independent of the gesture layer, bounded by config validation, so a stuck state machine cannot run away
- no runtime network calls, enforced in CI by a grep rather than by promise
- model SHA-256 pinned and verified on every load
- window titles deliberately kept out of log messages, with a test asserting it

Implemented: core types, validated config, `SafetyGate`, frame sources, MediaPipe wrapper, backend abstraction, pipeline, and a `foveo doctor` CLI. Left as specified stubs with failing-test contracts: feature extraction (M2) and the gesture state machines (M3), each with a worked example beside the task.

47 files, ~5,250 lines. 84 tests passing. ruff, mypy `--strict`, bandit and format checks all clean. CI configured across Windows and Linux on Python 3.10–3.12.

## What has not been verified

OpenCV and MediaPipe were never installed in the session that wrote this, so `MediaPipeLandmarker` is written against the documented API and has never run against a real camera. `estimate_head_pose` is standard `solvePnP`, but its tests assert well-formedness rather than specific angles, because the synthetic test face is not a real face. Both are Milestone 1's job to confirm.

## How to close this out

1. Create an empty `bimalthanet5/foveo` — no README, no .gitignore, no licence
2. The same tree gets pushed there as the initial commit on `main`
3. Close this PR and delete the branch; the `foveo/` directory here is then redundant

author: sqrt-of-2
body:
This PR packages the Schwarz--Christoffel boundary vertices as Mathlib's `Polygon`: for a nonempty finite ordered family of prevertices, place the finite vertices first and append their common boundary value at infinity. Compute the finite and infinite vertex values, all three kinds of edge, and the complete polygon boundary as a union of segments.

This advances the exact `ConformalMapping/README.md` L6 target "Schwarz--Christoffel: explicit conformal maps onto polygons, built on L4 + L5." It is the most effective next step because the analytic boundary values and individual interval-image theorems now need a single polygon object whose boundary they can collectively describe. After this PR, L6 still needs to identify the compactified boundary range with this polygon boundary, exclude intersections of nonadjacent sides to obtain global injectivity and the interior image, and solve the parameter problem for prescribed polygons.

The `Fin (n + 1)` indexing makes the finite list nonempty and produces an `(n + 2)`-vertex polygon after adjoining infinity. The extra vertex records the split between the two unbounded boundary intervals; under the classical exponent sum it may subdivide a straight closing side rather than form a geometric corner. The combinatorial definition is total, while the bridge to canonical finite boundary values states the exact local integrability hypothesis.

The implementation reuses Mathlib's `Polygon`, `Polygon.edgeSet`, `Polygon.boundary`, `affineSegment_eq_segment`, `Fin.lastCases`, and `finRotate`; no Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored. The mathematical organization follows the Ahlfors and Driscoll--Trefethen references cited in the module documentation.

The PR adds `TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/SchwarzChristoffel/Polygon.lean` (207 lines).

author: danathar-atomic-hive[bot]
body:
## Test Improvement

Covers the three systemd files that actually start
`system_files/usr/libexec/arch-bootc-prune-esp` on a booted system. Before this,
no test in either suite opened any of them:

- `system_files/usr/lib/systemd/system/arch-bootc-prune-esp.service`
- `system_files/usr/lib/systemd/system/arch-bootc-prune-esp.timer`
- `system_files/usr/lib/systemd/system/bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service.d/10-prune-esp.conf`

The script itself is the best-covered file in the tree. Nothing tested that
anything ever runs it.

### `tests/test-prune-esp.sh` — new group, 9 test functions, 22 assertions

It already owns the script under test, and the units are the activation half of
the same contract.

- Reads `ExecStart=` out of the service, maps it back through
  `COPY system_files/ /`, and asserts it is the script this file drives; asserts
  the `-`/`+`/`!`/`:` prefix set is empty, since a leading `-` would turn a
  failed prune into a success.
- Asserts `ConditionPathExists=` guards exactly the binary `ExecStart=` runs.
  This is the load-bearing one: move the script and the condition stops
  matching, at which point systemd skips the unit and **reports success** — the
  timer keeps firing, the journal stays clean, and the ESP fills up anyway.
- **Executes** the unit's own `ExecStart=` command line against a fixture ESP
  (through `BOOTC_PRUNE_ESP_PATH`, like every other test here) and asserts it
  removes the unreferenced deployment and keeps the referenced one. Adding
  `--dry-run` to the unit now fails instead of silently making the prune a
  no-op.
- Asserts `Type=oneshot`, so `Before=bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service` keeps
  meaning "finished before" rather than "started before".
- Joins `Before=` to the unit the drop-in **directory name** claims to extend —
  the only thing binding those two, and the only two places in the tree that
  spell `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.service`.
- Asserts the drop-in's `Wants=` and `After=` name the service file as shipped.
- Joins the timer's `WantedBy=` to the `.wants` directory the Containerfile
  symlinks it into, and the symlink source to the timer file in the tree. The
  Containerfile's dangling-symlink scan checks the link *source*; it says
  nothing about the directory the link is placed in.
- Asserts each directive sits in the section systemd reads it from.

Units are parsed by a small awk INI reader (`unit_values`,
`unit_sections_for_key`). Deliberately not `systemd-analyze`: the suite must run
on hosts with no systemd, and `systemd-analyze` answers none of these questions
anyway — it validates one unit in isolation, it does not join a unit to the file
the repository ships or to the symlink the Containerfile writes.

### `tests/check-invariants.sh` — list drift, 4 checks

- `just lint` must `systemd-analyze verify` exactly the unit files this repo
  ships. Its list is literal; the Containerfile's is derived. Add a third unit
  file today and the image build verifies it while the command CONTRIBUTING.md
  tells contributors to run silently does not.
- The image build must keep deriving its list (`find /tmp/shipped-units -maxdepth
  1 -type f`) rather than growing a literal copy that goes stale alongside the
  Justfile's.
- Every `*.d` drop-in directory must name a unit something else in the tree
  spells. Neither verify call reaches a drop-in — `-maxdepth 1` excludes them —
  and a drop-in directory named for a unit that does not exist is an error at no
  point. It simply never applies.

### Verification

- `tests/test-prune-esp.sh`: 107 assertions pass (8 skipped — no block device
  node in `/dev` in this container, pre-existing).
- `tests/check-invariants.sh`: 85 checks pass.
- `tests/run-tests.sh`: every file passes except `test-quickstart-baremetal.sh`,
  which fails here for the same pre-existing environmental reason (no block
  device).
- shellcheck clean on both modified files.
- **16 mutations to the committed tree, 16 killed.** Each new assertion was
  checked against the edit it is supposed to catch: `ExecStart=` moved to
  `/usr/bin`, `ConditionPathExists=` drifted off it, `--dry-run` appended to
  `ExecStart=`, a `-` prefix on `ExecStart=`, `Type=simple`, a one-character
  typo in `Before=`, the drop-in directory renamed, the drop-in's `Wants=`

author: nategrey0130
body:
Answers **D4–D8**. With this, **all eight decisions D0–D8 are answered** and the
Heroes Unlimited batch has nothing gating it.

`super_abilities` holds **364 rows** — 69 Revised core, 170 PU1, 125 PU3 —
exactly the total the survey predicted was waiting on the table.

**Documentation only.** No data, no schema, no code.

## D4 is the one with a finding in it

`catalog-diff`'s alias bucket was wrong on **six of seven** entries for this
book, so every one was resolved against production by hand. They split two ways.

**Five are the same row** under a spelling difference:

| the book prints | the catalog holds |
|---|---|
| `Invisibility (self)` | **`Invisibility: Simple`** L3/6 — *not* `Invisibility (Superior)` L7/20, which the matcher chose |
| `Dispel Magic Barrier` | `Dispel Magic Barriers` |
| `Breath Without Air` | `Breathe Without Air` L3/5 |
| `Sword to Snakes` | `Swords to Snakes` L9/50 |
| `Expel Devils/Demons` | `Expel Demons` L8/35 |

**Five more are new general rows, and that is the substantive half.** For each of
`Levitate`, `Mesmerism`, `Wall of Flame`, `Spontaneous Combustion` and
`Swirling Lights`, the catalog holds **only** a tradition-namespaced Warlock row
— `Air: Levitate` L2/7, `Fire: Wall of Flame` L3/15 — which is a separate and
cheaper row, never the general invocation.

So a Heroes Unlimited spell import would **add five general spells this catalog
has only ever held in Warlock form**. That is worth knowing quite apart from
this book: **a Rifts Ley Line Walker cannot reach `Wall of Flame` today either.**

`same_spell_as` is explicitly *not* the mechanism for that second group. It links
two retellings of one spell; a general invocation and its tradition counterpart
are different rows with different levels and costs — which is the whole reason
the tradition namespace exists.

## D5–D8

| | answer | why |
|---|---|---|
| **D5** spells-per-day and the 2/3 pick cost | **recorded, not modelled** | neither has a column, and inventing one now would be a schema change serving a class import that hasn't happened |
| **D6** the offensive-spell asterisk | **dropped** | nothing reads such a tag; a column written once and read never is the shape `claim-audit` keeps finding |
| **D7** the robot and super-vehicle builders | **not imported** | `BOOK-INGEST-AUDIT` F3's reasoning for Phase World's vessels — no builder exists and `gear` holds one `mdc` |
| **D8** the W.P. Ancient/Modern split | **one category** | the split isn't a property of a proficiency; it's which ones a **program** may draw from, which `skill_programs` already expresses. Splitting would rewrite 38 rows to model a restriction one level up |

## What was measured

- Every D4 row read from **production** (`--remote`), with level and P.P.E., not
  inferred from the matcher's output.
- The queue's three importable books move to **`imported`**; Powers Unlimited Two
  stays **`surveyed`**, which is what D0 decided for it.

## Posture

Two files: the survey's decision record and the queue. **115 insertions.** No
`apps/` code, no `db/`, no `scripts/`.

## Nothing regresses — checked, not assumed

- Smoke and regression exit 0.
- Survey invariants asserted in the edit script: **0 bare LF, 0 blockquotes**,
  and **0 `OPEN` decisions left** in the table.

## Decline path

- **D8 is the most arguable.** Two W.P. categories would match the book's own
  vocabulary more literally; I kept one because the split lives on the program
  and 38 rows would have to change to say otherwise.
- **D4's second group implies new spell rows** that nothing has written yet —
  this PR records the decision, it does not import them.

## What remains after this, and neither is blocked

- The core book's **spells** — ~12 new rows, five of them the general
  invocations above.
- The **ten Power Categories as classes**, which needs D1's slot mapping built.
  `campaigns.system` is still two values, so an HU *campaign* cannot be created
  yet — that was D2.

author: terasakisatoshi
body:
`Closes #394`

> **The diagnosis in #394 was wrong, and this PR was rewritten.** Codex caught it. The original change — serialising two test files that call `clear_cache()` — would have cost about two minutes of wall clock and fixed nothing, because both of those calls run in child processes with a **test-local `RUSTCALL_CACHE_DIR`** and cannot reach the shared cache. #394 now carries the corrected cause.

## The bug

`save_cargo_cached_library` (`src/cargobuild.jl`) and `save_cached_library` (`src/cache.jl`) published into the cache with

```julia
cp(lib_path, cached_path, force = true)
```

Julia's `cp(…; force = true)` **unlinks the destination and then copies**, and copying a multi-megabyte `.dylib` is not instant. Every RustCall cache key is the complete artifact identity, so two processes routinely want the same destination — and `CACHE_LOCK` cannot help, because it is process-local.

Measured directly: a reader polling one destination while twelve `cp`s ran.

```
reads=34615 missing=1182 short=32971
```

Those two windows are exactly the two failures reported in #394:

```
test_generated_includes:
  SystemError: opening file ".../cache-v2/cargo/d4aa1e39….dylib": No such file or directory
  [6] include_dependency  @ src/crate_bindings.jl:1081

test_pyo3_public_routes:
  InitError: could not load library ".../cache-v2/cargo/747bc68e….dylib"
  [3] load_artifact!  @ src/loadpolicy.jl:2020
```

— the *missing* window for the first, the *short* window for the second. It also accounts for everything else: two different victims on two runs of the same tree, each file passing alone (no concurrent publisher), each passing against a private `RUSTCALL_CACHE_DIR` (no sharing).

This is not really a test-harness bug. Sixteen parallel workers sharing one cache directory just make it likely; two Julia sessions building the same block at the same time can hit it.

## The fix

`_publish_cache_file(src, dst)` in `src/cache.jl`, used by both entry points. Two rules:

- **An existing `dst` is never touched.** The key is the whole identity of the artifact, so a file already there *is* this artifact; rewriting it could only replace equivalent bytes with equivalent bytes while exposing every reader to the window above. It may also be `dlopen`ed or mapped right now, which on Windows makes the rewrite fail outright.
- **A new `dst` appears whole.** The copy goes to a per-process, per-call temporary name in the *same directory* — so the rename cannot cross a filesystem — and `mv` without `force` publishes it. A rename is atomic: a reader sees either nothing yet or the finished file.

Losing the race is not an error: `mv` refuses an existing destination, so the publisher that arrives second drops its temporary and keeps what is there, which is the same artifact.

Two follow-ons from that:

- the **checksum** is computed from whichever file ended up in the cache, not from the local build — otherwise a publisher that lost the race would write a checksum of *its* bytes against someone else's file and condemn a good entry at the next verification;
- the **fixed `.tmp` suffixes** on the checksum and metadata writes are made unique per process and per call, for the same reason two publishers must not share a temporary name. (Those two writes were already rename-based; only their temporary names were unsafe.)

## Tests

`test/test_cache.jl` (serial, so it owns its cache):

| testset | asserts |
| --- | --- |
| a fresh destination is published whole | content published, `published == true`, no `.tmp` left |
| an existing destination is never rewritten | content, **inode** and mtime unchanged, `published == false` |
| a destination that exists never disappears under a reader | a reader that has already seen the entry never finds it missing or short across twelve republications — skipped below two threads, covered by the 4-thread job |
| the Cargo cache publishes through the same path | pinned at `save_cargo_cached_library`, the entry point both observed failures went through |

Verified against the restored `cp(…; force = true)`: **1335 vanished and 10168 truncated** observations, plus the content, inode and mtime assertions failing. They discriminate.

## Acceptance criteria of #394 (revised)

| criterion | evidence |
| --- | --- |
| a concurrent reader that has already seen an entry never finds it missing or short | "a destination that exists never disappears under a reader" |
| an existing entry is not rewritten | "an existing destination is never rewritten" (byte, inode and mtime identity) |
| losing a publication race is not an error and cannot leave a condemning checksum | `_publish_cache_file` returns `published`; `save_cached_library` checksums the published file |

## Result

`Pkg.test()`: **10712 passing / 13 broken** (parallel) and **743 passing / 1 broken** (serial — the thread-gated test) exit 0; the whole cache file green under `--threads=4`.

body:
## Summary
- `--export` is now a comma-separated list instead of the `all`/`none` enum. Existing `--export=all` and `--export=none` behave as before.
- A name exports that declaration even without the `export` keyword. It matches the short or namespaced name (`add`, `M.add`) and accepts globs (`M.*`).
- `!name` excludes a name and always wins over an including filter. With only exclusions (`--export=!sub`) the `export` keyword decides, minus the excluded names.
- Class and interface members are filtered by their owner's name. Each variable of one `export let a, b` statement is decided on its own.
- The rules live in `MLIRExportFilter.h` (`isExportedByFilters`), used by `getExportModifier`.

Example: `--export=M.*,!M.internal*,!M.b`

Note: in bash, quote values containing `!` (`'--export=!sub'`).

## Test plan
- [x] New `ExportFilterTest` unit tests (7) pass; `MLIRGenTests` 66/66
- [x] All 268 shared-library ctest tests pass
- [x] DLL export tables checked with `llvm-objdump -p` for no option, `none`, `M.add,sub`, `!sub` and `M.*,!M.internal*,!M.b`: each exports exactly the expected symbols, including per-variable filtering of `export let a = 1, b = 2`
- [ ] Known, not changed here: `--export=all` on a DLL that uses the default lib fails to link (LNK1242, a default-lib generic instantiation gets an invalid export name). A compiler built before this change fails the same way.

body:
Fila **#32** de `PLAN.md`. Origen: `handoff-…-apertura-menos-decisiones.md` §P4.

## La premisa de P4 no se sostiene, y se midió ANTES de construir

El handoff pedía «unificar los dos constructores en la regla de la skill» para vaciar el
residuo. Medido sobre **1.352 documentos de los diez expedientes con catálogo**:

| Escenario | Resultado |
|---|---|
| **A — el motor, antes** | 770/1.352 = **57,0 %** al residuo → parada |
| **B — la regla de la skill** (lo que P4 pedía) | **90,5 %** a `07. RECLAMACIONES`, y **0** de las 123 fotos en `00. FOTOS` |
| **C — unión de las dos** | 54,4 % — rescata 34 de 1.352 |

**B es peor.** `clasificar_por_patron` detecta fotos por `screenshot|captura`; el motor las
detecta **por extensión**. La skill puede permitírselo porque tiene un LLM leyendo detrás; el
motor no. Y **C apenas mueve la aguja porque el residuo no lo causa la regla**: los nombres no
llevan la señal. Con esos números Nikolai decidió el alcance: las dos piezas que sí quedaban
en pie, dentro del módulo.

## Qué entra

1. **`[APER-61]`** — la identidad y la titularidad dejan `06. PBC` por `01. ACTIVACIÓN`, la
   hoja de visita pasa a `03. OFERTAS`, y en PBC quedan solo los Anexos 1 y 2. La tabla era la
   causa **codificada** del síntoma del runbook («`03. OFERTAS` con 1 y `06. PBC` con 28»), y
   un test lo congelaba. **87 documentos cambian**: 59 de PBC a ACTIVACIÓN, 26 que salen del
   residuo, 2 que entran (falsos positivos de substring).
2. **La frontera del token** — el match era `in`, así que `Compa·nie·s` era PBC y `c·arras·co`
   era arras. Pero palabra entera rompía `oferta2.pdf` y `PBC1 ….pdf`. Es el límite
   **izquierdo y solo el izquierdo**, con la excepción de los tokens que acaban en dígito.
3. **La parada deja de ser verja** — el residuo recibe `08. PENDIENTE DE CLASIFICAR` y la sala
   se monta entera. El coste que quita está medido: **80** documentos a mano en W-030TZY y
   **21** en W-02NHNC *antes de que existiera nada que leer*.
4. **La frontera que eso destapó** — cinco caminos preguntaban «¿está clasificado?» por su
   cuenta y coincidían por accidente mientras el residuo salía sin tipo. La pregunta vive
   ahora en `es_decision()`.

## Lo que NO hace, dicho

La clasificación **no mejora**: el 55,2 % de los nombres sigue sin permitir afirmar categoría
y acaba en `08` en vez de en una parada. La ganancia es que la sala pasa de **no existir** a
existir, fechada y nombrada. La alternativa real no era una sala clasificada: era ninguna.

## Revisión adversarial

**R1 de Codex sobre el diff: NO-SHIP, 7 hallazgos, 7 confirmados contra la fuente, 0
refutados, todos remediados.** Los dos ALTOS eran regresiones de este mismo diff y comparten
frontera: apliqué el centinela nuevo a lo que se **escribe** y no a lo que se **lee**, así que
un `08` ya persistido con confianza 1.0 quedaba congelado, incorregible y **fuera de la
worklist**, con `organizar` diciendo cero pendientes.

- Adjudicación: [spec §4](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-p4-sala-lectura-sin-parada-design.md)
- Acta literal: [`…-r1-adversarial-review.md`](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-p4-sala-lectura-sin-parada-r1-adversarial-review.md)

Un cuarto defecto de esa familia lo encontré yo antes de que volviera el informe —la guarda de
`preparar-residuo`, que quedó **inerte**— y el mandato se lo dijo al revisor para que buscara
la familia en otros sitios. Encontró tres más.

## Verificación

- **Suite: 5.527 recogidos, 0 fallos, 0 errores, 94 skipped.** Referencia del 117º cierre:
  5.470/0/0/94. El **+57** cuadra: 29 tests de `p4_sin_parada` + 27 de `p4_r1` + 1 caso
  paramétrico.
- **Dos semillas (777 y 31337) verdes** por `session_close`.
- **Arnés `tests/_mutantes_p4.py`: 31 mutantes, 31 muertos**, 1 superviviente declarado con su
  razón (el remedio de H-01 volvió redundante a `_CONF_PENDIENTE`).
- **Dos defectos del propio arnés**, corregidos: el `try` que restaura empezaba *después* de
  mutar (un `OSError` dejaba el árbol mutado), y leía `rc=4` de pytest («test no encontrado»)
  como «el test ya estaba rojo» — un diagnóstico equivocado que manda a buscar donde no está.
- La cobertura del diff sale al 84 %: las nueve líneas que marca son **entradas de la tabla
  `_KEYWORDS` y comentarios `#:`**, ni una de lógica. No hay test que escribir; los 31
  mutantes acreditan la cobertura real mejor que el porcentaje.

author: philoyhc
body:
`guide/sweep_2026-09-05_spec-docs.md` is the repo's newest **corpus** sweep — the one that stays live in `guide/`, and the designated starting point for the next one. It carried its status in three places and only one was maintained.

| Surface | Said |
|---|---|
| §0 *Carried forward*, `Now` column | C2, C3, C5, C6 → **"still open"** |
| Headline numbers | Carried in / closed / **still open — 13 / 6 / 7** |
| Findings ledger | **"All eight findings are closed"** |

**The ledger is the one that's right.** I checked all eight against the tree rather than taking its word, including 2.3 — two `app/services/*.py` package-path references survive, but both are in `docs/status.md` dated timeline rows, which is exactly the exemption the ledger records.

§0 is section zero. It is where a sweeper starts, and it presented four closed findings as live work. The ledger's own preamble says it is kept current *"so the **next** sweep reads this table as its §0 carry-forward input"* — so the one surface designed to be read first was the one left frozen.

**Cause:** 19C Item 7 updated the ledger it was pointed at and left the other two alone.

## What the file says now

- **The four C rows** read **done**, each naming the PR that closed it (C3 → 19C Item 7 PR 1; C2, C5, C6 → PR 2) instead of pointing sideways at §2.
- **§0 states which surfaces are live** — the `Now` column and the ledger, ledger wins — and which are frozen at 2026-09-05. It also carries the current account, because §0 owns it: 10 settled / 3 declined, and the Tier 3 correction below.
- **Headline numbers is untouched at `13 / 6 / 7`.** See the third commit.
- **§7's "51 of 64 not read"** gains a dated update.

## Three commits, because the first two were wrong

This is the part worth reading. Each correction came from a checker, not from me re-reading.

**1 — I invented both dates in the sentence about keeping things current.** My §0 paragraph said the two surfaces drifted *"between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-13"*, for five days. Both endpoints were made up. Git history: the file was created at 13:01 on 2026-09-05 and the ledger reached *all eight closed* at **13:52 the same day** — fifty-one minutes later. Nothing touched it on 2026-09-08; the only touch before mine was the `sweep-scope` marker on 2026-09-12.

The drift was **eight days**, and the truth is sharper than my claim: **the two surfaces were never in step.** The same afternoon that closed the findings left §0 saying the opposite. That is what it says now, with both timestamps. The sentence I got wrong was the one explaining why this section must be kept current — written from the shape of the story rather than from `git log`.

**2 — the footnote overreached on one row.** It said each of the three standing declines *"reopens on a stated trigger and on nothing else"*. True for two. The Tier 3 row bundles three items with three different situations (`spec_sweep_11may.md` §10–§12): the new-session form deferred because Quick Setup already covers it — closer to a non-finding than a deferral; the drill-in pages deferred **until pilot feedback**; the outbox needing no spec **unless promoted into Segment 16A**. Two triggers and a non-finding, in one row.

**3 — [Codex P1](https://github.com/philoyhc/review-robin-web/pull/2380#discussion_r4001342523): I made the table live in the paragraph declaring it frozen.** The first commit added a present-tense `today 13 / 10 / 3` to Headline numbers — four lines after writing *"Everything else, Headline numbers included, is frozen at 2026-09-05"*. A commit fixing a self-contradiction introduced one.

Three reasons it had to come out, and the third is the one that decides it:

- `guide/sweep_template.md:106` — *"Comparable between sweeps only if the shape stays fixed — that is the point of a template"*, with the row specified as `N / N / N`.
- `AGENTS.md` L84–96 — say it once, in the section that owns it.
- **When a decline resolves, a maintainer following my own declaration updates §0 and the ledger and leaves the headline's `today` stale — recreating exactly the bug this change exists to remove.** A third live surface is a third surface to forget.

So the row is back to `13 / 6 / 7`, unchanged from the sweep, and the live account moved into §0. Net shorter than what it replaced. One vocabulary clash is flagged there rather than fixed, because it is inherited: the sweep figure counts a **decline** as *still open*, while the ledger's "seven actioned, one declined" counts it as *closed*.

## Deliberately not reconciled

**§7's "51 of 64" is not replaced with a smaller number.** The `spec/` half of that residue is genuinely gone — 19M read all 39 live `spec/*.md` files and this sweep's 38 are a subset — so the note says that, and says the remaining residue is the `docs/` + root half, which 19M's own Out of scope refused to sweep. But this file does not tabulate its 13 read files by folder, so any smaller count would be a reconstruction. A reconstructed number in a document read under pressure is worse than a stale one that admits it is stale.

## Verification

No corpus change; this is the file agreeing with itself. `test_guide_indexes`, `test_doc_conventions` and `test_sweep_cadence` pass. `close_check --stale` unchanged at 2026-09-05 — 8 d of 56, 265 of 500, not due — which is the point of keeping this sweep in `guide/` at all.

author: igorls
body:
### Summary

When agents or users query coordination events via MemPalace's lightweight MCP tool (`palace_coordinate`) or `tool_event_list` without an explicit resume cursor (`since_event_id`), the query previously defaulted to `order='asc'`, returning the oldest 50 events from the start of the database ("from far back") rather than recent activity. Additionally, the lightweight MCP server omitted pagination parameters (`order`, `limit`, `preview`, `since_created_at`) from the `palace_coordinate` input schema, and rejected uppercase `order` strings (`ORDER DESC`).

### Changes

1. **Context-Aware Default Ordering**:
   - In `tool_event_list` / `palace_coordinate`, when `order` is omitted:
     - Defaults to **`order='desc'`** (newest events first) when `since_event_id` is omitted (inbox sweeps, browsing).
     - Defaults to **`order='asc'`** (chronological forward order) when `since_event_id` is supplied (cursor resumption).
   - Explicit `order='asc'` or `order='desc'` continues to override this default.
2. **Case Normalization & Robustness**:
   - `Logstream.list_events` and `tool_event_list` now normalize `order` case-insensitively (`'DESC'`, `'ASC'`, `'desc'`, `'asc'`) and handle `order=None` cleanly.
3. **PQL Coordination DSL Shorthands**:
   - Added `INBOX to:<agent>` and `EVENT INBOX ...` (defaults to `order='desc'` and `preview=True`).
   - Added shorthand position/order flags: `DESC`, `LATEST`, `RECENT`, `TAIL`, `ASC`, `HEAD`, `OLDEST`, `FROM_START`, `PREVIEW`.
   - Guaranteed bare flags in `_parse_key_value_tokens` do not consume following tokens.
4. **Light MCP Schema Exposure**:
   - Added `order`, `limit`, `preview`, and `since_created_at` to `LIGHT_TOOLS["palace_coordinate"]["input_schema"]["properties"]`.
   - Updated tool description with `EVENT INBOX` and newest-first pagination guidance.
5. **Documentation & Protocol Alignment**:
   - Updated `integrations/shared/coordination-protocol.md`, `mempalace/instructions/shared_brain_rules.md`, and `website/guide/shared-brain.md` explaining that sweeps without a cursor return newest events first (`order='desc'`), while resuming with `since_event_id` walks forward in append order (`order='asc'`).

### Validation

- `pytest tests/test_logstream.py tests/test_cli_logstream.py tests/test_mcp_logstream.py tests/test_mcp_light_server.py tests/test_query_parser.py tests/test_cli_rules.py`: **250 passed**, 0 failed on Windows.
- Specific tests added for:
  - Context-aware ordering in `test_mcp_logstream.py` and `test_mcp_light_server.py`.
  - Uppercase `ORDER DESC` and `ORDER ASC` handling.
  - `EVENT INBOX`, `INBOX to:agent`, and shorthand tokens (`DESC`, `LATEST`, `RECENT`, `TAIL`, `ASC`, `HEAD`, `OLDEST`, `PREVIEW`) in `test_query_parser.py`.
  - `palace_coordinate` inputSchema properties in `test_mcp_light_server.py`.
  - Pinned rule templates and documentation consistency in `test_cli_rules.py`.

author: alonebutunsober
body:
Adds a third single-shot recorder next to MP4 and the PNG sequence: tick **Save animated GIF** in the Video Zoom dialog to write one looping GIF89a of the zoom. **No ffmpeg needed** — the built-in encoder handles it. Builds on the still-GIF encoder from #68.

## Encoder (`Engine/Imaging`)
- **`GifSequenceWriter`** — streaming multi-frame writer. `WriteFrame` snapshots the BGRA buffer and hands it to a **single ordered background encoder thread** through a bounded queue, so the zoom loop only pays a memcpy (mirrors `PngSequenceWriter`'s offload); the bound caps in-flight memory by blocking the producer when the encoder lags.
  - **Per-frame local colour table** — a zoom's palette drifts frame to frame, so a shared global table would band badly.
  - **Per-frame delay from the 100-ns capture timestamps** (real cadence), clamped to a sane centisecond range.
  - Loops forever via a **NETSCAPE2.0** application extension.
- **`GifEncoder` refactor** — quantize / table-geometry / LZW / container helpers are now shared (internal) with the sequence writer; the still-GIF `Write` path is behaviourally unchanged.

## Wiring
- `VideoZoomRequest.IsSaveGif` + `VideoRecordingResult.GifTempPath`.
- `FractalRenderHost.Video`: independent `_videoGifWriter` slot — start (stereo-aware dims), feed, finalise — matching the MP4/PNG recorder lifecycle. Any combination of the three can run in one zoom.
- Video Zoom dialog: **Save animated GIF** checkbox.
- `HandleRecordingFinished` + `PromptSaveGif`: SaveFileDialog → move temp `.gif` into place; discard on cancel/fault.
- Capture-Guide documents the recorder + banding/size caveats.

## Tests
`ImageExportAnimatedGifTests` round-trips through SkiaSharp's animated-GIF decoder (`SKCodec`): 3-frame colour/count, timestamp-derived delays, NETSCAPE loop block present, and a 24-frame run exercising the bounded queue's producer-blocks path. **16 imaging tests pass**; Engine + WinExe build clean.

## Caveats (documented)
256-colour banding on smooth gradients + large files — GIF suits short zooms / stickers / embeds; MP4 stays better for quality or length.

Closes #784

author: robertogabrieu
body:
O `update.sh` fazia `git pull origin master` na branch em que o servidor estivesse. Numa branch de teste, isso misturava a master nela e subia essa mistura sem aviso. Com um commit feito direto na master do servidor, o pull virava um merge local, e prod ficava numa versão que não existe no GitHub e que ninguém consegue reproduzir.

## O que muda

- O script recusa rodar fora da `master`.
- O pull passa a ser `git pull --ff-only`, que para antes do build em qualquer divergência, com o comando (`git log origin/master..master`) para conferir o que está sobrando.
- No fim, o script mostra o commit que ficou no ar, para bater com a master do GitHub.

## Validação

`bash -n update.sh` feito. Não rodado contra o Docker (exige VPS).

body:
Credit purchases could silently reduce a requested quantity, subscription status could report failed lookups as no access, and recurring charges could fall back from the selected consent. This change makes quotes exact, access status explicit, and renewal proposals require the selected approvals. Product catalogs also support a recipient override per product.

- Add `bb credit-tokens quote` and `standard_credit_tokens_quote`, exact bigint base/display amounts, explicit tier selection, observed approval versions, and rejection of over-limit or unsupported mint/payment shapes.
- Prefer current consent for status and inspect matching consents for due, unowned renewal intervals rather than letting an expired first match mask a usable one.
- Separate paid current/future access from recorded/expired renewal consent; preserve all ownership ranges and fail on unavailable balance state.
- Share these helpers with the frontend and regenerate builder schemas and CLI-first skill guidance. Existing standards and primitives are retained.

Validation: 203 SDK suites / 3,832 tests, CJS/ESM build/import checks, 90 packed CLI invocations, and 24 CLI/MCP comparisons against isolated API fixtures passed. SDK dependency audit is clean. The private worker integration separately executed a renewal on the accepted local chain pin and verified split payouts, fees and upcoming entitlement.

Tracks BB-144, BB-148, BB-151 and the status prerequisite of BB-146. Automatic plan switching, proration, refunds, consumption accounting and new standard proposals remain outside this change. Quotes do not prove eligibility or reserve funds. No production transactions or deployment.

Private frontend/indexer/docs companion: https://github.com/BitBadges/bitbadges-monorepo/pull/47. Consumers are locally smoke-tested against this SDK; SDK merge/publication and consumer version updates are required before consumer release.

A follow-up to #35, found while checking Xenoblade Chronicles in the browser (#41).

## The problem
`game:"Xenoblade Chronicles"` on the Mechanics tab listed 12 rows, 7 of them Xenoblade Chronicles 3's (M051–M057). `game:` matched whole words from the start of a title, and "Xenoblade Chronicles 3" starts with the whole words "Xenoblade Chronicles".

## The fix
- `matchesRowQuery` takes `exactTitles`. When a `game:` value names a roster title exactly (case and spacing folded), it matches only that game. Anything else keeps the whole-word rule, so `game:persona` still finds both Persona games.
- `gameTitleKey()` and `exactTitlesOf()` live in the data region beside the matcher. The Mechanics and Minigames tabs build the set once per render from `allGames()`.
- CLAUDE.md's row-search paragraph states the rule.

  - `game:"Xenoblade Chronicles"` gives only XC1, and so does a lower-cased, double-spaced spelling;
  - `game:xenoblade` gives both;
  - `game:"Persona 4"` gives one game and `game:persona` gives two;
  - with no roster passed, the old rule still applies.
- Two mutants were caught by that test: ignoring the exact titles, and a title key that keeps case. My harness's first run mis-typed the expected test name and reported both as MISSED; each failure list already showed the new test failing, and the corrected rerun reports CAUGHT.
- `node --test`: 172/172. `validate_codex.mjs --selftest`: all 89 sabotages caught. `check_changes.mjs`: clean.
- Local browser, on a cache-busted load:

  - Minigames `game:"Final Fantasy VII Rebirth"` shows its 4, and `game:"Final Fantasy VII"`, which is not a full title, still shows all three FF7 titles;

Merging deploys the live site.

author: ericgriffin
body:
## Related Issue

Closes #1915

## Summary

With a buddy filter active, the dive list, previous/next navigation on the dive detail page, and the map views did not update when a write touched only `dive_buddies` or `buddies`. That is exactly what a sync pull of a buddy link writes (the parent dive is never restamped since #1769), and what a buddy merge or rename writes. The filtered results stayed stale until something else reloaded the list.

Each of those lists now follows a new buddy change tick, but only while a buddy filter is set, so buddy writes never reload an unfiltered list (which matters during a sync pull or a bulk import). This follows the equipment-attribute filter's pattern from #1805.

## Changes

- `DiveRepository.watchDiveListChangesWithBuddyLinks()` and `watchDivesChangesWithBuddyLinks()`: the list tick and the dives tick with `dive_buddies` and `buddies` added. The buddy tables join a consumer's existing tick rather than forming a second one, because the dive editor's link writers write `dive_buddies` and then bump the dive row outside a transaction, and two separately debounced ticks would reload the list once for each write.
- `DiveFilterState.readsBuddyLinks`: true when the buddy (`buddyId`), buddy-name or no-buddy filter is set, the three filters that read `dive_buddies`.
- `PaginatedDiveListNotifier`: switches its list tick to the buddy-aware variant while `readsBuddyLinks` holds and reloads its loaded pages in place (no spinner). The existing equipment-attribute tick moves onto a small `_FilterTickFollower`.
- `DiveListNotifier` (the in-memory list behind the dive map, activity map and heat map): switches its dives tick the same way, and reloads once when a buddy filter turns on, since unfiltered it did not watch buddy writes. The maps apply the buddy-name and no-buddy filters; `buddyId` is #1919.
- `orderedDiveIdsProvider` (previous/next navigation): self-invalidates on the buddy-aware dives tick under a buddy filter.

Statistics were not affected: `watchStatisticsChanges()` already watches both tables.

## Test Plan

- [x] `flutter test` on the affected directories (dive_log, architecture, maps, buddies, statistics): 5,490 passed, plus the provider and maps suites after the last review fix
- [x] `flutter analyze` passes (whole project, no issues)
- [ ] Manual testing on: macOS (filter by a buddy, link that buddy to another dive from a second device, sync)

New tests in `buddy_filter_reload_test.dart`, run against a real in-memory database, with each write going straight to `dive_buddies` or `buddies` the way a sync pull does:

- a link-only write reloads a buddy-filtered page and its count
- a buddy rename reloads a name-filtered page
- a no-buddy list drops a dive that gains a link
- an unfiltered list does not reload on a buddy write, including after a buddy filter is cleared
- previous/next ids refresh under a buddy filter
- the in-memory list behind the maps refreshes under a buddy-name filter
- a local buddy edit (`addBuddyToDive`) reloads a buddy-filtered page once, and the maps list once (both reloaded twice before the ticks were combined)
- turning on a buddy filter re-reads the maps list after a link written while it was unfiltered

The first five behavior tests failed before the fix, each on stale data. `repository_tick_stream_test.dart` registers both buddy-aware ticks in the "silent until written" guard and checks that each fires on `dive_buddies` and on `buddies`; removing either table makes the matching test fail. `dive_filter_state_test.dart` covers `readsBuddyLinks`, including a blank-only name filter such as `' , '`.

author: ibrahim1774
body:
Ports PrimeHub's `/barber` gate to aibarber.org `"/"`, **plus** the Places fast path and two-key type-ahead. Left unmerged on purpose: it replaces the main signup funnel, so please look at the preview first.

## What changes
Bare root `"/"` only. The visitor is asked whether they have a booking link, then either the booking page is scraped (existing `/api/import-scrape`) or the Google listing is found. Both branches hand `handleGenerate` a **prebuilt** `WebsiteData`, so real photos, reviews, hours and rating survive rather than being regenerated.

`/booksy`, `/free-barber`, `/new`, `/generate` and the pricing-test paths keep `GeneratorForm` untouched. AI-Barber prices from the plan slug plus `window.location.pathname`, and `"/"` already priced as the homepage, so **no funnel's pricing moves**.

## Speed: Places first, Apify fallback
`find-business` and `import-business` try Google Places first (target ~1s) and fall through to the untouched Apify path when the server key is absent, Places misses, or Places errors. Each request logs which path served it and how long it took, so the speedup is visible in the function logs.

## The two keys, same as PrimeHub
| Variable | Where | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_PLACES_SERVER_KEY` | server | search, detail fetch, photo resolution, and the type-ahead fallback |
| `VITE_GOOGLE_PLACES_KEY` | browser | type-ahead straight from the visitor's browser, no server hop |

The dropdown works with either key present. The browser key must be referrer-restricted to `aibarber.org` in Google Cloud; if Google rejects it, the dropdown silently falls back to the server route. **Neither key is set on this project yet.** Everything still works today via Apify, verified live against a real shop (Iconic Cutz): correct phone, address, 10 photos, 7 days of hours, 4 reviews.

## Photos, and one thing that is UNVERIFIED
The API key travels only in the `X-Goog-Api-Key` header, never a query string. Each photo ref is resolved server-side to a Google-hosted URL, validated against the `googleusercontent`/`ggpht` host family, and dropped on failure. Raw refs ride along as `_photoRefs`, and `hostPhotos()` in `lib/gbp/gbpPlaces.ts` is the single seam where Blob re-hosting would go.

**Photo-URL longevity from the Places path is unverified** — Google's issue tracker has reports of these expiring. First thing to check once the key lands: import a shop, save a photo URL, re-fetch it a day later. If it rots, `hostPhotos()` is the one function to change.

## Deliberately not ported
`pricingTier` and PrimeHub's tier names (only comments remain), the NICHES system, and Blob photo re-hosting.

author: franklinhu1
body:
Removes the "Personal page" text from every page. ## Why #4 didn't already do this "Personal page" is **not in this repository** — grep finds it in no file. It comes from the GitHub repository's own *description* field (Settings → About), which currently reads `Personal page`. Removing the `description` key outright in #4 didn't leave the footer empty; it handed control to that fallback. GitHub Pages populates `site.description` from the repo description when the config doesn't set one, and minima's footer prints it unconditionally — [v2.5.1 `footer.html:29`](https://github.com/jekyll/minima/blob/v2.5.1/_includes/footer.html#L29): ```liquid

{{- site.description | escape -}}

``` So the long description was simply swapped for a shorter one. Verified on the live site after #4 merged — all five pages show `Personal page` in the footer, and it is back in ``, `og:description`, and the JSON-LD block. ## The fix ```diff +description: "" ``` An explicit empty string overrides the fallback, so the footer renders `

` with nothing in it. Confirmed by loading the config in Ruby: `description` is a `String` of length 0, not `nil`, which is what's needed — a missing key is exactly the condition that triggers the fallback. ## Why not just clear the repo description? That would also work, and it would remove the text from the site *and* from the About box on the GitHub repo page. Since you asked to remove it from the website, this PR keeps the change inside the repo and leaves your GitHub About blurb alone. Say the word if you'd rather clear that field too — it's a one-liner (`gh repo edit --description ""`), and then this PR becomes optional belt-and-braces. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## Summary

This PR is the pre-release routing eval that v1.9.1 carried over (`prompts/opchain-eval`, 40 cases, `pass_rate: 1.0`). The first run found one trigger-copy miss, and this PR fixes it.

**Method.** The eval runs through `/oc-prompt eval`, which calls a model, and no scripted runner exists. So it ran agent-driven in two stages:

1. **Router.** An isolated agent answered all 40 requests. It could read only a file with each invocable skill's frontmatter description and declared commands, plus orchestrator.md §4. It had no access to `expected.jsonl`, `tests/` or `src/`.
2. **Grading.** A script graded the 13 `contains` cases. A separate isolated `llm_judge` graded the 27 collision cases, using only each case's criteria and the router's output.

| Run | contains | llm_judge | Total | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (main at 7234ad6) | 12/13 | 27/27 | **39/40** | route-005 |
| 2 (this branch) | 13/13 | 27/27 | **40/40** | none |

body:
## What was done

Follow-up to #166. After that fix resolved the login/onboarding regression, a new agent still hit:

```
SessionStart:startup hook error
Failed with non-blocking status code: security-guidance: no working Python 3 interpreter found.
```

`dd11b02` baked the official `security-guidance` plugin into the agent image. Every one of its hooks (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop) shells out through `sg-python.sh`, which requires a real Python >= 3.10 interpreter (`claude_agent_sdk`'s minimum) to bootstrap a venv, falling back to `pip install --target` when it can't. `node:22-alpine` has never shipped a Python interpreter at all, so the hook's own interpreter search always came up empty.

Fix: add `python3` + `py3-pip` to the image's existing `apk add` line.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified `node:22-alpine`'s `python3` is 3.14.7, well above the SDK's `>=3.10` floor
- [x] Installed `python3 py3-pip` at runtime into the currently-published (pre-fix) image and ran the actual `sg-python.sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/ensure_agent_sdk.py"` SessionStart hook end-to-end: the interpreter is now found and the hook exits 0 (previously: "no working Python 3 interpreter found", exit 1)
- [x] The venv+pip install of `claude_agent_sdk` itself still fails in this sandbox's restricted network (`sdk_bootstrap_err: pip_no_match`) — an unrelated, already-documented sandbox limitation (same class as the gopls/plugin-marketplace network restrictions noted in #166's test plan). The plugin's own design degrades to pattern-based checks in that case rather than failing outright; the fatal interpreter error this issue is about is resolved
- [x] Confirmed the new `agent-image-smoke` python3 check **fails** against the current (pre-fix) published image — proves it would have caught this regression in CI
- [x] Confirmed the same check **passes** with `python3`/`py3-pip` added, in an isolated Dockerfile reproduction (full multi-stage build still can't run end-to-end in this sandbox for the same unrelated network reasons as #166)

body:
## Summary

`SignupScreen` never called the existing `validatePassword` util, so a password failing the backend's 12-char / uppercase / lowercase / digit rules only failed after a round trip, and `ValidationError` hardcodes "Invalid request" so the rule was never shown in any build. On 2026-09-06 an invitee failed 10 times (exactly the shared `authLimiter` cap), misread it as a bad invite code, and an admin cancelled a working invite chasing the wrong cause.

This PR enforces the cheap backend rules client-side before any network call, states the password rule on the field before the user types, anchors each error to its field, and makes the rate-limit outcome legible.

**Changes**
- **`TextInput`** (shared): additive `helperText` / `error` props. Error-coloured border outranks focus; `${testID}-error` (with `accessibilityLiveRegion`) and `${testID}-helper` nodes; a reserved two-line slot when a helper is present so the helper→error swap does not reflow the fields below (the `PasswordConfirmModal` pattern); `accessibilityLabel` / `accessibilityHint` on the native input.
- **`validatePassword`**: messages aligned verbatim with `Orbital-Backend/src/routes/auth.js`; `PASSWORD_RULE_HINT` exported as the single helper-copy source; the drifted `// Mirrors:` claim replaced by an explicit hand-maintained-parity note (bcrypt 72-byte ceiling, reset-screen mislabel caveat, references to #783 / #786).
- **`SignupScreen`**: pre-flight order required → email → username (3-50 chars, `[A-Za-z0-9_]`) → password → 20-char invite code, all before `setLoading`; each failure sets its field error, clears on edit, and never calls `signupUser`. Password field gains the helper text and `textContentType="newPassword"`. New `RATE_LIMITED` catch branch so a 429 no longer renders as "Server error — please try again".
- **`ResetPasswordScreen`**: weak-password failure routed to the field via the new `error` prop, with the same helper text. Code-length / mismatch stay on the banner.
- **`JoinOrbitScreen` / `CreateOrbitScreen`**: hand-rolled error `Text` + local `errorStyle` replaced by `error={error}` on the adjacent shared `TextInput` (DEBT-319).

**Plan review** (`plan-777-2026-09-13`): security-auditor, tech-debt-collector, api-integration-engineer. 0 blocking; 1 disputed (skeptic-refuted, adopted anyway); advisory items folded in (rate-limit branch, username/invite guards, reset field error, hint export, orbit-screen migration, exact-message tests).

**Follow-ups filed:** Mobile #783 (ValidationError allowlist), #784 (LoginScreen RATE_LIMITED), #785 (client email rule), #786 (parity detector); Backend #270 (silent invite-code lookup logging).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npx eslint` on changed files: 0 errors (1 pre-existing inline-style warning on main)
- [x] Full jest suite: 162 suites / 2717 tests pass, 0 skipped (verified twice: implementer + orchestrator)
- [x] New unit cases: too-short / no-uppercase / no-digit password → field error, no `signupUser` call; short / spaced username → field error; 19-char invite → field error; helper present on mount; error clears on edit; email guard wins over password guard (ordering pinned); `RATE_LIMITED` `ApiError` → "Too many attempts" banner; reset weak-password asserts the field node with the exact message; TextInput helper / error / suppression / border cases
- [ ] Manual iOS-sim smoke (Alex's merge gate): helper visible under Password before typing; 11-char, missing-uppercase, missing-digit → red border + inline message and no request in Metro; short / spaced username and 19-char invite → inline; valid → real request; typing clears each error; banner still shows server errors (taken username); light and dark mode; iOS strong-password suggestion passes validation. The 429 path cannot be smoked (limiter skipped in dev) and is unit-covered only.
## Fold-in after PR review (commit bbb6b77)

The review panel (run `pr-787-2026-09-13`: security-auditor, tech-debt-collector, qa-testing-specialist, react-native-engineer) returned **0 blocking, 0 disputed, 18 advisory**. Alex chose to fold the advisories in:

- **Stale banner fix** (3 reviewers): every error slot is cleared at the top of `handleSignup` / reset `handleSubmit`; two-submit regression tests on both screens.
- **JoinOrbit / CreateOrbit** (3 reviewers): `ErrorBanner` added; catch sites discriminate on error class (network / 429 / unknown → banner, `ValidationError` / `NotFoundError` → field); both slots clear on edit; JoinOrbit gets a 20-char pre-flight. CreateOrbit is banner-only because the orbit name is encrypted client-side and never validated server-side.
- **`inviteCrypto`** exports `V2_CODE_LENGTH` + `isValidV2InviteCode`; used by Signup and JoinOrbit.

Filed as follow-ups instead: #788 (iOS VoiceOver announcement + double label), #789 (TextInput convergence blockers). Full suite after fold-in: **163 suites / 2750 tests**, tsc clean, 0 lint errors.

Targeted re-review of bbb6b77 (run `pr-787-delta-2026-09-13`: security-auditor, react-native-engineer) returned **0 blocking, 12 advisory**. Folded in:
