author: asoldano
body:
This extends the validated MiniMax-H3 gfx1151 QKV packing range from 16.5k to 24k tokens and includes the actual token count in verbose fallback logging.

I tested the existing H3 benchmark beyond the current 16.5k limit on a Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S using:

  • PyTorch 2.14.0a0+rocm7.15.0a20260721

  • ROCm 7.15

  • AOTriton attention backend

  • BF16, B=1 H=56 D=128

Results:

Tokens | Strided SDPA | Packed SDPA | Speedup | Max abs error | Cosine similarity -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 18,000 | 2073.392 ms | 355.638 ms | 5.830x | 0 | 1.000000238 20,000 | 2681.392 ms | 424.049 ms | 6.323x | 0 | 1.000000000 22,000 | 3618.326 ms | 507.201 ms | 7.134x | 0 | 0.999999881 24,000 | 4498.734 ms | 607.641 ms | 7.404x | 0 | 1.000000119

So on this gfx1151 stack the packed path remains correct and the performance advantage actually increases beyond the previous 16.5k cutoff.

I also tested it with an actual MiniMax-H3 I2V workflow. At 0.5 MP, 5 seconds, 8 steps with the low-step LoRA, the attention sequence is T=20832. With the original 16.5k cutoff this fell back to the existing backend and sampling was around 24 minutes. Raising the limit allows QKV packing at T=20832; the sampling phase completed in ~6m15s — roughly a 3.8x end-to-end improvement.

This PR therefore:

  • raises MINIMAX_H3_MAX_PACK_TOKENS from 16500 to 24000;

  • raises the MiniMax-H3 benchmark UI limit to 24000;

  • includes T=<tokens> in verbose fallback logs when the token count is available.

The attention math/backend is unchanged; this only extends the existing QKV layout optimization to a range that the above gfx1151 tests show remains both correct and beneficial.

author: kusuconsult-ng
body:
`safeEqual` in `lib/crypto.ts` describes itself as *"for OTPs, signatures and
verification codes"*. It was called from **one** place — `verifyWebhookSignature`
— and of the three things it names, signatures were the only one it was used
for.

| Credential | Was compared with | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Webhook signature (mock gateway) | `safeEqual` | unchanged |
| **Remita notification secret** | `presented !== expectedSecret` | `safeEqual` |
| **OTP** | `sha256(code) !== code_hash` | `safeEqual` |
| Receipt verification code | matched in SQL | unchanged — different mechanism |

**The one that mattered.** The Remita notification secret is checked on a public
callback with no attempt limiting, so a caller may present guesses in a loop and
time them, and a short-circuiting compare returns sooner the earlier it meets a
wrong byte. It is the only credential a caller presents to this platform that
was compared that way.

**The one that did not.** The OTP compares two hex digests, so a timing
difference exposes bytes of the stored hash rather than of the code, and
`max_attempts` bounds guessing regardless. Close to worthless as a leak. Changed
because the helper's own comment names OTPs, and a control that names a use it
is not put to is the shape this repository keeps finding.

Behaviour is unchanged for every credential, right or wrong: `safeEqual` returns
false on a length mismatch and compares in constant time otherwise.

## Where the guard went, and why not at the call sites

Swapping `!==` for `!safeEqual(...)` is **observationally identical** when the
helper is correct. No test of those two sites could tell the versions apart:
reverting either changes no result, only a timing profile, and a test asserting
on timing would be flaky by construction.

What the substitution depends on is `safeEqual` itself — which **nothing
exercised**, and which is now load-bearing at three credential checks. A version
returning `true` on a length mismatch would have turned two comparisons into
open doors, quietly.

So the guard goes where the risk is: matching, differing in the first byte,
differing in the last, shorter, longer, empty, and hex digests the way the OTP
door now compares them.

Mutation-checked, **with one prediction missed and reported**: making it return
`true` on a length mismatch fails three cases, not the two I predicted — the
empty credential is a length mismatch too, which I had not counted. Removing the
length guard so `timingSafeEqual` throws also fails three, as predicted.

## Verification

API suite **2199/2199**. Typecheck and dead-predicate checks clean.

body:
## What

Add `onevcs recoverable --repo <PATH>` to list one repository identity’s preserved branches from any working directory. It shares `publish-branch --repo` resolution for aliases, checkout-root paths, identity keys, and normalized origins; unknown values and checkout subdirectories are refused.

Explicit scope is named in the output, composes with `--all`, and preserves JSON fields and recovery commands. Existing directory-based behavior remains unchanged. End-to-end coverage and a flag drift gate hold the behavior and documented usage together.

## Why

Operators supervising work in another repository previously had to change directories or sift through branches across every registered identity. Explicit repository selection lets them ask from their current checkout through the `just recoverable` wrapper, preserving the wrapper’s resume commands that prevent publishing with an empty description.

author: muriloalmeida-alt
body:
Closes #30.

## O que foi implementado

Integração real de WhatsApp por empresa via Zernio (Meta Cloud API), num módulo novo e isolado (`apps/api/src/integrations/zernio/`): autenticação server-to-server, criação/reuso idempotente de profile, onboarding via Embedded Signup hospedado, callback validado por correlação interna (nunca pelos parâmetros isolados), confirmação de estado só por consulta real ao provedor, webhook seguro (HMAC + dedup persistente + processamento síncrono), envio idempotente de mensagem, consulta de status real, e tratamento de desconexão.

`ResourcesService`/`PreparationReadinessService` (Track A, TD19) **não foram alterados** — o novo módulo só sincroniza a mesma linha `Integration` (`type: WHATSAPP`) que essas duas classes já leem, sempre com `connectionMode: REAL` (nunca `SIMULATED`).

Dois bugs reais encontrados e corrigidos durante o desenvolvimento dos testes e2e:
- **Bug de produção**: o bodyParser padrão do Nest consumia o corpo da requisição antes do `express.raw()` do webhook rodar, quebrando a verificação HMAC silenciosamente. Corrigido com `bodyParser: false` + registro manual dos parsers na ordem correta.
- **Achado de supertest**: `superagent` serializa (`JSON.stringify`) qualquer corpo não-`string` quando o `Content-Type` é JSON — inclusive um `Buffer` —, o que quebraria a assinatura testada. Os testes agora enviam a versão string (utf8) do buffer assinado.

## Arquivos criados e alterados

- **Novo módulo**: `apps/api/src/integrations/zernio/` (client HTTP, assinatura HMAC, config, métricas, tipos, serviços de conexão/mensagens/webhook, controllers, middleware, module) + 7 arquivos de teste unitário (60 testes).
- **Alterados**: `schema.prisma` (5 tabelas + 3 enums novos), `app.module.ts`, `main.ts` (bodyParser + validação de env no boot), `prisma.service.ts` (2 métodos de lookup RLS), `.env.example`.
- **Novo teste e2e**: `apps/api/test/zernio.e2e-spec.ts` (14 testes, Postgres real com RLS).
- **Documentação**: `docs/technical/21-zernio-whatsapp-integration.md` (novo), TD22 em `docs/technical/17-technical-decisions.md`, nota de ponteiro em `docs/technical/05-whatsapp.md`.

## Migrações necessárias

`apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260913223000_zernio_whatsapp_integration/` — precisa ser rodada em produção antes do deploy.

## Variáveis de ambiente

`ZERNIO_API_KEY`, `ZERNIO_BASE_URL` (opcional), `ZERNIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `ZERNIO_REDIRECT_URL`, `ZERNIO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (opcional) — documentadas em `.env.example`, sem valores reais. Sem `ZERNIO_API_KEY`, a integração fica desabilitada (não é erro). Com ela presente, produção falha no boot se faltar alguma das outras obrigatórias.

## Decisões e trade-offs

Ver TD22 (`docs/technical/17-technical-decisions.md`) e a seção 6 de `docs/technical/21-zernio-whatsapp-integration.md`: módulo isolado (não reaproveita `ResourcesService`); webhook processado de forma síncrona (sem fila, decisão documentada como reversível); métricas in-process como placeholder (nomes já na convenção Prometheus); dois padrões novos de RLS ("lookup por accountId/correlationId antes de conhecer o tenant" e `OR company_id IS NULL` para eventos órfãos); tipos do Zernio transcritos do contrato dado pelo PO, **não validados contra o OpenAPI real** (rede bloqueada neste ambiente) — flagueado para revisão antes de produção.

## Testes executados e resultados

- Unitários: **102/102** passando (14 suítes — 60 novos do Zernio + 42 pré-existentes).
- E2E: **53/53** passando (4 suítes — 14 novos do Zernio + 39 pré-existentes), contra Postgres real com RLS de verdade.
- `tsc --noEmit`: limpo. `nest build`: limpo.
- `npm run lint`: indisponível (ESLint não instalado nesta workspace — débito pré-existente, não introduzido nem resolvido aqui).

## Pendências ou riscos reais

- Tipos do contrato Zernio não conferidos contra o OpenAPI oficial (inacessível neste ambiente).
- Sem fila: processamento de webhook é síncrono, dentro da requisição HTTP.
- Sem consumidor de resposta automática (`standby`/`shouldAutoRespond` só documentam a regra).
- Sem tela dedicada no `apps/web` para o resultado do callback (fora do escopo confirmado desta issue).
- Registro do webhook (`ensureWebhookRegistered`) não é automático no bootstrap — precisa ser disparado manualmente uma vez em produção.
- `zernio_http_request_duration` não existe como métrica nomeada separada (duração é coletada sem breakdown).

## Passos manuais para configurar o Zernio e produção

1. Obter `ZERNIO_API_KEY` no Zernio.
2. Gerar `ZERNIO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` no BRAÇO e configurá-lo também no Zernio.
3. `ZERNIO_REDIRECT_URL` apontando para o domínio do **apps/api** (nunca o do apps/web).
4. Rodar a migração em produção.
5. Chamar `ensureWebhookRegistered()` uma vez (idempotente) com a URL pública do webhook e a lista de eventos.
6. Confirmar que as chaves nunca chegam ao frontend.
7. Revisar os tipos contra o OpenAPI real antes do primeiro cliente.

2. Re-rodei o bootstrap de IC95% (mesmo método de sempre — `node` importando `api/backtest-betting.js` com mock de `req`/`res` contra produção) em todas as 16 combinações de linha (6 total + 5×2 por time) × 2 ligas, sem filtro de modelo.

## Resultado

**O achado inicial de BSS positivo em cartões não sobrevive a dado real.** De 35 grupos com amostra >=20, nenhum é significativo (IC95% cruza zero em todos).

Mais revelador: as linhas baixas por time que antes do fix davam ROI **fabricado de +560% a +633%** (artefato da zeragem do agregado `discipline` do FotMob) agora **invertem pra -53% a -69%** com as MESMAS apostas, só que resolvidas contra o cartão real — confirmação definitiva de que aquele número era 100% artefato de dado corrompido, não sinal real do modelo.

## O que mudou

Só `CONTEXTO_PROJETO.md` — documenta a conclusão e fecha a pendência imediata que abriu esta investigação. Conferido que `model_betting_strategy` já tinha `estrategia='nenhuma'`/`'nunca'` pra toda linha de cartões antes desta investigação começar — **reconfirmado com dado corrigido, nenhuma escrita na tabela foi necessária**.

author: jacksonzheng07
body:
Answers the open question left at the end of `docs/design/2026-09-13-neutral-dark-palette-design.md`: nine sections separated by a single 15-value step read as one scroll, which is exactly what the light palette used five hues to avoid.

## Four steps, not two

| | deep | surface | raised | high |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | `#1a1a1a` | `#272727` | `#343434` | `#414141` |

An even 13 values apart, over a total range of **39** where it used to be 15. The inks lift with them — `muted` → `#c4c4c4`, `line` → `#dcdcdc`, `figure` → `#a6a6a6` — because the top of the ramp is brighter than anything the old inks were measured against.

Contrast over the grain, computed rather than estimated:

```
             deep  surface  raised   high   needs
  ink       13.84    11.64    9.59   7.83     4.5
  ink-brt   15.91    13.39   11.03   9.00     4.5
  muted      9.12     7.68    6.32   5.16     4.5
  line      11.60     9.76    8.04   6.57     3.0
  figure     6.54     5.50    4.53   3.70     3.0
```

**The lightest step is where the ramp stops, not where it ran out of ideas.** `muted` clears AA on `#414141` by +0.66; a fifth, lighter step would put the 11px specimen labels under the threshold. Two new tests hold that — one asserts the margin (and fails if there is suddenly room for another step, which would mean the ramp drifted), one asserts the four steps stay evenly spaced. A ramp that drifts reads as four arbitrary greys rather than as a scale.

## A drawn edge, because steps alone do not say *where*

13 values is enough to read as a change of band and not enough to read as an edge — and a band whose start you cannot locate is half the definition problem. Every band now draws its own top hairline: one pixel of the rule colour at 22%, inset.

`box-shadow` rather than `border-top` on purpose: a border would change the height of nine sections and would compete with the structural 2px rules the design already uses to mean something.

## Rhythm, verified rather than eyeballed

`tone-auto` cycles through all four steps instead of flipping between two, and the explicit tones were reassigned per page so no two adjacent bands land on the same value. The band that used to be `tone="night"` gets the deepest step back.

I checked this by reading the **painted** background of every band on every route, not by looking at it:

```
/                  39 -> 52 -> 26 -> 65 -> 39 -> 52   ok
/work/             39 -> 52 -> 65                     ok
/notes/            39 -> 52 -> 65 -> 52 -> 65 -> 39 -> 65 -> 26   ok
/work/pystruct/    39 -> 52 -> 39 -> 65 -> 39 -> 52 -> 65 -> 26 -> 52 -> 39   ok
/404.html          39 -> 52                           ok
```

That caught a real one: the home page's hero and its first `Section` were both painting 39, because the hero is a bare `<section class="tone-surface">` and the plan had given the band after it `surface` too.

## Verification

732 unit tests, 83 e2e, lint and `tsc --noEmit` clean, static export builds.

The e2e were run with `--workers=1`. The parallel runner masked 8 real failures earlier in this stack — it reported "75 passed" of 83 and exited 0 — so serial is the number I trust here. Worth pinning in `playwright.config.ts` separately.

author: shockstricken
body:
## Problem

OpenGameInstaller on the console (`packages/opengameinstaller.nix`, installed by `modules/nixos/console/launchers.nix`) runs its addons on Bun. On NixOS, OGI's upstream `application/src/electron/lib/bun-setup.ts` returns `ready` only when a `bun` is already on PATH, and `unsupported` otherwise — the curl-to-`~/.bun` installer path is skipped on NixOS by design. Without a system Bun, the addon runtime is simply unavailable.

## Change

Adds `pkgs.bun` to `environment.systemPackages` in `modules/nixos/console/launchers.nix`, beside `opengameinstaller`, with a one-line comment. OGI's AppImage wrapper (`appimageTools.wrapType2`) appends the host PATH inside its FHS env, so `/run/current-system/sw/bin/bun` is visible to OGI once this lands.

Also updates the `console/launchers.nix` row in `docs/component-inventory.md` and re-stamps the doc header to the `main` commit this branch is cut from (`440c427`, 2026-09-13).

## Why `modules/nixos/console/` and not a host tree

`modules/nixos/console/launchers.nix` is already console-only: `modules/nixos/console/default.nix` imports it explicitly (not autowired), and that module's own header states it "is imported only by the console host (`configurations/nixos/console/default.nix`), so it reaches neither desktop nor laptop." Adding `pkgs.bun` here reaches exactly the one machine that needs it.

## nixpkgs evidence

`nixpkgs.locked.rev` from this repo's `flake.lock`:

```
$ jq -r '.nodes.nixpkgs.locked.rev' flake.lock
eaad089433ca2bb662274377d33df3d0e51ef28b
```

`pkgs/by-name/bu/bun/package.nix` exists at that exact rev (fetched via octocode `ghGetFileContent`, `NixOS/nixpkgs@eaad089433ca2bb662274377d33df3d0e51ef28b`): `pname = "bun"`, `version = "1.3.13"`, builds `x86_64-linux` (among other platforms), `mainProgram = "bun"`. The `nixos` MCP server (`uvx mcp-nixos`) is not available on this runtime, so this file fetch is the evidence in its place.

## Scope note

`launchers.nix` is outside `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`'s format-check path list; this PR does not add it or touch that list.

## Success condition

After Kevin's next rebuild of the console host, OGI's Bun setup screen reports Bun as ready (no install prompt), and an OGI addon runs.

## Rollback

Revert this PR and rebuild the console host.

## Validation run (all cheap — no build/eval)

- `command -v nix` → empty, exit 1: **not format-checked locally** — `nix` is unavailable on this runtime; CI's `nix fmt -- --check` step is the gate.
- `git diff --stat` → exactly the two permitted files (`docs/component-inventory.md`, `modules/nixos/console/launchers.nix`).
- `jq -r '.nodes.nixpkgs.locked.rev' flake.lock` → `eaad089433ca2bb662274377d33df3d0e51ef28b` (as above).

Closes SHOC-335

author: mestopholis
body:
Compartments slice 3, the last slice of ADR-077's plan. The plan moves to `plans/completed/`.

## Extension upgrades

`maludb_vectors.reverify` runs inside the upgrade's per-tenant transaction, for any tenant that holds the vector store (enabled now or in the past):

1. re-derives the owner role's grants from the new extension;
2. **revokes what the new extension no longer needs**;
3. re-installs the wrappers and exercises them as `service_role`.

A release that breaks the wrappers rolls that tenant back.

- **Why grants converge here instead of refusing:** refusing an owner for holding a grant a release stopped needing would roll back every otherwise good upgrade. Enable still refuses a hand-added grant.
- **Why a full project can't block its own upgrade:** the wrapper check raises the limits inside a rolled-back savepoint and uses a compartment name no customer can already have. So a project at its limit, or on a zero-limit plan, still upgrades.

**Test gap:** this node's previous `maludb_core` predates vector compartments, so no tenant can be enabled and then genuinely upgraded here. Instead:
- `reverify` is tested on enabled tenants: narrowing a stale grant (with a control), passing at zero limits while leaving the limits unchanged, and leaving a vectors-less tenant untouched;
- the upgrade's call to `reverify`, and its rollback, are tested with a failing `reverify`.

## Official-client compatibility

`tests/compat/vectors.mjs` drives supabase-js through the real gateway, PostgREST and provisioner, in three phases: before enabling, after, and after turning it off.

| Area | Cases |
|---|---|
| Writes | create; insert with number-array embeddings; delete |
| Search | nearest-first with metadata; metadata filter |
| Errors | `PT403` with hint `vector_max_count`; `PT404` |
| Access | `anon` and a signed-in user refused by the function grant (`42501`) |
| Surface | `public` unchanged; refused by name when no MaluDB feature is on |

14 cases in all.

## Docs

- **Customers:** `docs/MALUDB-FEATURES.md`, including the server-side-only caveat and pgvector with RLS as the end-user search answer.
- **Operators:** `docs/MALUDB.md`.
- **Matrix:** `specs/compatibility-matrix.yaml` → `maludb_extensions.vector_compartments`.
- **Decisions:** the choices made during the build are recorded under ADR-077.

## Tests

170 passed across `test_maludb_vectors`, `test_extension_upgrade`, `test_grants_upgrade`, `test_compatibility` (full), `test_maludb_enable` and `test_maludb_jobs`.

Security-Review: none (commit trailer).

author: fijimunkii
body:
Device lists currently query only legacy claims and links. Add a transaction-scoped mixed list that preserves device-ID pagination, scope, retirement, independent claim expiry and original last-seen times. Devices present in both formats appear once. The existing list's treatment of link start/presence validity remains unchanged.

The reader uses an ordered device-ID range scan followed by indexed device-to-group and group-to-batch lookups. Its explicit join order avoids SQLite scanning all retained batches per cursor step. It validates selected original evidence using the same checks as detail reads, stops on proven last-seen/page bounds, and returns no partial page when corruption or the 1,024-batch work budget prevents completion.

Part of #150. No live runtime activation, new index, retention-policy change or daily footprint claim. Activity/other history readers, complete referential integrity, lifecycle, migration/rollback and runtime wiring remain before the unchanged full-controller workload can establish the 30 MiB/day budget.

# Pull Request

## Summary

Two tests had been red on `main` for a while. Both were mine, and both had rotted the same way: they asserted things about *how the code was written* rather than *whether it worked*, so a later refactor made them fail while the behaviour they cared about was fine — and, worse, they had stopped being able to catch the bugs they existed for.

Net diff against `main` is three files, all tests and scripts. No production code changes.

Full suite: **649 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed.**

> **Scope note.** This PR originally also added `response_format` to `LearningTask`. #48 (`codex/guided-teaching`) already carries that change and carries it further — a three-value Literal including `completion`, sequenced by an explicit gradual-release phase, with web/iOS/Android support already written. Mine was written without knowledge of that branch. Rather than make #48 rebase around a duplicate field, I reverted it in `9a5885a`; the revert commit explains why. What remains is complementary to #48 — see the [findings I posted there](https://github.com/Hectorg0827/LyoBackendJune/pull/48#issuecomment-5657290292).

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [x] Tests (adding or updating tests)
- [ ] CI/CD changes

## Changes Made

**`scripts/e2e_learner_loop.py` — the one test that walks the whole chain**

Step 8 ("a Classroom session on a planned topic reaches that plan") mocked `process_trigger` and hand-injected a Scene into `active_scenes`, then called `handle_quiz_submission` — which does nothing but delegate to `process_trigger`. The mock meant the step graded nothing at all. Separately, `process_trigger` now routes every turn through the adaptive session, which grades against the durable `GuidedState.pending`, never an injected scene. The step was testing a shape of the code that no longer exists.

It now drives the real path: a seeded checkpoint, a real trigger, real grading, the real evidence outbox, the real projections and the real readiness endpoint. Only `assemble_context` is stubbed — an authored course behind the session is not what this step is about — and DKT is held back so its absence cannot be what makes the step pass.

**`tests/test_skill_key_convergence.py` — every DKT call names the skill canonically**

It counted occurrences of the literal string `dkt_skill_id = self._canonical_concept_id(` and required exactly two. The quiz path was since refactored to reach mastery through the event processor, leaving one direct call site: invariant intact, count wrong, test red and saying nothing useful.

It now parses the engine with `ast`, finds every `update_mastery` call and requires the skill it names to be a variable bound from `_canonical_concept_id` — robust to renaming and to the number of call sites — plus a floor of one call site, so deleting the last one cannot pass vacuously.

**`tests/test_protocol_contract.py` — a missing optional dependency should not take down the suite**

It called `sys.exit(1)` at import time when `temporalio` was absent, turning a missing optional package into a *collection crash* that killed the entire run rather than one module. On a machine without `temporalio`, plain `pytest` reported `3 skipped` and nothing else. It now uses `importorskip`.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Integration tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [x] All tests pass locally

**Test environment:** Linux · Python 3.11 · SQLite (in-memory) for the e2e walk

**Test steps:**
1. `python3 -m pytest -q` → 649 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed.
2. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_e2e_learner_loop.py` → 40/40 checks.

**Both rewrites were mutation-tested** — broken on purpose, confirmed red, restored:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Evidence logging becomes a no-op | red |
| Outbox never written | red |
| File evidence under `learning_objective` (the original concept-identity bug) | red |
| Pass the raw concept id to DKT | red |
| Pass an un-checked name alongside a canonical one | red |
| Remove the DKT call entirely | red |

The third row is the one that matters: re-introducing the concept-identity bug — a learner completing sessions and being told they never started — now fails the walk, and **could not have been caught before this change**. That is the bug the walk exists for.

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines

None — tests and one script only.

## Reviewer Notes

Worth merging before #48 regardless of what happens to that PR: the `test_protocol_contract.py` fix is what lets CI report anything at all on a runner without `temporalio`, and these two tests are red on #48's head today for reasons that have nothing to do with it. Verified directly — with these three files applied on top of `22e0226`, that branch goes from 3 failures to 1, and the last one is a stale test I've patched [in a comment there](https://github.com/Hectorg0827/LyoBackendJune/pull/48#issuecomment-5657290292).
